Letter-free atlases were generated but are not accepted. Quick Pillow re-encodes show border and glow degradation (RGBA mean error 2.9 to 15.4). Uncompressed substitution is not justified, and the original loader's format flag mapping is not proven.
- **QTE captions: current bindings, compact names, original art on failure** [code-confirmed] Captions come from the current bindings (pc_binding_get). Default keyboard captions Spc, R, Q, F, M2 and M1 fit at three aspects. Trigger legends are Right mouse / C and Left mouse / V and fit a 108 px limit. A caption that does not fit (Pause at 35 px against a 28 px primary limit, or Right mouse / Backspace at 143 px) falls back to the original controller art. Unnamed VK codes show Kxx: Rebind, and invalid values show ?: Rebind. OEM names are spelled out. Non-ASCII labels fall back. *How:* Known limitation: a keyboard-only player can lose a usable label after a long rebind.
- **Trigger legends swapped so Mouse 1 (left) is on the LT slot and Mouse 2 (right) on the RT slot** [documented] W5 moved the keyboard and mouse legend for the original LT slot (207-210, right mouse / C) to the RT slot, and the RT legend (211-214, left mouse / V) to the LT slot. The authored delta of 76/80 is scaled by the 32 px icon width. All four states move together, and the mask and binding are unchanged. CPU checks: 1,696 checks, 0 failures. The native visual is pending.
- **Compact trigger legend fallback draws both bindings as two 16 px rows inside the icon** [documented] When an unrelated HUD rectangle blocks the external legend, the LT/RT icon shows both current bindings as centred 16 px rows inside its own 32 px icon. The default is LT M2/C and RT M1/V. Controller art is unchanged. Unknown or OEM keys still refuse the fallback. The candidate (SHA 76d4321a) passed 2,093 CPU checks with zero failures. The native case was not reached.
- **Native LT/RT failure: a QTE_TREE_BOX guard rejects the legend, offender still unidentified** [verified-in-game, open-question] In the A868 capture, LT (207) and RT (211) stop at tree_rect rejection while the ABXY widgets draw. qte_caption_box_reason returns QTE_TREE_BOX when another visible linked non-background component (not the QTE box) is present, but the log names only the target rectangle, not the offender. All 113 static rectangles pass the original test, so the runtime offender is dynamic. RECOMP_QTE_TRACE=1 logs up to 16 unique offenders once each. The guard is kept intact. POINTER 2026-11-10: tracked as W-102 (QTE and Press prompts fall back to controller letters for long or non-Latin key names). Not done in r26; stays open. *How:* Set RECOMP_QTE_TRACE=1 and read the [PC-QTE] lines in stderr.
- **An empty untextured bitmap cannot block the QTE legend, because the original bitmap draw returns early** [code-confirmed] The original known bitmap renderer returns before painting when its texture is NULL. A bounded empty bitmap therefore cannot obstruct the legend. The guard was corrected to match that original semantics (W5 3DB8 patch, 237 checks, 0 failures). It is not proof that the whole LT/RT failure is resolved.
- **Click Left thumbstick phrases resolve to the bound stick click, not W/A/S/D** [code-confirmed] The authored text 'Click Left thumbstick to jumpjet.' (offset 56368) was rewritten as W/A/S/D by a generic stick rule. The fix resolves Click/Press Left or Right thumbstick phrases first, using the current PC_LEFT_THUMB or PC_RIGHT_THUMB binding. Default jumpjet shows Press Shift. CPU checks: 41 of 41 pass against 7 failures before.
- **Bare Press A/B/X/Y in authored prompts are rewritten to current bindings; Press Any is unchanged** [code-confirmed] Authored prompts such as the NeuroHack, claw attach and BattleArmor exit lines use a bare Press A/B/X/Y (IDs 1112, 1108, 524754, 524755, 524909, 524673, 524958). A single bounded scan rewrites only the action token with current bindings and keeps casing and punctuation. The old unbounded Y substring also changed Press Any button. The fixture has 29 checks; 13 fail before and 0 after. *How:* tests: bringup/regression/prompt_text_test.cpp
- **Xbox Live dialog text 'or B to cancel' is rewritten to the bound cancel key** [code-confirmed] Three authored Xbox Live dialogs say 'or B to cancel' with no repeated Press. The fix binds the rewrite to the same Press clause and to the exact standalone cancel alternative. Keyboard menus show Esc, and gameplay shows the current B binding. Controller output is unchanged. Native reachability on the current PC menus was not observed.
- **Invert right stick Y was wired to the vibration flag; fixed to camera-pitch flag +76** `0021F989`, `00168464`, `0016842D`, `000EB9D4` [verified-in-game] The native controller row Invert right stick Y wrote profile +75 (vibration) and the Vibration row wrote +76 (camera pitch). The fix maps option 0 (invert) to +76 and option 1 (vibration) to +75. Camera branches at 0x174B4A and 0x175B3F test +5C bit 0 (mask 1) and flip the pitch sign. The feedback gate 0xEB9D4 reads bit 1 (mask 2) and dispatches through 0x1FD30. Raw stick values are not negated.
- **Native accept skipped the in-mission camera update, so inversion did not apply in play** `0021F989`, `00223DBC`, `000C98E7`, `000C9996` [verified-in-game] The native commit called base 0x21F989 directly, which saved profile bit 0 but skipped the in-mission camera update 0x223DBC. The derived accept type 0x48BF20 calls C98E7, C9996, C97BB and indirect 0x172953 to set the active actor camera +6E8, then persists. The fix routes that type through the camera update. Base type 0x48AF58 and unknown types keep the base fallback. CPU: 3744 checks, 8 failures before and 0 after, 144 cases.
- **Profile name entry uses MAKeyboardDlg; host text is queued and fed through the original handler** `00249E11`, `00249EA0`, `0024A564`, `0024A2E6` [code-confirmed] The name entry dialog is MAKeyboardDlg (vtable 0x48F7D0, constructor 0x249E11, form init 0x249EA0 loading dlg_keyboard.ggf, update 0x24A564, handler 0x24A2E6, case 0x24A071). It is reached from Avatar_locker 0x48C2F8 (event 0x224D27 action 1 through 0x1FB975). The name is at most 15 characters with a 55-slot grid. Host WM_CHAR text is decoded (ASCII, CP1252, CP932, UTF-8, Unicode) into a queue of 256 and fed to the original handler on the guest thread. Keyboard raw mouse is suppressed during text entry.
- **Name entry CPU verification: 4415 main checks and 200 original action comparisons** [code-confirmed] The name-entry source passed 4,323 bridge checks (actual bridge and original handlers), 40 native callback checks, 52 backend merge checks, and 200 original-XBE action comparisons with 0 mismatches. The total is 4,415 main checks. In-game typing, mouse and the packaged binary are still unconfirmed. *How:* python bringup/mission_agent_name_verify.py (standalone MSVC build; no game).
- **Controller and camera-inversion verifier: runtime-before/after and original opcode comparison** [code-confirmed] mission_agent_controller_verify.py has modes before, after, input, native, evidence, runtime-before and runtime-after. It runs the actual bridge with the unchanged generated commit and setter code under Unicorn. It compares 284-byte profile payloads for four slots (163,584 bytes). Disk writes are mocked. *How:* python "kit/source/game/bringup/mission_agent_controller_verify.py" runtime-after
- **Tank wrapper CPU proof: 11921 checks over the full original 109536 body** `00109536` [code-confirmed] The W3/W4 CPU proof runs the complete translated 109536 against the original at 30 Hz, 60, 144 and 480 Hz, and with 0.2 s hitches. It checks guest memory (8 MiB), registers, FP/SSE, and the 120 body/model/event boundary calls. It reports 11,921 checks with 0 failures. The child physics, weapon and collision bodies are substituted, so this is not a proof of their event safety.
- **Input fixture: 61 cases, 144 Hz pulses preserved through catch-up ticks** `001753DC`, `001753E6`, `00175466`, `001754BC` [code-confirmed] The input fixture runs the accepted Tank setter chain with a valid primary selection at 144 Hz with 24 phases of mouse and controller pulses, plus 2, 3 and 6 tick hitches. The maximum integral error is 3.2e-8 degrees with 1e-6 tolerance. A 144 Hz pulse gives 100.8 deg/s on frame 0 and zero after, so the input must be integrated over the frame before any skip.
- **replay_intro.py defaults to plan-only** [code-confirmed] replay_intro.py defaults to plan-only. Automated setup presses Space for at most 1.5 s, stops input when the Mission_01b scene appears, and waits for the HUD. The watchdog is 115 s, and the trace helper window is 10 s.
- **Navigator.cs samples the player and Scout positions from guest memory without changing the game** [code-confirmed] Navigator.cs finds the single human player (class 0x4EAED0, input component 0x4EAFA4) through the membership list at 0x50E280, resolves the Scout by UID 27269 through the B4F70 hash table, and reads actor+4C0 world positions. Mech vtable 0x469CD0 is the class of the Scout, and the Mech string is 0x46A034. It reads only through the owned process handle. Camera heading and the Hack-active state are not verified by it. *How:* Add-Type Navigator.cs, then ReadOwned with the owned process handle.
- **Checkpoint save path: 167B25 signs the 284-byte profile, then the WDF graph write runs** `00167B25`, `000B53E0`, `000B9400`, `000B97C0` [code-confirmed] The original 0x167B25 signs and writes 24 + 284 profile bytes before close. On the checkpoint path (0x167D26 to 0x167D85) it calls B53E0 and B9400 to write the object graph, header and directory, then closes with B97C0. The progress callback 0x15CED6 is reached through B9360 and throttled to 100 ms. SHA updates go 0x2BEA9B to 0x315D5A to kernel ordinal 336 (XcSHAUpdate, native). Timing only the 308-byte file misses the main save.
- **The save progress callback 0x15CED6 is wrapped by ma2_save_progress_probe** `0015CED6` [code-confirmed] recomp_lookup_manual returns ma2_save_progress_probe for VA 0x15CED6. It brackets the original callback with xbox_save_probe_callback_begin and xbox_save_probe_callback_end, which record its wall time. The generated RECOMP_ABI_CALL route bypasses manual_lookup, so an indirect callback must be wrapped manually. — recomp_manual.c:398
- **Save and checkpoint stalls: 20.5 s frame gap in menu, 3.7 s in gameplay, cause not found** [verified-in-game, open-question] MASave flags changed from 2 to 6 and back. The WDF file's mtime does not change when its hash does, so mtime cannot date writes. No storage or signature bug is shown. Diagnostic proposals instrument the kernel file calls (kernel_bridge.c 3023 to 3722), not the flush. POINTER 2026-11-10: tracked as W-20 of the public-release plan (measure the 'Saving progress' pause on the published build with RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY=1; needs a person at the PC). Not done in r26; stays open.
- **Captured checkpoint state: destination 3 (Mission_02), flag false, completed 0** [verified-in-game] The captured profile records current, highest and checkpoint destination 3, which the catalog maps to LEVEL050 missions/Mission_02.wdf. checkpoint_flag is false and completed is 0. One captured checkpoint write returned 1 and changed the graph hash while the profile stayed at destination 3. A Continue from that copy loads Mission_02. The Mission_01b shoreline checkpoint is not in these saves.
- **Campaign coverage overrides run only in a bounded probe with a logs save folder and a watchdog** [code-confirmed] ma2_campaign_probe_enabled is true only when RECOMP_SAVE_DIR and RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS are set (above 0) and the save folder is under bringup/logs. Only then do the probe overrides for campaign and mission selection run. A normal player's progress and start-up are not affected. — recomp_manual.c:982
- **Pulse weapon class is read at primary +17C; +15C is a heat float** `000CE027`, `000CC525`, `000D2035`, `000D3CD9` [code-confirmed] The serialization interface at primary +20 (vtable 0x465A60) has a deserializer 0xCE027 that writes BarrelClassName at interface +15C, which is primary +17C. Primary +15C is a float heat value (default 5.0). The earlier diagnostic read +15C as the class and so rejected every real laser and mortar. The v5 diagnostic reads +17C.
- **Pulse weapon chain: MAWpnGrp to MABarrel (class 7) to MAProjectile (type 1)** `000CC525` [documented] The pulse laser chain is MAWpnGrp (class id 31855) to MABarrel (31856, class 7) to MAProjectile (31857, type 1). The mortar uses class 12 and projectile 36048 and differs. The pulse body is 24 indexed-list vertices and the tip is 4 indexed-strip vertices, and the renderer expands them correctly (6 CPU index checks).
- **Invisible pulse laser: alpha may be discarded, cause and fix still open** [documented, superseded] The pulse body and tip materials are additive, material-only and two-sided, with 64x64 swizzled ARGB8888 textures. The body alpha max is 181, so a GREATER224 alpha test would discard it unless the final combiner alpha is larger. The shader state is unknown, so no alpha patch is justified. The next step is to bind one laser and one mortar event to the weapon class and texture digest with bounded logs.
- **A Mech (Scout) actor is 469CD0 and its world position is actor+4C0** [code-confirmed] The Mech constructor F7EA6 sets vtable 0x469CD0 and its name vt+10 returns the string at 0x46A034. The Scout is UID 27269 in Mission02. Cached world XYZ is at actor+4C0 (not the authored start position). Positions can span game updates.
- **Terrain normal provider chain: 17687C to F70FC to 2AAB80 (null terrain gives zero)** `0017687C`, `000F70FC`, `002AAB80`, `000464C0` [code-confirmed] The root normal provider is vtable 0x4770B8 +2C, which is 0x17687C. It calls F70FC, which reads the global terrain pointer 0x4EAF64, copies the position and calls 2AAB80. A null terrain returns zero. An out-of-bounds position returns the flat normal. No world matrix refresh is in this path.
- **Frame limiter and vblank: a limit of 0 does not wait; a 60 Hz vblank runs even when uncapped** [code-confirmed] The D3D11 frame limiter waits after Present only when the limit is above 0, and a limit of 0 clears the deadline. main.c sets RECOMP_VBLANK=1 by default, so a 60 Hz vblank interrupt runs even when uncapped. No host fixed simulation accumulator was found. The simulation step therefore follows the real clock producers.
- **recomp_lookup_manual is checked first, but RECOMP_ABI_CALL bypasses it** [code-confirmed] recomp_lookup_manual is the first override point. It returns the save probe for 0x15CED6, then the bringup lookup, and returns null otherwise. Generated direct calls made through RECOMP_ABI_CALL do not go through manual lookup, so a function like 0x1FE68D or the pulse function must be hooked at its generated body or wrapped at an indirect call site. The POV pitch adapter is called from the recovered F065C body for this reason. — recomp_manual.c:396
- **RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_AUTOPILOT feeds the test pad through ma2_bot_test_human_pad** [code-confirmed] In ma2_input_read, when the host pad is 0 (the test harness), the test hook ma2_bot_test_human_pad can supply the pad values. It is set by the RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_AUTOPILOT test setting in ma2_bots_core.c. Real pads are unchanged. — recomp_manual.c:570
- **APU register access goes through the guest read/write routes, not raw memory** [code-confirmed] ma2_apu_register returns true for the APU MMIO ranges (offset 0x30000 from 0xFE800000, 0x3F000 and 0x5F000 with 0x1000 spans). Such stores and loads go through apu_guest_write32 and apu_guest_read32. Other addresses use MEM32 directly. This avoids an access violation on every hardware access. — recomp_apu_io.h:8
- **DropPack does not appear in this pack's files or in the bots source** [inferred, open-question] The brief lists DropPack for this pack. No facts about DropPack are recorded here. — recomp_manual.c:1
- **Campaign pipeline reports in the pack are audio statistics, not checkpoints** [code-confirmed, historical] campaign-index-02 and campaign-mission-03 pipeline-report.txt hold per-phase audio RMS and step statistics (52,500 frames, 35 s). They contain no checkpoint or progression data.

## PC port: menus, input, settings, saves, packaging

## PC port: menus, input, settings, saves, packaging

### Overview

The PC port wraps the recompiled Xbox game in a native Windows front end. `main.c` starts the process, reads `pc_settings.ini` and turns each key into a `RECOMP_*` environment variable. `platform/pc_frontend.c` holds the shared, atomic state (settings, bindings, input context, mouse capture, display sizes, rumble policy). `pc_native_settings.cpp` draws and runs the PC-only settings pages (Display, Audio, Controls, Keyboard and mouse bindings, Controller) on top of the original Xbox menu objects. `pc_prompts.cpp` rewrites guest prompt text so it names the keys that are actually bound.

Guest menus call into the PC layer at a few hook sites. `patch_pc_frontend.py` re-applies those hooks after the generated code is regenerated, and each hook is anchored on a unique `loc_XXXXXXXX` label. The original menus are kept. The PC pages take over only when the matching menu vtable is active (0048B360 Video, 0048BE60 Volume, 0048BF20 Controls). Unavailable menu items (Xbox Live, System Link, Conquest, Game Demos, Add Guest) are shown disabled by the policy in `ma2_bots_ui.c`, which is not in this pack.

Settings flow: a key is changed on a page, the value is stored in `pc_frontend.c` at once (and applies immediately where the code allows), and the INI is written on Back (no window change) or Apply (window change). Env vars override the INI for a launch. Saves and profiles live per Windows user under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2`, and the installer ships none. Packaging is a single installer exe that unpacks a kit and runs the build; the release is PC Release only.

### Key code

| Address or function | What it does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `save_settings(bool apply_window)` | Writes all `[Display]`, `[Audio]`, `[Input]` and `[Bindings]` keys. Deletes `RenderScale`. Posts the window message only when `apply_window` is true. | `pc_native_settings.cpp:227` |

### Added code and hooks

Hook sites are in `bringup/patch_pc_frontend.py`. The file reapplies each change after regeneration and raises `hook changed; inspect` if an anchor is missing. Groups:

- Menus: `recomp_0051` (main menu pulse, movie skip at `loc_001F40D3`), `recomp_0052` (pause menu `loc_001FC712`, selection `loc_001FCEB6`, result `loc_001FD26E`, dispatch `loc_001FD243`, form load `loc_001FD869`, modal `loc_001FBE6A`), `recomp_0057` (settings submenus: video `loc_002206BD`, controls `loc_0021F8DF`, volume `loc_002202E8`), `recomp_0058` (destroy `loc_00223D8E`, `loc_00223D2D`).
- Text: `recomp_0020` (prompt text `loc_000C0FD0`, font width counter `loc_000C1640` and `loc_000C1755`), `recomp_0053` (`loc_001FFA04`, `loc_00200F56`), `recomp_0070` (localized text `loc_002B4979`).
- Input: `recomp_0039` and `recomp_0038` (mouse look), `recomp_0027` (input context `loc_0011ADCE`), `recomp_0041` (input mapping), `recomp_0003` (input converted, every occurrence), `recomp_0001` (input committed).
- Display: `recomp_0005` (aspect at `loc_00038309`, widescreen render width at `loc_000382C0`), `recomp_0007` (aspect scale), `recomp_0048` (loading form rects, `sub_001CCC10`).
- Audio: `recomp_0094`, `recomp_0095`, `recomp_0096` (trace points and reference counts).
- Movies: `recomp_0094` (Bink decode, release, copy).

Platform code: `platform/pc_frontend.c` and `.h` (settings, bindings, input context, capture, display, cinematic pacing, rumble policy). `pc_storage.h` declares the copy-missing helper. `pc_settings.h` declares the PC settings helpers used by the hooks. The `xbox_input` layer (`kit/source/game/src/input/README.md`) maps the Xbox XInput API to Windows XInput.

### Env vars, settings and test hooks

#### Settings file

`pc_settings.ini` lives beside the exe (packaged defaults) and in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2` (per user, written by the game). Precedence: env var, then INI, then built-in default. Out-of-range values fall back to the default (`main.c:135`).

| Section | Keys | What each changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[Display]` | WindowWidth, WindowHeight (default 1280x960) | Client size and scene render pixels |
| `[Display]` | Fullscreen | Borderless fullscreen |
| `[Display]` | VSync, FrameLimit (0-1000) | Present policy and frame cap |
| `[Display]` | PreserveAspect | 1 = Automatic (widened 3D), 0 = Original 4:3 |
| `[Display]` | SmoothScaling | Scale filter |
| `[Display]` | ShowFPS | ImGui frame-rate overlay |
| `[Display]` | DrawDistance (0-100, 50 = Original) | Fog, far clip and object visibility |
| `[Display]` | TextureQuality (0, 1, 2), FMVQuality (0, 1) | Enhanced packs (`game_files\texture_packs`, `D:\Movie\Enhanced\2x`) |
| `[Display]` | PreloadShaders | Pre-create shaders while loading a level |
| `[Display]` | RenderScale | Retired; deleted on save |
| `[Audio]` | Enabled | 0 clears `RECOMP_AC97_READY` so no APU is brought up (never saved) |
| `[Audio]` | Volume (0-100) | Master volume |
| `[Input]` | Keyboard, MouseAim | Keyboard bindings and mouse aim on or off |
| `[Input]` | MouseSensitivity | Mouse sensitivity (see gap below) |
| `[Input]` | InvertY | Invert mouse Y |
| `[Input]` | InvertFlight | Invert VTOL flight controls (consumer not in this pack) |
| `[Input]` | KeyboardLayout | Passed to `RECOMP_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT` (default `pc`) |
| `[Bindings]` | Start, Back, A, B, X, Y, White, Black, LeftTrigger, RightTrigger, MoveLeft, MoveRight, MoveBack, MoveForward, LeftThumb, RightThumb, MouseFire, MouseAltFire | Virtual-key code per action (`pc_native_settings.cpp:35-37`) |

Controller invert and vibration are not INI keys. They are options in the original player profile (`pc_native_settings.cpp:498`).

Sources: `main.c:175-201` for loading, `pc_native_settings.cpp:227-245` for saving.

#### Env vars

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `RECOMP_WINDOW_WIDTH`, `RECOMP_WINDOW_HEIGHT`, `RECOMP_FULLSCREEN` | Starting window and fullscreen |
| `RECOMP_VSYNC`, `RECOMP_FRAME_LIMIT`, `RECOMP_PRESERVE_ASPECT`, `RECOMP_SCALE_FILTER`, `RECOMP_SHOW_FPS` | Display policy |
| `RECOMP_DRAW_DISTANCE`, `RECOMP_TEXTURE_QUALITY`, `RECOMP_FMV_QUALITY`, `RECOMP_SHADER_PRELOAD` | Display content |
| `RECOMP_TEXTURE_PACK_DIR` | Where the 2x and 4x texture packs are looked for |
| `RECOMP_KEYBOARD`, `RECOMP_MOUSE_AIM`, `RECOMP_MOUSE_SENSITIVITY`, `RECOMP_INVERT_Y`, `RECOMP_INVERT_FLIGHT`, `RECOMP_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT` | Input |
| `RECOMP_AC97_READY`, `RECOMP_AUDIO_VOLUME` | Audio |
| `RECOMP_RENDER_SCALE` | Diagnostic 1-4 scale of the render height; default 0 |
| `RECOMP_CONSOLE` | Attach or allocate a console; otherwise stderr goes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\Logs` |
| `RECOMP_GAME_OVERLAY`, `RECOMP_CACHE_NAMESPACE` | Asset overlay folder and cache namespace (from `cache.version`) |
| `RECOMP_PB_EXEC`, `RECOMP_GPU` (d3d11), `RECOMP_TITLE_KEVENTS`, `RECOMP_VBLANK`, `RECOMP_FB_WINDOW`, `RECOMP_HEAP_RECLAIM`, `RECOMP_ASYNC_IO`, `RECOMP_USB`, `RECOMP_INPUT_LATCH`, `RECOMP_MOUSE_GUEST_POLL`, `RECOMP_EXIT_ON_CLOSE` | Launcher defaults (set to 1 when absent, `main.c:164-174`) |
| `RECOMP_USB_PADS` | Controller count; split-screen Add Guest needs 2 or more |
| `RECOMP_ONLINE_MENUS`, `RECOMP_SPLITSCREEN_MENUS`, `RECOMP_DEMO_MENUS` | Restore the disabled menu items (fork switches) |
| `RECOMP_NO_BARREL_ARROWS` | Turns off the barrel arrows and value-row clicks |
| `RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS` | Arms the hang watchdog (`main.c:619`) |
| `RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY=1` | Writes one `[SAVE-LATENCY]` line per save exit, and `[SAVE-LATENCY-UNCOVERED]` for callbacks outside a save |
| `RECOMP_SCENARIO_TRACE` | Removed from the scenario loader in the v5 fix |

#### Trace and test hooks

- `RECOMP_MENU_TRACE` prints `[PC-MENU]`, `[PC-MOUSE]`, `[PC-ARROWS]`, `[PC-POINTER]` and `[PC-GLOW]`.
- `RECOMP_MENU_DUMP=1` prints each menu's widget tree as `[MENU-DUMP]` (vtable, flags, state, action, text id, rect). Use it before changing a menu policy.
- `RECOMP_DISPLAY_TRACE` prints `[PC-DISPLAY]` for size, aspect and movie changes.
- `RECOMP_FOOTER_TRACE` prints `[PC-FOOTER]`.
- `RECOMP_UI_LIVE` uses the injected pointer for hover tests (`hovershot.py` takes `hover=WxH`).
- `RECOMP_HUD_TRACE` prints `[HUD-LAYOUT]` (widescreen HUD layout; see the HUD note).
- `RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY=1` for save attribution. Require a full-span record and no coverage error before optimizing.
- `RECOMP_GPU_RECOVERY_TEST` suppresses the renderer-error message box in tests.

Log lines: `[PC-MENU] saved settings WxH fullscreen=N` (or `failed to save`) is written on each Back or Apply (`pc_native_settings.cpp:244`). `[EXIT]` lines show the confirmed quit path.

### Menus, pause and input

- The main menu and HUB start screens use Enter to select. Escape there opens the EXIT GAME prompt, and a confirm posts `WM_CLOSE`. In gameplay, Escape opens the pause menu.
- Escape on a settings page closes the page (back, saving the settings). Settings pages never quit the game.
- Pause menu items are stored in action order 100, 200, 500, 600, 400, 11, 8, 9, 800. Action 600 is Add Guest in a networked session, otherwise Quit to Main Hub. Match on the action number and the text, not the slot.
- Mouse capture: a settings page captures the mouse on open and releases it on Back. Escape with the camera captured releases the camera and does not pause. Focus loss releases camera capture. F8 toggles capture; F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen.
- Mouse aim turns on when play resumes from a menu on keyboard and mouse (PC_WINDOW_AIM_MESSAGE).
- Input device: the last device used decides the prompts and whether rumble runs. Keyboard and mouse input stops controller rumble at once.
- Controls page rows: keyboard controls, mouse aiming, sensitivity (steps of 10), Invert mouse Y, Invert flight (VTOL), bindings, defaults, controller settings, back.
- Controller page rows: Invert right stick Y and Vibration (profile options), keyboard and mouse settings, back.
- Bindings: three pages of eight. Pick a row, press a key or mouse button; Escape cancels. Enter, Escape, F8 and F11 are reserved on menus.

### Prompts and text

`ma2_pc_prompt_text` rewrites the guest's authored strings before they are drawn. On keyboard it:

- replaces `Press A` / `the B button` / `White button` and similar with the bound key, in order, and keeps the authored case;
- maps `Pull the Right trigger` to a press of the mouse fire key, but only as a bounded trigger phrase;
- replaces `D-pad` with `arrow keys`, `left thumbstick` with the forward, left, back and right keys, and `right thumbstick` with `mouse`;
- maps `Click the Left thumbstick` and similar to the stick-click binding.

On a gamepad it keeps the controller words (A, B, X, Y, RB, LB, Menu). A/B menu commands use Enter and Esc only for the explicit command list. Everything else uses the current gameplay binding.

Footer legends (text ids 0x70010000-0x70010005) show Enter, Esc and the bound keys, with short names for mouse and special keys. QTE captions come from `ma2_pc_qte_caption` and use a font10 width table.

### Rumble

- Vibration reaches the native XInput motors through the XInput layer. It is controller option 1 in the profile.
- A device switch to keyboard and mouse stops the primary controller's feedback at the next report. Closing or switching away stops active motors at once.
- Candidate (not verified in play): a four-bit port mask for pause (`xbox_InputFeedbackPaused`), so physical output stops at pause and each port stays suppressed until its zero is retired.
- Candidate: the expiry block in `sub_0001FE60` (1FEC2-1FEF2) keeps a slot reserved until its zero is accepted. Without it, a skipped zero is never retried.
- The rumble scheduler (`sub_0001FD30`) takes the first duration-zero slot. There are ten slots; a pending zero uses one.

### Saves

- Location: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\Saved Games` for saves and caches; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\Logs` for logs. Profiles are shared per Windows user. The installer ships no save or profile data.
- Files: `MASave.sav` (308 bytes in a checked sample) and `Missions\MASaveGame.wdf` (3145728 bytes, preallocated checkpoint generation). The checkpoint writes the WDF to the cache path (Z: maps to the cache, from the original string `Z:\Missions\MASaveGame.wdf` at `00475FA8`). A profile-only span writes 380 bytes: 308 profile and 72 global settings.
- Storage helper: `ma2_pc_copy_missing` copies only missing files, so existing saves are never replaced (`pc_storage.h:9`).
- Chain: `sub_0015D4C7` -> `sub_0015EFF2` (checkpoint to cache, installs the progress callback) -> `sub_000B53E0` (the only direct caller of the common writer `sub_000B9400`). Profile envelope: `sub_00167B25`.
- Timing: the progress callback `sub_0015CED6` runs at 100 ms. Long callbacks can dominate the save. The graph phase is B53E0-inclusive.
- Save and Quit: the transfer before `sub_00167B25` (`2BD76E`) is not measured by the current probe.

### Packaging and launcher

- Launcher: `MechAssault 2.exe` is `main.c`. It loads `game_files\ma2.xbe` (error box if missing), sets up storage, and runs the entry point. It picks `pc_assets` for the packaged overlay.
- Installer: one exe (`release\MechAssault 2 Recomp Installer.exe`, about 108 MB). Its stub unpacks an LZMS kit to `%TEMP%\MA2RecompInstaller-<id>` and runs `installer\gui.py` (or `install.py` with arguments). The kit is built by `assemble.py`, `cmake_patch.py`, `gen_patch.py make`, `make_payload.py` and `installer-exe\pack_installer.py`.
- Install steps: unpack the XISO, run xboxrecomp, apply the patch set, build with MSVC (VS Build Tools are fetched if no compiler is found; the fetch path was not exercised end to end), and copy out a clean PC Release. A CLI end-to-end run passes 11 steps; the objcompare check gives 201 of 202 objects identical (only the path-hashed `.data$rs` differs).
- Accented Windows user names: the build moves to an ASCII folder `<drive>:\MA2RecompBuild-<hash>`, because link.exe reads the response file in the ANSI code page.
- Publish: PC Release only. `publish.py --freeze/--stage/--install`. PC Release Bots is abandoned.
- Release notes: rerun `make_payload.py` after each publish and before packing. `release.json`'s exe hash is provenance only.

### Facts

- **Video settings menu is the 0048B360 vtable** `0048B360`, `002206BD` [code-confirmed] The Video Calibration menu uses vtable 0048B360 and is settings page type 0 (Display). ma2_pc_video_menu_update calls ma2_pc_submenu_update(object, 0x48B360). Its update hook is recomp_0057 at loc_002206BD. — pc_native_settings.cpp:514
- **In-game Volume menu is the 0048BE60 vtable** `0048BE60`, `002202E8`, `00223D2D` [code-confirmed] The Volume menu is vtable 0048BE60 and settings page type 1 (Audio). Its update hook is recomp_0057 at loc_002202E8 and its destroy hook is recomp_0058 at loc_00223D2D. — pc_native_settings.cpp:514
- **In-game Controller Options menu is the 0048BF20 vtable** `0048BF20`, `0021F8DF`, `00223D8E` [code-confirmed] The Controller Options menu is vtable 0048BF20 and settings page type 2 (Controls). It opens page 4 (Controller) instead when a gamepad was the last device. Its update hook is recomp_0057 at loc_0021F8DF and its destroy hook is recomp_0058 at loc_00223D8E. — pc_native_settings.cpp:514
- **Keyboard text-entry dialog is the 0048F7D0 vtable** `0048F7D0`, `001FD869` [code-confirmed] Name entry uses interface\menus\dialogs\dlg_keyboard.ggf. ma2_pc_form_loading detects it when the form owner's vtable is 0048F7D0, clears queued text events, sets pc_input_text_capture(1) and releases camera capture. Keyboard bindings are suppressed while text capture is on; the physical gamepad stays active. — pc_native_settings.cpp:349
- **Main menu and HUB Start vtables gate the Esc exit prompt** `00481B70`, `00482170`, `00481EF8` [code-confirmed] Escape on the main menu (0481B70) or the HUB start screen (0482170) with no submenu open requests the EXIT GAME dialog. The HUD vtable 0481EF8 is excluded from menu_available. 0482170 is also the title input context. Confirming the dialog with result 1 or 3 posts WM_CLOSE. — pc_native_settings.cpp:39
- **Where the PC menu pulse is hooked into guest code** `001F34BE`, `001FC712`, `001FD243`, `001FCEB6` [code-confirmed] ma2_pc_menu_pulse(object,vtable) is called from loc_001F34BE (Auto Menu: Main Menu, recomp_0051), loc_001FC712 (Pause Menu, recomp_0052, owner ~Pause Menu#5), and loc_001FD243 (Base Dispatch, Select Mission, Mech Selection and Restart confirm, recomp_0052). loc_001FCEB6 and loc_001FD26E feed selection and result. The pulse drives barrel arrows, menu policy, the input context, the footer glow and the RECOMP_MENU_DUMP tree. — patch_pc_frontend.py:28
- **Modal dialog pulse hook at 001FBE6A** `001FBE6A` [code-confirmed] The modal pulse ma2_pc_modal_pulse runs at loc_001FBE6A. It calls sync_text_dialog, and while a modal is active (guest[0x5240D4] > guest[0x5240D0]) it re-runs ma2_pc_menu_pulse with the last menu object. The underlying menu keeps its input context, and Escape never turns into Start while a modal is up. — patch_pc_frontend.py:101
- **Unavailable menu items are shown disabled, not removed** `001FCBA6`, `00224520`, `002CD920` [verified-in-game] Conquest (main action 7), Game Demos (action 8, launches cdx.xbe), System Link (2), Xbox Live (3) and Add Guest (4) are shown with the game's own disabled state 5. The pause menu hides the Xbox Live status box (text 0xAC8) and the R Sign In legend (0x70010002, action 9). Some items are re-decided every frame and are answered at 00224520 (no network link, so System Link is disabled) and 001FCBA6 (no free controller, so Add Guest is disabled). The fork switches RECOMP_ONLINE_MENUS, RECOMP_SPLITSCREEN_MENUS and RECOMP_DEMO_MENUS restore the original items. *How:* Run with RECOMP_MENU_DUMP=1 to print the [MENU-DUMP] widget tree of the actual context before changing a policy. — pc_native_settings.cpp:370
- **Pause action 600 is Add Guest or Quit to Main Hub, decided by text** [verified-in-game] Action 600 is Add/Remove Guest (text 0x7D00/0x7D01) only when byte 0x50C94D is set (a networked session). Otherwise it reads Quit to Main Hub (text 0xE) and is enabled. The policy had matched the slot alone, so bot matches had no exit from 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-19. The fix also matches the text.
- **Pause menu slot order** [documented] The Pause Menu constructor stores items from +0x6C in action order 100, 200, 500, 600, 400, 11, 8, 9, 800. So the slot at +0x78 is action 600 and Multiplayer Options is at +0x7C. Match on the action number, not the slot offset.
- **Main menu action numbers used by the policy** [documented] Main menu actions are 2 = Multiplayer System Link, 3 = Xbox Live, 4 = Add Guest, 7 = Conquest and 8 = Game Demos. The policy disables them with state 5. Hub button activatecommand CRCs are not in this pack.
- **Settings page type and page numbers** [code-confirmed] The page type comes from the vtable: 0048B360 gives 0 (Display), 0048BE60 gives 1 (Audio), 0048BF20 gives 2 (Controls). A gamepad last-device opens page 4 (Controller) from type 2. Pages are 0 Display, 1 Audio, 2 Controls, 3 Keyboard and mouse bindings (three pages of eight), 4 Controller. — pc_native_settings.cpp:514
- **Rows per settings page** [code-confirmed] Page 0 (Display) has 13 rows, page 1 (Audio) 5, page 2 (Controls) 9, page 3 (Bindings) 10 (8 bindings plus Next and Back) and page 4 (Controller) 4. Page 0 rows start at y 90 with step 23; the other pages start at y 99 with step 28, in 640x480 units. — pc_native_settings.cpp:273
- **Back and Escape return from each settings page** [code-confirmed] page_key returns 2 (close) on Escape or Backspace, except on the bindings page (3), which goes back to page 2 with selection 4. activate returns 2 for Controls row 8 (Back), Volume row 4 (Back) and Controller row 3 (Back). ma2_pc_submenu_update then saves (save_settings(false)), clears the page and releases mouse capture, and returns 2 to the guest. Controls row 5 opens bindings (page 3) and row 7 opens the controller page. Controller row 2 returns to Controls with selection 0. — pc_native_settings.cpp:504
- **Settings pages do not quit the game** [code-confirmed] When a settings page returns 2 the guest menu gets the Back result and nothing exits the process. The window hook only turns Escape into the exit prompt on the main menu and HUB start screens. — pc_native_settings.cpp:569
- **Controls opens the page for the device last used** [documented] When the Controls menu opens and the last device was a gamepad, the page starts on the Controller page (page 4); otherwise it starts on the keyboard and mouse Controls page (page 2). Each page links to the other device's page, so the mouse can configure the controller without the page changing underneath. — pc_native_settings.cpp:519
- **Where pc_settings.ini lives** [code-confirmed] The packaged default is pc_settings.ini beside the exe, or one folder up. The per-user copy is %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\pc_settings.ini, found through ma2_pc_settings_path. Preferences persist across launches and survive an executable update. The game writes the INI on Back (save_settings(false)) or Apply (save_settings(true)). — main.c:156
- **Precedence: env var, then INI, then built-in default** [code-confirmed] main.c reads each INI key with its fallback and clamps it to a range, then writes the value into the matching RECOMP_* env var. If the env var is already set the INI value is skipped. ma2_pc_settings_initialize then reads each env var with its own default. So an env var beats the INI, the INI beats the built-in default, and an out-of-range INI value falls back to the default. — main.c:135
- **[Display] keys and what they change** [code-confirmed] WindowWidth and WindowHeight (default 1280x960) set the window and the scene render pixels. Fullscreen selects borderless mode. VSync and FrameLimit (0-1000, 0 = unlimited) set the present policy. PreserveAspect (1 = Automatic, 0 = Original 4:3) controls the 3D camera widening. SmoothScaling sets the scale filter. ShowFPS draws an ImGui frame-rate overlay. DrawDistance (0-100, 50 = Original) scales fog, far clip and object visibility. TextureQuality (0 Original, 1 2x, 2 4x) and FMVQuality (0 Original, 1 Enhanced) choose the enhanced packs. PreloadShaders pre-creates level shaders. RenderScale is deleted from the INI on each save. UPDATE 2026-11-04: FrameLimit 0 no longer means unlimited; 0 reads as 144 and the default is 144 (t28.frame-limit-no-unlimited-default-144). — main.c:175
- **[Audio] keys** [code-confirmed] Enabled (RECOMP_AC97_READY) is a presence switch: 0 clears the env var so the APU is not brought up, and the save never writes it. Volume (0-100, default 100) is the master level and is saved as [Audio] Volume. The effects, speech and music levels are in the guest profile, not the INI. — main.c:199
- **[Input] keys and their ranges** [code-confirmed] Keyboard (0/1) enables keyboard bindings, MouseAim (0/1) enables mouse aiming, MouseSensitivity (INI accepts 1-500; the UI steps 10 to 500, default 100), InvertY (0/1) inverts mouse Y, and InvertFlight (0/1) inverts the flight controls for VTOL. KeyboardLayout (string, default pc) is passed through RECOMP_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT. — main.c:190
- **Mouse sensitivity INI range is wider than the UI range** [code-confirmed] main.c accepts MouseSensitivity 1-500, but the Controls row changes it with change(. 10, 500, direction*10). So a saved value below 10 jumps to 10 on the first change of that row. The row text shows the stored value unchanged until then. — main.c:192
- **[Bindings] section: virtual-key code per action** [code-confirmed] Each action is a Windows virtual-key code under its name: Start, Back, A, B, X, Y, White, Black, LeftTrigger, RightTrigger, MoveLeft, MoveRight, MoveBack, MoveForward, LeftThumb, RightThumb, MouseFire, MouseAltFire. Values outside 1-255 fall back to the default. Defaults are Enter, Backspace, Space, F, R, Q, 1, 2, C, V, A, D, S, W, Shift, Ctrl, Left mouse and Right mouse. — pc_native_settings.cpp:35
- **Window messages used by the settings and frontend code** [code-confirmed] PC_WINDOW_CONFIG_MESSAGE (0x8051) applies window size and fullscreen, and is sent only by Apply. PC_WINDOW_CAPTURE_MESSAGE (0x8052) updates mouse capture. PC_WINDOW_MOUSE_MESSAGE (0x8053) and PC_WINDOW_CAMERA_MESSAGE (0x8054) handle pointer and camera capture. PC_WINDOW_RENDERER_ERROR_MESSAGE (0x8055) shows the renderer error and closes the game. PC_WINDOW_AIM_MESSAGE (0x8056) turns on mouse aim when play resumes from a menu on keyboard and mouse. — pc_frontend.h:68
- **Apply saves and applies window geometry; Back saves without it** [code-confirmed] Row 11 'Apply display settings' calls save_settings(true), which writes all keys and posts PC_WINDOW_CONFIG_MESSAGE. Back calls save_settings(false), with no window message. Restore display defaults (row 12) resets PreloadShaders, VSync, FrameLimit, RenderScale, Aspect, Filter, ShowFPS, DrawDistance, TextureQuality and FMVQuality. It does not change window size, fullscreen or any key. The values are written on Back or Apply. — pc_native_settings.cpp:485
- **RenderScale is retired and deleted on save** [code-confirmed] The 1x-4x rendering multiplier is no longer used. Save deletes the RenderScale key from the INI. RECOMP_RENDER_SCALE remains only as a diagnostic: main.c defaults it to 0, and pc_display_render_extent uses it only when it is 1-4. — pc_native_settings.cpp:232
- **Texture and video quality fall back to Original when packs are missing** [code-confirmed] check_optional_content runs when the Display page opens. It checks game_files\texture_packs (or RECOMP_TEXTURE_PACK_DIR) for the 2x and 4x index.json, and D:\Movie\Enhanced\2x. If the saved choice's content is missing it is reset to 0 at runtime, and the row text says 'enhanced packs not installed'. Cycling skips uninstalled texture choices. — pc_native_settings.cpp:259
- **Frame limit row cycles fixed presets** [code-confirmed, superseded] The row cycles 0 (Unlimited), 30, 60, 90, 120, 144, 165, 180, 240 and 360. The source searches only for an exact preset, so a saved value of 75 falls through to index 9: Left goes to 240 and Right to Unlimited. A candidate chooses the adjacent offered preset instead (75 -> Left 60, Right 90). SUPERSEDED 2026-11-04 (c3bee9c): Unlimited was removed and a value that is not a preset counts as 144. See t28.frame-limit-no-unlimited-default-144. — pc_native_settings.cpp:478
- **Draw distance row and slider** [code-confirmed] The value is 0-100 with 50 = Original. Row 7 steps by five with Left and Right. A click or drag on the bar (x 315-566, row 7) sets the value from the pointer, (x-325)*100/230, and dragging continues while the button is held. The hint line reads 0 = 0.5x, 50 = Original, 100 = 2x. The renderer applies the distance (fog, far clip and visibility); that code is not in this pack. — pc_native_settings.cpp:481
- **Controls page keys and what each changes** [code-confirmed] Row 0 toggles keyboard controls, row 1 mouse aiming, row 2 changes mouse sensitivity in steps of 10, row 3 Invert mouse Y, and row 4 Invert flight controls (VTOL), the only UI entry for InvertFlight. Row 5 opens the bindings screen, row 6 restores control defaults (all bindings, sensitivity 100, no inversion, mouse aim and keyboard on), row 7 opens the controller page and row 8 is Back. — pc_native_settings.cpp:490
- **Controller invert and vibration are guest profile options, not INI keys** [documented] Row 0 'Invert right stick Y' and row 1 'Vibration' read and write the original player profile through ma2_gui_controller_option, ma2_gui_controller_set and ma2_gui_controller_commit. They persist across restarts in the profile, not in pc_settings.ini. Mouse inversion stays in the INI. Row 2 goes to the keyboard and mouse settings. — pc_native_settings.cpp:322
- **Volume page: master and guest-side channel levels** [code-confirmed] Row 0 is the master volume in PC_VOLUME (INI [Audio] Volume), in steps of 5. Rows 1-3 are Effects, Speech and Music. Those are written into the guest object at +0x84 + (row-1)*4 as 0.65535, in steps of 3277. They show as ((value*100)+32767)/65535 percent and are committed through ma2_gui_volume_commit on Back. — pc_native_settings.cpp:487
- **Binding capture: waiting, Escape cancels, reserved keys** [code-confirmed] Selecting a binding sets waiting_binding. The next key press or mouse button is stored with pc_binding_set, except Escape, which cancels. Menu Enter and Escape and F8 and F11 stay reserved. Each change bumps the input revision so prompts redraw. — pc_native_settings.cpp:506
- **Bindings screen: three pages of eight** [code-confirmed] The bindings screen shows eight rows per page. Row 8 is 'Next page' and cycles 0-2, and row 9 is 'Back to controls'. Rows past PC_BINDING_COUNT are hidden on the last page. Keys are named by key_name: mouse buttons, Enter, Esc, and GetKeyNameText for the rest. — pc_native_settings.cpp:317
- **Controller D-pad and A are gated while a binding is captured** [code-confirmed, open-question] Controller button edges, the last axis and repeat timers update on every frame. The D-pad and A dispatch is gated on !capturing_binding. A private candidate (F3) also suppresses stale controller edges after capture begins. Its status is not confirmed against the source checked here. — pc_native_settings.cpp:558
- **Mouse hit testing on settings pages** [code-confirmed] Pointer coordinates map into a 640x480 canvas, centred and letterboxed with scale min(w/640, h/480). A row is hit for x 70-570 and a valid row index; a left click activates it and a right click decreases it. Esc: Back is clickable in x 392-466 (plus or minus 8) on the hint row. The ESC_BACK constants are the source of this area. — pc_native_settings.cpp:535
- **Input context and when it changes** `00482170` [code-confirmed] ma2_pc_input_context_update picks MOVIE while a movie plays, MENU while a modal is up, GAMEPLAY when no menu has pulsed in the last 250 ms, TITLE for vtable 0482170, and MENU otherwise. Entering any context other than gameplay or movie posts PC_WINDOW_CAPTURE_MESSAGE. Returning to gameplay on keyboard and mouse with mouse aim on posts PC_WINDOW_AIM_MESSAGE. — pc_native_settings.cpp:338
- **Mouse capture: how it is taken and released** [code-confirmed] The settings page captures the mouse on open (pc_frontend_capture(1)) and releases it on Back. Escape while the camera is captured releases the camera and does not pause. WM_KILLFOCUS releases the camera capture. A left click on the 3D lobby scene (x 0-1, y below 0.64, main menu only) starts camera capture. Escape restores the cursor in the lobby, and F8 toggles capture. — pc_native_settings.cpp:521
- **F8 and F11 bypass the menu hook and keep working** [code-confirmed] While a settings page owns input, F11 and F8 are returned to the window procedure (return 0) instead of being queued, so the window shortcuts keep working. F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen. — pc_native_settings.cpp:609
- **Escape is the gameplay pause; Start and Escape are shown as Esc in prompts** [code-confirmed] During gameplay Escape opens the pause menu, and controller Start or Menu does too. - **Intro skip and title continue** `001F40D3` [code-confirmed] Enter, Space, Escape or a left click skips a prerecorded intro. Controller Menu/Start also skips. - **Last-used device decides prompts and rumble** [code-confirmed] pc_input_note_gamepad makes the gamepad the active device when a button is newly pressed, or when an axis moves past its deadzone (stick deadzone 7849 left, 8689 right; trigger threshold 30). An axis counts as activity when it changes by more than 4 (triggers) or 512 (sticks) between reports. Any keyboard or mouse event calls pc_input_note_keyboard. A device change bumps the input revision and runs the output-policy callback, so rumble stops when keyboard or mouse takes over. — pc_frontend.c:187

That the Invert Y and sensitivity settings are applied inside this hook is inferred from its name and arguments, not read from its body. — patch_pc_frontend.py:148
- **Invert flight's consumer is not in this pack** [inferred, open-question] The setting is stored in the INI and shown as 'Invert flight controls (VTOL)'. Its consumer in the guest flight code is not in the pack. The UI sets PC_INVERT_FLIGHT and it is saved, but no reader is visible in these files. *How:* Grep the generated code for PC_INVERT_FLIGHT or pc_setting_get(PC_INVERT_FLIGHT) to find the reader. — pc_frontend.h:20
- **Keyboard layout setting** [code-confirmed] KeyboardLayout is a string, default pc. main.c passes it into RECOMP_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT unless that env var is already set. pc_prompts.cpp reads the Windows layout with GetKeyboardLayout(0) to decide when cached prompt text is stale. — main.c:196
- **Prompt text rewrite: ma2_pc_prompt_text** `000C0FD0`, `001FFA04`, `00200F56` [code-confirmed] Guest text draws are rewritten at loc_000C0FD0 (recomp_0020), loc_001FFA04 and loc_00200F56 (recomp_0053). The rewrite turns authored 'Press A', 'the B button', 'White button' and similar into the current bound key names. Gamepad prompts keep A, B, X, Y, RB, LB and Menu. Results are cached by source text per input revision and keyboard layout, up to 128 entries. — pc_prompts.cpp:130
- **Prompt context: menu commands versus gameplay actions** [code-confirmed] A/B wording in a menu context becomes Enter/Esc only for the explicit command list: continue, confirm, select mission, join, update, try again, read this message, start the troubleshooter and cancel. Other A/B wording uses the current gameplay binding. 'Press START' becomes Esc in gameplay and objective-review lines. 'Pull the Right/Left trigger' becomes a Press of the mouse fire key on keyboard only. — pc_prompts.cpp:44
- **D-pad becomes arrow keys on keyboard prompts** [code-confirmed] Keyboard prompts replace 'D-pad' with 'arrow keys'. 'left thumbstick' becomes the current forward, left, back and right keys, and 'right thumbstick' becomes 'mouse'. Changing movement bindings does not change the D-pad wording. — pc_prompts.cpp:197
- **Text ID ranges routed by ma2_pc_localized** `002B4979` [code-confirmed] ma2_pc_localized (hooked at loc_002B4979 in recomp_0070) routes by text id: 0x00F00000-0x00FFFFFF to the scenario text (ma2_scn_text), 0x70020000-0x7002FFFF to the bots text (ma2_bots_localized), and 0x70000000-0x70000FFF to the settings page text (ma2_pc_page_text). Id 94 is 'Press Enter or click to start' (or 'Press Menu to start' on gamepad). Ids 0x70010000-0x70010005 are footer legends: Enter, Esc, then the bound keys for X, Y, RB and LB, with short names (LMB, Bksp, PgUp and so on) for mouse and special keys. — pc_prompts.cpp:212
- **QTE captions use the bound key** [code-confirmed] QTE masks map to actions: 4 = A, 1 = X, 2 = Y, 0x40 = B, 0x10 = mouse alt fire (LT alternative) and 0x20 = mouse fire (RT alternative). The label is the bound key in short form (M1, Spc, Ent and similar). Dual bindings give a 'primary / alternative' legend. Gamepad input returns no caption. Captions wider than 28 units (or a legend over 108) are rejected. — pc_prompts.cpp:269
- **Prompt font width compensation for the HUD** `000C1640`, `000C1755` [code-confirmed] A thread-local counter ma2_pc_font_virtual is incremented at loc_000C1640 and decremented at loc_000C1755 around glyph submission. While it is non-zero the widescreen centring offset is skipped. The counter is static TLS in gen0020. — patch_pc_frontend.py:69
- **Settings page text entries** [code-confirmed] The text id picks the page: entry 0 is the page title (DISPLAY SETTINGS, AUDIO SETTINGS or CONTROLS), entries 1-13 are rows, 18 is the draw-distance hint, and anything else is the hint line. The hint is gamepad text (D-pad, A, B) or keyboard text (Arrows, Enter, Esc). — pc_native_settings.cpp:328
- **Vibration reaches the native XInput motors** [documented] PC_CONTROLS.md says vibration reaches the native XInput motors. Switching to keyboard and mouse stops primary-controller feedback on the next game report, and switching away or closing the window stops active motors at once. Vibration is controller option 1 ('Vibration: On/Off') in the profile. — pc_native_settings.cpp:322
- **Pause rumble candidate: four-bit port mask and paused branch** `0001FE60` [code-confirmed, open-question] A private candidate (pause-candidate) adds xbox_InputFeedbackPaused(blocked_ports), a four-bit port mask. It changes the sub_0001FE60 entry and its paused branch in recomp_0001 and xinput_device.c. On pause it suppresses physical output at once, clears stale effects, and keeps each resumed port suppressed until its zero is retired. Checked by 48 combined CPU scenarios and 47 expiry regressions. It is a separate candidate queue and was not verified in play. Status is open.
- **Rumble expiry bug: a skipped zero is never retried** `0001FE60`, `0001FE00`, `0001FD30`, `0002B990` [code-confirmed, open-question] The accepted manager clears an expired effect's duration, start, magnitudes and port even when its single zero request is skipped because a previous transfer is pending (status 997). A later completion cannot recover that zero, so the motors can keep running. The candidate keeps the slot, port and duration reserved until the wrapper reports the zero accepted. Checked by a 789-event CPU comparison; motor sensation was not tested. Status: candidate, not confirmed as shipped. Stays open.
- **Rumble effects: ten slots, scheduler takes the first duration-zero slot** `0001FD30`, `0001FE00`, `0001FE60` [code-confirmed] The scheduler sub_0001FD30 picks the first slot with duration 0, so a retained retry slot is not overwritten. sub_0001FE60 runs expiry and sub_0001FE00 is the cancel path. There are ten slots. A pending zero occupies one, so when all ten are reserved the scheduler refuses new requests until a stop is accepted and a slot is released.
- **USB dispatch crash: stack-matched dispatch region candidate** `0042532E`, `00424AF2`, `0042441E`, `0041D8B6` [code-confirmed, open-question] Observed crash (run 2026-10-10) at native RVA 0x0310AF47, mapping to sub_0042532E+0x507 during USB SET_REPORT construction. Demonstrated defect: kernel_thunk_dispatch_body advances g_esp before the IRQL bridge call, so the HAL stack matcher can skip the USB dispatch lock or misclassify direct native calls. Candidate: bridge_KfRaiseIrql and bridge_KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel bracket the HAL call with xbox_DispatchRegionEnter and Leave, and the stack matcher goes. A pool race was reproduced in CPU tests. The crash is not claimed resolved.
- **USB ISR, completion DPC and request builder addresses** `0042441E`, `00424AF2`, `0042532E`, `00425264` [code-confirmed] The hardware ISR is sub_0042441E, registered by sub_0041D8B6 through import 425A24. It handles status and MMIO and queues the controller DPC through import 425A30. The completion DPC sub_00424AF2 is registered (recomp_0102.c:16240) through import 4259EC for object+440. The request builder sub_0042532E calls the allocator at 00425264. The submission entry 004257C4 raises IRQL through 4259E0.
- **Restart heap free-tail candidate (D27)** [code-confirmed, open-question] Candidate D27 changes the normal allocator in xbox_memory_layout.c. When a bump request would pass the heap top, it joins the highest free descriptor that ends at the watermark, provided the whole aligned request fits. Controlled CPU cases (request 3761904, watermark 48785136, capacity 50855936) reject on baseline and succeed on the candidate. The native restart repair is unproven: it needs a repeat restart capture.
- **Saves, profiles and logs are per Windows user** [code-confirmed] Saves and caches are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\Saved Games. Logs go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\Logs, named by time and pid. main.c creates the folders from LOCALAPPDATA, and falls back to the exe folder if that fails. The installer ships no save or profile data, and a fresh install on a machine with a profile shows that profile. Profiles are shared per Windows user, not per install (decision 2026-10-20). — main.c:108
- **Storage copies missing files only** [code-confirmed] pc_storage.h declares ma2_pc_copy_missing(source, destination). It copies a file only if the destination is missing, so an existing save is never replaced. main.c calls ma2_pc_storage_initialize(YOUR_GAME_DIR) during startup, after the kernel init and before the kernel bridge. — pc_storage.h:8
- **Profile save file names and sizes** `00320D69`, `0015EFF2` [code-confirmed] A save holds MASave.sav (308 bytes in a checked sample) and Missions\MASaveGame.wdf (3145728 bytes, preallocated checkpoint generation). The checkpoint writes MASaveGame.wdf to the Z: cache path, from the original string Z:\Missions\MASaveGame.wdf at 00475FA8. A profile-only span writes 380 bytes: 308 profile and 72 global settings. Field meanings are not in this pack.
- **Checkpoint write chain in the original code** `0015D4C7`, `0015EFF2`, `00167B25`, `000B53E0` [code-confirmed] sub_0015D4C7 calls sub_0015EFF2 (checkpoint to cache). sub_0015EFF2 prepares the root, temporarily installs the progress callback 0015CED6, calls B53E0, and restores state. B53E0 is the only direct caller of the common writer B9400. Its other callers are sub_00167B25 (existing profile envelope, gen0037) and sub_00167D16 (overlapping generated entry). sub_00167B25 writes 24+284 signed profile bytes and then runs the checkpoint graph through B53E0.
- **Save progress callback 0015CED6 runs at 100 ms** `0015CED6`, `000BBAF0`, `000BCAD0` [code-confirmed] The progress callback 0015CED6 calls BBAF0 and sometimes BCAD0. The serializer gates it at 100 ms, so a long callback can take most of the save interval. Reducing how often it runs would change behaviour unless its side effects are shown to be independent. A wrapper in recomp_manual.c overrides 0015CED6, calls the generated callback once, and times it when RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY is set.
- **RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY diagnostic (opt-)** [code-confirmed] When RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY is exactly 1, one [SAVE-LATENCY] line goes to stderr at each save exit. It gives whole-save, pre-graph, graph and post-graph ticks, the callback count and wall time, native IO per file bucket (b0 MASave.sav, b1 MASaveGame.wdf, b2 cache WDF, b3 other, b4 unresolved) and an 'other' remainder. Ticks convert with ms = ticks*1000/hz. Disabled, it makes no clock calls or path lookups. Callbacks outside a save print [SAVE-LATENCY-UNCOVERED]. Probes wrap create, write, flush, close and set-information classes 19 and 20 only. *How:* Set RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY=1, do one normal Save and Quit or checkpoint, then read the [SAVE-LATENCY] line. Require the full-span record and no coverage error before optimizing.
- **Save pause attribution: measured spans miss most of the checkpoint** [code-confirmed] Observed profile spans have graph ticks of 0 and do not time the reported Saving pause, because the checkpoint-to-cache path bypasses sub_00167B25. A 3690 ms PERF-PACING window was seen near one save, on a different thread, so it is only temporal proximity. The Save and Quit transfer (sub_167DB6 and sub_167ED9 call 2BD76E before sub_167B25) is not measured.
- **Superseded save-latency reservation: recomp_0019 and recomp_0035** `000B9400`, `0015EFF2`, `00167B25` [code-confirmed, superseded] The later latency proposal dropped those for kernel_bridge.c, recomp_manual.c and recomp_0037.c (sub_00167B25 graph phase), and that is the scope approved and implemented. The three-file plan with 0019 and 0035 is superseded.
- **Save latency measurement must not change save semantics** [code-confirmed] The probe keeps guest registers, stack, memory and results identical, and keeps the flush, preallocation, callback order and signing. Disabled paths change no result. The measured graph interval is B53E0-inclusive: checkpoint creation, preallocation, serialization, header work and the final close.
- **Installer save data policy** [documented] The installer carries no save data. Saves and settings stay in the per-user folder, and a new install does not delete an existing profile.
- **Playtest capture kit: Resume and Continue (historical kit README)** [documented, historical] The playtest kit's Start-Playthrough.ps1 starts a playthrough once and resumes it later. Resume uses the saved profile under PC Test Kit\Test Results and never silently creates a new one. Logs stream to disk: each raw channel keeps 8 MiB chunks, the timeline 16. This README is from a previous kit.
- **MechAssault 2.exe launcher and startup order** [code-confirmed] WinMain configures logging, opts the process out of EcoQoS power throttling, looks for pc_assets\common.mgf (else .\pc_assets), reads the cache namespace from cache.version, then loads game_files\ma2.xbe, showing 'Failed to load game_files' if that fails. It initialises the kernel and storage, starts the kernel bridge, arms the watchdog, and runs the recompiled entry point. — main.c:451
- **Launcher sets process defaults before the game starts** [code-confirmed] configure_pc sets RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 and RECOMP_GPU=d3d11, and RECOMP_TITLE_KEVENTS, RECOMP_VBLANK, RECOMP_FB_WINDOW, RECOMP_HEAP_RECLAIM, RECOMP_ASYNC_IO, RECOMP_USB, RECOMP_INPUT_LATCH, RECOMP_MOUSE_GUEST_POLL and RECOMP_EXIT_ON_CLOSE to 1, each only if unset. It also sets RECOMP_RENDER_SCALE to 0. — main.c:164
- **Console and log file env vars** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_CONSOLE set to a nonzero value attaches or allocates a console and points stdio at it. Otherwise, when neither stdout nor stderr is a disk file or pipe, stderr goes to a timestamped log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\Logs and stdout goes to NUL. Both streams are then unbuffered. — main.c:99
- **Window and display env vars** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_WINDOW_WIDTH and RECOMP_WINDOW_HEIGHT (default 1280x960) set the starting client size. RECOMP_FULLSCREEN (default 0) starts borderless. RECOMP_DISPLAY_TRACE prints [PC-DISPLAY] lines for client size, aspect and movie changes. — pc_native_settings.cpp:689
- **Menu, footer and pointer trace env vars** [verified-in-game] RECOMP_MENU_TRACE prints [PC-MENU], [PC-MOUSE], [PC-ARROWS] and [PC-POINTER] lines, and [PC-GLOW] shows under it. RECOMP_UI_LIVE uses the injected pointer instead of GetCursorPos. RECOMP_FOOTER_TRACE prints [PC-FOOTER]. *How:* RECOMP_MENU_DUMP=1 RECOMP_MENU_TRACE=1, then open the menu and read [MENU-DUMP] in the log. — pc_native_settings.cpp:362
- **Texture and FMV env vars** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_TEXTURE_QUALITY (0-2) and RECOMP_FMV_QUALITY (0-1) override the INI keys. RECOMP_TEXTURE_PACK_DIR changes where the 2x and 4x index.json files are checked; the default is game_files\texture_packs. — main.c:187
- **RECOMP_SHADER_PRELOAD and per-level shader lists** [verified-in-game] RECOMP_SHADER_PRELOAD (default 0) pre-creates a level's shaders while it loads. It is the same as the [Display] PreloadShaders key and Display row 10, 'Load level shaders when loading'. Per-level lists are recorded even when the option is off, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\xboxrecomp\shader-cache\levels\LEVEL.txt. The shipped lists are pc_assets\shader-levels.txt. *How:* Desktop A/B on Bogged Down: miss-path CPU time 107 ms to 9 ms, 70 shaders pre-created in 15 ms (2026-10-15). — main.c:189
- **Input env vars and their INI twins** [code-confirmed] Each Input INI key has a RECOMP_* twin (RECOMP_KEYBOARD, RECOMP_MOUSE_AIM, RECOMP_MOUSE_SENSITIVITY, RECOMP_INVERT_Y, RECOMP_INVERT_FLIGHT). RECOMP_USB, RECOMP_INPUT_LATCH and RECOMP_MOUSE_GUEST_POLL default to 1. RECOMP_USB_PADS sets the controller count, and the split-screen Add Guest menu needs it at 2 or more. — main.c:171
- **Audio and watchdog env vars** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_AC97_READY gates the APU: when it is absent the APU is not initialised. RECOMP_AUDIO_VOLUME (0-100) overrides the master volume. RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS arms the hang watchdog only when set, and the watchdog must be started on the guest thread, after the dispatch init. — main.c:548
- **RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY gate** [code-confirmed] The variable is read once per process and only the exact character 1 enables it. It is never written to the INI. The disabled save path does no clock or path work.
- **Cache namespace from cache.version** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_GAME_OVERLAY defaults to pc_assets if it holds common.mgf, else .\pc_assets. RECOMP_CACHE_NAMESPACE is read from the first line of cache.version, but only when that line is letters, digits or hyphens. A missing or bad file leaves it unset. — main.c:484
- **Frontend setting storage and atomics** [code-confirmed] PC settings and bindings are atomic ints stored as value+1, so zero means unset and the fallback is returned. Reads are acquire loads and writes are interlocked. Bindings bump the input revision on change. Output-policy callbacks (used for rumble) run when the captured state, input context or device changes. — pc_frontend.c:164
- **Cinematics are paced to 30 Hz** [code-confirmed] pc_display_cinematic(1) sets the original 4:3 view and a 30 FPS cap until it is cleared, without changing the saved settings. pc_cinematic_pace holds each frame to 1/30 s just before present, using a high-resolution waitable timer and a short spin. A lower user frame limit still applies after it. — pc_frontend.c:85
- **Aspect and movie rules** [code-confirmed] pc_display_aspect(original) returns the screen aspect when PC_ASPECT is on, a size is known and no cinematic is active; otherwise it returns the original. Movies keep their own shape because the movie player lays them out from the screen size it is given. The earlier forcing of 4:3 for movies was removed on 2026-10-14, since it squeezed a widened frame. — pc_frontend.c:98
- **Scene render size comes from the selected resolution** [code-confirmed] The scene render size is the selected resolution, not a multiplier. pc_display_render_extent fits a 4:3 scene inside the selected pixels, unless RECOMP_RENDER_SCALE gives a diagnostic height. With no render size set, pc_render_size_get falls back to the display size, then to 640x480. — pc_frontend.c:69
- **Render runs on the GPU thread; window callbacks must queue events instead of touching the immediate context.** [code-confirmed] Render runs on the GPU thread; window callbacks must queue events instead of touching the immediate context. — pc_frontend.h:6
- **Installer is one exe that holds the whole kit** [code-confirmed] The release deliverable is one installer exe (about 102 MB, later 107-108 MB), the only file in release\. A native stub unpacks an LZMS-compressed kit (Windows Compression API) to %TEMP%\MA2RecompInstaller-<id>. It runs the bundled Python 3.13 pythonw on installer\gui.py (tkinter), or installer\install.py when given arguments, and deletes the unpacked copy on exit. Enhanced textures and videos can be added later by running the same exe on the install folder.
- **Installer pipeline: XISO to xboxrecomp to MSVC to PC Release** [code-confirmed] The install runs 11 steps: unpack the XISO, run xboxrecomp, apply the patch set, build with MSVC and copy out a clean PC Release. The rebuild order is assemble.py, cmake_patch.py, gen_patch.py make, make_payload.py, then installer-exe\pack_installer.py. The asset chain is build_pc_assets.py (12 rows, with the Bots wrapper, display_rows and QTE icons). make_payload.py records the installed PC Release exe, so rerun it after each publish and before packing; release.json's exe hash is provenance only.
- **Installer fetches VS Build Tools when no compiler is found** [documented] When there is no compiler, install.py downloads Microsoft's vs_buildtools.exe (aka.ms/vs/18/stable, then 17/release), checks its Authenticode signature (unsigned files are rejected), and runs it elevated with the VCTools workload and the VC Redist component. Hidden flags: --vs <VS folder> to reuse an install, and --until <step>.
- **Accented install paths: build in an ASCII folder** [verified-in-game] An accented Windows user name breaks link.exe, which reads Ninja's .rsp in the ANSI code page (LNK1181). Installer.build_root puts src and build in <drive>:\MA2RecompBuild-<hash> (fallbacks ProgramData, Public) when the work folder is not ASCII. finish removes that folder. build.cmd starts with chcp 65001 for UTF-8 under cmd, but chcp alone does not fix the link step. *How:* Test with the real build; a small test project hides the link problem (no response file).
- **Installer end-to-end test and checks** [verified-in-game] The CLI end-to-end run executes all 11 steps with --xiso and --dest as absolute paths (a relative --xiso stops at step 1), with --keep-work. Checks: objcompare (201/202 objects identical, the only difference the path-hashed .data$rs), common.mgf inner files identical, the editor exe identical, and a 6v6 bot match or a scenario playing from the install. replay.py honours REPLAY_GAMEDIR. *How:* python objcompare against <_work/build>; replay.py with REPLAY_GAMEDIR. Use absolute --xiso and --dest.
- **Publish only to PC Release** [documented] Publish only to MechAssault 2\PC Release and its Playthrough Capture kit. PC Release Bots was abandoned after the 2026-10-14 merge (57702bc3). Laptop zips cover PC Release files only. publish.py CURRENT must stay at the installed exe hash that --stage asserts on.
- **Superseded: publish to both PC Release and PC Release Bots** [documented, superseded] Earlier notes say to update both PC Release and PC Release Bots. That is superseded: only PC Release is updated.
- **Assembled resource fix v5: Sky_Test and Small_TeamDestruction hang on loading** [verified-in-game, open-question] In run v5 the Sky_Test and Small_TeamDestruction scenarios hung on the loading screen after the level-resource gate fired. The load stalled after a directory open and before the Partition5 cache. The desc hook was reverted in v6, which removed the hang but gave a black match with an empty board. The only change kept is removing the RECOMP_SCENARIO_TRACE probes. Scenarios that need an assembled archive (Scn*.mgf) do not load yet. POINTER 2026-11-10: to be checked once in the W-90 campaign gate run (all 41 campaign entries on the installed build); Sky_Test and Small_TeamDestruction are not campaign entries, so check them by hand. Stays open until then.
- **patch_pc_frontend.py reapplies hooks after code regeneration** [code-confirmed] patch_pc_frontend.py reapplies the menu, text, input, audio and display hooks to generated recomp_00xx.c files after regeneration. Each edit anchors on a unique 'loc_XXXXXXXX:' line and is idempotent. If an anchor is missing it raises 'hook changed; inspect'. It covers recomp_0020 (prompts and font), 0051 (main menu and movie skip), 0052 (pause and dispatch menus), 0053 (text prompts), 0057 and 0058 (settings submenus), 0039 and 0038 (mouse look), 0041 (controller), 0095 and 0096 (audio trace) and others. *How:* Run after regenerating generated recomp code (made at install time, not in the repository); it raises if a hook anchor changed. — patch_pc_frontend.py:7
- **xbox_input layer: Xbox XInput API to Windows XInput** [documented] The xbox_input layer maps the Xbox controller API to Windows XInput (xinput_xbox.h and xinput_device.c). Buttons are a bitmask; the analog A, B, X, Y, Black, White and trigger values are 0-255 with a press threshold of 30. Black maps to RB and White to LB. Ports are 0-3. xbox_InputSetState takes motor speeds 0-65535. — README.md:3
- **Default PC key for each Xbox input** [documented] Defaults: Enter or Escape = Start/pause, Space = A, F = B, R = X, Q = Y, 1 and 2 = White and Black (RB and LB on a pad), WASD = left stick, mouse movement = camera and aim, IJKL = right stick, Left mouse or V = right trigger, Right mouse or C = left trigger, Shift and Ctrl = stick clicks, Arrows = D-pad, Backspace = Back.
- **Fidelity review brief: scope and PC feature list** [documented] The fidelity review brief lists PC features to review, including keyboard and mouse, resolution and aspect settings, enhanced textures and FMVs, wider draw distance, menus, saves and capture. It treats PC_CONTROLS.md as the intended-behaviour reference, warns that it may contain older claims, and asks for checks against current code and logs. It is a review brief, not a spec.
- **Status of the PC polish candidates** [documented, open-question] The candidate is not in the the game source tree source checked here. The backlog is coordination text, not a spec.
- **Prompt candidate P1-P5: status and results** [code-confirmed, open-question] A prompt-only candidate changes the authored-text rewrite: A, B, X and Y after Press are mapped in order, Pull becomes Press only in the trigger phrases, explicit thumbstick directions use the current movement keys, D-pad stays arrow keys, and context is applied per instruction. Of 181 rows, 31 change. A focused fixture passes 113 checks (42 failures on the baseline). P6 ('or B' without a repeated Press) and P7 are outside this batch. <a id="t07_stability"></a>

## Runtime, kernel and stability: memory map, threads, freezes and crashes

## Runtime, kernel and stability: memory map, threads, freezes and crashes

Pack `t07_stability`. Facts are in `.\facts\t07_stability.json` . Sources are cited by file name and line. Full paths are in the facts file.

### Overview

The recompiled game runs against a memory map that copies the Xbox layout at its original addresses. Guest RAM is one 64 MB page-file mapping, mapped at a host base and mirrored 28 times at 64 MB steps, so guest addresses wrap as they do on the 26-bit Xbox bus. The XBE sections are copied to the addresses they were linked . The fake TIB sits at 0x00004000, the main stack at 0x00780000 (8 MB, growing down), the kernel data exports at 0x00740000, and the heap from 0x00F80000 to the top of the mapping. Unlike the older docs, the TIB is no longer at address 0, so a null dereference faults where it happens.

Kernel imports are not resolved by the XBE loader. Each thunk slot holds `0x80000000 | ordinal`, and init rewrites it to a synthetic VA at 0xFE000000 + 4 x slot (data exports get the VA of their data). A recompiled indirect call to that VA reaches `recomp_lookup_kernel`, which picks the bridge; the bridge reads stdcall arguments from the simulated stack at `g_esp`, does the Win32 work, and returns in `g_eax`. Hardware apertures (NV2A at 0xFD000000, MCPX at 0xFE800000, flash at 0xFF000000) are plain zeroed RAM, and a background thread clears the NV2A busy bits that D3D8 spins on.

Threads are real. `PsCreateSystemThreadEx` calls `CreateThread`, and critical sections are shadowed onto host locks keyed by the guest pointer. Timing is Windows timing: `KeDelayExecutionThread` becomes `Sleep`, and one kernel timer thread drains guest DPCs, the 60 Hz vblank and guest timers. Windows does not give that thread 1 ms resolution unless the process asks for it. A bare-process measurement of `Sleep(1)` averaged about 15.5 ms, so a guest 1 ms sleep may take that long; the in-game figure is not confirmed. Most of the freezes in this pack were a spin or a lock that waited on something that never changed. The fixes were loop guards, locks taken in the right order, and early-outs for dead sockets.

Stability work came in three waves: the 2026-10-10 hitch and crash investigations (measurements and one crash, no fixes); the 2026-10-14 single-player audit, where the XACT guards were in PC Release 57702bc3 but the CRT trig fix and the XACT DPC lock patch were not yet; and the heap and lock work after that. The table under "Bugs and fixes" says which build each fix is .

### Facts

- **Guest RAM is a page-file mapping mirrored 28 times** `00010000` [code-confirmed] Guest RAM is one page-file-backed CreateFileMapping, sized to the mapped range (64 MB by default). It is mapped at the base view, and 28 mirror views of the same pages sit at base + N x mapped size, so guest addresses wrap as on the Xbox 26-bit bus. A write through one mirror is visible through every other. Plain VirtualAlloc would give separate copies, which is why file mapping is used. — xbox_memory_layout.c:1772
- **Base view tries fixed host bases, then lets the OS choose** `00010000` [code-confirmed] The base view is mapped at the first free of 0x00010000, 0x00800000, 0x01000000, 0x02000000, 0x10000000, then host-chosen (sentinel 0). The loop now runs the sentinel too; the old condition stopped at the zero, which broke arm64 macOS hosts where all fixed bases fall inside __PAGEZERO. The docs' 0x00010000 'ideal' base is therefore not guaranteed on Windows. — xbox_memory_layout.c:1793
- **Windows does not pre-reserve the mirror span** [code-confirmed] On POSIX the whole base-plus-mirror span is reserved first and each view is carved out of it. On Windows that is skipped, because VirtualFree cannot release part of a reservation and the base view then never maps. Mirrors on Windows are placed one at a time at fixed addresses, so some can fail; the docs record about 4 of 33 failing near 0x76000000 on Windows 11. — xbox_memory_layout.c:1812
- **Mirrors that overlap the tiled aperture are skipped** [code-confirmed] When the mapped size is large enough that a wrap mirror would cover 0xF0000000, that mirror is skipped and logged as 'overlaps the tiled aperture'. The specific tiled alias is considered worth more than one generic wrap mirror. Mirror m covers guest (m+1) x mapped size. — xbox_memory_layout.c:2585
- **Section addresses come from the XBE header at runtime** `00010000` [code-confirmed] Section VAs are parsed from the XBE header at load and are not hard-coded, so the runtime works with any title. The numeric section table in docs/technical/memory-layout.md (.text 0x00011000,rdata 0x0036B7C0,data 0x003B2360) is one Burnout 3 example, not Mechassault 2's layout. The XBE header itself is copied to 0x00010000. — xbox_memory_layout.h:112
- **Main-thread fake TIB sits at 0x00004000, not page zero** [code-confirmed] The fake Thread Information Block for the first thread is at 0x00004000 (XBOX_TIB_MAIN). fs: is based at a per-thread g_fs_base, which starts at that value. The TIB was moved off page zero so that a null dereference faults instead of reading or overwriting the SEH chain head. — xbox_memory_layout.h:338
- **Older docs put the TIB at address 0** [documented, superseded] The memory-layout doc describes a fake TIB at 0x0 with MEM32(0x04), MEM32(0x08), MEM32(0x28) and so on, and says fs: lowers to MEM32(0x28) from low memory. The header now says the TIB is at 0x4000 and fs: resolves through g_fs_base. Treat the doc's 0x0 layout as historical. — xbox_memory_layout.h:338
- **Main thread stack: 8 MB at 0x00780000 growing down** [code-confirmed] The main stack region is XBOX_STACK_BASE 0x00780000 for 8 MB; the initial ESP is base + size - 16 (0x00F7FFF0). The 8 MB size was chosen because failed RECOMP_ICALL indirect calls can leak stdcall arguments onto the stack every frame. — xbox_memory_layout.h:335
- **Heap runs from 0x00F80000 to the mapped top** [code-confirmed] The dynamic heap starts at XBOX_HEAP_BASE 0x00F80000, directly above the main stack. XBOX_HEAP_TOP is the mapped size if set, otherwise RAM (64 MB retail). Startup logs 'Heap: N MB at Xbox VA'. The memory-layout doc's code sample with base 0x00880000 is an old illustration and is superseded. — xbox_memory_layout.h:413
