Custom Scenarios is hub action 8. Each step focuses an item via sub_001CAD40 (recomp_0048.c, 121 bytes) and clicks it, and selects barrel values with sub_00208BF9 (recomp_0054.c, 76 bytes, 44 callers). Enter is posted as WM_KEYDOWN and WM_KEYUP.
- **Autostart gives up after 15 s without menu progress** [verified-in-game] If a menu makes no progress for 15 seconds, the autostart logs that it gave up, the menus are returned to the player, and the player's own bot values are restored immediately. Give-up is tested with the stall hook.
- **Game type numbers used by autostart (sub_001661C1)** `001661C1` [code-confirmed] Game type numbers used by the autostart barrels: TeamDestruction 3, Destruction 0xA, CTF 0xE, BaseWar 0x10, SnatchIt 0x11, CheckIt 0xF, TeamLastManStanding 1, LastManStanding 9, NotIt 4 and Grinder 6. The barrel values equal these numbers. The function is 376 bytes in recomp_0037.c.
- **Bot test config held in memory, never written to the INI** [code-confirmed] ma2_bots_test_config sets the red, blue, FFA and skill values in g_cfg with g_cfg_test=1, and config_set never writes pc_settings.ini while the flag is set. In the match, ma2_bots_test_release(0) sets g_cfg_test=2, and the next New Game reloads from the INI. Release(1) is used for a give-up.
- **Open: single custom mission plays the campaign intro** [documented, open-question] A single custom mission plays the roughly 70-second campaign intro movie before the mission. This is pre-existing behaviour and is not yet changed.
- **ma2_scn_level_load mounts Scn<ID>_assets archive (sub_00013550)** `00013550` [code-confirmed] The scenario [Assets] loader is hooked at loc_000138A0 at the end of the level mount block in sub_00013550 (recomp_0000.c, 2189 bytes). It reads the world path from [[0x524A60]+4], takes its basename Scn<ID>, and mounts T:\scenarios\Scn<ID>_assets_<hash>.mgf through mount_archive (sub_00025B70 with args 0,0). This runs whether or not the gate mounted.
- **ma2_scn_level_unload unmounts the scenario archive (sub_000171E0)** `000171E0` [code-confirmed] The unload hook at loc_000178C9 in sub_000171E0 (recomp_0000.c, 2336 bytes) calls sub_00025C90 with the file system and name, then sub_00025D10 to reset lookup state, following the native code. It joins the level unload's three unmount branches.
- **sub_00025B70 mount_archive: mounts an archive by name** `00025B70` [code-confirmed] sub_00025B70 (122 bytes, recomp_0002.c, 24 callers) mounts an archive. It needs the file system object at fs+0x148. The arg2 value selects drive-sector streaming mode, and the level mount uses 0,1 while boot and index mounts use 0,0. The note suggests the wrong streaming argument was a likely cause of an earlier black T: mount.
- **sub_00025C90 unmount by name; sub_00025D10 resets lookup state** `00025C90`, `00025D10` [code-confirmed] sub_00025C90 (127 bytes, 14 callers) unmounts an archive by name and is stdcall with ret 8. sub_00025D10 (69 bytes, 14 callers) resets the file system lookup state and is called after a successful unmount.
- **sub_00025BF0: already-mounted check by name** `00025BF0` [code-confirmed] sub_00025BF0 (89 bytes) returns 1 when an archive is already mounted by name, and the mount helper uses that result to skip a second mount.
- **sub_0002EA10 creates a 0x2C archive object (mgIO\mgStream)** `0002EA10` [code-confirmed] sub_0002EA10 (808 bytes, recomp_0004.c) creates the new 0x2C archive object used by mount_archive. Its string table includes mgIO\mgStream.
- **sub_00026890: list push_back for fs+0x18C** `00026890` [code-confirmed] sub_00026890 (51 bytes, recomp_0003.c, 19 callers) is the push_back used for the file system list at fs+0x18C.
- **Level descriptor global at [0x524A60]** `00524A60`, `004539D4` [code-confirmed] The level descriptor at [0x524A60] has the world path char* at +4, the resource std:string at +0x10 and a no-cache flag at +0x68. The string d:\allmissions.mgf is at 0x4539D4 and is unmounted by the level unload when level+0xB4 is set.
- **Scenario [Assets] fix verified: Sky_Test plays on Bogged Down** [verified-in-game] Scenarios with a non-empty [Assets] list play: Sky_Test plays on Bogged Down with the aurora sky, and Small loads GoCommando night sky and conifers with BattleArmor spawns. Quit to main hub unmounts and remounts, and the sweep passes 18 of 18 with no faults. A failed write now plays without the assets instead of dropping the scenario.
- **T:\scenarios directory created before the first assets write** [code-confirmed] The T:\scenarios directory is created before the first assets write (scenario_dir). A failed write now plays the scenario without its assets rather than dropping it, which had caused a retail map to load.
- **ma2models: decoder library for templates, models and textures** [verified-in-game] Its API is ma2models.h (namespace ma2m) with API.md. build.cmd builds release and debug at /W4, and tools/modeldump.cpp is the test tool. It decodes 2,892 of 2,892 MP-map templates, 950 of 950 shipped GlobalEntities model and mtb pairs, and all 21,376 .tif files on the disc. A 12,000-case fuzz run passes.
- **Game space is left-handed, Y up, models face +Z** [verified-in-game] Game space is left-handed with Y up, and a 'Mech's front faces +Z. This was verified on a sign texture with glyphs.
- **ma2m ResolveModelPath search order** [code-confirmed] Templates name atlas.NODE, VMil_VTOL.MGMODEL and similar, but MP levels ship only *_low.* files. ResolveModelPath tries, per archive in priority order, the name as written, then _low, then the .NODE .MGMODEL swap.
- **Scenario [Assets] dependency rule** [documented] To build a scenario's [Assets] list, open the ArchiveSet as Base, then common.mgf, then the rest. Run CollectTemplateDependencies over every template in templates.wdf and list dependencies whose archive is neither Base nor common, skipping entries with found == false. Retail itself references missing files, such as every 'Mech's MechClawDecal = tmpDev/claw/claw.mat.
- **MATerrain TerrainHeight Field is an L8 MGIc picture** [code-confirmed] The MATerrain TerrainHeight Field is an MGIc picture in L8 (flags 0x4, format code 4, 64-byte row pitch). DecodeTexture reads it, and modeldump --texture-file decodes a saved blob.
- **Multiplay MountainHigh and TroubledWaters .mgf files are not on disc** [documented] The Multiplay folder lists MountainHigh and TroubledWaters, but their .mgf files are not on the disc.
- **Only two culled MP templates resolve outside their level archive** [code-confirmed] In the MP maps only two culled templates resolve outside their own level archive. Everything else a level's templates name is inside the level archive.
- **Object dictionary rebuild pipeline** [documented] Rebuild the object dictionary with python extract_data.py, extract_code.py and make_slices.py (about 25 s) to regenerate reader then write <Class>.json, and python merge.py and build_page.py write, MA2_Dictionary.md, coverage.json and page/. Curated cross-group facts live in overrides.json.
- **resolved_hex.json names 131 CRC keys from XBE format strings** [documented] maps 131 CRC keys to names that were built from XBE format strings.
- **Boardable: Nation 0, StartAbandoned 1, owner controller, AI off** [documented, open-question] A vehicle is boardable when Nation is 0, StartAbandoned is 1, it has a child MAOwnerController whose MoverTemplateUID equals the TemplateID, and m_bAIEnabled is 0. Retail data shows this, but the runtime check was not found in code, and whether m_bAIEnabled 0 is required in play is not verified. Loki and Stiletto have identical flags, and the Stiletto's configuration is outside BoggedDown's culled set.
- **Battle Armor pink blocks: ForceUseLowDetail=1** [documented] Battle Armor shows as a pink block on multiplayer bases because those levels ship only the low-detail model. Setting ForceUseLowDetail=1 avoids this. UPDATE 2026-11-09 (t27): the pink pole-and-cube is the game's marker for ANY object whose build failed (sub_D8221/sub_D8391), not only a missing model. Other causes: a template named inside the object's .mtb (debris, rubble, dust, explosion effects) whose files the scenario did not ship, and the 4 hard-coded MABuilding effect files on a Base without buildings. Editor d34766e + dcdcad4 (PC Release editor d062003f) ship all of these. See pink-placeholder-is-failed-object-build, pink-placeholder-mtb-template-refs, mabuilding-hardcoded-effect-files.
- **MARoot StartVehicles<GameType> leads to the body template** `000F26D9` [code-confirmed] MARoot's StartVehicles<GameType> property (format string at 000F26D9) points to an MAPlayerConfigurationContainer, which leads to an MAPlayerConfiguration whose CorporealTemplateUID is the body. The Generic game type value is 1F13DE84.
- **Mission_02 vehicles and mid-mission swaps** [documented] Mission_02 uses template 125894, then 125897, then 125891 NearClip BA. Mid-mission vehicle swaps use MAActionChangePlayerVehicle.
- **MARoad is a prefab tile, not a spline** [code-confirmed] MARoad is a prefab tile from a .road file, not a spline. All 799 of 799 joins check out.
- **MAWater size and MATerrainInfo water types** [code-confirmed] MAWater's size is the bounding box of its model, centred on CorporalPos. Gameplay water is the MATerrainInfo type map: 8 is shallow, 16 is deep and 32 is waterway.
- **Mission_02 orange slabs are MATriggerCuboidalVolume tripwires** [documented] The orange slabs in Mission_02 are MATriggerCuboidalVolume tripwire boxes named TB. The purple cubes are 39 MAWaypoint patrol points.
- **Open: 20 of 919 keys on placeable classes unknown** [documented, open-question] Of 919 keys on placeable classes, 20 remain unknown: 7 unnamed CRCs and 13 named fields whose values do not show a role.
- **IDE channel export regression test** [code-confirmed] A test with synthetic imports for IdexChannelObject and XboxSignatureKey checks that the exported IDE channel has a circular empty DeviceQueue.DeviceListHead and independent storage. The old initialisation left null links at +0x28 and +0x2C, inside the key region. The guest DeviceQueue starts at +0x24 and its list at +0x28. It initialises an empty host-backed queue and does not implement IDE hardware. *How:* cmake -S tests/idex_channel -B build/idex-channel -A x64, then ctest.
- **Synthetic WMA decoder fixture sine.wma** [documented] sine.wma is a generated 440 Hz tone: 0.25 s, 44,100 Hz, stereo, WMA v2 at 64 kbit/s, public domain. The test checks successful decoding and PCM metadata, then injects a source reader error after the first sample to check partial-output cleanup. FFmpeg is needed only to regenerate the fixture. *How:* Regenerate with the ffmpeg lavfi sine command in the README.
- **Diagnostic probes are owned, bounded and leave user data alone** [documented] Diagnostic game processes are owned by the probe harness and bounded by a watchdog.
- **v16 normal campaign: first checkpoint and resume (historical)** [verified-in-game, historical] The staged v16 normal campaign boots through the retail lobby, reaches first-mission gameplay and passes about nineteen minutes of monitored movement, aiming and combat. Three further restarts advance controller reports from 38,412 to 42,804, and the process closes with exit 0. A fresh process restores the private checkpoint through the lobby. This checks the initial checkpoint only.
- **Packaged startup skip taps and root menu checks (v15)** [verified-in-game, historical] The packaged v15 root launcher passes 30 ms skip taps with Enter, Space, left click and controller Start. Its native menu test passes mouse navigation, Escape and click Back, input-device switching, scene camera capture and release, settings and exit confirmation. Texture switching and keyboard adjustments pass.
- **First-mission and Mission 16 performance samples (v11 and v15, historical)** [verified-in-game, historical] Undisturbed 20-second samples at 3840x2160 with 4x textures and original draw distance measure 154-163 FPS in Mission 16 and 186-187 FPS in Mission 1, with no frame intervals above 16.7 ms in the sampled views. These are not campaign-wide minimums.
- **Ten-minute packaged soak (earlier build)** [verified-in-game, historical] A ten-minute packaged soak closed cleanly with zero runtime errors, underruns or engine glitches, with 181-190 FPS samples at 2x using real app-data preferences and saves. This was an earlier build.
- **Mission 09b interaction runs (v17 and v18 diagnostics)** [verified-in-game] The v17 fifteen-minute Mission 09b run at 3840x2160 acquired seven live actors across six reloads, and shutdown returned 0. The v18 six-minute run measured the USB clock at 999.8 ms per real second. These bounded interaction runs do not prove objective completion.

## Scenario editor: verified findings

## Verified in game: unit models and boarding

- **Pink units.** A unit draws its template's model, chosen by the instance's ForceUseLowDetail and ForceUseHighDetail flags (code 0xD7584). Most levels ship only `_low` models, so set ForceUseLowDetail=1. A missing model is only one cause of the pink marker: any failed object build draws it (see the t27 article).
- **Boarding.** A unit is boardable with StartAbandoned=1, AttackPilot=0, OverrideEnable=0 and an MAOwnerController child (MoverTemplateUID = the unit's template). Enter it by tapping Q.



### Facts

- **Units draw their template's model, picked by the instance's detail flags** `000D7584`, `000D7508`, `00027480` [verified-in-game] A placed unit is drawn with its TEMPLATE's Corporal3DObj from retail GlobalEntities, plus the INSTANCE's detail flags (code 0xD7584). ForceUseHighDetail uses the exact path. ForceUseLowDetail tries "<name>_low.<ext>" first (built at 0xD7508, exists-check sub_27480), then the exact path. With neither flag, missions use the exact path. The scenario's own templates.wdf is skipped (ma2_scenario.c:856). Templates name full models (ymir.NODE, loki.NODE, powerarmor.node) that most levels ship only as _low, so they draw as a magenta pillar placeholder: the 'pink cube' and 'pink Battle Armor'. UPDATE 2026-11-09 (t27): the pink pole-and-cube is the game's marker for ANY object whose build failed (sub_D8221/sub_D8391), not only a missing model. Other causes: a template named inside the object's .mtb (debris, rubble, dust, explosion effects) whose files the scenario did not ship, and the 4 hard-coded MABuilding effect files on a Base without buildings. Editor d34766e + dcdcad4 (PC Release editor d062003f) ship all of these. See pink-placeholder-is-failed-object-build, pink-placeholder-mtb-template-refs, mabuilding-hardcoded-effect-files. *How:* Set ForceUseLowDetail=1 and ForceUseHighDetail=0 on units whose template model the level mounts only as _low.
- **What makes a placed unit boardable** [verified-in-game] A neutral unit can be entered when it has StartAbandoned=1, AttackPilot=0, OverrideEnable=0 and an MAOwnerController child whose MoverTemplateUID is the unit's template. Child order does not matter: retail puts the OC at index 0, 1 or 2. InitiallyCollidable=1 is fine. Entering takes a Q TAP (climb animation, then the 'Mech HUD); a Q HOLD does not enter. The [PLAYER-CONTEXT] log line does not change when boarding a 'Mech (only for a tank or the pilot), so it is not a boarding signal.

<a id="t12_code_research"></a>

## Code research: object properties, triggers, rendering, audio and editor-to-game mapping

## Code research

Facts about the recompiled game code gathered by reading generated C, vtables, property tables and run logs: object properties (MA* classes), scenario triggers and actions, XACT audio, radar, spawners, water, camera, save and menu code, and how editor settings map to what the game does.

Newer facts and the `status` field win; `superseded` and `historical` facts stay for the history. Facts that disagree are reconciled in `wiki/overrides.json`. Related topics: scenario and editor t04, t11, t15, t16; gameplay t05; audio t02; bots t01a, t01b, t19 to t24.


### Facts

- **Four unnamed MAMech keys are the 'Standard' damage type of the shield table** `00186A44`, `00186EA5`, `00459970` [code-confirmed] A loop over 5 damage-type names (Standard, Energy, Ballistic, Explosive, Flame; name table at 0x459970, stride 0x100) formats %sDamageAbsorbed, %sDamageFactor, %sRecoveryDelay and %sDamagePassedOn. Write and read functions are 0x186A44 and 0x186EA5 (vtable 0x478B90). The Standard versions are the keys 34F74FCC StandardDamageAbsorbed (0.0), 67759A78 StandardDamageFactor (1.0), DCC47761 StandardRecoveryDelay (2.5) and 56E328C5 StandardDamagePassedOn (flag).
- **MATriggerCounter CheckType compares the count** `0014FD36`, `0014FD7B` [code-confirmed] CheckType: 0 means fire when the count equals CounterValue, 1 when greater, 2 when less, and any other value when not equal (code 0x14FD36-0x14FD7B).
- **Camera path timing fields** `001C9369` [code-confirmed] MACameraProperty pathDurationType: 0 means the time comes from the path, 1 from the controller (editor enum registered at 0x1C9369). Its 'flags' field: 0 means times are counted from the beginning, 1 from the end.
- **MAWaypointGroup TraverseType 2 makes a closed loop** `00183E95`, `00185EAE`, `001860C1` [code-confirmed] TraverseType 2 makes the patrol route a closed loop (code 0x183E95, 0x185EAE, 0x1860C1). 1 is the constructor default. The code read does not distinguish 1, 3 and 4.
- **Start vehicles need their exact body files in [Assets] (verified)** [verified-in-game] For every container MARoot references, the editor now walks container → MAPlayerConfiguration → unit and ships Corporal3DObj, TransitionModel and AbandonedModel from the first archive that holds the exact name, without the _low variants (Battle Armor from cinema_5_4.mgf: powerarmor.node, PilotToPowerArmor.node, AbandonedPowerArmor.MGMODEL; Rommel from mission_05.mgf: VMil_RommelMK2.MGMODEL). On a mission_09b base, the Battle Armor and Rommel starts then spawn the player, who can move and fire. Without the files there was no player.
- **Mechs outside the Base's culled set board fine** [verified-in-game] Neutral Stiletto, Ymir, Wendigo, Nova Cat and Loki placed on a Bogged Down base all board with a Q tap and can walk and fire (runs BRD2_*/BRD3_*). Nothing is needed beyond the owner controller and the unit's own files. This settles the open Stiletto (124691) plus config (124694) question: the culled set does not matter.
- **Without an owner controller a unit cannot be boarded** [verified-in-game] A unit with StartAbandoned 1 and m_bAIEnabled 0 but no MAOwnerController child (the editor's 'Player can climb in' unticked) shows no prompt, and Q does nothing (run LOCK0).
- **Terrain detail and micro-detail tiling values are repeats across the whole map** `000F6F20`, `002A54C0`, `002A69B0`, `002A6D40` [code-confirmed] The base-map UV spans the whole terrain (u 0.1, v 1.0, set in the ctor sub_002A54C0). TerrainDetailMult, TerrainDetailMult1 and TerrainMicroDetailTiling0/1 multiply that UV: uv_detail1 = uv_base*Mult, uv_detail2 = uv_base*Mult1, uv_micro_i = uv_base*Tiling_i. So they are repeats across the whole map, not per block or per metre. Metres per tile = (samples-1)*WorldScale/Mult: Mission_02 (257 samples, scale 8, 2048 m) gives 32 m for detail 1 (64), 21.3 m for detail 2 (96) and 8.5 m for micro (240). sub_000F6F20 copies the properties into the terrain object (+0x8B4 Mult, +0x8B8 Mult1, +0x8BC DetailBlend, +0x8C0/+0x8C4 Tiling0/1, +0x814 WorldScale, +0x818 CellSize). With two detail maps the multiply is a vertex-shader constant (Mult,Mult,0,1) / (Mult1,Mult1,0,1) bound per draw by sub_0006FEF0; the single-map path bakes uv1 = Mult*(uv0 - blockOriginUV) into the vertex (sub_002A69B0). *How:* The vertex-shader multiply itself is inferred from its constants (the VS microcode was not decoded); the baked single-map path and the whole-map base UV were read. Retail range: Mult 32.145, Mult1 32.128, micro 96.1280; the 8192 m maps all use Mult 32.
- **TerrainCellSize is cells per mesh block side; WorldScale is metres per cell** `002A69B0`, `002A6D40` [code-confirmed] Each terrain render block has (CellSize+1)^2 vertices (CellSize 16 in all 60 worlds). TerrainWorldScale (8 in 59 worlds, 2 in 3DLobby) is world units per height-field cell, so vertex x = col*scale, z = row*scale, and a block is 128 units across. Height fields are 129, 257 or 1025 samples square.
- **Terrain colour map and detail textures combine in an NV2A register-combiner shader** `002A7AB0`, `0006FFB0`, `0006FD90` [verified-in-game] sub_002A7AB0 picks the material: DETAIL_BLENDED with two detail maps, DETAIL with one, BASE with none, SOLID as fallback. In DETAIL_BLENDED, T0 = colour map, T1 = TerrainDetailMap, T2 = 'TerrainDetailMap 1', V0 = vertex colour (presumably the lighting), and pixel-shader constant c0 = DetailBlend. mix = lerp(T2, T1, T0.a), so colour-map alpha 1 shows detail 1 and 0 shows detail 2. TerrainDetailModulate 0 (shader 0x4A4760): out = 2*V0*lerp(T0, mix, DetailBlend). TerrainDetailModulate 1 (shader 0x4A4940): out = 2*V0*(2*T0*saturate(2*mix*DetailBlend)). DetailBlend is not TFACTOR and does not fade with distance. With fog on (flag [0x50C7A0]) the fog variants 0x4A4670/0x4A4850 add a fog ramp on T3. *How:* The x2 output shift (bit 16) and the final-combiner passthrough were not checked against an XDK header. The single-detail DETAIL shader was not decoded.
- **Terrain micro detail is a second multiply-2x pass that fades to neutral grey** `000620A0` [inferred] Micro detail is drawn only when both TerrainMicroDetailMap0 and 1 exist. sub_000620A0 sets it up as an extra pass over the base pass with blend DESTCOLOR*src + SRCCOLOR*dst, i.e. out = 2*src*dst, where grey 0.5 is neutral. Its shader (0x4A3D90) averages the two micro maps 50/50, m = 0.5*T0 + 0.5*T1, then src = lerp(m, 0.5, T2). T2 was read as a distance fade, but traces show no fade: the pass is drawn only on blocks within about 128 m (terrain-near-block-passes) (a VS constant 0.02 is set at 0x621A1). DetailBlend does not apply to micro detail, and there is no mask. *How:* The distance-fade reading of T2 is inferred. The KillingField trace shows out = dst*lerp(M0, 2*M0*M1, 0.5)*2, which disagrees with this static decode; use the traced form (kf-paving-is-terrain-micro). The UV x5 there fits Tiling/WorldScale-style repeats, not checked.
- **material_water parameters: offsets, ranges and retail values** `0004EC40`, `0004B930`, `000541B0`, `000547F0` [code-confirmed] The water material is parsed by sub_0004EC40 (model XML) and sub_0004B930 (.mat). It holds wavetexture (+0x68, plus sampler state), an optional reflectiontexture (+0x80, a sky env map), wave_factor (+0x98, 0.64.1.0), distort_factor (+0x9C, 0.5.0.85), fresnel_max (+0xA0) and fresnel_min (+0xA4) (0.1.1.0), and deep_color (+0xA8) and shallow_color (+0xB8) as 0.255 ints scaled by 1/255 and stored in reverse order. There is no scroll-speed or animation-rate parameter. Retail: Env_Water1000x1000(_CityNight) wave 0.85, distort 0.85, fresnel min/max 0.77/1.0, deep 100,122,101, shallow 137,137,97; swamp 0.64, 0.5, 0.2/0.6; Hesperus oil 1.0, 0.7, 0.1/0.1. All use Water_006_NewWater.tif; only CityNight has a reflection map. The draw (sub_000547F0) picks one of 6 routines by the mode byte [0x50C720] and pushes NV2A vertex programs; the renderer object (sub_000541B0) creates the lookup textures Z2WLookup0 (256x64) and PrecisionLookup (1024x1). *How:* Parsing, offsets and retail values are code-confirmed; the draw-time formula is verified by frame trace in t15. — generated recomp_0008.c (made at install time, not in the repository):0
- **Custom Scenarios hold [0x50CA4A]=1 so custom missions skip SPIntro** `0050CA4A`, `002439B7` [verified-in-game] Custom Scenarios mode zeroes profile+0x90 (campaign index), so every custom mission passed the SPIntro test in sub_002439B7 and played the intro. ma2_scenario.c now holds [0x50CA4A]=1 while custom mode is on and restores it on leaving. Verified in test42: Custom Scenarios to mission in 1.3 s with no SPIntro; the real Campaign still plays Movie\60\English\SPIntro.bik.
- **Editor hidden start activated its window and stole keyboard focus** [verified-in-game] The game's hidden mode (RECOMP_FB_HIDDEN) never changes the foreground (0 events in 3 runs). The fix belongs in the editor (add SWP_NOACTIVATE); open until the editor owner ships it. *How:* Log foreground changes with editor/tools/fglog.py while launching.
- **'To the Rescue' is Mission_05** [documented] campaign0.ini section LEVEL100 has file = missions\Mission_05.wdf, titleid 524787 and descriptionid 524788. In text.mgf (interface/Text/English/Mission.mgText) 524787 is 'To the Rescue'. The world is Missions/Mission_05.wdf in common.mgf, with 1,354 objects.
- **Campaign reinforcements are mostly dormant unit sets switched on by a trigger** [verified-in-game] Mission_05 ('To the Rescue') keeps its reinforcement units placed in the level from the start, with IsActive 1 and m_bAIEnabled 0, grouped in a MoeEntitySet. At start-up, MATriggerTimer 74702 'TT - StartUp' (TrgTimerDuration 0) hides each set with MAActionShow Enable 0, EnableTree 1, AISet <set>. Later a trigger shows and wakes them with child actions: MAActionShow Enable 1 + EnableTree 1, MAActionAI EnableAI 1 and usually MAActionNation (5 hostile, 6 friendly), all on the same AISet. Example: MATriggerCuboidalVolume 125707 'TB - 2nd Wave Catch' (VolumeWidth 250, PlayerEntitesOnly 1, TypeOfCheck 3, TriggerAutoReset 0) fires 157381 Show, 125822 AI, 125821 Nation 5 on set 125717 (MATank 125696/125698 Partisan, template 116804; MAMech 141346 Cougar, template 27265). Across the 22 campaign missions: 187 EnableAI-1 and 78 Show-1 actions on units, 49 start-up hides; 521 of 1,008 units start with AI off. *How:* Editor 'Spawn units' recipe: put the units in a new MoeEntitySet with m_bAIEnabled 0. Hide the set at start-up (Show Enable 0 under a 0-second timer; REQUIRED, verified in game: see dormant-units-need-startup-hide).
- **Triggered MASpawner reinforcements: NULL corporeal > spawner > unit** [documented] The second pattern is a MACorporeal on template 32093 'NULL' (IsActive 1) holding a MASpawner with Enabled 0 and TriggerEnableID = the trigger UID, holding the unit (Nation 5, AttackPilot 1, m_bAIEnabled 1). In Mission_05, MATriggerRadius 126257 'TR - Return from 3' (EncounterRadius 500) enables spawners 141817 (Cougar), 126237 and 126240 (Partisan tanks), each MaxSpawners 1, MaxActiveSpawners 1, SpawnRate 0, SpawnDelay 0. Spawner 157338 repeats cargo copters (MaxSpawners 10, MaxActiveSpawners 2, SpawnRate 15), enabled by volume 125991. Across 22 missions there are 167 spawners; 157 are Enabled 0 with a TriggerEnableID, triggered most by MATriggerRadius (45), MATrigger (34) and MATriggerCuboidalVolume (22). *How:* Use for 'N units over time'; for a one-off wave, the dormant-set pattern is the common one.
- **Dropship and swap-set actions are rare and cinematic in the campaign** [documented] MAActionDropShip appears 3 times (missions 04, 05, 07). In Mission_05 the Icarus dropship MAFlyer 131758 (IsDropShip 1) is woken by MAActionAI and lands 6 s later (125626 Land 1) as staging; it delivers no units. MAActionAddCargo is never used. MAActionSwapSetIn is used 4 times, only in 06b and 11a (5 MASwapSet objects).
- **Editor palette: 801 placeable templates, 279 have no model on any disc** [verified-in-game] From the editor's --dump-palette over GlobalEntities, 801 templates are placeable. 279 have no model in any disc archive (cut content). The rest the editor groups as 'Foliage & Natural' (112) and 'City & Man-made' (390) by category path and name keywords. These groups are editor-made, not engine data.
- **Template-name prefixes and faction codes** [inferred] Inferred from category paths and names: BldCom = civilian/commercial building, BldMil = military, BldInd = industrial; VMil / Vciv = military / civilian vehicle; Pep_Civ = civilian person; Bb_/Bd_ = 'Building Base Textures' ground plates (NNxNN = size); LP = low-poly; MP = multiplayer variant; WOB = Word of Blake; DAN/HES/NOR/THE/TER = Dante/Hesperus/Northwind/Thestria/Terra.
- **Template-name suffixes: _CS/_WS/_DS are destroyed states; others unclear** [inferred] _CS: a MABuilding in a 'Collapsed States' category that is the CorporalDestroyed target of the base template (e.g. BldMil_Icarus_LaunchPad_CS 125902 for 124311); read as 'collapsed state' (role data-confirmed). _WS: also destroyed husks (BldCom_Office07_WS 124224, BldMil_HES_MechFactory_WS 125374; models named *_WS_CS); a WS Talon dropship is a live crashed building in Mission_02, so perhaps 'wreck state' (inferred). _DS: wreck of scenery, vehicles, turrets and civilians (221 MACorporealDestroyed templates; Env_TunnelC_DS 124437 is a building). 'No CS': BldInd_CityGenerator - No CS (36767) has no destroyed variant while 36632 has one, though Vmil_Dropship_Talon (No Adv CS) has one. _BV: collidable, indestructible copies (Env_PedBridgeB_BV 32467 vs a destructible base; Env_TER_BossBV 126168, 17 uses), perhaps a blocking volume (inferred). Canal_Wall _QTR/_HLF probably quarter/half lengths; _CP and _ST unknown. _Vert (BldMil_ResearchCenter_Vert, Canyon_Home_Vert) are unused variants; meaning unknown. *How:* Safe for the editor: show _CS/_WS/_DS as 'destroyed' variants; keep the others under their official names.
- **Far objects: frustum + far plane + model LOD, all automatic; no per-object cull data** `0008C5B0`, `0008C870`, `000836D0`, `00257740` [code-confirmed] The scene renderer (sub_0008C5B0/sub_0008C870) frustum-culls every node: vfunc +0x4C (sub_000836D0) tests the node's bounding sphere against 6 planes (sub_00257740). The far plane (camera+0x80, sub_00044BE0) comes from the camera template's CameraFarPlane (default 475, retail 150.4000), scaled by the PC DrawDistance setting. NodeSwitchLod (sub_000848E0) hides a model beyond radius^2*1.21 of its own .NODE LOD data and fades between LODs. There is no per-class or per-object cull radius, no sectors or portals and no occlusion; bounds come from the model and the placed transform at run time. Fog (FogStart/FogEnd) only colours. So a custom scenario gets the same treatment as retail with no editor-set property: a city in the far corner is not drawn until it is inside the far plane and its models' LOD range. *How:* Per level, the editor can tune FogStart/FogEnd and the camera far plane; set ForceUseLowDetail where only _low models ship.
- **SDS sphere tree is built at run time from node positions and radii** `0008ED20` [inferred] Strings show an 'SDS' binary sphere tree (NodeAdd id,(x,y,z),radius; GetVisibleNodes; GetNearbyNodesSphere; GetNearbyNodesRay) created by the scene manager in sub_0008ED20. Membership is computed at run time, nothing is baked at export. Which queries the renderer uses versus collision is not traced.
- **Campaign AI freezes when no player is within its range** `00183345`, `0016A806`, `0016AE44` [code-confirmed] Every 1.0.1.4 s think cycle (sub_00183345 > sub_0016A806 > sub_0016AE44) an AI unit may run only if some player is within max(actor config range at [actor.vt+0x200]+0x1D0, player body radius). Otherwise comp+0x144 |= 0x60 zeroes its velocity and skips its step. Bypasses: flag [sub_18F10]+0x69 and bit 8 of [actor+0x80]. Far units in a custom scenario therefore sleep automatically; no per-object property is needed.
- **Dormant reinforcements must be hidden at start-up, or they stand visible** [verified-in-game] In game (PC Release 5508c574, a mission_05-based scenario), units saved with m_bAIEnabled 0 but no start-up hide stand visible from the start (two Cougars 90 m ahead, AI asleep). With a start-up MATriggerTimer (duration 0) running MAActionShow Enable 0, EnableTree 1, nothing is visible and no radar dots show. Per-unit actions with ActionEntity work in place of a MoeEntitySet with AISet. Wake-up verified on a map whose only enemies were the two reinforcement Cougars: when a MATriggerRadius fired per-unit MAActionShow Enable 1, MAActionAI EnableAI 1 and MAActionNation 5, two enemy radar dots appeared at once and the units attacked the player with lasers and autocannon. *How:* Editor 'Spawn units': always emit the start-up hide; per-unit ActionEntity or one set with AISet both work.
- **MAPointLight LightMap=1 adds a disc to the 512x512 ground light map** [verified-in-game] The per-frame 512x512 ground light map covers a camera-placed window at about 4 m per pixel. Each MAPointLight with LightMap=1 adds one disc of diameter 2*LightMapRadius in LightMapColor.rgb at alpha 0x60, blended SRC_ALPHA,ONE. Measured: 49.2 px for R=100 and 98.4 px for R=200; draw colour 60436363 for LightMapColor FF436363. Correction: the map is a camera-placed window about 2 km square, not the whole terrain (ground-lightmap-is-camera-window).
- **Water without a reflectiontexture reflects MAEnvironment EnvironmentMapName** [verified-in-game] When the water model's material has no reflectiontexture, the water reflection pass uses the level's MAEnvironment EnvironmentMapName cube. Models use the same cube. The old .mat 'type = WATER' form (waves=, fresnel_min/max, deep/shallow) feeds the same 5-pass water renderer.
- **Swamp moss is a separate alpha-blended DETAIL-material corporeal** [verified-in-game] The moss on swamp water (Bogged Down) is a separate MACorporeal whose model has a DETAIL material with blending=alpha: rgb = lerp(base, detail, 0.5)*2*light, alpha = base.a*detail.a. It is not part of the water material.
- **Editor: water wave texture decodes as a 32^3 volume and the env map as 6 cube faces** [documented] The editor's models library already decodes Water_006_NewWater.tif as a 32x32x32 volume and EnvMap_Sky_CityNight_sm.tif as 6 frames. Uploading them as Texture3D and TextureCube works with no decoder change; the 3D Morton unswizzle is already in texture.cpp. Visual check only.
- **Editor: road markings come from the COMPLEX .mat colorshift colours plus the mask** [documented] Legacy INI road .mat files (type COMPLEX) carry colorshift0_color and colorshift1_color. Adding mask.G*colorshift0 + mask.B*colorshift1 after lighting gives the blue dashed centre line and yellow kerb dots in the editor, and a mirror sampler fixes the jumbled texture. Visual check only.
- **node_light inner/outer angles are probably half-angles** [code-confirmed] Reading light_inner_angle/light_outer_angle as half-angles gives Env_Highway_Light a 12.5 m pool at 15 m height, which matches its lightmap min_radius 12. Supports the half-angle reading; not traced. UPGRADE 2026-10-24: now code-confirmed (see spot-cone-half-angles-confirmed).
- **Open render unknowns from editor pass 8** [inferred, open-question] Open: (a) cube-map face order (editor assumes D3D +X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z) (the wave volume's channel order is now answered: blue = up, see water-normal-volume-channels); (b) the water thickness LUT scale (editor uses vertical depth / 4 m); (c) the 64x64 ground falloff texture 80679000's curve (editor uses smoothstep); (d) the spot-light direction axis in node space (editor assumes -Y) and what lightmap min_color/max_color do. Answered: lightmap channels (terrain-lightmap-channels). The 512 px ground map is a camera-placed window (ground-lightmap-is-camera-window), and MAPointLight's ground disc uses LightMapRadius, not LightRadius (see pointlight-ground-splat). Not cheaply traceable now: RECOMP_TEX_DUMP stops after 64 first-use textures in this build. Update: cube face order answered (cube-face-order), falloff curve answered (radial-falloff-lut), lightmap min/max fields laid out (node-light-lightmap-fields). Still open: spot axis in node space, min/max_color reader.
- **Mech damage/heat/shield overlays are hidden meshes shown only in that state** [verified-in-game] 'Mech models carry additive, self-lit overlay meshes that the game hides at rest: cracks_* (atl_cracks, mad_cracks, mech_crack_glow) appear when damaged, heat_lleg/heat_rleg/heat_back (mech_heatsink) when overheated, and shield* (target_jamming material_distort, Wpn_Shields_Anim) when shielded. A viewer should hide them by default. Editor pass 8 confirmed from model data: in a plain renderer these show as white blocks on Atlas, Ymir, Catapult, Loki and MadCat; mech_heatsink is additive with selfillum 255 and an .mtb heat tint.
- **material_env glass: 2*V0*base + base.a*cube.a*tint at constant-alpha opacity** [verified-in-game] mech_glass (material_env) has diffuse 0, opacity 0.5.0.75, reflectivity 0.5 and alpha blending. Combiner: out = 2*V0*base + base.a*cube.a*tint, blended at the material opacity through CONSTANT_ALPHA.
- **COMPLEX material: glow mask, tint variant, detail gated by 1-mask.a, constant-alpha translucency** [verified-in-game] COMPLEX materials add glow mask.g*colorshift0 + mask.b*colorshift1 after lighting. A tint variant instead multiplies the light by colorshift1 under mask.b (selected by colorshift1_diffuse=true, see complex-colorshift1-diffuse). An optional detail layer is gated by (1-mask.a), and translucency is the opacity through CONSTANT_ALPHA blending. Correction: the glow is not added after lighting; out = 2*(light*lit + mask.g*C0 + mask.b*C1), see complex-glow-doubled.
- **material_specular_mask: 2*V0*base + mask.r*cube.a*spec_color** [verified-in-game] material_specular_mask draws out = 2*V0*base + mask.r*cube.a*spec_color: the mask's red channel gates an environment-cube specular in spec_color.
- **Coplanar DETAIL decals draw with depth EQUAL** [verified-in-game, superseded] Coplanar DETAIL decals (KillingField paving) are drawn with depth test EQUAL over the surface below: out = lerp(base, 2*base*detail, 0.5)*2*light. CORRECTED by editor pass 8: the KillingField depth-EQUAL 'paving' draw is the terrain micro-detail pass (see kf-paving-is-terrain-micro), not a decal object.
- **Levels without a ground light map light terrain and water by vertex colour** [verified-in-game] On levels with no ground light map (NewRiverCity), terrain and water lighting is the vertex colour V0, and the terrain also adds V1. New River City's MadCat uses model_low/madcat.mgmodel with the materials above.
- **Env_Highway_Light's bulb, cone and spot light sit under an .mtb-hidden 'lightbulb' node** [documented] In Env_Highway_Light the lightbulb mesh (material_color_shift), the additive cone mesh and the spot node_light all sit under the node 'lightbulb', which the lamp's .mtb hides with MAModSubObjectShow (turned_on true). The game shows them lit at night. The editor draws .mtb-hidden subtrees that hold a node_light when Scene lights is on. Open: what drives the rule (night flag or a lights-on event). A candidate is MAActionLights (LightSet, LightAction 2 = on, 3 = off; 14 uses), not checked. NOTE 2026-10-24: any claim that bulbs are lit at night is unverified; see lamp-bulb-no-runtime-switch. UPDATE 2026-10-24: resolved in favour of hidden-by-default (highway-lamp-mtb-hides-bulb).
- **Lamp ground-pool radius lerp is unclamped, with height measured from the terrain** [inferred] Mission_02 street lamps stand about 26 m above the TERRAIN (the streets are plates about 16 m up). The unclamped lerp min_radius + (max-min)*h/max_height = 12 + 8*26/15 = 26 m matches the traced 13.2 px quad. So the node_light lightmap radius lerp is unclamped, and the height is measured from the terrain, not the street plate.

- **Static lightmap (MAEnvironment LightMapName) is A8L8: L x ambient = L.rgb, A = shadow mask = L.a** `00052F90`, `00124CC1`, `00123746`, `002A69B0` [verified-in-game] The terrain lightmap is not a MATerrain property. It is MAEnvironment LightMapName (key A6B3EE2E, a \Terrain\*.tif; blank in 20 worlds, which then use vertex lighting). Mission_02's is 128x128 swizzled A8L8. Each frame the LightMap Manager (sub_00052F90) draws it into the 512x512 ground map: L.rgb = lightmap.L x LightAmbientColor (C0 = FF1B213B in Mission_02) and L.a = lightmap.A; light splats then add rgb only (colour mask 00010101), so L.a stays the lightmap alpha. Terrain (trace line 1321, T3 = the map) lights with light = V1.rgb*V1.a*L.a + L.rgb and outputs 2*light*albedo. So A is a shadow mask (0 = shadowed) gating V1, and L is a baked ambient/sky term. The asset audit confirmed this with the files: Terrain/*_lightmap.tif is A8L8 (MGIc flags 0x17) and terrain light = sun*max(N.L,0)*A + ambient*L (+ lamp pools); near blocks redo the lighting per pixel (terrain-near-block-passes). The map's extent is built from the camera frustum clamped to the level limits in sub_00052F90, so it may be a moving window rather than the whole terrain. *How:* Editor: light = sun*N.L*lightmap.A + lightmap.L*ambient + lamp splats; albedo per terrain-detail-combine.

T0 and T1 are the SAME texture 809CA000 at the same tc (59.255,171.977), sampled value M = (0.7112,0.6832,0.604). T2 (mode 4) supplies a per-vertex fade value: 0.33473 at the pixel (vertices 0.196/0.437/0.288). The combiner output (rc_eval) (0.7355,0.7043,0.6159) fits src = M + t*(M-0.5) = lerp(M0, M0+M1-0.5, t), with t ~0.112 (possibly fade^2), to 4 digits on all three channels. The blend is 2*src*dst; the observed src (0.67,0.64,0.60) from dst (44,40,25) -> (59,51,30) is ~9% below rc_eval, unexplained (fog 80808080 with factor 1.68 is the suspect). The editor uses lerp(m0, 2*m0*m1, 0.5) (taken from KF), i.e. a product instead of ADD_SIGNED and a constant 0.5 instead of the distance fade: at M = 0.71 the editor gives 0.86 vs the game's 0.7355. This micro pass is the source of the UC 1.78x over-brightness at this texel. Confidence: formula medium-high; the fade t -> distance mapping low (needs more micro-draw pixels). 12-pixel table (audit #3, stageprobe4m): the micro draw has T0 = T1 = the same 256x256 DXT1 texture, T2 mode 4 = an interpolated per-vertex fade attribute, and stage 1 and 2 C0 = 0.502. rc_eval = M + t*(M-0.5) holds on all 12 pixels, with the same t in R, G and B. Observed t ~ 0.70 - 1.70*T2: t goes from +0.63 near to -0.31 at T2 0.587 far, so the detail contrast inverts with distance. That is consistent with pass 15's single point (0.70 - 1.70*0.335 = 0.13 vs t 0.112) and rules out t = T2^2. T2 grows with view depth: pos.w 4.2 -> 0.0099, 9.5 -> 0.057, 15.5 -> 0.098, 20.8 -> 0.196, 32 -> 0.437, 44 -> 0.775. The micro draw is the last writer on all 12 terrain pixels. This is an observation; the final fit is pass 15's. Pass 15 fit (medium confidence): src = lerp(M0, M0+M1-0.5, t) = 0.5 + (M-0.5)*(1+t) (T0 = T1, the same texture). t = 0.706 - 1.73*T2 (rms ~0.015 over the 6 pixels with |M-0.5| > 0.15). T2 (the per-vertex tex2 fade) ~ (0.0497 + 0.0189*viewdepth)^2 (vertex values: depth 4.2 -> 0.0099, 9.5 -> 0.057, 20.8 -> 0.196, 32.1 -> 0.437, 43.9 -> 0.775). So the contrast gain 1+t ~ 1.706 - 1.73*T2 (~1.7*(1-T2)): near terrain gets ~1.6-1.8x detail contrast, and beyond ~37 m the gain is below 1. - **UC ground map content = the retail A8L8 light map; the shade gap is a PC-port swizzle bug, not the sun term** [verified-in-game] Audit #3 (2026-10-22), UnderCover: the game's 512x512 ground-map texture (T3) is the retail baked A8L8 light map (128x256 texels covering 1024x2048 m), written at 1 texel per window pixel with wrap. It is tinted by C0 = LightAmbientColor (FF313326), plus 11 tiny additive blobs (lamp pools; their alpha is not written). The editor's light map equals the retail one (same stats), so the map is not the cause of the UC shade gap. The gap: game shaded ground 2-16 vs editor 30-50, while lit patches match at 0.95-1.25x. Leading explanation (inferred): the game's sun term V1.rgb*V1.a (vertex specular output, not captured in the trace) is ~0 in shade, while the editor uses per-pixel N.L*lm.a there. Open: the actual V1 value in shaded areas; it needs d1 (the specular vertex colour) added to the frame trace. SUPERSEDED (audit #3, stageprobe6): V1 at the dark UC pixel is (0.482,0.443,0.349,0.703), the same as at a lit texel, so the sun term is NOT ~0. The real cause is the runtime ground-map swizzle bug (see rt-swizzle-ground-map-bug): the game samples the 512x512 fmt-06 (swizzled) ground map from a render target that the PC runtime wrote LINEAR, so every fetch is Morton-scrambled. The combiner with the scrambled T3 reproduces the traced pixel (24,22,15) exactly; a correct linear readback would give ~50. The editor's smooth retail light map is the intended look. *How:* Editor: no change; keep the smooth retail light map. Do NOT chase the darker shaded ground seen in the PC port; it is the runtime bug.
- **Model vertex light V0 = matDiffuse x (ambient + max(N.L,0) x sun), with per-vertex normals normalised in the shader (M15 facade and vents explained)** [verified-in-game] SOLVED v103. The lit model programs (hashes 037fde9c, 4bb785f4) compute, per vertex: Nw = normalize(n.x*c4 + n.y*c5 + n.z*c6) (n = vertex input v1; the world matrix rows are c4-c6; dp3 + rsq normalise in the shader); V0.rgb = c15.rgb * (c12.rgb + max(dot(Nw, -c13), 0) * c14.rgb); V0.a = c15.a. Constants are NV2A c[i] (D3D c(i-96)). c12 = LightAmbientColor (0.106,0.078,0.086); c13 = MAEnvironment DirectionalLightDirection (-0.317,-0.560,0.766), so the light vector is -dir; c14 = DirectionalLightColor (0.392,0.318,0.235). c12/c13/c14 are IDENTICAL in every draw of the frame. Only c15 changes: it is the per-material diffuse colour + alpha (e.g. 1,1,1; 0.647,0.608,0.529; 0.702 grey; facade 0.263,0.267,0.275). There is NO per-instance sun scalar, shadow, occlusion or vertex colour. FACADE: draw 4792724 has c15 = (0.263,0.267,0.275), so V0 = 0.26 x ambient where N.L <= 0. A lit vertex reproduces exactly: n (0,-0.149,0.988) -> Nw (0.608,-0.149,-0.778), N.L 0.706 -> d0 0.1006 (game 0.100618). VENTS (16 Env_WallVent instances, grill 140-vert and sideduct 60-vert parts, matched to draws by world position): c15 = white; per vertex, k = (V0.r - amb.r)/sun.r equals max(Nw.L,0) with max error 0.0000 on every vertex of all 32 draws. Per-instance mean k is 0.19-0.30 for both parts, with every instance lit somewhere. The k=0.74 vs k=0 contrast was a per-PIXEL/per-vertex sample of differently-facing smoothed normals, not a per-instance factor. NOTE: the stored mesh normals are NOT unit length (vent normals have length 0.121); the shader renormalises them. An editor that uses the raw normals, or face normals, will get the sun term wrong. Earlier hypotheses (light-map alpha, point lights, ShadowDiffuseFactor, occlusion ray) are all moot. *How:* Editor rule: per vertex, V0 = matDiffuse.rgb * (LightAmbientColor + max(dot(normalize(R * n_vertex), -DirectionalLightDirection), 0) * DirectionalLightColor), alpha = matDiffuse.a. R = the instance rotation (heading + the editor's existing z-flip convention, which matches the game's c4-c6). n_vertex = the mesh's own per-vertex normal, NORMALISED (raw lengths are ~0.12), interpolated across the triangle. matDiffuse = the material's diffuse colour (c15): facade 0.263,0.267,0.275; many materials are white. The game's world matrix (model VS c4.c6 = columns, c7 = position) equals Ry(h)*Rx(p)*Rz(r) with column vectors and standard right-handed matrices: Ry(h) maps local +Z to (sin h,0,cos h); Rx(p) maps +Z to (0,-sin p,cos p), so positive pitch tips the +Z end DOWN; Rz(r) maps +X to (cos r,sin r,0), so positive roll tips the +X end UP. Heading is used unwrapped (770, 1542 occur). Verified against existing stageprobe traces: IYF Env_CityTree_02 (854.74,36,1274.66) h810 r15 -> X column (0,0.259,-0.966); KF Env_Hesperus_Rock (565.63,63,1495.89) p25 -> Z column (0,-0.423,0.906); order fit over 5 objects with pitch and roll both non-zero (UnderCover x3, KillingField h15 p150 r75, Mission_15 h770 p180 r-90): YXZ max error < 0.001, every other order >= 0.77. Model geometry plus a same-pose game frame show the beam follows the NODE's local -Y (node-light-spot-beam-direction-is-the-light-nodes-local-minus-y-not-plus-z-geometry-and-game-frame, runtime-observed HIGH). Both hold if the engine applies a basis change from node to light matrix. For editor authoring use node -Y. Editor caveat: it turns light directions by heading only (no pitch/roll; M01b searchlights are pitched 60). *How:* Open: in-game check of which side the pool falls on.

- **Trace 'textures %05X' word = NV097 SHADER_STAGE_PROGRAM, 5 bits per stage** [inferred] The textures word in nv2a_gpu_d3d11.c (key.words[2]) is the NV097 SHADER_STAGE_PROGRAM register (method 0x1E70), 5 bits per stage. 00C01 = stage0 2D(1), stage1 off(0), stage2 CUBE(3); 00C21 = same with stage1 2D(1). So bit 0x20 is NOT a specular gate: it is whether stage 1 (detail/mask texture) is on; the cube sits in stage 2 in both. Static program sets are D3DPIXELSHADERDEF (0xF0 bytes, PSTextureModes at +0xD8): family 0x4A5480 has texmodes 0x401 (no detail) / 0x421 (detail); 0x4A5C00 family (via inst+0x4C when [inst+0x20]&7==4) has 0x8001/0x8021; 0x4A5840 family in inst+0x50 unused-as-found. Tables hold no cube mode; the draw-time D3D code (function 0x40FBD0, writes method 0x41E70 at 0x40FF3E) remaps each stage mode by bound texture: test dl,4 at 0x40FDEC turns modes 1.3 into 3 (CUBE) when the texture format word has bit 2; else 2 (3D) for flag 0x40000000 or (fmt&0xF0)==0x30, else 1 (2D). jns tests at 0x40FE45/0x40FEBD zero a stage mode unless 4,5,0xA,0x11 (per-stage no-texture gate, field unconfirmed). Shadow PSTextureModes at device+0x790 (0x40C16C, set at 0x40C0A0). Lamp vs mech difference is per material/per draw: non-empty mat+0x98 detail_blend string (0x421 family) or a texture actually bound at stage 1; not object class, dynamic light or vertex format. The material parser 0x4CFE0 reads cubetexture into material+0x74 (0x4D228-0x4D26C) but sub_00073340 / setup 0x736B0 never bind it. Unknown: who binds the stage-2 cube (global or per draw); why the mech has a stage-1 binding with only a basetexture (parser 0x4D172-0x4D18D appears to fail on an empty detail_blend list). *How:* Do not gate the specular stage on word bit 0x20 as a material property; treat the cube as always present in stage 2 for these programs and stage 1 as the mask/detail. — nv2a_gpu_d3d11.c:

- **Engine render-state ids are XDK D3DRS indices; fog is TABLE LINEAR** [inferred] Flush sub_0003BC10 (only caller driver 0x3B2F0 at 0x3B313) pops the 0x870 dirty list (node=id+1; 12-byte records +0 requested, +4 last flushed, +8 pending) and dispatches by id: id < 0x5C -> descriptor table 0x45B0E0 into thunk 0x40CF80; 0x5C.0x87 -> OR mask from 0x45AEC0 into dirty word 0x41BC70 and cache value at 0x41BC78+id*4; id >= 0x88 -> stdcall handler from table 0x4181A0. 0x40xxxx-0x41xxxx is the statically linked XDK D3D library; the layout is the XDK render-state layout (simple states first, deferred states starting at D3DRS_FOGENABLE cached in D3D__RenderState with dirty bits, complex states with handlers), so ids are Xbox XDK D3DRS indices: 0x5C FOGENABLE, 0x5D FOGTABLEMODE (=3 LINEAR), 0x5E FOGSTART, 0x5F FOGEND, 0x8A FOGCOLOR: TABLE fog, LINEAR (strong inference). Consumer 0x410150 reads the four fog values (dirty bit 0x2000 shared by 0x5C-0x5F): enable 0 exits; mode 0 -> start=end=1.0 and 0x2601; mode 3 -> linear path (reciprocal of end-start); also ids 0x60/0x61. 0x8A handler 0x40C600 writes NV2A push-buffer method 0x2A8 (count 1) with the colour's bytes 0/2 swapped (ARGB->ABGR), raw value to 0x41BEA0. Closes the id->D3DRS map open in fog-only-linear. UPDATE 2026-10-24: keys 0x5C-0x5F are not D3D8 RS numbers (fog-helpers-emit-nv2a).

- **Water thickness pass is an NV2A register-combiner program** [verified-in-game] First per-plane water pass (lines 6700-6709): NV2A register-combiner, not an SM pixel shader: 4 stages, ctl 0x00011104, prog 0x005E1, final 0x0000000C/0x00001C80, colour mask 0x01000000 (alpha only), z func 203 (LESS) mask on, blend off. T0 = 640x480 fmt 0x12 surface 0x80488000 (dependent-AR source into T1); T1 = 256x64 LUT 0x81271000 fmt 0x1A; T2 = 1024x1 LUT 0x81279000 fmt 0x1A. Stage 2 const C0 = 0x08FFFFFF. Decoded (rcdec): alpha = 8*(T1.b-T2.b) + V0.a^2 + (T1.a-T2.a)*C0.a, agreeing with the t15 thickness formula (resolves the thickness conflict in favour of t15; confirms water-z2w-meaning). Diffuse V0.a = 5.27 in the trace (unclamped as logged). Stage 3 shows non-zero ICW/OCW (D4D420DC/0C00): probably a pass-through. PC translation kit/source/game/src/kernel/nv2a_gpu_d3d11.c pixel_program (~391-428) specialises shaders keyed on use_rc, rc control, stage program, final combiners and per-stage ICW/OCW; RECOMP_PIXEL_SPECIALIZE=0 falls back to the generic PS (code-confirmed). Open: which code writes the combiners (SetPixelShader token vs raw NV097) and its caller; whether WATER material routine 0x4EC40 issues it; which LUT is Z2W and which PrecisionLookup. *How:* Editor: use the t15 form 8*(T1.b-T2.b)+V0.a^2+(T1.a-T2.a)*C0.a.

- **Frame delta 0x4E2428 and the fps ring** [code-confirmed] 0x4E2428 (double) = SCALED FRAME DELTA in seconds: dt = timescale 0x4A14F0 (set 1.0 by sub_0001DD00 init) * e (elapsed given to the producer); game clock 0x4E2440 += dt; 0x4E2418 = e (recomp_0001.c:11360-11364). In producer sub_0001DD80 only, float 0x50BA70 overrides e when > 0 (fixed-step override?). fps ring: 0x50BA78 = ring head h (0.63) of 64 double timestamps at 0x4E2200 (stamp 0x4E2408 from indirect clock [0x4A1500]); 0x50BA7C (M) and 0x50BA80 (N) = producer-call counters zeroed by DD00. sub_0001DC30 fps = k/(T[j1]-T[j0]), j1=h-1, k=min(M-1,W), W=clamp(entry eax,4,63); returns 30.0 if N <= 4; no zero-span guard. Other globals: 0x4E2438 unscaled sum of e; 0x4E2424 = int(dt*1000); 0x4E2430 = int(clock*1000) cumulative ms (WIKI.md:604 step stamp is WRONG); 0x4E2420 frame count. So the camera-pan chase (c0 = 0x4E2428) is frame-rate independent. Open: which producer runs live (DD80/DDB4/DE70); the wiki's 0.2 s dt cap (WIKI.md:4556) is not in DD80/DDB4 (check DE70); writers of 0x50BA70/0x4A14F0 after init.

- **The vertex program draws constants c[b+0x61.0x63]** [verified-in-game] The vertex program draws constants c[b+0x61.0x63]. Model program: c18=(-E/(E-S), -P/(P-Q)), c19=(-1/(E-S), 1/(P-Q)), c20=(-1,0,V2,1), eye world position in c17; terrain program: c24/c25/c26, eye in c27. oFog(o5) = clamp01((1 - min((E-d)/(E-S),1)) + max(min(t,1),0) x min(d/(P-Q),1)), where d = |world_pos - eye| (3D radial distance, NOT eye depth), t = (P-y_world)/(P-Q), S/E = FogStart/FogEnd (DD-scaled), P/Q = FogTop/FogBottom. Fog colour = lerp(col, FogColor, oFog) (0.1 fixed range per fog mode 2). So the height term fades in over the first (P-Q) m from the eye and is zero above FogTop; the distance and height terms ADD. Validated by emulating the dumped NV2A program per vertex: 556 vertices below the band matched the dumped out[12] within 0.003 (Deliverance, FogTop 7.5, FogBottom 0.9, S/E 200/500 at DD50); pilot-start terrain (y 7.5-9) correctly gets 0. Editor implementation: render.cpp fog_amt (branch fidelity 43c1b7d). - **0x40C050 = CreatePixelShader-shaped helper; owner of loc_0006FAE7 = sub_0006F8C0, ctor of the detail-blended terrain material; [esi+0x44] selects PS def 0x4A4760 (0) or 0x4A4940 (nonzero)** [code-confirmed] sub_0040C050 (recomp_0101.c:208020, cdecl 2 params): allocs 0xFC bytes (tag 0x24800000, via 0x12260; OOM -> 0x8007000E), sets +0/+4 refcounts to 1, copies 0x3C dwords (240 B, a D3DPIXELSHADERDEF) from arg1 into obj+0xC and stores the object pointer into *arg2; callers include 0x41E70, 0x6F8C0, 0x6F9FC, 0x6FFB0; 11 callers total. So 0x4A4760 / 0x4A4940 (and fog variants 0x4A4670 / 0x4A4850) are XBE DATA pixel-shader definitions. loc_0006FAE7 lies in sub_0006F8C0 (610 B, recomp_0011.c:16625; sub_0006F9FC is a second copy of its tail), the constructor of the detail-blended material (vtables 0x461360 family, wiki 'material_detail_blended'): it builds three texture/sampler objects at this+0x34/+0x38/+0x3C from descriptor slots +0x68/+0x80/+0x98 (five sampler setters each), sets this+0x40 = descriptor+0xB0 value, this+0x44 byte = 0, this+0x4C = PS handle (written by 0x40C050 via arg2 = &this+0x4C), then this+0x14 = (this+0x14 & ~0x100) | 0xC0. Micro pass: separate draw, T0/T1 micro maps (+T2), dst' = 2*src*dst, only blocks within ~128 m. - **The game's glow is a bloom post-process: mask = framebuffer ALPHA written only by draws whose colour-mask includes alpha; chain 640x480 -> 320x240 -> 160x120 -> 4 blur passes -> max-blend into 320x240 -> added to the frame** [code-confirmed] Decoded from trace bdp4far_f1_trace_raw.txt lines 6178-7741 (rcdec.py). (1) Mask: material_color_shift writes colorshift0_bloom x base.a (rgb = 2x(V0xT + C0.rgb x T.a); bloom values 0.1.1.0 in retail, e.g. 0.25/0.5/0.73/1.0); COMPLEX writes colorshift0_bloom x multi.g + colorshift1_bloom x multi.b + specular_bloom x multi.r x cube.a; specular_mask writes specular_bloom x mask(base.a) x cube.a (specular_bloom 0.0.2 in Mission_02 materials). All other draws (colour-mask 00010101) leave alpha alone. (2) Chain: 640x480 frame -> 320x240 (4 taps = 4x4 box; rgb x alpha via blend SRC_ALPHA/ZERO) -> 160x120 (4x4 box) -> 4 blur passes V,H,V,H (taps at +-1.5 and +-0.5 texels, weights 0x3F, 0x3F?, 0x7F, 0x7F constants = 0.247/0.498; ~1.49 gain per pass, 8-bit clamp each pass) -> upsampled and max-blended (blend eq 0x8008 MAX) into the 320x240 target -> added to the 640x480 frame (blend CONSTANT_COLOR/CONSTANT_COLOR, eq ADD; blend colour not in the trace, assumed 1). - **Map > Environment and Time of day/weather: what each control writes to MAEnvironment/MASky2 and how the game uses it (sun, shadows, fog, sky picker, Look/Night, lit windows = IsNightTime, weather = PrecipEffectID/EnableRain, lightning = LightFlash, flash timing)** [code-confirmed] Source: editor kit/source/game/src/app/app_tabs.cpp, app_weather.cpp, core/weather.h (research 2026-10-23 citing recomp sub_00124CC1 reader, sub_00126060 update, sub_0012693E precip start, sub_001263F8 lightning). the source only; no run. Writes are HIGH (read from code); game-side effects MEDIUM-HIGH (cited in weather.h, match wiki menv-lightning-night / isnighttime-buildings-only). Fields are MAEnvironment unless noted. [Sun direction / Sun height] write DirectionalLightDirection = (sin yaw*cos elev, -sin elev, cos yaw*cos elev); marks the lightmap stale. [Update shadows / Update shadows for the new sun] re-bakes the scenario lightmap from the sun (editor bake; the game uses the stored lightmap as its ground light map). [Fog distance] FogStart, FogEnd (m). [Height fog band] FogBottom, FogTop (m); the game uses the band only when FogMode = 2 (editor warns when ground sits inside it). [Fog colour] FogColor (u32 ARGB, alpha byte kept). [Sky picker] copies Corporal3DObj (sky model), CorporalMTB, SkyTerrainSkyScale, SkyTerrainSkyOffset, position and heading from a retail world that uses that sky into MASky2; SkyFogTop/Bottom left alone (wiki skies-masky2). [Night checkbox + Look list] apply a whole LOOK copied from a retail world: sun, ambient, fog and shadow colours, fog distances, reflection map (EnvironmentMapName) and the MASky2 sky. The look also sets IsNightTime to the retail world's own value (look.lit): lit for Go Commando, Ill Wind, Bogged Down; not lit for New River City, Witch Cauldron, Cold dusk. The Night box itself does not write IsNightTime; the picked look does. [Lit building windows] IsNightTime (0/1). Game: only MABuilding reads it. It darkens nothing: Mission 06a is flagged 1 with a warm sun, Mission 12 is dark and flagged 0. [Weather: None/Rain/Snow/Dust] write PrecipEffectID and EnableRain (the game starts the precipitation object each frame when EnableRain is set; PrecipEffectID 0 = nothing). The disc has only two MAPrecipitation templates: 31780 Env_Snow_Blowing (Missions 10, 11a, 11b) and 31516 Env_DustStorm_Wst. RAIN is not a game template: saved as the snow template 31780, plus the scenario archive carries a rain streak particle (.mgparticle XML, about 70 KB) in place of the snow effect's particle. On load, a snow world whose archive carries that particle reads as rain again. On Missions 10/11 as the base level the game's own snow files may win, so rain can show as snow. Editor's in-memory rain id is 990001. Snow/Dust add the effect files to the scenario if the base level lacks them. [Lightning flashes] write LightFlash, SkyFlash and EnableLightning together. Game: LightFlash drives the flashes (bursts up to MaxFlashes, next burst FlashTimeMin.FlashTimeMax ms later) and ThunderCueID (0 in every retail world, so no thunder); EnableLightning is stored only (a trigger action sets it; nothing reads it). The flash is a light on mechs, vehicles and people, not a ground/sky change. [Flash timing 'every N to M s'] FlashTimeMin, FlashTimeMax stored in ms (UI seconds, 1.60). The game picks the next burst with a remainder by (max - min), so equal values crash it; the editor forces min < max (min 1-59, max min+1.60) and fixes it again on save (weather:to_game). Tags for the wiki section: Map > Environment; Map > Time of day and weather. NOTE: the game reads only LightFlash; SkyFlash and EnableLightning are never 1 in retail and are not tested (see lightning-gate-is-lightflash-only-.). *How:* Part of 'How the editor maps to the game' (see page t16_editor_to_game). Editor writes read from code (HIGH unless marked); game-side effects carry the cited facts' confidence. Open items are listed inside.
- **Terrain > Paint: textures 1/2 = TerrainDetailMap pair mixed by colour-map alpha (255 = T1, 0 = T2); pattern size = TerrainDetailMult; close-up = micro detail; 3+ textures = PC ground layers; tint = colour-map RGB; boundaries = terrain type map** [code-confirmed] Source: editor kit/source/game/src/app/app_paint.cpp (header comment + enable/disable_ground_layers, fill_ground, tint_ui, boundaries_ui). the source only; no run. What each control writes: HIGH (read from code). Game-side effect: MEDIUM-HIGH, cites existing wiki facts. [Ground textures: Texture 1 / Texture 2] MATerrain TerrainDetailMap and 'TerrainDetailMap 1' (paths stored as \Terrain\<name>.tif). The brush writes the COLOUR MAP ALPHA (TerrainBaseMap tif): alpha 255 = Texture 1, alpha 0 = Texture 2, in between mixes (fill_ground: layer 0 -> 255, layer 1 -> 0). Matches the game: lerp(T2,T1,T0.a). Works in every game version. [Pattern size] TerrainDetailMult, TerrainDetailMult1: how many times each texture repeats across the whole map (wiki terrain-detail-uv-repeats). [Close-up detail / Close-up size] TerrainMicroDetailMap0/1 + TerrainMicroDetailTiling0/1. Not painted: two fine textures averaged over everything within about 128 m; the game draws them only when BOTH maps are set (wiki terrain-microdetail-pass). [Add a texture (3rd and more, up to 8)] switches the scenario to the P4 GROUND LAYERS (PC build only; core/ground_layers.h): per-texture weights stored in the scenario, starting as the colour map alpha mix so nothing changes visibly; each layer has its own repeats (layers 0/1 take TerrainDetailMult/Mult1). The original Xbox game and older PC builds show only Texture 1 and 2 there. The p4 exe logs '[TERRAIN-LAYERS] N layers . t3 512x512'. [Remove texture / Back to 2 textures] bakes the pair's share of the weights back into the colour map alpha, so the map is a plain retail pair again. [Colour tint] the colour map RGB, which multiplies the textures. [Tint the whole map with this colour] sets every colour-map RGB, alpha kept. [Repaint ground colours from height] regenerates the colour-map RGB from height/slope (procedural colour map, theme colours), keeps the alpha (the texture mix). [Show it in its own colours] (texture brush option): also moves the colour map under the brush to neutral, because ground = texture x colour map. CAUTION: the editor comment on tint_ui says '4 x detail x colour'; the traced law is 8 x TerrainDetailBlend, so any 'neutral = 1/(4 x DetailBlend)' value in code is 2x the traced neutral unless the editor lighting carries the other factor. [Boundaries: Playable / Border / Out of bounds / Water] writes the GROUND-TYPE LAYER (the map's terrain-type grid, 'typemap'; storage record not checked, MEDIUM). Meaning from the editor help: spawn points, vehicle pads, flags and objectives must stand on Playable (or Water) ground; bots never walk onto Out of bounds ground; Border is a band round the arena; Special is water/waterway inside the arena. Overlay colours: clear playable, orange border, red out of bounds, blue water. [Make the whole map playable] sets every cell Playable. Tags for the wiki section: Terrain > Paint > Texture; Terrain > Paint > Colour tint; Terrain > Paint > Boundaries. WITHDRAWN: the '2x too bright on the lit path' caution is wrong. The editor's albedo carries 4 x DetailBlend and its ambient/sun are already x2, so editor total = the game's 8 x C0.a; neutral 1/(4 x DetailBlend) gives the texture's own colour in both. The law stays 8 x TerrainDetailBlend total gain including the light doubling. *How:* Part of 'How the editor maps to the game' (see page t16_editor_to_game). - **Map tab basics: Name/Author/Description, Kind, Built on (base retail level), Size, What the player starts , Game types, Check scenario (graphics memory ~58 MB crash limit), Sky and fog colour** [code-confirmed] Source: editor kit/source/game/src/app/app_tabs.cpp (tab_map, sky_picker). the source only; no run. Writes HIGH where the code names the field; storage places not checked are marked. [Name / Author / Description] scenario info the game shows in its map or mission list (stored with the scenario; exact record not checked, MEDIUM). [Kind] multiplayer map (played against bots) or mission (enemies use the campaign AI); decided when the map is created, shown read-only on the tab. [Built on] the retail level (archive) the map copies: its ground textures, lighting and buildings come from there; the scenario file refers to that base. Graphics memory counts the base theme's textures and models plus anything placed from other levels. [Size] read-only from the terrain (size_x x size_z in m; cell scale from TerrainWorldScale, 8 m per cell in retail). [What the player starts in] MARoot's player configuration container: on foot, Battle Armor (Mission 2), or already inside a 'Mech or tank (Missions 5 and 13). Saving adds the model files that body needs. [Game types] (multiplayer only) the types list the map supports; each type needs its own objects: spawn points for every type, flags for Capture the Flag, bases for Snatch It; the editor re-syncs the spawn groups when a type is ticked or unticked. [Check scenario] runs the validator (the game would not load or would break); Test runs it first. It also reports graphics memory: real levels use about 25 MB of the 64 MB; past about 58 MB the game crashes while loading. [Sky] writes MASky2 (model, mtb, scale, offset, position, heading) from a retail world that uses the sky. Picking a sky by hand makes the look read 'Custom'. [Use this sky's fog colour] copies FogColor from the level the sky comes ; off = the base level's own FogColor. [Fog colour swatch / Advanced: fog colour numbers] both write FogColor (u32 ARGB, alpha kept); the numbers (R,G,B 0-255) sit under Advanced. Tags: Map > Scenario; Map > Game types; Map > Sky; Map > Check. *How:* Part of 'How the editor maps to the game' (see page t16_editor_to_game). Cause OPEN, two leads from the code: (a) the ms clock [0x4E2430] vs the burst timers env+0x164/+0x168 in sub_001263F8 (a time-base mismatch would stop bursts from ever starting); (b) the flash light at env+0x358 (a directional light that should light dynamic objects) is created and toggled but never reaches the shader. Hand to the runtime owner; the editor keeps writing LightFlash 1 (correct for the original game). Tags: Environment > Weather > Lightning flashes. TRACE: clue (a) RULED OUT: [0x4E2430] is ms, env update ~110/s, bursts run (flash-on sub_001262A2 / off sub_0012612E fire; 1 flash at 0.2 s, 5 by 14.4 s; count 3/4 -> 0/4; next burst 13.2 s). Light object env+0x358 exists (vtable 0x00463600, same class as the sun at env+0x354), colour env+0x18E. So bursts run and the light toggles, but the render path never uses it (clue b). Next: RECOMP_LIGHTNING_HOLD + light field dump. GATHER: the per-object light gather fills the unit vertex shader's ONE directional slot (c13 dir = sun light +0x48, c14 colour) with the sun only (c12 ambient, c15-c23 up to 3 point lights). With the flash light held ON, c13/c14 are byte-identical and no white directional appears: the registered, enabled flash light is never chosen. Remaining cause = the gather's selection rule (first/brightest directional, list order) or a PC-side change; writer of c13/c14 not found. NOT FIXED: env DirectionalLightColor (env+0x88) equals the unit shader c14 at load, but raising it, its 3 RAM copies or the sun light while the flash is on does NOT change unit lighting (RGB 38 off vs 31 held); writing the flash into NV2A constant slot 110 in nv2a_pb_exec.c also changes nothing. So the unit c14 is a CACHED value that reaches the GPU by another path. Next: log the caller of sub_0040BF20/BF70 for registers 0x6D/0x6E during a mech draw (15 SetVertexShaderConstant(13/14) sites). FIXED: see lightning-flash-fixed-in-pc-shim-unit-sun-colour-constants-get-the-flash-added-per-draw (unit sun-colour constants were uploaded once; the shim now adds the flash per draw while it is on). *How:* Observation HIGH (retail positive control); cause OPEN, owner = runtime (not the editor). - **text.mgf interface/Text/<Lang>/{Credits,Mission,Persistent}.mgText = MGIc container with a TEXT chunk: count, lowest/highest id, header size 16, then count x (id, offset) and zero-terminated UTF-16LE strings** [code-confirmed] Verified by code + fmt_test. File: text.mgf, interface/Text/<Lang>/Credits.mgText, Mission.mgText, Persistent.mgText. Container 'MGIc'; the 'TEXT' chunk (tag, 0, size, 7) holds a 'ver ' sub-chunk (12 bytes) then 'data' (tag, size). The data block = u32 count, u32 lowest id, u32 highest id, u32 header size (16), then count x (u32 id, u32 offset from the start of data); strings are zero-terminated UTF-16LE. English: Mission has 592 ids 524288-525060 (524370 = 'Press A to open the gate.', 524787 = 'To the Rescue'); Credits has 333 ids from 262144; Persistent has 1694 ids 1-131181. Ids are the numbers that map files and triggers use to name briefing, objective and message text, so the editor looks strings up by id (GameData:game_text). *How:* Look up a message/briefing/objective id: pick the language folder, read Mission.mgText (ids 524288+) for mission strings, Persistent.mgText (ids 1-131181) for the shared UI/weapon/unit names, Credits.mgText for credits. Editor controls that show 'the game's text for id N' use this table.

- **Power-up collect rule (game, sub_131C9A): armour only when damaged, weapon power-up only when a weapon needs ammo or a class can level up** [code-confirmed] From BOTS-REVIEW rows t4-D1/D4 (recomp_0030.c:14136-14328, sub_131C9A, code-read). WEAPON branch: if pickup+0x1A8 bit 0x01 (refill) and sub_12AD65(arsenal = [actor+0xA4]) == 0 (not all full) -> true; else for c in 0.5 with pickup+0x1B4[c] != 0: sub_12B749(arsenal, class c) / sub_12AED4 says the class can still rise -> true; otherwise false and the pickup stays. - **Bots on editor-made (custom) maps: navigation always works; the retail node graph is used only on 4 bases; missing helipads / flags / bases degrade gracefully** [code-confirmed, superseded] From BOTS-REVIEW rows t3-custom-A01.A06, t3-custom-path-A01/A02, t3A-08 (code read in the game source tree source + 3D's custom 6v6 log; HIGH for code). (1) NAVIGATION: the walking planner (ma2_bot_path.c grid A*, 2 m cells) ALWAYS runs on an obstacle grid built at match start from the live terrain + colliders (core.c ensure_nav -> ma2_trav_build, then a fine prop pass), on every map, retail or custom. The coarse 20 m node graph (roam points, flank via-points, connectivity) is generated from that grid on any map whose base ships no 'Mech graph: log '[BOT-NAV] obstacle grid ok 508x508 . source=generated:gen_B670C477 nodes=2601 components 1'. (2) RETAIL GRAPH TIE: the nav graph is picked by the LOADING ARCHIVE (ma2_bot_mapid.c maps[] of 14 MP archives + core.c k_nav_archives; core.c ~1232-1247); a custom map reports its BASE archive, so ONLY on the 4 bases that ship a graph (In Your Face, New River City, Rush Hour, Witch Cauldron) does a custom map get the RETAIL graph (roam/flank picks then use retail ground while paths still follow the real terrain; row t3A-08, proposed fix: skip the shipped graph on a [SCENARIO] custom map). An unknown cache id -> terrain-match against the 4 shipped graphs (accepted at score >= 0.5 and 0.2 ahead of the next), else a graph is generated and cached as %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\BotNav\gen_<terrain fingerprint>.map (edited terrain = new fingerprint). Otherwise the bot code is map-agnostic: no retail UIDs, template ids, coordinates or map names (features are found BY CLASS: MAFlagCTF, MACheckpoint, MASnatchItDataCore, MAPowerUp, MACollectionArea, MABuilding; fixed tank guns by property comp+0xBC/0xC0 = 0). 'Home' is wherever the bot first spawned (brain.c ~2485), not the team base. The optional stuck-memory file (RECOMP_BOT_STUCK_MEMORY=1, off) is keyed by archive name so custom maps would pollute the retail map's file. (3) LANES: discovered from the live terrain at t >= 1 s in TEAM modes: plan team-centroid -> enemy-centroid on the obstacle grid, add a danger corridor, re-plan twice -> up to 3 lanes ([BOT-LANES]), each bot takes one; none when the bases are < 300 m apart or in FFA modes. (4) FALLBACKS: helipad = any MABuilding with an MACollectionArea child (core.c ~2363, ma2_bot_pad_add); the editor palette's 'Military VTOL pad' carries one. A damaged VTOL (hp < 20-45 % by skill) heads for an armour pack within 300 m (no enemy within 120 m), else the nearest pad within 2.5 km; with neither it just fights on (brain.c ~1697-1726); ground units do not use pads. Objective scoring runs only when both sides' pieces exist (brain_obj.c ~47-57, 269-283): CTF with no flags / Snatch It with no bases or cores scores 0 and the match plays as Team Destruction (no freeze); the editor already flags those as Must fix. The game does not require a helipad, so a 'no VTOL pad near the base' Check warning is only a suggestion (row t3-custom-A05). Confidence HIGH for code; one proof pending (damaged VTOL on a no-pad map). *How:* Use for editor docs on what a custom MP map needs for bots (pads, flags, bases) and why terrain edits are safe for bot walking; test maps (id 0DAA6085) and bots_custom_stripped.ma2map (id 1C6565DE).

- **NeuroHack is effectively never attempted by BattleArmor bots: G_HACK score drops to 0 the moment the target turns on the BA (13 hack decisions in 442 s, 0 clamps)** [code-confirmed] BOTS-REVIEW row t4-C2 (4C long 6v6 UnderCover copy, 442 s, 11 bots; code HIGH, run counts measured). The BA's G_HACK utility exists only while the target 'Mech is < 45 m, or < 120 m AND shooting someone else (ma2_bot_brain.c:1849-1863), so it drops to 0 the moment the target turns on the BA or the BA is pushed back; no hysteresis applies to a 0 score (brain.c:1917-1919 hysteresis only if s > 0); cover (0.95 when att >= 2), powerup (1.0-1.15) and attack then win. - **MAMech torso yaw: 3-axis rotation controller at actor+0x2B8; current angle actor+0x31C (likely), target +0x358, velocity +0x368; written by sub_0018AFDB -> sub_002AE360 -> sub_002AE200** `0018AFDB`, `002AE360`, `002AE200`, `002AC380` [inferred] Research-. A MAMech embeds a 3-axis rotation controller at actor+0x2B8 (constructed by sub_002AC380, vtable 0x4930B8, destructor sub_002AC800). Its sub-objects: +0x40 = current state (vt 0x4934B8; actor+0x2F8) and +0x7C = target/velocity state (same vtable; actor+0x334); a speed/scale float sits at +0xCC. vt 0x4934B8 slot +0x20 = sub_002B2830 reads [obj+0x24] = actor+0x31C (axis 0 = yaw); slots +0x30/+0x38 read +0x2C/+0x38 (the other axes). Target yaw is written by slot +0x24 (sub_002B2840) to [+0x24] = actor+0x358; velocity by slot +0x44 (sub_0006C790) to [+0x34] = actor+0x368. Writer chain for bot/AI torso aim: sub_0018AFDB(eax=ai, arg=target) takes the actor from [ai+0x20], builds the direction vector (target pos - own pos), applies sub_0017AC19, then calls sub_002AE360(ecx=dirvec, eax=0, dl=1, 1.0, esi = actor+0x2B8 when [actor+0x400] != 0 else [actor+0x8C]); mode 0 computes atan2(dir.x, dir.z) * const at 0x524A08 and calls sub_002AE200(ecx=ctrl, eax=0, yaw), which limits/normalises the yaw (sub_002ACB30), writes it as target through [esi+0x7C] vt+0x24, reads the current yaw through [esi+0x40] vt+0x20, computes a turn step (sub_002ACF40) times [esi+0xCC] and writes it as velocity through vt+0x44. The bots' only torso call is sub_18AFDB (ma2_bot_ctrl.c:499). The integrator tick (candidates sub_002AD120 / sub_002AC9C0) was not verified. So actor+0x31C is MOST LIKELY the torso yaw (current angle) and the readout of 4A is probably the controller's limit-folded/absolute angle, not an animation phase; but the sign/range behaviour (never negative, changes at rest) is unexplained. FreeTorsoRotation = qword bit 42 at +0x268 (existing wiki fact). Cheapest check: trace actor+0x31C, +0x358 and +0x368 in game while a bot torso-aims (target moves -> +0x358 should follow atan2 of the direction); also resolve what sub_002ACB30 does to the angle. *How:* For read/trace actor+0x31C vs +0x358 with the target moving before using it as a torso-vs-leg yaw; do not call it an animation phase.
