- **Measurement of the bots' leader focus (menace_of, RECOMP_BOT_LEADER_FOCUS, ma2_bot_brain.c: menace = clamp((ki** [code-confirmed] Measurement of the bots' leader focus (menace_of, RECOMP_BOT_LEADER_FOCUS, ma2_bot_brain.c: menace = clamp((kills - field average - 2) / 5, 0, 1.5), i.e. Two uses in code: (a) choose_target multiplies a candidate's score by 1 + lead_w[skill] x menace, lead_w 0.10/0.20/0.32/0.45 (Recruit.Elite), so at the cap 1.5 the factor is x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.48 / x1.675, small next to the finish (up to x2.5), busy (x1.5) and range/visibility factors; (b) the roam/hunt pick draws a weighted random enemy with weight 1 + hunt_w x menace, hunt_w 0.5/1/2/3. WHAT THE LOGS EXPOSE: only [BOT-HUNT] lines (DIAG on), one per hunt pick, with skill, the picked player, its kills, its menace and the total weight 'of N'. The target-choice candidate list (' [kind d in pot ttk s]') has the score but NOT the menace, and no log has the candidate set, so 'target share on the leader vs menace' and 'damage on the leader' CANNOT be computed. From 34 runs: 2727 hunt picks; 24 of 34 runs have at least one pick with menace > 0; share of hunt picks that were a menace > 0 player: Recruit 4.4 % (mean menace 0.38), Regular 4.7 % (0.27), Veteran 9.5 % (0.31), Elite 7.5 % (0.42); max menace seen 1.5 (a bot 10+ kills clear). So in these 5-minute 6v6 matches a clear leader exists only briefly and the push is rarely active. EXPECTED PICK PROBABILITY from the formula (6 live enemies, one leader): menace 0.5 -> leader picked Recruit 1.25/6.25 = 20 %, Regular 25 %, Veteran 33 %, Elite 2.5/7.5 = 33 % (uniform 17 %); menace 1.5 (cap) -> 26 / 33 / 44 / 52 %. It only decides who bots walk toward when nothing is in sight (roam, ~60-90 % of roam decisions), not who they shoot at once enemies are visible (there it is a x1.1-1.7 nudge). WOULD IT KEEP A MUCH STRONGER HUMAN'S MATCH CLOSE? Rough estimate (confidence LOW, no measurement): it saturates at 10 kills over the average, so a player 17 kills to 7 reaches the cap and then roughly 2 of the 5-6 enemy bots head for him when idle, plus a x1.1-1.7 target nudge; that is a real but moderate pressure (rough estimate +30-60 % incoming engagements), not a rubber band: it adds no handicap to damage, accuracy or spawn, and the kill/team score gap is mostly decided by team strength, so a very strong human would still win comfortably. Then the share of picks/damage on the leader vs its menace can be tabulated per skill. A test: one editor/retail run with the human playing hard (not idle) and RECOMP_BOT_LEADER_FOCUS=1 vs 0, compare the human's deaths per minute. — ma2_bot_brain.c:

Run A (5v6 = 11 bots + idle human): wall fps 80-100 after t~40 (dip to 53-69 at t~20-40 at first contact), median frame 10.7-12.2 ms, sim fps 87/59/79/88/89/89 at t=10/30/60/100/150/200. In run A the GPU draw time stays about 1 ms/frame, buffer upload about 0.5 ms; the bots' own CPU ([BOT-PERF]) is 110-120 ms per second = about 1.3 ms of an 11 ms frame, and the other ~8 ms over run C is the game's own simulation and render of 12 units fighting (effects, physics), not bot code. Nothing grows with match length (run A t=60 to 200: 79 to 89). *How:* When fps drops during a bots match, look at units in combat and other running games first; do not blame match length or the brain.
- **Not It/NRC crash = delete(NULL) from the XACT update engine+0x5C list walk (no NULL guard), right after the +0x64 guard relink; same corrupt-XACT-list family** `003DEA53`, `003E2FF5`, `003E0EC7`, `003DFA8D` [code-confirmed] Crash analysis for 4D's notit-nrc-crash1. The crash is a delete(NULL): the faulting read is [ptr-0xB] with ptr = 0 inside the CRT heap block-size query, which tagged delete calls first. Guest stack decoded: 0x2BBC32 is in thunk 0x2BBC21 (20 B: pushes the CRT heap handle [0x534E1C], 0, ptr; calls sub_2BA13D, the _msize-style block-size query that does mov al,[ecx-0xB]); 0x2B83E7 in 0x2B83D0 (26 B, block-size dispatcher on the pool tag: bit 31 clear -> 2BBC21, set -> 2BBDEC); 0x12348 in 0x12330 (195 B, tagged delete wrapper: size 2B83D0, free 2B83B6, stats add via sub_1BE20; esi 0x84 / edi 0x6484A000 are the pool tag); 0x3DDEAC in 0x3DDE9E (15 B, delete(ptr) with fixed tag 0x6484A000); 0x3DFAA6 in 0x3DFA8D (33 B, node destructor sub_3E0E67 then delete when flag 1); 0x3E0ED8 in 0x3E0EC7 (21 B, Release: dec [obj+0x40], at 0 calls 3DFA8D(obj,1)); 0x3E3286 in 0x3E2FF5 (686 B, recomp_0097.c, per-node processor of the engine+0x5C list; the release is the call 0x3E0EC7 at 0x3E3281 with eax = the node); 0x3DEAFF in sub_003DEA53 (XACT per-frame update) right after call 0x3E2FF5 at 0x3DEAFA. 0x3E869C is a data address (the XACT lock pushed at 0xBBFB1), a stale stack word, not a frame. This is memory-heap code reached from the XACT update, not sound code. Walk order in sub_003DEA53: loop 1 walks edi+0x64 and calls 3DFCDF on node-8 (0x3DEAD9-0x3DEAEC); loop 2 walks edi+0x5C and calls 3E2FF5 on the raw [esi] link (0x3DEAEE-0x3DEB01). Neither loop checks for a NULL link: a zero link satisfies esi != head, so node 0 is processed. The guard's log line ('[XACT-LIST] engine list +0x64 head=009FACC4 relinked: invalid link at 00000000') matches loop 1; the crash came in loop 2 right after. VERDICT: very plausibly the known XACT list corruption (wiki xact-list-spin / xact-list-guard / xact-list-walk-freeze / xact-root-cause-open), now as a null free instead of a spin; the +0x5C walk is not covered by the guard (code-confirmed for the function identities and the [NULL-0xB] fault; the NULL node reaching the release is inferred). Possible low-cost mitigation (suggestion only, nothing changed): a NULL check in 3DDE9E and in the 0x3DEAF5 loop-2 walk; low guest memory reads without faulting, so the refcount at guest 0x40 is unknown. Open: does ma2_xact_list_repair also cover the +0x5C loop; what writes the links (root cause); a watchpoint on engine+0x5C and +0x64 link writes or a node-chain dump when the guard fires would settle it. *How:* When a crash/AV appears with [XACT-LIST] just before it, treat it as the XACT list corruption; the +0x5C loop at 0x3DEAEE-0x3DEB01 has no NULL guard.

- **Crash xact-notit-4 (174273e, t=253.7): AI setmode(5) -> stop-in-place sub_183FAC -> sub_2AD5C0 reads max speed through a garbage body pointer (not XACT code)** `00183FAC`, `002AD5C0`, `00183B9D`, `001840A4` [documented, open-question] The crash (AV fault Xbox VA 0x8D10C49F, guest stack 0x183FBE, 0x183C9B, 0x184137, 0x15D313) is in the game's AI movement controller, not in XACT. Chain: sub_15D2E9 (vtable+0x1C dispatcher) -> sub_1840A4 (move-step: calls MoveTo vtable+0x38, then at 0x18412B calls setmode(5) when the controller is in the stop state; skips it only if [0x4EAF98] matches) -> sub_183B9D (setmode, ecx = controller, eax = new mode, stores mode at +0x12C) -> sub_183FAC (enter-mode-5 handler: edx = [ctrl+0x24] = the body/actor, eax=1, push 0; calls sub_2AD5C0; then reads [[ctrl+0x20]+0x28] , if it differs from [0x4EAF98], calls a vtable+0xC method of [[[ctrl+0x20]+0x8C]+0x10C] with a zeroed vec3) -> sub_2AD5C0 (set forward speed as percent of max: cvtsi2ss(percent) * [body+0xBC] * [0x493B44], clamped against [body+0xC0]). The fault is the first body read: [body+0xBC] with body = [ctrl+0x24] = ~0x8D11C3E3, a non-pointer (host region 0x8D11C000 is unmapped, outside guest RAM). Controller esi = 0x023B9200 is an ordinary guest-heap AI component (same range as the bot vehicles 0x023D5A10, 0x024B0320), so its +0x24 field was stale/overwritten: the controller (or the heap block under it) was freed and reused, or the body was torn down, while the AI tick still held it. Context: two bots were killed 1 s earlier (BOT-KILL t=252.7 bots 1 and 9) and bot 4 retargeted a vehicle at t=253.7. The XACT guard in 174273e only runs inside the XACT list walks (+0x44/+0x64/+0x5C), writes nothing outside the XACT node it cuts, and logged 0 [XACT-LIST] lines in this run, so it did not execute before the crash. A direct code path from the XACT guard cut to this crash does not exist; the only possible link is memory corruption (a freed XACT-pool block, allocator id 0x84, that overlaps or was recycled into the AI block, or a write through a stale XACT pointer into a recycled block). UPDATE: seen ONCE in 13 Not It NRC runs (5 on a67af79 + 8 on guard exes), 1 s after BOT-KILL of bots 1 and 9; not reproduced since. a stale AI controller after a kill. Root cause unknown. *How:* Treat as a separate AI stale-controller use-after-free candidate. With the ce2470b tracer (XMemFree ring + [XACT-UAF]), after a crash like this look up who freed the block covering the crash controller (esi in the crash line, 0x023B9200 here) in the free ring: an XACT-pool free covering it = XACT-related, any other free = AI/vehicle teardown bug. Dump 0x20 bytes of the controller (+0x20/+0x24/+0x12C) at crash time. Compare with the a67af79 baseline crash stacks to see whether it is the same stack (it would then predate the XACT guard). — generated recomp_0040.c (made at install time, not in the repository):
- **XACT objects are freed by the game's own XMemFree sub_00012330 (allocator id 0x84 -> pool [0x50BA38]), never by xbox_HeapFree; XMemFree rejects NULL** `00012330`, `0001BE20`, `002B83D0` [documented, open-question] XACT engine objects are freed through the game's own XMemFree sub_00012330(ptr, attrs): the allocator id is attrs byte 2, and 0x84 selects the XACT pool [0x50BA38] via sub_0001BE20. These frees never reach the host's xbox_HeapFree, so a UAF hook on xbox_HeapFree alone cannot see XACT block frees. The game's XMemFree does not accept NULL: sub_002B83D0 reads [ptr-0xB], so XMemFree(NULL) faults. Node offsets inside the XACT objects: the +0x44 list node = obj+0x58, the +0x64 node = obj+8, the +0x5C node = obj+0. *How:* To trace XACT use-after-free, hook sub_00012330 (as the t4c-xact ce2470b tracer does) and filter on attrs byte 2 == 0x84; a free of an object that still has a linked node (obj+0x58 / obj+8 / obj+0) is the bug. Skip and log XMemFree(NULL) rather than calling it.

## Code research, first pass: editor and render details

### Facts

- **The Mission_03 burning barrel is the model Env_BarrelDrumFire, whose effect chunk uses the particle file Env_Fire_SM_Loop_01** [code-confirmed] mission_03.mgf lists the model Env_BarrelDrum_Fire.MGMODEL (sub-meshes embers, rubbish, barrel_farm, sign1). Its .mtb references SpecialEffects/Environment/Env_Fire_SM_Loop_01.mgparticle, whose emitters are fire 1-3, smoke (bd_smoke_sm.tif) and sparks. No MAEffect is placed on Mission_03, so the flame and dark smoke column come from the model's own effect chunk. The placed object that uses this model was not decoded. *How:* Open: which placed instance uses Env_BarrelDrumFire on Mission_03 (scene data not decoded). In-game trace or decoded object list needed.
- **The game draws the Env_Highway_Light lightbulb mesh at night on Mission_01b, so the .mtb hide rule does not remove it at run time** [verified-in-game] On Mission_01b at night (IsNightTime=1, LightsOn=1) the running game draws the lightbulb mesh once per lamp: an opaque material_color_shift draw (texture Misc_168_LightPost, 81043000; 43 vertices; colour C0 255,255,228; writes alpha 0x34), which renders white. So the .mtb MAModSubObjectShow rule (Enable=0, EnableTree=1) does not hide the bulb in the running game under those flags. An Ill Wind 'post only' trace conflicts with this and is unexplained. *How:* Open: why the Ill Wind trace shows post only. Check LightsOn and LightsDisabled on that lamp (flag bits are in the wiki).
- **On Mission_03 the sky is the sky_main alpha layer over a cleared black frame, with no opaque dome drawn** [verified-in-game] On Mission_03 the game draws the sky_main alpha layer over a cleared black frame; no opaque sky dome is drawn. The sample pixel at game 640,60 of 1280x960 reads 29,27,25. *How:* Open: single-pixel sample. Confirm on a second pixel before relying on it. The additive star layer (Sky_034_Stars) on the same map is a separate open question. Caveat: MCP/tracetools runs render at 640x480, so this reference pixel and any thin-detail reading may understate detail at a 3840x1600; confirm at that resolution.
- **The Mission_04 pad floor draw uses two detail textures (808D1000 and 80E99000), both trilinear with no anisotropy, mixed by stage constant 7F7F7F7F** [verified-in-game] Game trace of the M04 pad floor (block draw 3104941, prog 00021, 3 stages, pixel 480,400 of the 640x480 frame): t0 = 808D1000 128x128 DXT1 (Details_010_cracked), t1 = 80E99000 256x256 DXT1 (Terrain MissionXX_Detail01.tif). Both have filter word 02062000 (min trilinear, mag linear, mip bias 0) and control0 4003FFC0 (aniso 1x, full mip chain 6/7, wrap). Stage constant C0 = 7F7F7F7F (0.5). UV of vertex 0: tex0 15.4844, tex1 1.49805. The colour map is not in this draw.
- **A node_light lightmap min_color equals the ground-pool splat colour (M02 trace matches a retail point light exactly)** [verified-in-game] On M02 the traced ground-pool splat colour C0 = 557F7A69 equals the min_color 127, 122, 105 of the 255,245,211 point light in gocommando.mgf exactly. So the lightmap min_color of a node_light is the splat colour C0.rgb. Only one instance was compared, and min equals max in every retail lamp seen, so the lerp between min and max is untested. *How:* Open: test a lamp whose min_color differs from max_color before relying on the lerp.
- **The Mission_01b pavement pixel is a MARoad complex road slab drawn in two passes (programs 0A624 and 08C21)** [code-confirmed] Pixel 150,320 of the Mission_01b frame is MARoad 131795, a complex road slab. Pass 1 (program 0A624: t0 PASSTHRU, t1 DOT_PRODUCT, t2 DOT_ST, t3 2D = 512 ground map 80A61000) gives R0 = ((2T0-1).(2V0-1)) x T3.a x C0 (sun 4E3F34) + T3.rgb, then x V1. Pass 2 (program 08C21: t2 CUBE, t3 = framebuffer) gives 2x(T3 x lerp(cube, base, base.a) + multi.g x (.18,18,1) + multi.b x (1,97,31)) + multi.r x T3.a x 0.698. Decoded with rcdec. *How:* Open: the sun constant and the ground-map sampling are from one pixel; check on a second road pixel.
- **Three editor paths do not draw the Mission_04 pad floor: ground_mix final lerp, its tile uv scale and the stage-19 detail line** [verified-in-game, open-question] In the editor, forcing ground_mix final lerp to a constant 0.5, scaling the tile uv by 0.0484 (game uv ratio 10.3) in ground_mix and in the stage-19 line, all give bit-identical M04 pad-shot images. So none of these draws the pad floor. The editor pad shot shows detail0 x colour x light (mean 36,34,35) with colour-map alpha about 1 at the pad. The stage-19 detail1 tile alone is smeared streaks (mean 70,73,68), not the crisp game grid. The owner of the pad floor draw in the editor is unknown. *How:* Open: candidates are the layer-array path ginfo.x>1.5, or a different shader or dpar branch. Or trace a game prog-00021 floor on another map. Status: M04 floor OPEN.
- **MAPointLight census of retail Mission_03 and Mission_01b: 18 of 21 M03 lights have LightMap=1 and all 5 M01b lights have LightMap=0** [code-confirmed] Editor dump of retail data. Mission_03: 18 of 21 MAPointLights have LightMap=1 (LightRadius 60-80 object reach, LightMapRadius 20 ground disc, LightMapColor equal to LightColor); 3 have LightMap=0. Mission_01b: 5 of 5 have LightMap=0 (LightRadius 5-10), one of them LightOn=0. Consistent with the existing pointlight-ground-splat fact. RECOMP_CAM_SET moves the eye field but the 3D scene goes black, so the M05 pose is not yet unblocked. *How:* Superseded in part: the pose override (RECOMP_CAM_SET) now WORKS (verified 10-25 on M04, see recomp-cam-set-pose-override-works-m04-verified). The earlier 'scene goes black' statement is out of date. The texstate/vertex/ctxwrite flags stand.
- **In-game A/B on a Mission_03 copy: MAPointLight LightMap=1 paints a bright ground disc plus object light; LightMap=0 gives object light only** [verified-in-game] In-game A/B on a Mission_03 copy with one authored MAPointLight. LightMap=1 gives a bright ground disc plus object light. LightMap=0 gives object light only. This confirms the ground disc is controlled by the LightMap flag. *How:* Open: the disc alpha 0x60 value is still unverified in-game (see the census fact).

The human view (camera+0x200) points at its builder via MEM32(view+0x154) (vtable 0045DDD0, = camera+0x390). The builder state S sits at builder+0x14 (S+0 eye, S+0x10 look vector, S+0x1C up, rows right/up/forward at S+0x28/0x38/0x48, w=0); the camera keeps a copy at camera+0x238. Writing S+0x88. (the derived block) caused the earlier black or garbled scenes, so the fix writes only S and the camera+0x238 copy. Custom-scenario campaign levels (e.g. M05) have no camera object behind the human view, so [CAM-POSE] falls back to the newest view's builder. *How:* Gameplay pose starts at game time ~23-30 s; do not press Enter; the pose does not apply during cinemas.

- **The Mission_05 final water pass (program 00421) mixes tinted refraction with a lit cube reflection, then fog** [code-confirmed] Decoded from the M05 trace (program 00421): out = fog(lerp(tint x refraction320x240, 2 x cube x light, F x sat(4a))). - **How deep retail water is where the type map says wade (8) or deep (16): shallow cells are about 0.3-2 m under the surface (flat MP lakes 2.9-4.4 m), deep cells 2-8 m** [documented] Measured on all 15 campaign worlds and 15 multiplayer worlds with MAWater planes: for every type-map cell with bit 8 / 16 / 32 inside a plane, depth = plane CorporalPos.y minus the bilinear terrain height (8-bit height field, TerrainMinHeight.MaxHeight). SHALLOW (8): median 0.3-1.2 m and 90th percentile <=1.6 m on nearly every map: Bogged Down swamp median 0.9 / p90 1.2 / max 1.7; Mission_07 1.0 / 1.3 (max 5.0); New River City 1.2 / 1.6 (max 2.3); Mission_06a 0.3 / 1.1; Mission_14 0.7 / 1.4 (max 4.6); Mission_11a 0.8 / 2.5 (max 4.0). Flat-bottomed MP lakes are deeper but uniform: No Man's Land 2.9 m, Troubled Waters 4.4 m. DEEP (16, campaign only): Mission_01b night harbour 8.1 m, Mission_02 median 5.9 (p10 2.9), Cinema_1_3 5.9, Mission_11a median 4.7 (p90 6.8), Mission_14 median 2.2 (p90 4.1), Mission_06a 1.9. WATERWAY (32): median 0.6-1.2 m, p90 <=1.4 on most worlds. So retail never has an 8-marked wading cell deeper than about 4.4 m (typical <2 m) and puts bit 16 only where the water is deeper than about 2-3 m. The game does not read a depth to decide wading: gameplay water is the type-map bit plus the MAEnvironment per-type values (Speed / Damage / Cooling / 'Mech may enter' / Pilot in - shallow, deep, waterway). The editor's default dig makes a 200x120 lake ~8 m deep at the middle with every cell below the surface marked 8 (water_ux.cpp dig_water_basin: depth = min(pond_depth_ 8, max(1, 0.3 x shorter half side))), 2-4x the deepest retail shallow water; in game the on-foot pilot walks out of the start, sinks fully under the surface and the camera sits at the waterline. *How:* Use for the c3 water owner: a wadable lake should dig 1-2 m (retail median 0.9-1.2 m, p90 <=1.6; 2.9-4.4 m exists only as flat MP lakes) or be warned/capped. Visibility trade-off: the editor comment says shallow water is faint in the game (thickness alpha ~ vertical depth/4, medium, see water-thickness-alpha-samples), which is why pond_depth_ starts at 8. Open: no game code was found that drowns, slows or pushes out a pilot below the surface (the pilot follows the terrain bed; no swim state found); what bit 16 does for an on-foot pilot (Pilot in - deep water: 1.0 x51, 100.0 x11, 0.0 x3, 10.0 x1 in the catalog, meaning unconfirmed) is untested; planes overlapping a larger plane (OverFalls pool 7.5 m) and a few negative depths come from cells outside the assumed plane extent (model size from the template name 1000/500/250). — water_ux.cpp:197

- **The game reads MAAttack AttackTimeout in sub_001854C5 (a 'choose target' helper): with AttackPlayer 1 the unit sticks to its current target until elapsed time since a per-unit stamp exceeds AttackTimeout, then takes the order's target; AttackPlayer 0 always takes the order's target, AttackPlayer 2 (the player) switches when the player is farther than a range** [code-confirmed] recomp_0040.c:17651-17800 sub_001854C5 (edi = the AI unit; code-confirmed incl. the x87 order: clock - [unit+0x100] is compared with the timeout, ja = elapsed > timeout). Steps: the unit's current order event is [unit+0x1A8], its behaviour [event+0x7C]; the behaviour's class id [beh+0x28] must equal MEM32(0x4EAF1C) (MAAttack, else the helper just returns the current target [unit+0xB4]); unit+0xF0 = the behaviour's +0x2C, the order's target is resolved by sub_001855E7(unit, behaviour) (runtime AttackUID at beh+0x78, AttackSet +0x7C), validated by sub_000B3C50 and stored to unit+0xF4. If the unit has NO current target ([unit+0xB4] == 0) or AttackPlayer (beh+0x84) == 0 the order's target is returned at once. AttackPlayer 1 ('attack a unit'): elapsed = the live clock (double at 0x4E2440) minus the float stamp [unit+0x100]; if elapsed > AttackTimeout (beh+0x80) it returns the order's target, else it keeps the current target. AttackPlayer 2 ('attack the player'): no timeout test; it takes the distance between two positions (the current target and the order's target) and returns the CURRENT target if the squared distance is below [[unit+0x20]+0x200] squared (a range read from the unit's class data), otherwise the ORDER's target. Runtime object offsets are the serializer offsets + 0x20 (the constructor sub_000D476C stores the vtable at obj+0x20): AttackUID +0x78, AttackSet +0x7C, AttackTimeout +0x80, AttackPlayer +0x84. Callers store the result into unit+0xB4 after a unit vtable +0x20 call (nine sites: recomp_0046.c:15293, 27730, 27952, 29373; recomp_0047.c:7841, 8068, 30150; plus 0x1BACF6 x2). *How:* Meaning for authors: AttackTimeout is NOT a countdown that ends the order. It is how long the unit may go without a fresh 'event' stamp before it re-targets the ordered unit; the stamp [unit+0x100] is written by sub_0018519F (shifts +0xF8/+0x100 history, stores the clock; probably last hit or last engagement - inferred). A large value (9999) keeps whatever the unit is fighting; 3 s snaps back to the ordered target quickly. Open: callers of sub_0018519F (stamp meaning) and what happens when the returned target equals the current one; AttackPlayer 0 is used by 2 of 89 retail attacks, 1 by 42, 2 by 45. — generated recomp_0040.c (made at install time, not in the repository):17651

## Movies and front-end flow

## Movies and front-end flow

Generated C: `generated (made at install time, not in the repository)`. Facts: `facts/t13_movies_frontend.json`.

### Overview

Two front-end screen classes play movies through a movie object stored at `this+0x64` (opened with `sub_000B0CF0(path, &this+0x64)`). The Title/Legal Screen (vtable 00481D00) plays the startup logos (MAIntro.mgv). The Attract Screen (vtable 004820C8) plays AttractMode, ConquestIntro and SPIntro. It takes its path from a table at 0x00459FE8 (stride 0x104) indexed by the global `[0x0050C9EC]` (0 attract, 1 Conquest, 2 SPIntro).

SPIntro starts from the mission-start state `sub_002439B7`. For a mission with no `loadmovie` entry, outside the demo, and only the first time (`[0x0050CA4A]` is 0), it sets `[0x50C9EC]=2`, switches to the Attract Screen state `[0x004EC04C]` and sets `[0x50CA4A]=1`. The second pass sees the flag and loads the mission. A mission with `loadmovie` plays a loading-screen movie and skips this path.

The Attract Screen update (slot 5, `sub_001F84DE`) ends the screen with result 2 when the movie object is gone, a pad 0 button is down (`sub_0001EE70(0)`), a key word is set (`sub_0001EDD0`), the PC movie-skip request is pending, or the movie reports finished (vtable +0x28). Returning result 2 uses the normal screen exit slot, which releases the movie.

### Key code

| Address | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 001F84DE | Attract Screen update; `loc_001F8521` returns 2 (done) | recomp_0052.c:8623 |
| 001F8439 | Attract Screen init; opens the movie from table index `[0x50C9EC]` | recomp_0052.c |
| 001F84B3 | Attract Screen exit; releases the movie | recomp_0052.c |
| 002439B7 | mission-start state; selects SPIntro once | ma2.xbe |
| 001F40B3 | Title/Legal update; PC hook at line 33742 | recomp_0051.c |
| 0001EE70 / 0001EE10 / 0001EDD0 | any pad button / Start-range button / any key words | ma2.xbe |

### Added code and hooks

`pc_input_movie_skip_pending(1)` is consumed by both `sub_001F40B3` and `sub_001F84DE`. Safe-start is rearmed in each screen initializer and consumed only once: repeatedly asserting it made the Title/Legal player restart its seek/stop transition every update and loop the Day 1 Studios logo. The native Bink path also rearms only when its fullscreen movie count changes from inactive to active, not for nested increments.

The Attract hook sits after the movie-null check and before `loc_001F84E7`: `if(pc_input_movie_skip_pending(1))goto loc_001F8521;`. No direct decoder return is needed; the existing screen lifecycle performs cleanup.

### Open questions

- The Apple guest currently stubs the native Bink path, so lifted retail playback does not drive `pc_display_movie(+1/-1)`; the native FFmpeg implementation does.
- `[0x4E4BB8]` and `[0x4E4BBC]` as any-key words is inferred.
- The 002439B7 flow is read from disassembly only (not generated C, not run).



### Facts

- **SPIntro is played by the Attract Screen class, not the Title/Legal screen** `001F8439`, `004820C8`, `0050C9EC`, `00459FE8` [code-confirmed] Attract Screen init (vtable slot 14, sub_001F8439) opens its movie with sub_000B0CF0(path, &this+0x64), where path = 0x00459FE8 + [0x0050C9EC]*0x104. The table holds Interface\Movie\AttractMode\AttractMode.mgv (index 0), Interface\Movie\Conquest\ConquestIntro.mgv (index 1, set at 001F3EEA) and Interface\Movie\SPIntro\SpIntro.mgv (index 2, string at 0045A1F0). The .mgv names the Movie\60\English\SPIntro.bik clip. The idle attract loop uses the same class and the same movie-object slot (+0x64), so SPIntro is not driven by the Title/Legal player at 001F40B3. — generated recomp_0052.c (made at install time, not in the repository):8623
- **Mission-start state 002439B7 selects SPIntro once for a mission with no loadmovie** `00168D4A`, `00224E15`, `00224F8C`, `002439B7` [code-confirmed] sub_002439B7 (mission-start state, recomp_0061.c) picks SPIntro at loc_00243BC8 when all three hold: [0x50C949]==0 (not demo), profile+0x90 (campaign index, in edi) ==0, and [0x50CA4A]==0. The checks are at loc_00243A2D.39 (first pass) and loc_00243B3F.4C (second pass). [0x50CA4A] and [0x50CA49] are cleared together at sub_00224E15 loc_00224F8C. *How:* To bypass instead of skip, preset the byte [0x0050CA4A]=1 before this state runs. — generated recomp_0061.c (made at install time, not in the repository):0
- **Attract Screen update (slot 5, 001F84DE) ends on a button or key press and returns 2** `001F84DE`, `0001EE70`, `0001EDD0`, `001F8521` [code-confirmed] Each frame sub_001F84DE does: if this+0x64 (movie) is 0 go to loc_001F8521; if sub_0001EE70(0) is true (any of the 16 buttons on pad 0 newer than the input stamp [0x4E3BAC]) go to loc_001F8521; if sub_0001EDD0(0,0) is true ([0x4E4BB8] or [0x4E4BBC] nonzero, the any-key words, which is why Enter works) go to loc_001F8521; if movie vtable +0x28 returns 0 (finished) go to loc_001F8521. Otherwise it calls movie vtable +0x4C and tail-jumps sub_001CAC30. loc_001F8521 is push 2 / pop eax / ret, the screen's done result; the exit handler (slot 15, 001F84B3) then releases the movie via sub_00208F42. There is no +0x68/+0x69 flag and no seek or stop call, unlike 001F40B3. — generated recomp_0052.c (made at install time, not in the repository):8623
- **Historical gap: the Attract Screen did not read the PC movie-skip flag** `001F84DE`, `001F40B3` [code-confirmed, superseded] Before the Apple Silicon movie-skip work, the only consumer of pc_input_movie_skip_pending was the hook in sub_001F40B3 (Title/Legal Screen). sub_001F84DE did not read it, so SPIntro ignored the PC flag and a quick-test thread had to post Return. The generated patch now adds the missing Attract Screen consumer. — generated recomp_0051.c (made at install time, not in the repository):33742

That is the screen's normal result 2, so its existing exit slot releases the movie. The request is consumed once rather than repeated every update. The same lifecycle rule applies to startup movies and native outermost fullscreen movies. — generated recomp_0052.c (made at install time, not in the repository):8623
- **Title/Legal update 001F40B3: +0x68 skippable, +0x69 done latch, loc_001F40F6 seek/stop** `001F40B3`, `001F40F6`, `001F4146`, `001F413E` [code-confirmed] Object +0x64 is the movie, +0x68 a skippable byte, +0x69 a done latch. Flow: movie null returns 2; movie +0x20 call, then +0x4C if it returned 0; the PC hook (skip pending) goes to loc_001F40F6; else movie +0x28 == 0 or +0x69 set goes to loc_001F4146 (movie +0x14, return 1); if +0x68 is set and sub_0001EE10(0) (buttons 4.15) is true go to 001F40F6. 001F40F6 gets the player via sub_000B0E70(0), seeks (+0x18) near the end (0x2EF, or 0x2EF-0x7D when player+0x108==0x32), stops (+0x4C), closes (+0xC), sets +0x69=1, then tail-jumps sub_001CAC30. — generated recomp_0051.c (made at install time, not in the repository):33690
- **Movie and campaign-script entry points** `000B0CF0`, `000B0E70`, `000B06F0`, `000B0BB0` [code-confirmed] sub_000B0CF0(path, out) opens an .mgv movie into *out; sub_000B0E70(0) returns the current movie player; sub_000B06F0 is the movie update (recomp_0018.c); 000B0BB0 and 000AFE90 name Movie\Bink, Movie\Manager and Movie\Movies. 00168C11 maps a section type word (INIT, END, LEVEL, MOVIE) to an index; 00168D4A reads one campaign record (type, next, file, titleid, descriptionid, holographicid, loadmovie, levelsetup, returntolobby). loadmovie is a movie played while the mission loads, not the SPIntro cutscene. — generated recomp_0018.c (made at install time, not in the repository):1
- **SPIntro is skippable in retail by any pad 0 button or key** `001F84DE`, `0001EE70`, `0001EDD0` [code-confirmed] Any of the 16 buttons on pad 0 (A, Start and the rest) or a key ends SPIntro, because sub_001F84DE tests sub_0001EE70(0) and sub_0001EDD0. The PC port needs no new behaviour, only the pc movie_skip flag wired into the same exit. — generated recomp_0052.c (made at install time, not in the repository):8623

## Bot pathing and performance pass (2026-10-27)

### Facts

- **AI-drive flags on an ejected bot write into a non-body object** [code-confirmed] The bot controller sets actor+0x1E8 |= 3 (ma2_bot_ctrl.c:219/231/268/301). That is valid only on MAMech/MAMover bodies. On a NeuroHack-ejected bot, +0x1E8 is an embedded object's vtable pointer. Fixed by ma2_bot_body_ok in actor_ai (push-w1 3fb8ed5, RECOMP_BOT_BODY_GUARD).
- **Signature of a vptr shifted by 3 in [ICALL] lines** [verified-in-game] A vptr shifted by 3 shows up as [ICALL] targets that are code addresses shifted left 8 bits (0x01ECA000 = 0x0001ECA0, 0x0817E000 = 0x000817E0).
- **The [CS] waits on 0x003C4598 in that log are normal contention (all acquired), not the cause.** [verified-in-game] The [CS] waits on 0x003C4598 in that log are normal contention (all acquired), not the cause.
- **NeuroHack QTE: setting +0x18 to +0xA8 wins the round** [verified-in-game] In the NeuroHack QTE, setting the hacker's +0x18 to +0xA8 (target) ends the round as a WIN: the victim is ejected and the 'Mech is left empty. Holding the victim's +0x18 at 0 alone does not win. Test hook RECOMP_TEST_HIJACK (ma2_bots_core.c; hk2/hk3).
- **Bot code must never write unit HP** [verified-in-game] Writing a unit's HP (+0x260 block +8) from bot code revives units whose death handler already ran. It then crashes later in the deferred-delete walk (B5D60/B5350/B4EF0; hj1-4, hj7). Never write HP, even in test hooks.
- **RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS is not a hang detector** [verified-in-game] RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS terminates the process after N seconds (hk1 first launch died at load). It is not a hang detector; use RECOMP_BOT_STALL=1 instead.
- **[ICALL] log lines include ret, ecx, tid and stack words** [code-confirmed] [ICALL] log lines now include ret, ecx and tid plus 8 stack words (recomp_manual.c recomp_icall_not_code_log, push-w1 aa31817).
- **NeuroHack victim holds a plain MACorporeal placeholder** [verified-in-game] After a won NeuroHack, the victim's player holds a plain MACorporeal (class CA77C1A6, vtable 00466BA0, 0x1A8 bytes, one child class D8CDB49A) at the 'Mech for about 8-12 s. Deaths +1 at about +9 s, then he respawns about 900 m away as a fresh pilot MAMech. No MAMech/MAMover among the children, so no pilot to drive (w1b-r0.r5). W6b later showed ordinary deaths do not produce it.
- **A won NeuroHack kills the victim** [verified-in-game] A won NeuroHack kills the victim (deaths +1). The bot does not land as a pilot near the 'Mech.
- **sub_C8E6A first MACorporeal child is the respawn placeholder** [code-confirmed] sub_C8E6A's 'first MACorporeal child' is the placeholder during the respawn wait. actor_kind now maps exact MACorporeal to MA2_KIND_NONE (ma2_bots_core.c actor_kind, push-w1 fb892dc; switch RECOMP_BOT_PLAIN_CORP, default 1).
- **A write at +0x1E8 on a MACorporeal lands in the next heap block** [code-confirmed] MACorporeal objects are 0x1A8 bytes (factory 0xD6FE8). Any write at +0x1E8 (MAMover AI flags) on one lands in the next heap block.
- **A human must board an emptied 'Mech on foot** [verified-in-game] In a BattleArmor, Q climbs out. A human (or test hook) must board an emptied 'Mech on foot.
- **All 4 RECOMP_TEST_HIJACK launches on w1b5 completed a hijack** [verified-in-game] All 4 RECOMP_TEST_HIJACK launches on w1b5 completed a hijack this time (t=104-179 s). The earlier 'about half' was a W1b hook issue, not a fix issue.
- **Destroyed hijacked 'Mech respawns the human as a pilot** [verified-in-game] A destroyed hijacked 'Mech sends the human to a fresh pilot (kind 1, hp 10/10) without faults (w1c-r3 t=133-148).
- **UC match start: ensure_nav grid costs 1.1-1.2 s** [verified-in-game] On UC match start, ensure_nav (ma2_bots_core.c) builds the obstacle grid with 566,702 physics rays: 1.1-1.2 s on the game thread (baseline). trav_fine_props adds about 0.4 s.

## Bot surprise behaviours and navigation (2026-10-30)

## Push surprise, navigation and the push-merge (2026-10-30)

The bots push of 2026-10-30 added three groups of work on top of push-final (c44d849) and merged them into the branch `push-merge`:

- **Surprise behaviours** (push-s1, s2, s3): rare, skill-scaled human-like tricks that all start through one rarity gate, `sp_roll` in `ma2_bot_surprise.c` (switch, 20 s hold-off, per-bot cooldown, random roll, per-victim budget of 2 per 600 s, no repeat, 45 s spacing). Task A (s1): revenge, grudge, mood (hot/cold streaks), rookie mistakes A-F. Task B (s2, `ma2_bot_surprise_b.c`): bait, pincer, Elite power-up timing and denial. Task C (s3, `ma2_bot_surprise_c.c`): Level, Stomp, Hack cover, Peel-off. Each trick keeps its own state, steers through the existing tactical-point fields or a replacing order, and counts itself in `[C7] sp_*` pieces. Fair damage: tricks change decisions, aim gate, timing and target only.
- **Ground navigation and high ground** (push-x, x2, x3): NoPathHold and SnapWide remove the Nuclear Reactor C ledge trap, SwapUnstick bounds a stuck vehicle swap, the BA wall climb gets real roof candidates from a raster roof scan, and the R13 review fixes make the path planner NaN-safe and epoch-correct.
- **VTOL carrier fetch / ferry and threat altitude** (push-y): LiftClaimFix, LiftBoardFix, VtolThreatAlt, and the APU front-end trap fix (`apu_vp.c`, env only).

### Where things live

| Piece | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Rarity gate, killer table, revenge, grudge, mood, rookie | `kit/source/game/src/bots/ma2_bot_surprise.c/.h` | included into `ma2_bot_brain.c` before `ma2_bot_brain_obj.c` |
| Bait, pincer, power-up timing and denial | `kit/source/game/src/bots/ma2_bot_surprise_b.c` | included before `brain_tick_body`; hooks `sp2_dead`, `sp2_tick`, `sp2_order` |
| Level, Stomp, Hack cover, Peel-off | `kit/source/game/src/bots/ma2_bot_surprise_c.c/.h` | hooks `spc_tick` and `spc_order`; new plumbing Ma2Senses.bld_ray/bld_get, Ma2Order.ff_skip/ff_rider |
| Roof scan | `kit/source/game/src/bots/ma2_bots_core.c` roofs_step / sn_roofs | feeds `tac_climb` in `ma2_bot_brain.c` |
| Wall climb on order | `kit/source/game/src/bots/ma2_bot_ctrl.c` climb_order | state reset on a new body (merge safety pass) |
| C7 diagnostics table | `kit/source/game/src/bots/ma2_bot_c7.c` | 256 pieces x 128 counters after the merge |

### Switches

Every approved behaviour ships ON (Design rule: 10-30). Master `RECOMP_BOT_SURPRISE` / `[Bots] Surprises`; per trick `RECOMP_BOT_SP_<NAME>` / `Sp<Name>`; navigation `NoPathHold`, `SnapWide`, `SwapUnstick`, `ReplanFix`, `NavFix`, `NavGuard`, `LanePin`, `UnreachableGoal`; lift `LiftClaimFix`, `LiftBoardFix`; `VtolThreatAlt`. Only `CarrierDanger` stays off. The shipped `pc_settings.ini` `[Bots] PathSlice` should be 1 (the code default is already ON).

### Status of the proofs

Proven in game: revenge and mood (forced), Level end to end once, bot-carrier VTOL fetch and ferry once, NRC ledge trap fixed (0 traps in 3 runs against 4 of 4 on the base), roof candidates on UC. Unproven (shipped ON, event-gated): Stomp, Hack cover action path, Peel-off, pincer arrival, power-up timing and denial, VtolThreatAlt effect, the BA claw climb to a roof, Grudge payback (8 %).

### Integration test + install (2026-10-31, exe C01EA259 = push-merge 65fcef1)
- 4 runs, 0 ICALL/FAULT/CRASH/R6025, 0 BOT-TRAPPED (NRC CTF PathSlice=1 included), no [C7] table full. UC TD 5v6 Mixed ON vs OFF: team-0 kill share 55 vs 57 %, frame median 9.4 vs 9.2 ms, p99 18.6 vs 17.3 ms, first-10 s HITCH counts 34 vs 37 (same causes). Surprise code cost [C7] sp_all tick_ms=0.013, tick_max=0.48.
- RECOMP_BOT_DIAG=1 is what prints [BOT] t= / [BOT-SUM] (stalls, kills); RECOMP_PERF=1 alone gives only [BOT-PERF] and [PERF-PACING]. A UC TD 5v6 match ends on its own at ~t=420 s.
- Roof scan (x2) is sliced (400 rays/step): the [BOT-ROOFS] line appears at game t~25 s (UC, 8 roofs) / ~49 s (NRC, 46 roofs); no load stall.
- NRC CTF pathslice jobs 2704 per 300 s (0.82 plans/bot/s) vs 4243 on c44d849; vtolpads always skips the enemy pad (picks = skip_enemy), vtpad heal runs <= 2.9 s.
- Pre-existing: bot ticks of 70-200 ms carrying ~6000 rays occur 9-20 times per 300 s, identical with surprises ON or OFF.

### Easy wins B11: recompiled-code hazards and the frame clock (branch ew-b11, 2026-10-30)
- Frame clock: 0x4E2428 = scaled frame dt (double s), 0x4E2440 = game clock (double s), 0x4E2430 = ftol(game clock*1000), 0x4E2424 = per-frame integer-ms step = ftol(dt*MEMD(0x493B58)). Producers sub_0001DD80/DDB4/DE70 (recomp_0001.c:11376/11464/11642); sub_0001DD00 (clock init) zeroes the step. sub_00160DF4/00160E76 (recomp_0036.c) snapshot/restore all of them.
- Truncating the step loses game time at every frame rate: measured 85-86 % of real time at ~250 fps (menus/attract) and 96 % at ~90 fps (UC TD 5v6). ma2_ms_step_carry (recomp_manual.c) carries the fraction: 100.0 % in both runs over 300 s ([MS-CARRY] lines, RECOMP_MS_CARRY_STATS=1). Switch: [Display] FrameClockCarry=1 (default), env RECOMP_MS_CARRY=0/1. No fps cap.
- Loading screens run above 1000 fps: in the first 10 s of a match 5,392 truncated steps were 0 ms (4,914 with the carry, which still gives 0/1 steps whose mean is exact).
- The prebuilt recomp_0001.c.obj is the copy (it has the rumble-pause code at ~19081); `generated recomp_0001.c (made at install time, not in the repository)` lacks it. 0065/0075/0086 are identical in both trees.
- CRT cos/sin/acos/asin (recomp_0077.c sub_0030C659/0030C709/0030A43D/0030C4D5) now take the NaN/Inf path from `eax & 0x7FF00000` (the ZF of _fload_withFB sub_00310AB5/00310AF8 was lost across the call). RECOMP_CRT_SPECIAL_TEST=1 self-test: +-Inf gives FFF8000000000000, NaN passes through, cos(1)/sin(1)/asin(1) are exact, stack and FPU balanced.
- The newly reachable special path: Inf loads the indefinite NaN (0x4A03A8) with eax=1 (_DOMAIN); NaN goes through sub_00310A9C (tests the quiet bit, eax & 0x80000), then, unless 0x4CDDF4 is set, sub_00310A33 (_startOneArgErrorHandling, op 0x12 for cos). Before B11.1 these handlers were never called.
- CPU probes: sub_00334C40 (MMX, render init) and sub_002E0F4C (HasSSE via sub_002E0FBA) are native in recomp_manual.c (lifts kept as *_unused_lift); results unchanged (MMX 0, HasSSE 0), no ebx/esp corruption. sub_0026D650 and sub_002E4180 pin edx/ebx/ecx to 0 before the no-op cpuid. sub_0026D650 runs 7 times per boot (movie path); the stale edx never had the MMX/SSE bits ([CPUID-PIN] never printed), so the pin changes nothing observed.
- Audio spins bounded: NEW_VOICE waits (recomp_0096.c 0x3AEA7F, 0x3AF1D4) and the XACT packet 0x103 wait (recomp_0098.c 0x3E51DB) give up after 250 ms with [VOICE-NEW-WAIT]/[XACT-WAIT] (RECOMP_AUDIO_WAIT_MS, 0 = unbounded). 0 such lines in a 5-minute 5v6 match.

- ma2_bot_nav.c: every grid epoch bump (tg_epoch_bump) logs the changed cell rectangle (64-entry ring); ma2_trav_changed_since(epoch, world rect) tells a bot or a queued A* whether a commit touched cells near its route. ctrl_route_stale (ctrl.c) replaces the blanket "epoch" replan; pq_step restarts a search only if the change is within 50 m of its from/to box.
- A destroyed building's reprobe (r=22 m, ~380 cells x 16 rays, ~6000 rays, 70-180 ms in one step) is now sliced (ma2_trav_reprobe_begin/step, 3 ms per step, RECOMP_BOT_WRECK_MS, switch WreckSlice) and committed once; UC 300 s: worst bot tick 18.4 ms, no tick above ~850 rays, 0 HITCH lines after 60 s.
- A grid commit (2 chamfers + 2 component floods, whole grid) costs 9 ms on UC and up to 24 ms on NRC; a stall used to do up to 3 (reprobe, wall_sweep, turrets_reapply), now one (StallBatch). NRC stall ticks of 20-54 ms remain (830-ray reprobe + commit).
- g_flagged[24] (body_drive'd vehicle actors) is cleared in runtime_free_level, and ai_drive_sweep frees slots whose actor is unmapped or not a MAMover ([C7] safety flag_stale = 14-20 per match).
- Safety: NaN axis/point guards in ctrl_send_frame, body_moveto, body_steer and the VTOL altitude write; nearest_in clamps its start cell (a 1e7 m query no longer runs millions of rings); ma2_pathq_reset at level free.

### Two riders and close-range hacks (2026-11-01)
- **VtolTwoRiders** (`RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_TWO_RIDERS` / `[Bots] VtolTwoRiders`, on): the VTOL holds (VtolMuster) while fewer than two ride, the player first, also on its own flag run at pickup/inbound 400 m+ from their flag; with one aboard `lift_hold` hovers for the second (bot 10.5 m, player 12 m ahead) or fetches the run's BattleArmor within 150 m; the second rider becomes `g_frun[n].ba2`, drops at their flag, goes for it, and whichever takes the flag is flown home. Proof: [BOT-TWORIDERS] carries two (player + bot) in tests wa2r3 and wa2r4, both captured.
- BattleArmor side: no muster boarding for a hop under 150 m (claw on/off loop every 2 s at our stand after a capture).
- **BaHackClose** (`RECOMP_BOT_BA_HACK_CLOSE` / `[Bots] BaHackClose`, on): an enemy 'Mech within 25 m is rolled for once per encounter, Recruit 45 / Regular 60 / Veteran 75 / Elite 85 %, +15 against the player (cap 95); a win = hack utility 1.4. [BOT-HACKROLL], [C7] bahackclose.
- Test hooks: `RECOMP_TEST_BOT_BA`, `RECOMP_TEST_BOT_VTOL` (bot index), `RECOMP_TEST_HFERRY_REACH=1`.
- Pre-existing, seen in the tests: VtolWaitPlayer restarts a player run every tick while the VTOL is below the give-up health (started_player 13 / ends_damaged 11 in wa2r4): its start test has no health check.

### VTOL air routes, map edges and BattleArmor flee (91392af, 2026-11-01)
- **VtolLaneRoute** (`RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_LANE_ROUTE` / `[Bots] VtolLaneRoute`, on): VTOL legs of 150 m+ are an A* on a 20 m air grid (walk-grid surface, highest per cell): length x lane factor x (1 + height over the start/goal height / K) + 2 per metre climbed, pulled tight where a cut stands no more than `slack` over the cells it replaces. Deliverance ferries now follow the valley (median 28-36 m, was 104-107 m over the middle hill); Bogged Down's plateau ferry stays near-straight (848 m vs 834 m). `[BOT-VROUTE]`, `[C7] vtlane`.
- **VtolRouteVary** (`RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_ROUTE_VARY`, on): per flight K 45-90, favoured lane, smooth +-35% cost field (160 m lattice), slack, cruise band; seeded per match/bot/flight. `[C7] vtvary`.
- **VtolEdgeKeep** (`RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_EDGE_KEEP`, on): the MATerrainInfo type map (key 1F1646EA) read at run time like sub_F7AC7 -> sub_189E62 -> sub_1899C6 -> sub_2674A0 (TI [0x50C8E0], layer [TI+0x84], picture [layer+0xC], base +0x4C, bpp +0x24, pitch +0x50, size +0x58/+0x5C). Routes never cross out-of-bounds (1) cells and keep 25 m off; band (2) cells cost x1.5 (Bogged Down marks inner cliff faces 2); goals on 1 cells are pulled ; fight hide/slide spots keep off. `RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_EDGE_DUMP=1` prints the map. `[BOT-VEDGE]` per-flight closest approach, `[C7] vtedge`.
- The invisible wall is at the **2/1 edge** and holds at any height (VTOL stopped at x 590-600 at 100-111 m on Deliverance's hill). Deliverance's middle hill is all type 1.
- **BaHackFlee** (`RECOMP_BOT_BA_HACK_FLEE`, on): an enemy BattleArmor inside 18 m of a bot 'Mech is a 26 m hazard in ctrl_bomb_escape with the death blast's reaction by skill; not once clamped on. `[C7] bahackflee`.
- Test scenarios (not tracked): `IllWind_Test.ma2map` (editor copies of the stock maps, CTF ticked).



### Facts

- **Surprise behaviours go through one rarity gate, sp_roll** [code-confirmed] ma2_bot_surprise.c sp_roll_p is the only way a surprise trick starts. Order: trick switch (master RECOMP_BOT_SURPRISE / [Bots] Surprises, then RECOMP_BOT_SP_<NAME> / Sp<Name>); 20 s hold-off per bot per trick; per-bot cooldown (cool_min x 0.7-1.3); the random roll p[skill]; per-victim budget (2 per rolling 600 s, per trick); no same trick on the same victim back-to-back (not applied to side keys 0xFFFF0000|nation); 45 s spacing per victim. Counters go to [C7] sp_all (rolls, blocked_cool/budget/repeat/spacing, victim_human, trick_s, bot_s, tick_ms). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SURPRISE=0 turns every surprise off (A/B arm). RECOMP_BOT_SP_FORCE=revenge,grudge,mood,rookie|all makes p=1 and skips cooldown/budget/repeat/spacing (trigger conditions still apply). — ma2_bot_surprise.c:162
- **Killer of a player = the scoreboard kill (stat 2) that went up within 1 s** [code-confirmed] sp_world_tick diffs each slot's kills/deaths once per frame, keeps a ring of kill events and death events, and matches each death with the nearest unused enemy kill within +-1 s (an enemy by nation in team modes). A death with no kill after 0.4 s is resolved with an unknown killer. Position of the victim is its last live position. Same attribution idea as hg_kills (high ground). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SP_DIAG_KILLER=1 logs [SP-KILL] per death with victim and killer slots. — ma2_bot_surprise.c:222
- **Revenge on a teammate's killer (12)** [code-confirmed] A bot that sees a teammate die within 80 m (inside its field of view and a budgeted ray clear) rolls; the first witness to pass becomes the avenger for 30 s. The killer's target score is x1.3/1.5/1.8/2.0 by skill, the hunt pick weighs him x8 and always hunts, and an knowledge entry is injected at the death spot. Not for pilots on foot, objective locks or vehicle trips. C7 sp_revenge: witnessed, fired_<skill>, found (killer visible within 15 s), avenged, avenger_died. Forced run: 9 witnessed, 9 fired, 8 found. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SP_REVENGE=0 / [Bots] SpRevenge=0 — ma2_bot_surprise.c:286
- **Grudge: same killer twice within 5 min** [code-confirmed] On our death the killer is stored; a second death to the same player within 300 s rolls a grudge. After the next spawn, for 60 s that player's target score is x1.3-1.9 and his hunt weight x2; an entry is seeded at the killer's position. Ends on a kill of him (paid_back), our next death, or 60 s. C7 sp_grudge: armed, fired_<skill>, paid_back, expired, grudge_s_sum, grudge_kills, grudge_alive_s. Forced run (first death arms): 37 fired, 3 paid back (8 %), so the spec's 25 % payback line is not met by this mild bias. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SP_GRUDGE=0 / [Bots] SpGrudge=0 — ma2_bot_surprise.c:318
- **Momentum mood: HOT after 3 kills, COLD after 3 deaths** [code-confirmed] One roll per streak (the kill/death that makes streak 3; COLD waits for the respawn), p 0.5/0.45/0.35/0.25, budget key per side. 60 s. HOT: aggr +0.25, retreat_hp x0.8, flank chance x1.5 (flank_try), fight_band x0.85. COLD: caution +0.3, retreat_hp x1.2, G_COVER floor 0.92 when hurt (<75 %) and under fire. HOT ends on death, COLD on a kill. Deltas are applied to b->aggr/caution/sk.retreat_hp and subtracted at the end. C7 sp_mood: hot_/cold_<skill>, hot_/cold_/base_ kills, deaths, seconds, attack and cover seconds. RECOMP_BOT_SP_MOOD_STREAK=2 shortens the streak for tests. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SP_MOOD=0 / [Bots] SpMood=0 — ma2_bot_surprise.c:358
- **Rookie mistakes A-F (Recruit p 0.12, Regular 0.04)** [code-confirmed] A tunnel vision (hold the first-picked target 12 s, choose_target hook), B ignore flanks (look_start skipped for 10 s, ends at 25 % health lost), C straight lines (Ma2Order.sp_straight: ctrl_fight lateral=0, dodge off, no peek_search; 12 s), D fire out of range (Ma2Order.sp_far: ctrl_fire weapon range x1.4; 8 s; triggered when the target is just beyond the shortest gun group), E chase a visible VTOL (10 s), F re-target whoever hit last (12 s). One mistake at a time per bot; ends on a heavy hit, a retreat/cover/objective goal or the target gone. C7 sp_rookie: <sub>_<skill>, died_during, mistake_s_sum, ended_time/interrupt/target/death. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SP_ROOKIE=0, or RECOMP_BOT_SP_ROOKIE_<A.F>=0 for one. RECOMP_BOT_SP_SKILL=0 makes every brain a Recruit for tests. — ma2_bot_surprise.c:384
- **C7 table limits matter for the surprise pieces** [code-confirmed] c7 allows 96 pieces and 24 counters per piece. sp_mood uses 22 counters; sp_rookie 18; adding counters to those pieces silently drops the extras. Surprise pieces: sp_all, sp_revenge, sp_grudge, sp_mood, sp_rookie. — ma2_bot_surprise.c:505
- **Time in tricks is dominated by mood and rookie episodes** [verified-in-game] With the spec's first probabilities (mood p .5/.45/.35/.25 re-rolled every 20 s, rookie p .35/.12, 120 s moods) the share of alive bot-seconds in any trick was 9-10 % in natural UC runs. Rolling mood once per streak, 60 s moods, rookie p .12/.04 and shorter episodes brought it to 3.4-4.6 %. The module's own CPU cost is about 0.02 ms per frame (tick_max under 1 ms); no frame-rate change versus OFF once other game processes are accounted for. — ma2_bot_surprise.c:505

Compare only runs that had no other game running, or use the module's own tick_ms. — ma2_bot_surprise.c:505

Those points sit on a hard-blocked cliff mass (free ground x<=368; mesa 47-49 m high at 450,1356). Stall recovery (ma2_bot_ctrl.c ~2150) hops up again, the bot ends about 27 m up in a pocket with path=0/0, and trapped-bail ejects it after 4 stalls (BOT-TRAPPED). Deterministic at 384,1168 in 4 of 4 base (c44d849) NRC CTF runs. PathSlice made the no-route window common.

- **VtolLaneRoute: VTOL long legs planned on a 20 m air grid (valley/lane following, no gratuitous climbs)** [verified-in-game] In a playtest (11-01) Deliverance VTOLs climbed high over the hill instead of following the valleys. Legs of 150 m+ are planned by an A* on a 20 m grid built once a match from the walk grid's surface (highest per cell): cost = length x lane factor (0.9 on a lane, 0.75 on the flight's favoured lane) x (1 + height over max(start, goal height)/K) + 2 per metre climbed, then pulled tight where the straight cut stands no more than `slack` over the cells it replaces. A goal on a plateau costs nothing extra (Bogged Down ferry 848 m vs 834 m straight); a wide high crossing costs about a 1.5x valley detour. Routes needing a climb past a learned cap or 90 m still take the ground route; short legs stay VtolTerrainClimb's straight line. Before: Deliverance VTOLs at 104-107 m over the hill (max_y 107.6, ground_tall 25 a match); after: ferries along the valley at a median 28-36 m, flag runs completed inbound -> grab -> extract with the rider on. Plans cost 1-2.6 ms max. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_LANE_ROUTE=0 / [Bots] VtolLaneRoute=0 restores the straight leg. RECOMP_BOT_DIAG: [BOT-VROUTE] per plan (straight vs route length, hi400, closest edge, roll, points). - **SUPERSEDED: a bot VTOL ferrying a bot BattleArmor crawled 4-9 m/s at full stick -- NOT the height ceiling; real cause = stale AI forward speed (see vtol-ferry-stale-ai-forward-speed)** [verified-in-game] CORRECTION 2026-11-10: the 2026-11-04 "height ceiling" resolution was wrong. Real cause: the AI MoveTo of the rider pick-up hover left a forward-speed target on the flight comp (comp+0x98 = -53.4 m/s), and the body integrator sub_002AD940 adds heading x that ground speed to the stick flight velocity, so 60 m/s forward on the stick became ~6 m/s. Fixed in v26-vtol b91f768 (vtol_stick_take, StickSpeed0). Original observation kept: e1c20284, Bogged Down weB0, bot 10 (team 1) flew a bot rider (bot 6, BattleArmor, ord idle, ctl=attack, firing at a target) toward 495,903: stick branch, thr 1.00, err 0-3 deg, no climb demand (c90 0), y held at 47.2 (that match's max_y so far), speed 3.6-9.6 m/s from t=14 to ~79 s. Other bot-rider ferries flew 40-106 m/s. Cause not found; suspects: the rider's attack state pulling on the clamp, or a height cap. [BOT-VCRAWL] missed it because the speed jittered over 9 m/s; it now uses a 1.5 s smoothed speed. RESOLVED 2026-11-04: 47.2 m was Bogged Down's stick-flight ceiling there (terrain height + MaxVTOLHeight 55 - ~6.6; the stick cannot climb further), so the ferry at full stick could only press on level, slowed by whatever stood ahead at that height (cause inferred from the same picture; the ceiling and its terrain dependence measured 11-04). Fixed by StickCeil (the planner knows the ceiling) and RiderRay (real collision rays at ceiling - 9 m shut the way); see facts ctfvtol-maxvtolheight, ctfvtol-tall-areas. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:2393

The planner's up-link limit is jet_gain-2 where jet_gain is learned from ground hops (9-15 m); measured full-tank burns (fuel 2.0): BA median 16.9 m, p90 18.5 m, best 34.5 m ([BOT-JETGAIN] over the 30-cell sweep). So a BA that stepped into a canal planned no way out (sw62 bot 4 stayed 127 s until it died; navfix.end_hold_frames 13601). g_upx = max(g_up+4, 20) now bounds the up-link search; a link taller than g_up costs +40 (PATH_UP_STRETCH_PEN), so ramps and plain jet-ups still win; the plan_begin 'higher goal' test no longer needs the goal within 150 m when it is 6 m+ up. RECOMP_BOT_UP_STRETCH / [Bots] UpStretch; counter upstretch.links. sw62 end_hold_frames 13601 -> 5744, pathcap.hits 40 -> 7, no_path spans 7 -> 3.
- **PitPartial: a search that ran dry never ends its partial route on a one-way drop landing** [inferred] plan_run keeps best0 = the reached cell nearest the goal without a drop link (S.ow[] marks cells reached through one). When the heap runs dry and the goal was not found (not capped), plan_finish ends the route at best0 instead of the overall nearest cell. Before, a BA planned a drop 35 m into a gully 22 m from a roof powerup (sw14, 223-240 s, hp 350) and stood there. A best0 equal to the start gives a one-point route at the start (the controller holds and reports no path) rather than the raw line to the goal. RECOMP_BOT_PIT_PARTIAL / [Bots] PitPartial; counter pitpartial.replaced.
- **PocketDrop: a body on a small raised island (pilot on a 2-cell ledge top, tank on a tactical move) re-plans with a 40 m drop limit** [inferred] Proving Ground has 2-cell ledge tops at y=174 inside blocked terrain, 25-35 m above the ground (NAV-REGION dump, region 340,420,740,720). Pilots (drop limit 10 m) and tanks on a tactical move (limit 0) explored those few cells, found no goal, and stood still (sw33 bots 0 and 9: 21-43 s). A search that ran dry over < 40000 cells with the nearest reached cell > 30 m from the goal is restarted once with g_drop = 40 (second pass, new generation stamps, obstacles re-marked). RECOMP_BOT_POCKET_DROP / [Bots] PocketDrop; counter pocketdrop.restarts. The routes now exist (sw33: pilot with have_path 1 and a 2.6 m end gap) but the pilot's step-off walk (ctrl drop leg / RaisedGuard) can still stand still on the edge: execution is in ma2_bot_ctrl.c.
- **ma2_path_same_ground(a, b, heavy): is b on a's walkable region (no drop or jet link)? 1 / 0 / -1 unknown** [inferred] Added to ma2_bot_path.c / ma2_bot_api.h in the 1.0 pass. Compares the grid's connected-component ids at the two points (nearest walkable cell within 8 m). A roof powerup (In Your Face 793,805,y18: mech held 27 s at its foot) or a pickup in another pocket returns 0, so the brain can skip it. Not yet called from the brain.

Mechs/tanks board from anywhere inside r (dz up to 4.9 of 6.8). BattleArmor: the successes (sw14 dz 0.8, sw63 dz 0.7) stood within 1 m of the centre; every failure (sw30/34 pre-fix 3.7-3.8 of r 4.0, sw30 after BoardDeep 2.0) stood further out. The BA zone is centred on the BA (entry-hull 0 m) and the planner keeps the pilot a hull outline (1.8 m) off it, so the pilot never reaches the 1 m. Brain: BaEnterBan bans BA 150 s for the pilot after one failure and for the roster after 2 failures with 0 BA boardings ([C7] baenterban ba_fails / ba_boarded). Open for ctrl: walk a pilot into the BA centre. Two tanks (02121070, 02134850 on In Your Face) refused pilots at 1.5 m of a 6.1 m-offset entry in all runs. *How:* Read before changing BA pilot boarding. — ma2_bot_brain.c:
- **HopOut: a dry search for a jet body gets a third pass with wall hops and steep-face climbs** [inferred] ma2_bot_path.c plan_run: when pass 1 (and PocketDrop pass 1) ends dry 10 m+ short of the goal and the body has jets (g_up>0), pass 2 (st->boost==2, <=50000 expansions) adds one-way jet-up legs (drop kind 2) from any surface: a hop over a blocked band <=12 m whose tops <= start+g_up-1, onto ground 60 m down.stretched climb up; or a climb up a face <=28 m that never rises above the landing. Cases: sw81 Ill Wind yard (raised built platform with rim colliders: no drop from built ground, goal 112 m, 48.6 s no_path), sw54 Proving Ground mesa behind a 10 m low-wall band, sw85 Rush Hour 25 m plateau over a 45-degree embankment (heavy-blocked by slope, 2 m rise per 2 m cell). A goal the pass failed to reach is memoised 20 s per start ground region. Switch RECOMP_BOT_HOP_OUT, counters hopout.* (links, climbs, found, failed, memo_skips). LinkFoot (RECOMP_BOT_LINK_FOOT) inserts the start cell centre as pt[0] for kind-2 first legs. Plain drops (kind 1) from the start cell are not changed (walking at the landing steps off anyway).

## Mission start vehicles

### Facts

- **A start container resolves through four templates before the body** [code-confirmed] MARoot has 18 StartVehicles* keys (retail, one per game type; 1F13DE84 is StartVehiclesGeneric, the one single player uses). Each holds an MAPlayerConfigurationContainer UID. Its child MoeEntityReference (ReferenceUID) names an MAPlayerConfiguration. The config holds CameraTemplateUID, CorporealTemplateUID and OwnerControllerTemplateUID. For vehicles and mechs the body is the MAOwnerController's MoverTemplateUID (an MAMech or MATank); the body has children MAWeaponLoadout, MAPowerupDrop and effect templates. On-foot avatar containers (123726, 123999) point through a second container to several configs (Nemesis, Alera, Pilot, Natalia, Foster) whose CorporealTemplateUID is an MAMech and whose OwnerControllerTemplateUID is 0.

The estimated graphics total of S_ba is 25.6 MB (limit ~63.5), so the memory budget is not the cause. *How:* Add to [Assets] from mission_07.mgf (or 01b/02): everything under Models/Mechs/PowerArmor/PowerArmor/Model, PilotToPowerArmor/Model, AbandonedPowerArmor plus the two .node files; from mission_13a.mgf (or 05): every VMil_RommelMK2.MGMODEL entry with its {sub-buffer} entries. - **Rule for which containers a scenario Base can start in** [verified-in-game] 1) The Base's culled set is irrelevant (templates come from the full GlobalEntities). 2) A container is usable if every model file its chain names, by the exact template path, is mounted: in the Base .mgf, common.mgf or the scenario's [Assets]. - **Containers valid for a mission_09b scenario** [inferred] Verified in game (playtest): 123999 Low Rez Avatar (foot) and 124698 Stiletto work; 124001 BA, 124052 Rommel fail (and 125894 NearClip BA, same chain, fails). Vehicle-type containers (Rommel variants 125370 and 126165, VTOL 124051, Turret 124334, Elemental 125292) need the same fix as BA/Rommel plus the enter sequence.
