- **How to compute valid start containers for any Base** [verified-in-game] For Base B: build the mounted set M = files of B.mgf + common.mgf + the scenario's [Assets] (case-insensitive, backslash equals slash). For each MAPlayerConfigurationContainer U in GlobalEntities, walk U -> child MoeEntityReference.ReferenceUID -> config(s) -> CameraTemplateUID, OwnerControllerTemplateUID, CorporealTemplateUID and the alternate camera UIDs -> mover (owner controller MoverTemplateUID) -> every UID-valued property and every child (weapon loadouts, drops, effects, destroyed corporeals). Collect the string properties Corporal3DObj, TransitionModel, AbandonedModel and effect models. U is usable when every exact path is in M; otherwise list the missing files so the editor can add them from the first retail archive that has them (high-detail names live in mission_xx.mgf, low-detail ones in multiplayer maps). The culled set of B can be ignored. Practical shortcut: restrict the start picker to ControlBehavior 0 and 2 containers whose body Corporal3DObj is in M, and offer BA and vehicles only once the exact files are added.

<a id="t14b_start_vehicle_logs"></a>

## Mission start vehicles: run-log evidence

### Facts

- **Bad start vehicles first differ at the in-mission camera: no owner, unknown class** [inferred] All four runs are identical through the menu, Custom Scenarios hub, scenario mount and mission_09b resource redirect (no errors, no 'not found', no assert, no fault, no exception in any of them; every run ends only with a WM_CLOSE exit). The first difference is the camera line printed when the mission's view is first drawn. Good runs (Stiletto, on-foot) print 'cam=. Third owner=<player object> target=3E800000'. Bad runs (Battle Armor, Rommel) print 'cam=. ? owner=00000000 target=30000000' (Battle Armor) or 'target=00000000' (Rommel): the camera class is not one of the known camera vtables and it has no owner. The mission loaded and the vehicle HUD loaded, so the failure is after template load, in attaching a camera/controller to the new player.
- **CAM-WATCH lines, good vs bad, quoted** `0046D348`, `0046D208` [code-confirmed] Stiletto: '[CAM-WATCH] t=0.0 view=0227FB40 vvt=00463518 cam=0227F940 Third owner=01991560 target=3E800000'. On foot: '. cam=02266E10 Third owner=011452A0 target=3E800000'. Battle Armor: '[CAM-WATCH] t=0.0 view=022BB570 vvt=00463518 cam=022BB370 ? owner=00000000 target=30000000'. Rommel: '. view=022C1800 cam=022C1600 ? owner=00000000 target=00000000'. The label comes from cam_vt_name in ma2_bots_core.c, which knows Third 0046D348, First 0046D208 and others; '?' means the camera's vtable is none of them. The line after it (BOT-TRACE site=30) shows the player object (a=) exists in all four runs. — ma2_bots_core.c:3301
- **[CAM-SET] fires only in the bad runs** `000C9084`, `000C9113`, `0016B2F1` [inferred] Both bad runs log exactly one '[CAM-SET] t=0.0 slot=1 table=0052A280 cam=. cls=7594AFD6 owner=. caller=000C92DA' just before the camera-watch line. Neither good run has a CAM-SET line at all. Caller 000C92DA is the vehicle-camera block (sub_C9084/sub_C9113) that installs a camera into the player's screen slot. cls=7594AFD6 is not the third-person (7ECA8E3B) or first-person (C8894008) class named in the wiki, and the CAM-WATCH camera (cam=.370/600) is a different object from the CAM-SET camera (cam=.3E0/670). So for Battle Armor and Rommel a different camera class is built and installed, and the camera the view draws from has no owner. Not refused as a bot camera (no '(BOT: refused)' suffix). Which class 7594AFD6 is and why the owner field stays 0 is not yet known. Note: CAM-SET only prints when RECOMP_BOT_DIAG is set, so the good runs having none means the call never ran or was not logged; not checked whether DIAG was on in them (it must have been, since the same binary printed it for the bad runs, but verify).
- **HUD form set follows the vehicle type; the vehicle is created in the bad runs** [inferred] After the mission mounts, the HUD forms loaded show the player's vehicle type was resolved. Stiletto and on-foot load HUD_Blank, FS_Rocket, FS_Pilot, FS_Mech, HUD_Text, TimeLimit. Battle Armor loads FS_Rocket, FS_Pilot, FS_Mech, FS_PowerArmor, HUD_Text, TimeLimit. Rommel loads FS_Rocket, FS_Pilot, FS_Mech, FS_Mover, FS_Sniper_Zoom, HUD_Text, TimeLimit. So the container UIDs 124001 and 124052 resolve to real templates and their vehicle HUDs are built; the template is found. The bad runs do not fail on a missing UID.
- **Player look/mouse component never replaced in the bad runs** [inferred] Good runs log 17 '[MOUSE-DIAG] look component=.' lines; after the mission starts the look component changes from the menu's 01C4DC80 to a new one (022A79C0 in the Stiletto run, line 1439), i.e. a player control component is created. The bad runs log only one look line (the menu one, ST_ba line 990, ST_rommel line 1036) and every later 'context mapping' line still shows component=01C4DC80. No player look/control component ever exists, consistent with a player with no controller-owned camera and no HUD.
- **The bad-run stderr has no error, assert or fault text** [inferred] A grep of the four stderr files for fault, exception, assert, not found and MISSING finds only the usual ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND for TDATA contentmeta.xbx (line 513 ST_ba, same in all four, harmless). The scenario assets mount reports 'ok' and '0 missing' (ST_rommel 909). The bad runs are therefore a silent logic failure; more evidence needs a trace on the camera install (sub_C9084/sub_C9113) or the player-controller attach, not just stderr.
- **Run setup and what differs between the four runs** [documented] All four use the same base mission (mission_09b.mgf, scenario 629EFA27 'test', Custom Scenarios entry 0) and identical pc_settings.ini sizes; only the scenario assets .mgf hash differs (_8A1AA11C ba, _D9B52BDE rommel, _2916A1C1 stil and foot). Autostart reaches 'in the mission' at 73 s in each. The only commands sent are key 87, two clicks and close.

<a id="t15_editor_render_gaps"></a>

## Editor rendering gaps: what the scenario editor shows differently from the game (2026-10-21)

## Editor rendering gaps

### Ranked gaps

1. **Terrain detail textures** (47 of 60 worlds, every mission and MP map). The editor draws the colour map and lightmap only. The game multiplies two tiled detail textures (picked per pixel by the colour map's alpha) and two micro-detail textures over it. All data is in MATerrain plus Terrain/*.tif in the level archive. Painting textures = painting the colour map's alpha.
2. **Water material** (23 worlds). The water model's `<material_water>` has a wave texture, a sky reflection map, wave/distort factors, fresnel and deep/shallow colours. The editor draws a flat translucent tinted slab.
3. **Lighting and time of day** (all worlds; 34 are night). Ambient and directional colours and IsNightTime are ignored; everything is lit like noon.
4. **Fog** (all worlds). FogStart/End/Color and the height band are edited on the Map tab but never drawn.
5. **Model materials beyond the diffuse texture**: no reflection, animated frames, detail or emissive (self-illum); glass/chrome panels without a base texture show as white blocks.
6. **MAEffect fires/smoke** (6 worlds; Mission_02 has 11 oil fires on the crash scar): orange boxes in the editor.
7. **Culture scatter** (22 worlds): grass/bush/rock scatter generated from the MATerrainInfo culture map; not drawn (fades out by about 75 m in game).
8. **Rain and point lights**: rain in 5 worlds, MAPointLight in 27; previews missing, low priority.

Not gaps: craters and weapon scorch decals are made at run time (MAModSubObjectDecalStamp/DecalObject). The sky dome, buildings, the crashed dropship, rubble chunks and road tiles already render correctly.

### How the comparison was run

- One game at a time, quit after each.
- Data: `inspect_wdf.parse_wdf` over common.mgf `Missions/*.wdf` and `Multiplay/*.wdf`; level archives listed with `inspect_mgf.Mgf`.



### Facts

- **Gap 1: the editor draws terrain with the colour map only; the game adds two tiled detail textures and two micro-detail textures** `000F63D2`, `000F691E` [verified-in-game] Every mission and multiplayer world (47 of the 60 worlds; only 3DLobby and the space/interior cinemas leave them blank) names detail textures on MATerrain: TerrainDetailMap (89F575C2) and 'TerrainDetailMap 1' (1DF99D12), repeated TerrainDetailMult (DFD3B53D) / TerrainDetailMult1 (09699F9E) times across the map, mixed by TerrainDetailBlend (02D57475) and multiplied with the colour map when TerrainDetailModulate (215EEDCA) = 1 (50 of 60 worlds); plus close-up TerrainMicroDetailMap0/1 (FE6BA2CC / 896C925A) tiled TerrainMicroDetailTiling0/1 (9DC8435C / EACF73CA) times. The .tif files are MGIc pictures in the level archive's Terrain/ folder (Mission_02: Dante_Detail_06.tif + Dante_Detail_03.tif, repeats 64 and 96, micro Dante_Detail_03 x240, blend 0.3). The colour map's alpha channel picks between detail 1 and 2. The editor's terrain pixel shader (render.cpp tps) samples only the colour map and the lightmap, so ground that is one flat colour in the colour map (the crash site and canal banks of Mission_02, the swamp in Bogged Down) shows as flat olive/green, while the game shows cracked, scorched earth. *How:* Load the four .tif paths from MATerrain with the editor's existing MGIc decoder (core/mgic.cpp), bind them beside the colour map and in tps: d = lerp(detail1(uv*Mult), detail2(uv*Mult1), colormap.a); col = Modulate ? colormap.rgb * lerp(1, d*2, Blend): colormap.rgb + (d-0.5)*Blend; then the micro layer near the camera. The exact NV2A combiner formula is not traced; check against the game with a side-by-side shot. — render.cpp:68
- **Gap 2: water is a flat tinted quad in the editor; the game draws an animated, reflective material_water** `0004EC40`, `0004EB90` [verified-in-game] MAWater objects (57 in 23 worlds) point Corporal3DObj at a water MGMODEL whose material is <material_water>: wavetexture (e.g. Texture_Dump\Environment\Water\Water_006_NewWater.tif), reflectiontexture (an EnvMaps\EnvMap_Sky_*.tif matching the sky), wave_factor 0.85, distort_factor 0.85, fresnel_min 0.77 / fresnel_max 1.0, deep_color 100,122,101, shallow_color 137,137,97, spec_color, shin_strength (Env_Water1000x1000_CityNight in Mission_02). The game scrolls/distorts the wave texture and blends the sky reflection by fresnel, so the Mission_02 canal is dark, rippled water reflecting the night sky. The editor (app.cpp ~1103) draws a 0.5 m box the size of the model's bbox in one hard-coded colour chosen by model name, alpha 0xA0, with no texture and no animation: a light-green slab with the grid showing through. The material_water parser is sub_0004EC40 (recomp_0008.c, reads shallow_color.wavetexture); sub_0004EB90 matches the 'material_water' tag. *How:* Parse <material_water> from the model (the ma2m loader already lists wavetexture and reflectiontexture slots, models/src/model.cpp kTextureSlots) and draw water with its own shader: two scrolling samples of the wave texture (time * small speed, scaled by wave_factor) perturb the UV of the reflection map (distort_factor); colour = lerp(shallow, deep, fresnel) + reflection * lerp(fresnel_min, fresnel_max, 1 - N.V). Keep the bbox-sized plane (dictionary MAWater rule). — app.cpp:1103
- **Gap 3: the editor ignores the level's light colours and night setting; everything is lit by a white sun** `00124CC1`, `0012FB98`, `00130290` [verified-in-game, superseded] SUPERSEDED (v249, t16 survey): the editor now draws game lighting (View > Game lighting); see t16-map-terrain-env-surprise-8. MAEnvironment carries LightAmbientColor, DirectionalLightColor, DirectionalLightOn, IsNightTime (1 in 34 of 60 worlds), EnableMechDarken, ShadowColor, EnableShadows and EnvironmentMapName. Mission_02: ambient FF1B213B (dark blue), directional FF4E3F34 (dim brown), night 1. In game the city is dark blue with lit windows; Bogged Down is a dim, hazy dusk. The editor's terrain shader uses nl = 0.45 + 0.55*N.L (or the baked lightmap) and the model shader 0.5 + 0.5*N.L with white light, so both maps look like noon. The Night/Sun controls on the Map tab change the saved data only. Readers: MAEnvironment field list at 0x124CC1 (dictionary); MAEnvState (+sub) readers 0x0012FB98 / 0x00130290 (recomp_0030.c) hold the live fog/directional state. CORRECTION 2026-10-24: sub_0012FB98/sub_00130290 are MAEnvState's load/save serializers, not live state. *How:* Feed ambient and directional colour (and the sun direction already shown) into both shaders' constant buffer: col = tex * (ambient + directional * N.L * lightmap); darken by IsNightTime only through those colours, as the game does. Add self-illum (gap 5) so windows and road lights still glow at night. — render.cpp:71
- **Gap 4: no distance or height fog in the editor view** `0012FB98`, `00130290` [verified-in-game] Every world sets FogMode (1 = linear in most, 2 in 7 worlds), FogStart/FogEnd (Mission_02 149-223 m, Bogged Down 175-450 m), FogColor and a height band FogBottom/FogTop. The game fades distant terrain and models into FogColor (Bogged Down horizon is hazy grey-green); the editor's Map tab edits these values but neither viewport shader applies fog, so far hills are sharp and bright. *How:* Add linear fog by view distance (FogStart.FogEnd) plus the height band to the terrain, model and water shaders; give the view a 'game fog' toggle so editing at long range stays possible. FogMode 2's exact curve (exponential?) is not traced. — render.cpp:68
- **Gap 5: model materials are drawn with the diffuse texture only (no reflection, detail, animation or self-illum)** [code-confirmed] The ma2m loader reads basetexture, detailtexture, multitexture, cubetexture, wavetexture, distortiontexture, normal_map and reflectiontexture slots and the frames of animated textures ('X 01.tif', 'X 02.tif'.), but the editor's model cache (model_cache.cpp ~157) uploads only diffuse_texture plus a colour of diffuse*tint + selfillum, and skips distortion meshes. Effects seen: Mission_02's video billboards are frozen on frame 0 (they animate in game); window and road light strips are not emissive at night; parts of 'Mechs and pads in Bogged Down (glass/chrome panels whose material has no base texture) draw as flat white blocks. *How:* Bind the reflection texture as a sphere/env map (or the level's EnvironmentMapName) for reflective materials, cycle animated frames by time, add selfillum as emissive after lighting, and multiply detailtexture where present. The white-panel cause is inferred from the code path (material without diffuse texture -> white colour); confirm by dumping the material of one white mesh. — model_cache.cpp:157
- **Gap 6: MAEffect fires and smoke are orange 2 m boxes in the editor** [verified-in-game] MAEffect objects play a particle model: Mission_02 has 11 'BD HES OilFire 01' (SpecialEffects\Environment\Env_HES_OilFire_01) along the crash scar; NoMansLand 7, Mission_15 5, Cinema_1_3 21, Cinema_4_6 11. In game they are burning flames with smoke. The editor (app.cpp ~1095) draws a fixed 2x2x2 orange box. Particle systems live .mgparticle files beside the model. *How:* Short term: draw a billboard flame icon sized like the effect's bounds; better: a simple sprite emitter using the model's particle texture. Do not try to run the game's particle code. — app.cpp:1095
- **Gap 7: culture scatter (grass, bushes, small rocks) is not drawn** [inferred, superseded] SUPERSEDED (v249, t16 survey): the editor now draws ground scatter (View > Ground scatter); see t16-map-terrain-env-surprise-8. 22 worlds (BoggedDown, NoMansLand, ProvingGround, UnderCover, WitchCauldron, TroubledWaters, Missions 03/05/06a/07/08/09A/09b/12/13a/13b/14/15, SPDemoMission and 3 cinemas) scatter small objects at run time: MATerrainInfo's culture map (key 89FB5118) says where, MACultureSystem > MACultureType > MACultureGenerator says what (GenerationTemplate, e.g. Bogged Down 'Env_Grass' template 36018, Density 800, GridScale 10x10, RandomScaleRange 0.25, AlignWithSlope 1, StartFade 0 / StopFade 75 m). The editor keeps the map but draws nothing. Because the scatter fades out by ~75 m it matters only for close views. *How:* Generate the same scatter on load (seeded, per culture-map cell, Density per GridScale cell) and draw it instanced with the template's model, fading at StopFade. The Density unit and the culture-map value -> type mapping are not confirmed in code. — scenario.cpp:147
- **Gap 8: rain and point lights are not previewed** [documented, superseded] SUPERSEDED (v249, t16 survey): the editor previews rain/snow/dust; see t16-map-terrain-env-surprise-9. Rain: EnableRain 1 with PrecipEffectID 31780 in Mission_10, Mission_11a, Mission_11b, Cinema_3_1a and Cinema_3_5 (EnableLightning is 0 in every retail world). MAPointLight: 27 worlds (NoMansLand 28, Mission_13b 26, Mission_03 21) light nearby objects with LightColor/LightRadius; the editor shows them only as helper markers. Both are low priority next to gaps 1-4. *How:* Rain: a screen-space streak overlay when EnableRain is ticked. Lights: add up to N point lights per draw in the model/terrain shaders, using the dictionary MAPointLight rules for parent transforms.
- **Not a gap: craters and weapon scorch marks are made at run time, not stored in the level** `00143DD9`, `001A64AA` [inferred] Level archives carry decal materials (SpecialEffects/Effects_Decals/env_crater.mat, Expl_decal_shock.mat, BD_HoleDecal.mat, Texture_Dump/Scorch/*.tif) but no world object places them; they are stamped when weapons hit (MAModSubObjectDecalStamp vtable ~0x143DD9, MAModSubObjectDecalObject ~0x1A64AA). The editor should not try to show them. The Mission_02 crash scar is detail texture + rubble models + oil fires (gaps 1 and 6). *How:* Ignore runtime decals when matching the game's look; check gaps 1 and 6 instead.
- **Checked OK: sky dome, building/ship models and rubble render in the editor (roads do NOT: see road-mirror-addressing)** [verified-in-game] In Mission_02 and Bogged Down the editor draws the sky model (draw_sky), the crashed Talon dropship (MABuilding Vmil_Dropship_Talon_Ale_WS), the 37 rubble chunks with positions matching the game. CORRECTION 2026-10-21 round 2: road tiles are placed right but textured wrong (MIRROR addressing, gap road-mirror-addressing). Remaining differences on these are lighting/material ones (gaps 3 and 5). *How:* No action beyond gaps 3 and 5.
- **Colour-map alpha 255 shows TerrainDetailMap, alpha 0 shows TerrainDetailMap 1 (verified)** `004A4760`, `004A4940` [verified-in-game] In game on PC Release 5508c574, a Bogged Down copy had TerrainDetailMap = Space_Null_Terrain (black) and 'TerrainDetailMap 1' = NORthwind_Detail_04 (bright). Whole-map colour-map alpha 255 rendered black everywhere, alpha 0 rendered bright, and a painted alpha-255 cross showed black at the spawn. This matches the decoded combiner mix = lerp(T2, T1, T0.a). Detail textures from other levels also work once copied into the scenario archive under the same path. *How:* Paint the colour-map alpha to choose detail 1 (255) or detail 2 (0) per texel.
- **Road textures need MIRROR addressing; the editor wraps them, which jumbles the lanes** [verified-in-game] Road .mat files (roads/*/Models/*/Materials) set base_tiling = U_MIRROR | V_WRAP for straights and U_MIRROR | V_MIRROR for intersections and ends. The meshes depend on it: Straight60 UV U -1.1 V -11.1, Intersection_90 U 0.2 V 2.3.58, Intersection_4way U -1.15.1.15. The texture holds half a road (kerb to centre line) and is mirrored for the other half. The game trace shows the road draw with tex0 (-0.999,-11). The editor (a0414027) has only CLAMP/WRAP samplers, so each lane shows the kerb strip in its middle and the joins mismatch. *How:* Bind a D3D11 MIRROR sampler per mesh from Material.mirror_u/mirror_v (already parsed in models/src/model.cpp).
- **Road COMPLEX material: a mask texture adds emissive blue/yellow lane lights and specular** [verified-in-game] Road materials are type COMPLEX with base = Road_014.tif (256x128) and multi = Road_014_cmplx.tif (128x64), colorshift0 47,47,255 and colorshift1 255,246,80. The game combiner (trace line 2545) computes lit = lerp(envCube, base.rgb, base.a); glow = mask.g*colorshift0 + mask.b*colorshift1 (not lit); spec = mask.r*lightbuffer.a*0.698; out = 2*(V0+lightbuffer)*lit + glow + spec, then fog. The glow is the blue dashed centre line and the yellow kerb dots seen at night. *How:* Load the multi texture and add the glow after lighting in the editor's model shader.
- **How the game draws water: 5 screen-space passes with a volume normal map, a cube reflection and a GPU ripple simulation** `0004EC40` [verified-in-game] Traced in Mission_02 (PC Release, RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE). The wavetexture (Water_006_NewWater.tif) is a 32x32x32 volume normal map (MGIc flags 0x80000011 = R5G6B5 swizzled, 6 mips, user chunk /animFps:24 /filter:NormalMap:4), bound in tex mode 3D with W = frac(t*24/32) and UV = mesh UV (~0.03/m, repeats every 33 m). The reflectiontexture (EnvMap_Sky_CityNight_sm.tif) is a 6-face 16x16 cube map read with DOT_RFLCT_SPEC. Per plane, the game draws:
1. a thickness pass writing alpha only: the depth buffer is read as a texture through two LUTs, a = sat(8*(sceneDepth-waterDepth)+V0.a^2);
2. a half-res scene copy;
3. a normal pass: the wave volume is lerped with a 256x256 G8B8 ripple height field. The ripple field is simulated on the GPU by ping-pong render targets with a 4-neighbour Laplacian, and its weight is 0.847*(1-r^2);
4. a refraction pass that offsets the scene copy by N (DOT_ST);
5. a reflection and fresnel pass: R = cube(reflect), F = lerp(fresnel_max, fresnel_min, N.V);
6. a composite: lerp(sceneBehind*lerp(shallow,deep,a), 2*R*(V0*L.a+L.rgb), F*sat(4a)), then fog, with L = the 512x512 terrain light map. Night levels therefore get near-black, high-contrast animated water. *How:* Editor: sample the wave volume as the normal, the cube with reflect(-V,N), and use the composite above. Ripples can be omitted (flat when undisturbed).
- **Road centre lines and yellow caution dots come from the road material's mask, not from objects** [verified-in-game] No world object or decal places road markings. Each .road file names RWmodel (*.NODE, not shipped) and model (*_rw.node, the only road model on the disc, with no LODs). The markings are the COMPLEX material's multi mask (e.g. Road_014_cmplx.tif): mask.g*colorshift0 (47,47,255) = blue dashed centre line, mask.b*colorshift1 (255,246,80) = yellow kerb dots, added unlit after lighting (trace line 2545). Correction: the markings sit inside the final x2, out = 2*(lit + mask.g*C0 + mask.b*C1), so they are doubled (complex-glow-doubled). *How:* The editor must sample the multi mask and add the colorshift glow (spec R2-2), together with mirror addressing.
- **Lamps light the ground through a per-frame 512x512 light map built from model light nodes** [verified-in-game] Light sources are <node_light> elements inside models (light_type point/spot, light_color, light_inner/outer_radius, light_inner/outer_angle, light_priority), plus MAPointLight objects. Each has a <lightmap min_height max_height min_radius max_radius min_color max_color/> child. In Mission_02 (no MAPointLight objects), 28 Env_Highway_Light lamps (spot, 255,255,235, radius 44, splat 12-20 m over 0-15 m height) and 3 Ullers give 31 lights. Every frame the engine rebuilds a 512x512 light map (render target 00AC1000): the static lightmap times LightAmbientColor, then one additive quad per light (blend SRC_ALPHA,ONE; 64x64 L8 falloff texture; colour 0x557F7A69, roughly light_color/2 at alpha 1/3; 13.2 px wide in this frame). Terrain, water and roads sample this map. Models get per-object lighting from at most MaxAreaLightsPerObject lights. *How:* Editor 'Scene lights' preview (spec R2-4): splat the same discs into a ground light map and light models with the nearest 3 lights. The map's world scale and the falloff curve are still to be measured (RECOMP_TEX_DUMP on the falloff texture).

## Native pipeline performance: frame profile, render path, guest CPU, kernel and threading (2026-10-31)

## Native pipeline perf: guest CPU, kernel and threading (2026-10-30, P-B)

One codegen measurement was made (recomp_0048.c compiled to asm); no game was run.

### Overview

**Game logic is single-threaded by design.** MA2 creates two guest threads:
- the game itself, which the first `PsCreateSystemThreadEx` runs inline on the main thread;
- one event worker, `sub_00394790`.

**Guest code also runs on two host threads besides those two:**
- the kernel timer thread, for vblank, DPCs and timers;
- the NV2A executor, for software methods (`ma2_gpu_software_method` → `sub_004152E0`).

`RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK` is off, so all of these run in parallel. The game thread is the critical path.

**Lifted code pays two big per-instruction costs:**
1. **Guest registers are TLS memory.** `g_eax.g_edi` and the x87 stack are `__declspec(thread)`. Guest memory pointers are made from integers, so MSVC must assume a guest store can alias a register, and every register access becomes a load or a store. A `/volatile:iso` build changes nothing, so aliasing is the cause.
2. **In the bots overlay, every register-addressed access goes through `ma2_tank_scoped_pointer`.** This is the tank fixed-step clock scope. It is a range check plus a TLS flag test, and it reloads `g_xbox_mem_offset` each time.
   - Measured on recomp_0048.c: 90,736 instructions with the scoped accessor, 41,634 with the plain pointer.
   - The 59 prebuilt gen objects already use the plain pointer.

The kernel layer handles about 125k calls per second in a 6v6 match. That is not a throughput problem, but locks and the single timer thread couple audio stalls into timing.

### Key code

| Address or function | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `XBOX_PTR` / `ma2_tank_scoped_pointer` | Overlay memory accessor with the clock-scope check | `generated recomp_types.h (made at install time, not in the repository)`, `ma2_tank_step_scope.h:11` |
| `RECOMP_ICALL*` | Indirect call: 3 shared trace stores, manual lookup, flat table, kernel |  |
| `kernel_thunk_dispatch` | Every kernel call: optional guest lock, GetTickCount, counters, 2 s summary |  |
| `xbox_cs_create` / `xbox_RtlEnterCriticalSection` | Shadow guest locks, spin count 0 | `kit/source/game/src/kernel/kernel_rtl.c`, `:562` |
| `kernel_timer_thread` | 1 ms high-resolution timer → vblank (60 Hz), DPC drain, 32 timers |  |
| `nv2a_idle_wait` | Executor yield policy: `Sleep(0)` while active and for 2 ms after, then 250 µs | `kit/source/game/src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c` |
| `nv2a_gpu_wait_word` | GPU fence wait through WaitOnAddress, 2 ms bound |  |
| `ma2_ms_step_carry` | Frame clock fractional-ms carry (ew-b11) | `kit/source/game/src/recomp_manual.c` |
| `optimize_leafs.py` | Precedent: registers as locals for 2 Bink leaves | `kit/source/game/bringup/optimize_leafs.py` |

### Measurements

- **Codegen, recomp_0048.c** (build flags `/O2 /Ob2`, no `/GL`):
  - scoped accessor: 90,736 instructions, 636 KB obj;
  - plain accessor: 41,634 instructions, 416 KB obj;
  - the `/volatile:iso` asm is the same size.
- **Lifted functions:** 25,841, of which 5,245 are leaves (no call, ICALL, ITAIL or MMIO).
- **Kernel calls per second** (NRC 6v6):

| Call | Rate |
  |---|---|
| RtlLeaveCS | 51k |
| RtlEnterCS | 39k |
| KfLowerIrql | 16k |
| KfRaiseIrql | 14k |
| KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel | 2.4k |

- **Bots, median ms per second of play:**

| Item | Median | p90 |
  |---|---|---|
| Total | 119-144 | 170-187 |
| Brain | 37-41 |  |
| Ctrl | 44-55 |  |
| Rays | 21-24 |  |
| Plans | 4-20 | up to 61 |
| World view | 16-31 |  |

That is about 2 ms of a 14 ms frame.

### Planned switches (see PIPELINE-B.md; none implemented yet)

| Switch | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `[Cpu] FastCode` / `RECOMP_FASTCODE` | Fast bodies (plain pointer, local memory offset, registers as locals) |
| `[Cpu] KernelThreads=split\ | single` |
| `[Cpu] CsSpin=auto` | Critical-section spin count |
| `[Cpu] ThreadPlacement=auto\ | off` |
| `[Cpu] Nv2aWake` | WaitOnAddress executor wake |
| `[Bots] PathWorker` |  |
| `RECOMP_KERNEL_SUMMARY` | Kernel summary on demand |

Proposed test hooks:
- `RECOMP_PERF_CPU`: per-thread CPU time.
- `RECOMP_FIXED_DT` + `RECOMP_STATE_HASH`: a bit-exact A/B state hash, using the 0x50BA70 fixed-dt override (unverified).
- `[CPU-TOPO]`: the detected CPU topology.

### Open questions

- The split of game-thread time: guest code, bots, waits on the executor. This needs P-A's PROFILE.md.
- Which producer (DD80, DDB4 or DE70) is live in each mode, and whether 0x50BA70 gives a usable fixed dt for hashing.
- Whether any function called inside a tank contact scope, in a prebuilt gen file, reads the clock block. This decides whether a swap-based scope is exactly equivalent.

## Audio: APU, XAudio2 and DirectSound/XACT sync (2026-10-31, P-C)

Numbers are from `[APU-TIME]` lines in earlier runs (ewm_a/ewm_b, ew-b8 m1, wperf armA/B). No game was run.

- **Audio CPU on the the main test desktop CPU** [measured, logs]
  - GP DSP interpreter: a constant 1,527-1,640 ms per 5 s, which is 30-33% of one core (up to 36%), in menus too.
  - EP: 125-145 ms per 5 s (2.5-2.9%).
  - VP: 393-560 ms per 5 s on average (8-11%), and 986-1,904 ms at peak (20-38%) at 65-129 voices per frame (max 151).
  - That is about 2.0 µs per voice-frame. The laptop memory gives about 3 µs on an E-core, and the GP at about 54% of an E-core.
- **APU frames are GP-bound.** The DSP thread runs frame n's GP while the APU thread mixes frame n+1. The APU thread joins before each frame, so a frame takes about max(VP, GP), about 0.21 ms, until a fight passes about 100 voices. Sources: `apu_dsp_runtime.c:678` (join) and `:691` (SetEvent every frame).
- **The throttle waits only on every 8th frame** [code]. `apu_core.c:539` returns unless `ep_frame_div % 8 == 0`. So the APU runs 8 frames in a burst (about 1.7-2 ms on the desktop), then idles about 3.3 ms per 5.33 ms EP period.
- **The libsamplerate sinc is about 80% of VP time** [code + measured]. `SRC_SINC_FASTEST` (half length 2463, increment 128) uses about 38 taps per channel per output sample at ratio 1 or above. Each tap is a double coefficient interpolation plus 2 MACs. That is 1,232 taps per stereo 32-sample voice-frame, which matches the measured 2 µs.
- **`mcpx_apu_phys` is not inline** (`apu_core.c:80-89`, another translation unit). Every `voice_get_mask`/`set_mask` (about 40 per voice per frame) and every sample read in `voice_get_samples` (`apu_vp.c:1197-1416`, with a per-sample SGE page lookup) is a cross-TU call.
- **Unbounded hot spin at 0x3AA7DF** [code, new]. `recomp_0095.c:13597-13600`: after copying a DSP command block and writing the doorbell word (`ma2_register_dsp_doorbell`), the title spins with no yield until the GP program clears the word. That needs the GP's next frame, which can be a whole burst gap (about 3.3 ms). It is the last unbounded audio spin. Its call rate is unknown.
- **Every sound start waits for the VP** [code]. 0x3AEA7F and 0x3AF1D4 (`recomp_0096.c:9517`, `:11044`) wait for NEW_VOICE (PAR_STATE bit 0x100000), which `voice_get_samples` clears (`apu_vp.c:1240`) on the VP's next pass. With the burst cadence the estimated mean is about 1.2 ms and the maximum about 3.6 ms per start (unmeasured; B11.3 logs only waits of 20 ms or more). A sweep log shows 45,500-77,500 ISR voice-release attempts per In Your Face 6v6 run.
- **The XAudio2 queue sat at 3 of 4 x 1024 buffers** [measured, ewm_a 290 s]: `queued=3`, `backpressure=0`, underruns 0. So the APU loop is not blocked on the device today. Latency is about 64 ms.
- **The default VP voice_lock does not take `d->lock`.** Only `RECOMP_APU_VOICE_LOCK=frame` and the host mixer do, so `d->lock` is effectively uncontended. Voice locks run at 2,600-3,200 per second, and the title waits 0.4-0.5 ms per 5 s in them.
- **The DirectSound ISR runs on the APU thread** (`apu_core.c:143-195`), at the end of each loop iteration, with `d->lock` released. It is held off only while a thread is at IRQL 22 or above (`kernel_hal.c:145-149`).
- **The VEH APU trap calls `getenv("RECOMP_APU_TRACE")` on every trapped access**. Only recomp_0095/0096/0098 use the `ma2_store32`/`ma2_load32` fast path.
- **The exe imports `xaudio2_9.dll` statically**, so it runs on Windows 10/11 only.
- **Prior art.**
  - xemu: VP worker threads; `audio.use_dsp_jit` (default false) uses mborgerson's MIT `dsp56300` Rust/Cranelift JIT, which is hardware-differential tested.
  - Cxbx-Reloaded: DirectSound HLE on host `IDirectSound8`, with `SetEffectData`, `SetI3DL2Listener` and `SetMixBinHeadroom` stubbed. That means no DSP effects.

### Planned switches (PIPELINE-C.md; none implemented)

| Switch | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `RECOMP_AUDIO_WAIT_STATS` | `[AUDIO-WAITS]` / `[APU-WAIT]` / `[APU-VEH]` counters |
| `[Audio] ApuPacing=kick\ | smooth\ |
| `RECOMP_APU_DEVICE_CLOCK` | Throttle trimmed to the XAudio2 queue depth (±200 ppm) |
| `RECOMP_APU_VP_FAST`, `RECOMP_APU_SRC=ref\ | simd` |
| `RECOMP_APU_DSP_ENGINE=interp\ | fast\ |
| `RECOMP_APU_VP_WORKERS`, `[Audio] Threads=auto` | Order-preserving parallel VP render; one audio thread at 4 or fewer logical CPUs |

## Frame profile and render path (2026-10-31, P-A)

Profiler: branch (eace004, 820bc2b), `kit/source/game/src/pl_prof.c`; summariser. All runs were solo, through MCP `game_*`, at 3840x1600, TQ1, DrawDistance 100, uncapped, on the the main test desktop.

### Overview
- **The game thread is the frame-rate limit.** Its CPU time per frame equals the frame time:
  - UC 5v6: 15.9 ms in a 16.4 ms frame (60 fps).
  - Mission 01b copy: 9.5 of 10.2 ms (101 fps).
  - It is blocked only 0.2-1.4 % of the time.
- **The NV2A executor (`nv2a_ack_thread`) is second.**
  - Pushbuffer work: 6.8-7.7 ms per frame, plus 1.3-1.7 ms of `Sleep(0)` spin.
  - In M01b it is idle only 1.75 ms per frame. It would cap the game at about 120-130 fps even with a free game thread.
- **The executor's time goes to the per-word method loop**: 330-460 k words per frame, mostly ARRAY_ELEMENT16 index pairs. D3D11 itself is cheap: about 3 us per draw for 1,100 draws, with d3d11 plus the driver at 4 % of executor samples.
- **The GPU is not the limit on the 3090** (37 % utilisation).
- **High-level D3D8 is not where the time is.** Guest D3D is 6.7-7.3 % of the game thread, and the title is D3D8LTCG.

### Measurements

|---|---|---|---|
| fps (gameplay windows) | 60.1 | 57.8 | 101 |
| frame p50 / p99 (ms) | 16.35 / 23.9 | 16.63 / 27.0 | 10.17 / 18.3 |
| game-thread CPU per frame (ms) | 15.86 | 15.90 | 9.54 |
| executor pushbuffer work / spin / idle (ms per frame) | 7.68 / 1.64 / 6.61 | 8.06 / 1.58 / 7.02 | 6.83 / 1.39 / 1.75 |
| draws per frame, ms | 1,108, 3.37 | 1,052, 3.66 | 1,119, 3.86 |
| pushbuffer words per frame | 461,730 | 428,623 | 353,033 |

**Threads (CPU % of one core, UC 5v6):**

| Thread | CPU % |
|---|---|

### Planned switches (PIPELINE-A.md; none implemented)
- `[Render] PbBulk` / `RECOMP_PB_BULK`: bulk 0x1800/0x1808/0x1818 payloads in `nv2a_pb_consume` (E1).
- `[Render] ExecWake` / `RECOMP_NV2A_WAKE` (spin, poll, event, auto): no `Sleep(0)`; KickOff event wake (E2).
- `[Render] DrawFast` / `RECOMP_DRAW_FAST`: constant dirtiness, CPU vertex shader only when needed, one constant Map, dirty-page vertex uploads (E3).
- `[Render] ExecSplit` / `RECOMP_EXEC_SPLIT`: decode plus submit threads; reserve, gated on 6+ P-cores (E4).
- `[Render] FrameLatency` / `RECOMP_FRAME_LATENCY`: waitable swap chain (E5).
- Dev only: `RECOMP_PROF`, `RECOMP_PROF_HZ`, `RECOMP_PROF_AFFINITY`.

### M0 shared plumbing (0517065, 2026-10-31)

M0 is the commit both pipeline tracks branch . It changes no behaviour. It moves the guest audio helpers to a file the audio track owns, and adds the switch reader and the CPU-topology API that both tracks call.

| File | What it holds | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `kit/source/game/src/apu/ma2_audio_guest.inc` | Verbatim move of the API lock 0x3C4598, the ISR try-enter, the stop assist and the B11 bounded waits. recomp_manual.c #includes it at the two old places (`MA2_AUDIO_GUEST_PART` 1 and 2). The object is byte-identical apart from its timestamp. | T2 |
| `kit/source/game/src/platform/pc_switch.h` | Header-only `pc_switch` / `pc_switch_choice` / `pc_switch_text`, read as env > ini > default. The ini step is a selectany pointer that main.c `configure_pc` sets. | T1 |
| `kit/source/game/src/platform/pc_cpu_topo.h/.c` | The `[CPU-TOPO]` detection (CPU Sets under the mask, P/E, LLC, battery, tier), `pc_cpu_logical`, and `pc_thread_role_enter/leave`. Library code reaches it through the selectany `pc_cpu_topo_api`. The .c is #included by main.c. | T1 |
| `kit/source/game/src/main.c` | `RECOMP_AFFINITY=<hex>` (test only) and the `[CPU-TOPO]` line at the top of WinMain, plus the ini hook for pc_switch. | T1 |

### Track 2 (T2-0.T2-2)

T2-0 (measurement and bring-ins) passed its gates. T2-1 (bulk pushbuffer words) and T2-2 (executor wake) are in the branch with their switches default OFF; neither flip is done yet.

- **Bulk words.** RECOMP_PB_BULK / [Render] PbBulk (nv2a_pb_scan.c bulk branch + nv2a_pb_exec.c nv2a_pb_exec_bulk) decodes whole non-incrementing 0x1800/0x1808/0x1818 payloads in one call; 2.48 M verified packets (UC + M01b), 0 mismatches; executor loop 8.95 -> 3.79 ns/word.
- **Words per frame vary.** UC 5v6 matches range 140-450 k pushbuffer words per frame between 5 s windows and runs (t2r0 median 363 k, t2b1 179 k); compare executor cost per word, not per frame.
- **Heavy-frame word mix.** UC 5v6 heavy frame: idx16 178 k, const/program 104 k (already bulk), inline 39 k, state 24 k, immvtx 6 k, tex 5 k words; 872 draws; 4.3 kicks.
- **Executor wake.** RECOMP_NV2A_WAKE=sleep0|poll|auto ([Render] ExecWake, RECOMP_NV2A_ACTIVE_US) in xbox_memory_layout.c nv2a_idle_wait; poll+timer cuts executor spin from 1.67 to about 0.1 ms/frame, but at 4 logical CPUs the 250 us timer raised UC p99 +9 % and >33 ms frames 18 vs 4 (one run); default stays sleep0.
- **No game-thread audio waits.** with RECOMP_AUDIO_WAIT_STATS, a 5 min UC 5v6 fight showed 0 NEW_VOICE, 0 DSP-CMD (0x3AA7DF), 0 XACT packet waits on the game thread; the APU thread sleeps in its throttle 3.3 s per 5 s and waits on the DSP join 1.2 s per 5 s.
- **Resampler ratio.** [APU-SRC] in UC 5v6: about 67 % of voice-frames resample with ratio >1, 33 % at ratio 1, <1 % ramping, none <1.
- **GP program static.** [APU-DSP] GP PRAM sampled every 8th APU frame showed 0 changed words during a fight (GP program static after load), which favours the T2-7 AOT hash gate.
- **Capture under silent.** RECOMP_AUDIO_CAPTURE writes the post-gain PCM in mcpx_apu_monitor_frame before RECOMP_AUDIO_SILENT zeroes the device buffer, so captures work in muted MCP runs.
- **Guest CS contention is ~0 in UC 5v6 too.** [PERF-RATE] at FULL: 3 contended RtlEnterCriticalSection/s, 0.0 ms/s blocked; at 4T (mask 55) with spin 200: 2/s, 0.0 ms/s; all on 0x3C4598. The CS thunk share is uncontended Enter/Leave (ord 294/277 at 41-48 k / 30-35 k per s), so a CS spin (RECOMP_CS_SPIN, default 0) gains nothing. Evidence: t1p2_stderr.txt.
- **ICALL lookup path (T1-2 input).** RECOMP_ICALL (recomp_types.h:1061) calls recomp_lookup_manual BEFORE recomp_lookup. g_flat_table is `static` in recomp_dispatch.c, and recomp_dispatch.c / recomp_bringup.c are prebuilt, so an inline flat probe (O2b) needs recomp_dispatch.c brought in to export the table.
- **Tank-step scope and prebuilt code (T1-2 input).** 54 of 104 gen files are still prebuilt objects that inline ma2_tank_scoped_pointer (reads TLS ma2_tank_step_scope.active, offset 0). A plain-pointer + 48-byte swap design must therefore keep `active`=0 while swapped (so prebuilt scoped code reads guest memory) and move the "inside a tank step" logic flag (ma2_tank_contact_begin re-entry guard, ma2_spring_rate.h:45 in the game source tree recomp_0038.c) to a NEW TLS symbol; never retype ma2_tank_step_scope.
- **B4.3 volume query.** MA2 issues FileFsSizeInformation in normal play; with B4.3 the root is the handle's volume (logged once as `[FILE] volume size query: root=C:\ .`).

### Facts

- **The tank-step clock accessor doubles the overlay's lifted code** `004E2420` [code-confirmed] In the bots overlay, XBOX_PTR is ma2_tank_scoped_pointer. Every register-addressed MEM8/16/32/F/D range-checks 0x4E2420.0x4E2447 plus a TLS flag, and reloads g_xbox_mem_offset. The 59 prebuilt gen objects already use the plain form, so the scope only covers code in the 45 overlay files. No XDK, CRT, audio or D3D function (0x2B0000 and above) references the clock block by constant. *How:* PIPELINE-B O1: use the plain pointer in fast bodies, and implement the scope by swapping the 48 clock bytes in ma2_tank_contact_begin/end. — generated ma2_tank_step_scope.h (made at install time, not in the repository):11
- **Guest registers are TLS memory, and MSVC cannot keep them in host registers** [code-confirmed] g_eax.g_edi, g_esp and the x87 stack are __declspec(thread) globals. In the /O2 asm, every guest register read or write is a [tls+offset] load or store, because MEM32 pointers are made from integers and may alias the registers. A /volatile:iso build produced an identical asm size, so the cause is aliasing, not volatile. The fix pattern is registers as function locals, published at calls and returns; bringup/optimize_leafs.py already does this for two Bink leaves in recomp_fastpaths.c. 5,245 of the 25,841 lifted functions are leaves. — generated recomp_types.h (made at install time, not in the repository):167
- **Every ICALL writes three shared non-TLS globals** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_ICALL, _SAFE and _AT store into g_icall_trace[16], g_icall_trace_idx and g_icall_count (plain volatile globals) before they call recomp_lookup_manual (a compare plus the recomp_lookup_bringup switch) and then the flat dispatch table. Guest code runs on the game, guest-worker, timer/DPC and executor threads, so these cache lines bounce between cores. The overlay has 10,221 ICALL sites. The guarded-arm devirtualisation (RECOMP_ICALL_FEEDBACK) is unused in this generation: there are 0 GUARD_HIT sites. — generated recomp_types.h (made at install time, not in the repository):1061
- **The exe is built without LTCG or PGO** [code-confirmed] The gen and runtime objects compile with /O2 /Ob2 -MD /bigobj and no /GL. There is no inlining across the 104 gen translation units, and no profile-guided layout for about 100 MB of code.
- **The kernel call rate in a 6v6 match is about 125k per second** [verified-in-game] From the [KERNEL] summary deltas in an NRC 6v6 match: about 250k kernel calls per 2 s. RtlLeaveCriticalSection is 51k/s, RtlEnterCriticalSection 39k/s, KfLowerIrql 16k/s, KfRaiseIrql 14k/s and KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel 2.4k/s. That is about 1,400 calls per frame, roughly 1% of a core. Each call also runs GetTickCount, plus a 2 s summary that is not thread-safe, so two threads sometimes both print it. — kernel_bridge.c:10005
- **Shadow critical sections are created with spin count 0** [code-confirmed] kernel_rtl.c xbox_cs_create calls InitializeCriticalSectionEx(&slot->cs, 0, CRITICAL_SECTION_NO_DEBUG_INFO). So any contention on a guest lock goes straight to a kernel wait and a context switch. An example is the DirectSound API lock 0x3C4598, contended between the game thread and the DPC. *How:* PIPELINE-B O5: scale the spin count by logical CPUs (0 below 4). — kernel_rtl.c:332
- **Guest threads run truly in parallel (RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK is off)** `00394790`, `002B8F54` [code-confirmed] kernel_bridge.c has a guest CPU lock in the style of N64 ultramodern: one guest thread at a time, released for every kernel call. It is opt-in with RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK=1 and off for MA2. — kernel_bridge.c:9945
- **The kernel timer thread waits on a 1 ms high-resolution timer, then runs vblank, DPCs and timers** [code-confirmed] kernel_timer_thread waits on a CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION timer (1 ms). It then runs kernel_vblank_tick (a 60 Hz QPC deadline, enabled by RECOMP_VBLANK=1 from main.c), kernel_drain_dpcs, and kernel_timer_fire_due over 32 timers. A DPC queued by KeInsertQueueDpc waits for the next pass, up to 1 ms. A DPC blocked on 0x3C4598 delays vblank and every timer. This supersedes the older wording that the thread sleeps with Sleep(1). — kernel_bridge.c:3034
- **The NV2A executor thread also runs guest code** `004152E0` [code-confirmed] NV097 software methods are delivered at FIFO exit by ma2_gpu_software_method. It allocates its own guest stack and TIB, and calls the XDK miniport handler sub_004152E0 (QueueFlip, fences, callbacks). So guest code runs on four host threads: game, guest worker, timer/DPC and executor. — recomp_manual.c:586
- **Bots cost 12-14% of the game thread in 6v6 matches** [verified-in-game] From [BOT-PERF] (t of 30 s or more) over three push-s1 matches: bots median 119-144 ms per second of play (p90 170-187). Brain 37-41, ctrl 44-55, rays 21-24 (920-1,190 rays/s), plans 4-20 (p90 up to 61) and world view 16-31 ms/s; 620-814 player ticks/s, about 70 fps with 11 bots. All of it runs on the game thread.
- **The process opts out of EcoQoS and timer-resolution throttling correctly** [code-confirmed] main.c sets ProcessPowerThrottling with ControlMask EXECUTION_SPEED|IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION and StateMask 0 (an opt-out), then calls timeBeginPeriod(1). Per Microsoft's docs this keeps HighQoS, and keeps the 1 ms resolution on Windows 11 even when the window is occluded or minimised. The side effect is that every helper thread is HighQoS and competes for P-cores. Per-thread EcoQoS (THREAD_POWER_THROTTLING_EXECUTION_SPEED) is not used anywhere. — main.c:545
- **The executor spins Sleep(0) while PUT moves and for 2 ms after** [code-confirmed] nv2a_idle_wait yields with Sleep(0) whenever the last activity was less than 2 ms ago; otherwise it waits 250 us on a high-resolution timer. In play PUT moves several times per frame, so in effect it spins a logical core, which can be the game thread's Hyper-Threading sibling. The guest writes PUT with a plain store, so a WaitOnAddress design needs a wake hook at the XDK KickOff site. *How:* RECOMP_NV2A_SPIN=1 restores the always-spin behaviour. — xbox_memory_layout.c:883
- **0x50BA70 is the candidate fixed-dt hook for determinism hashes** `0050BA70`, `0001DD80` [inferred, open-question] The producer sub_0001DD80 takes the float at 0x50BA70 as the elapsed time when it is above 0 (wiki frame-delta-and-fps-ring). PIPELINE-B TH-2 proposes RECOMP_FIXED_DT plus a periodic state hash, so that codegen changes can be proven bit-exact across builds. Unverified: which producer runs live in each mode.
- **Prior art: registers as locals is the main static-recompiler speedup** [documented] XenonRecomp's README calls its [optimizations] options (non_volatile_as_local, non_argument_as_local, cr/ctr/xer/reserved_as_local, skip_lr) its largest gain: in Unleashed the exe was about 20 MB smaller and frame time dropped by several ms. It recommends Clang or clang-cl. N64ModernRuntime runs each guest thread on a host thread, but passes a single run token so only one runs at a time. Cxbx-Reloaded polls guest dispatcher headers (WaitApc), and its KeDelayExecutionThread uses SleepPrecise: sleep the interval minus 2 ms, then spin.
- **The game thread is the frame-rate limit: its CPU time per frame equals the frame time** [verified-in-game] runs on ew-merge 97f02c3 at 3840x1600, TQ1, DrawDistance 100, uncapped, the main test desktop: UC 5v6 60 fps, frame p50 16.35 ms, game-thread CPU 15.86 ms per frame (97 %); Mission 01b 101 fps, 9.54 of 10.17 ms (94 %). The game thread is blocked only 0.2-1.4 % of its 1 kHz samples. *How:* Speeding up any other thread does not raise fps until the game thread gets faster; compare builds by ms per frame, not fps (run-to-run spread is about 10 %).
- **The NV2A executor is the second bottleneck and binds first near 120-130 fps** [verified-in-game] Executor pushbuffer work (time inside nv2a_pb_consume) is 7.68 ms per frame in UC 5v6 and 6.83 ms in Mission 01b, plus 1.3-1.7 ms of Sleep(0) spin. Its idle wait is 6.6 ms per frame in UC but only 1.75 ms in M01b (busy about 83 %). At 144 fps the budget is 6.9 ms. — xbox_memory_layout.c:915
- **MA2 sends 330-460 thousand pushbuffer words per frame, most of them 16-bit index pairs** [verified-in-game] Words per frame in UC 5v6 (M01b): ARRAY_ELEMENT16 0x1800 238,623 (128,552); vertex constants and program 0x0B00-0x0BFF 127,115 (170,722); INLINE_ARRAY 0x1818 46,799 (17,353); other 3D state 32,870 (24,327); immediate vertex attributes 7,975 (5,196); texture stage 6,855 (3,506); semaphore/software 1,276 (324); total 461,730 (353,033). There are 1,100 draws and 5 PUT kicks per frame.
- **Only constant uploads have a bulk path; every other pushbuffer word costs about 10 ns** [code-confirmed] nv2a_pb_consume does a volatile load, a 16-entry recent[] ring write, a volatile GET publish and one nv2a_pb_exec_method call per word. Only methods 0x0B00-0x0BFF are taken in 32-word bulk chunks (280-308). The roughly 335 k non-bulk words per frame in UC cost about 3.5-4 ms (nv2a_pb_exec_method 13 % plus nv2a_pb_consume 7 % of executor samples). ARRAY_ELEMENT16 just appends 2 indices through nv2a_index_stream_method. *How:* PIPELINE-A E1: bulk paths for 0x1800/0x1808/0x1818 payloads, exact by construction. — nv2a_pb_scan.c:259

- **Kit hazard: kit/source/game/src/kernel, kit/source/game/src/apu and kit/source/game/src/platform land in the runtime tree** [code-confirmed] The kit's assemble.py places every bots-tree file under kit/source/game/src/{apu,audio,d3d,input,kernel,nv2a,platform,usb,video} into runtime\src, and the rest into game\src. The xbox_kernel target only has -I runtime\src\kernel and runtime\src, so a header kept at bots kit/source/game/src/ is invisible to kernel and apu code in the kit, while the game target does see runtime\src. That is why the M0 headers sit in kit/source/game/src/platform and the .inc in kit/source/game/src/apu one include spelling works in both the bots ninja build and the kit. *How:* New shared headers go in a RUNTIME_DIRS folder; include them relative to the including file.

MSVC names lambdas with a hash of the source path, so a new worktree path reorders those COMDATs; the code is the same. *How:* Compare builds by string literals and per-object bytes, not exe hashes, when the worktree path changed.

## How the editor maps to the game

## How the editor maps to the game

Pack `t16_editor_to_game`. For every user-visible control of the MechAssault 2 Scenario Editor: what it writes to the map file, how the game uses that data, and the wiki facts that explain it.

Confidence: 'code-confirmed' means the write was read in editor code; the game-side meaning carries the linked fact's own confidence.

### Map, Terrain, Paint, Water, Plants, Environment, View

Wiki: non-superseded facts only. All paths below are relative to `editor\src`.

Reading the tables: "Code ref" is where the write was read. Confidence = `code` (I read the write in editor code) + the game-side fact's own confidence in brackets. "gap" = no wiki fact explains the game effect. File names use the saved-archive convention `Terrain/Scn<id>_*.tif` (core/scenario.cpp:1863-1895). Everything lands in `world.wdf` (the MAEnvironment / MATerrain / MASky2 / MATerrainInfo / MARoot objects) or in a file of the .ma2map archive.

Abbreviations: ENV = MAEnvironment (found with `find_class(K_ENV)`), TER = MATerrain, TI = MATerrainInfo, SKY = MASky2.

#### Gaps (controls or written fields with no game-side wiki fact)

1. Ground layers 3-8 (Add a texture. Remove, layer Pattern size): the PC-only `MA2L` layers file format, weight texture resolution (4x colour map) and how the runtime combines layers have no spec fact. Only three log-only facts exist (m06b-layered-terrain. paint-neutral-colour-game-match. terrain-layer-recognition-key.).
2. Lightning `SkyFlash` (written with LightFlash): offset 0x18C is only listed in menv-weather-layout; no fact says what reads it. `EnableLightning` is documented as never read, yet the editor still writes it.
3. `LightningColorRed/Green/Blue` (read for the preview, never edited): offsets only, no behaviour fact.
4. `ShadowColor`, `EnableShadows`, `EnableMechDarken`, `DirectionalLightOn` (written by Looks / read by Game lighting): named in gap-environment-lighting but no fact says how the game uses them. `ShadowColor` is written by every Look.
5. `EnvironmentMapName` (written by every Look): used as the water fallback reflection (water-reflection-falls-back-to-envmap) and as the model env cube; no fact covers the Look-list map choices.
7. "Repaint ground colours from height": the procedural theme colours have no game-side fact.
8. Water Description encoding (size/shape in `Description`, name) and the Dig-a-basin / pond helpers are editor logic; custom water model is only [runtime-observed] with "draw and CorporalHeading unverified".
9. MAEnvironment water-zone properties (DamageLava, SpeedShallow .), `WindDirection`, `WindSpeed`, `NoShadowDistance`, `MaxShadowAngle`, `RainEffect`, `InstanceTimeMin/Max`: not exposed in this area (menv-unread-props-sweep says no fact).
10. Graphics-memory estimate (58 MB crash threshold): no wiki fact.
11. FogMode and the sky fog fields (`SkyFogOn`, `SkyFogColor`, `SkyFogTop/Bottom`) cannot be changed from these panels; the Height fog band only appears when the Base world already has FogTop/FogBottom.

#### Surprises (editor vs wiki disagreements or wiki-internal conflicts)

1. Sun direction consumer: menv-fog-setter-args says "DirectionalLightDirection is never read by name (sun direction has no consumer, open)", while m15-model-v0-sun-has-extra-factor (verified-in-game) shows models light with c13 = DirectionalLightDirection, and menv-sun-colour-direction infers the offset. The editor's Sun sliders and lightmap bake assume the field is used.
2. Lightmap contents: the editor bakes sun diffuse into L (0.35 + 0.65 x N.L) and shadow into A. terrain-lightmap-channels says the game treats L as a baked ambient/sky term (x LightAmbientColor) and A as a shadow mask gating the vertex-lit sun term, whereas mgiC-terrain-pictures says "L is diffuse light". The editor's bake is not game-verified on an editor-made map.
3. Ground-layer neutral colour: "Show it in its own colours" uses 1/(4 x DetailBlend); terrain-detail-colour-gain-. (verified-in-game, UC/KF/NRC) says the gain is 8 x DetailBlend, RESOLVED: not a mismatch; the game's 8x includes the light doubling, the editor's albedo is 4 x DetailBlend with x2 light, so 1/(4 x DetailBlend) is right in both (render.cpp tps; matched in game on a new map 10-25).
4. Type map value 8: terrain-type-map says 8 = special (water/waterway), the editor uses 8 as "Water/special"; bs-mawater-size says 8 = shallow, 16 = deep, 32 = waterway. The editor only knows 0/1/2/8.
5. Description default text: editor-null-description-bug says "A custom scenario (by <author>)."; the code writes "A custom scenario by <author>." (core/scenario.cpp:1997) and strips that form when loading.
6. IsNightTime wiki conflict: isnighttime-values-unknown-and-only-reader-building-light-127ed7 / editor-evening-look-ui-grouping (values unknown, Bogged Down maybe 1) versus isnighttime-retail-values-all-worlds-34-on-26-off (full list). The editor's Look constants match the full list (Go Commando, Ill Wind, Bogged Down lit; Cold dusk, New River City, Witch Cauldron not).
7. The Night checkbox label implies darkness, but the game's IsNightTime does not darken (menv-lightning-night, isnighttime-buildings-only). When no Look matches, the box simply mirrors `IsNightTime`, so a bright map with lit windows shows Night ticked.
8. gap-environment-lighting and gap-culture-scatter (still "inferred", status not superseded) say the editor ignores lighting / does not draw culture scatter; both are now implemented (View > Game lighting, View > Ground scatter) and the "Night/Sun controls change saved data only" statement is stale.
9. gap-weather-lights says rain is not previewed; the editor now previews rain/snow/dust (screen-space) and snow via the game's particle effect.
10. Fog: fog-applier-modes-and-shadow-pass-mode-3 says FogMode 2/3 are identical fixed 0.1 VS-driven fog; the editor treats mode 3 as plain distance fog (app/app.cpp:2027) and only draws the height band for mode 2. Not exposed in these panels, but the Height fog band help text is true only for mode 2 (matches fog-mode-2-vertex-program-height-band-formula-verified).
11. Editor writes `EnableLightning` although menv-lightning-night / menv-weather-layout say it is never read (harmless).

Row count: Map identity 8, Environment 9, Time/weather 9, Sculpt 8, Paint 20, Water 6, Plants/culture 3, View 7 = 70 rows in total. Gaps: 11. Surprises: 11.

#### Gaps (controls with no wiki fact explaining the game effect)

1. Palette note "AI only" (palette_kind_ ai_only_actor): origin of the classification is the palette_sweep, no fact says why a MAPerson/others "cannot be climbed into".
2. MABuilding placement warning ("added buildings do not show on a level without buildings"): only a code comment, no wiki fact; mabuilding-factory-sub-127d22 says dispatch unknown.
3. MADefend.Radius ("Radius (m)", default 60): F-GIVEORD says write unread; catalog "inferred". No game read found.
4. MAFollow.FollowRadius / FollowDefenseRadius semantics: catalog "inferred" only; no code-level fact.
5. Patrol path following: F-PATROLRUN verifies load and AI active only; MAWaypointGroup.WaypointID first-vs-last convention unreconciled (F-AIPATH); editor does not write TraverseType (loop) or WptPauseTime semantics beyond 0.
6. Inspector VisibleEntity ("Visible") and IsActive ("Active"): no fact states the runtime effect of an initial 0/1 on a unit; F-DORMANT shows only the trigger-based hide works.
7. InitiallyCollidable ("Starts solid") for non-vehicle units, OverrideEnable beyond bit-1: no fact on effect in play.
8. MACheckpoint helper: serialization/restoration unproven (checkpoint-serialization); no fact says what placing one does in a mission.
9. MATriggerMenuActivate helper: nationtypetotest-is-live explains one field; the menu-entry trigger purpose in an editor-authored map is not explained, and inert-property-keys still says NationTypeToTest is inert.
10. Vehicle pad: nothing says whether pad+MASpawner placed off a retail clone respawns vehicles in custom maps (only code-confirmed spawner rules, type-map validation).
11. MALevelStart.RandomDistance and spawn heading zero (heading-direction-open): editor writes StartOrientation, spawn facing in game not verified.
12. Road path nodes ([Roads] section, AI sidewalk/road/centreline nodes): road-nodes-confirmed shows loading, but no fact says whether editor-placed pieces make AI/bots path on them or whether MAPathDB regenerated at save includes them (mappath-db is documented only).
13. place_water does not mark the MATerrainInfo type map 8 (only the dev Pond tool does), so wading/waterway gameplay for UI-placed water has no fact (terrain-type-map explains values only).
14. Custom water draw: F-CUSTWATER says draw unverified; code comment (S:1276-1283) says tested in game 2026-10-24.
15. Multi-selection edit (Team/Side/Visible with): F-MULTISEL describes it, not in this master (see Surprises).
16. Water "Type" visuals in editor vs game: gap-water-material is verified-in-game but older; later water facts (m05-*, audit18/19) show editor still off.

Gap count: 16.

#### Surprises (editor vs wiki disagreements)

1. **Multi-selection inspector**: F-MULTISEL says Team/Side/Visible with are editable for several selected objects. Master 534d702 prints only "N objects selected" and returns (T:1844-1847). The Selection "Side:" buttons (T:1306) are the only multi-edit of Nation in master.
2. **Default order**: F-GIVEORD says the order defaults to Patrol; the UI always adds MAAttack (T:1331, AT:1221, TR:1099). Patrol is the default only in the trigger-effect "Orders" compile path.
3. **water-extent vs bs-mawater-size vs editor**: water-extent says size comes from the template name and defaults to 500 m; bs-mawater-size says it is the model bounding box. The editor stores size in Description ("[W x L m]") and writes a generated model, matching bs-mawater-size; water-extent looks stale.
4. **Player start identity**: F-LSTART says the game finds the start as a child named 'Player Spawner'; the editor's "Move player start" moves the first MALevelStart in file order (A:3009-3015), and a new start is named "Start Point" (players.cpp:218). Works only when the first MALevelStart is the player's (F-PLACEREL notes the same trap for `--place`).
5. **Neutral boarding**: neutral-unit-boarding (inferred, "unpublished", scripted Q did not change actor) conflicts with boarding-rule/no-owner-controller-no-boarding (verified-in-game, Q tap enters). bs-boardable-definition says m_bAIEnabled 0 may not be required; the editor writes it anyway (players.cpp:400).
6. **Defend radius**: editor shows a "Radius (m)" field for MADefend; F-GIVEORD says that write is unread by the game.
7. **Hidden units**: the inspector's Visible box edits VisibleEntity, but F-DORMANT proves start-up hide needs a trigger (MAActionShow Enable 0). There is no "hidden at start" control on a unit.
8. **Heading units in one slider**: CorporalHeading/VolumeHeading are degrees, StartOrientation and RoadRotation[0] are radians; the slider converts all, but heading-direction-open says zero direction for spawns is unverified.
9. **Menu trigger**: nationtypetotest-is-live corrects inert-property-keys, but inert-property-keys is still listed (not superseded).
10. **Palette placeable set**: editor-palette-groups says 801 placeable, 279 cut; the code also allows MAEffect (Effects/) and "Heavy Bomb" (VTOL Bombs) classes; counts in the fact predate those unlocks (palette-sweep-gaps-1023).

### Objectives & Triggers: conditions, actions, shapes, Sets, Used by, AI orders

Read-only research, 2026-10-25. Sources: editor `kit/source/game/src/app/app_triggers.cpp` (AT), `kit/source/game/src/core/triggers.cpp` (CT), `kit/source/game/src/app/app_sets.cpp` (AS), `kit/source/game/src/app/app_trigger_gizmo.cpp` (AG), `kit/source/game/src/app/app_cutscenes.cpp` (AC), `kit/source/game/src/app/app_tabs.cpp` (ATB), `kit/source/game/src/core/scenario.cpp` (SC); wiki fact packs (non-superseded); dictionary; `retail-authoring-from-wiki.md` sections 3-4.

#### 0. How the tab really works (read first)

- The current Triggers tab edits the level's own native objects in place (MATrigger*, MAAction* children, MAEvent orders, MoeEntitySet, MASwapSet). It writes **retail classes only**, copied from a retail prototype per class (`load_trigger_prototypes`, CT:103; `add_trigger_object` CT:919; `add_action_object` CT:953). There is no hidden compiled group for anything created in this tab (AT:1-3 header comment).
- The older model (`condition_kinds` / `effect_kinds`, CT:22-67: "When the mission starts", "Bring in reinforcements", etc.) survives only as a **legacy loader**: a file that still has `Scenario:triggers` is compiled once into ordinary objects by `convert_legacy_triggers` (CT:1179; called at SC:2170 on load, and `compile_triggers` at SC:1950 on save). Compiled legacy objects live in group "Editor Triggers" with names prefixed `[ed] `; the conversion strips the prefix and renames the group to "Triggers" (CT:1163-1177). Section 7 documents these legacy kinds because wiki facts `editor-workflow` and `editor-trigger-actions-map` still describe them as the live path.
- Tab header radio buttons (AT:438-450): "Triggers", "Cutscenes" (tab_cutscenes, out of scope here), "AI orders" (tab_orders_by_unit, AC:433), "Sets" (tab_sets, AS:99).
- Read-only retail levels: all widgets disabled (`Dis d(ro)`), text at AT:451.

Confidence key: **E:code** = confirmed by reading the editor code; the game side uses the fact's own label (code-confirmed / verified-in-game / runtime-observed / data-verified / documented / inferred). "none" = no wiki fact found.

#### Gaps

Kinds the editor offers with **no game-side wiki fact** (or only an inferred one), and missing editor controls for known game fields:

1. Circle "Fires when something is inside (untick: outside)" (InRadiusCheck): no fact states the game meaning.
2. Box "outside" (VolumeStateTest 2): inferred only.
3. Box "Units that set it off" = entity set (EntitySetUID, TypeOfCheck 2): only the cuboid property-map fact (inferred); the circle case is the one proven in game.
4. Timer: which of TrgTimerDurationSeconds / TrgTimerDuration the game reads is not recorded (editor writes both).
5. MAActionMissionVariableSet "clear" (VariableState 0): retail always 1; clearing is untested. The "Variable number (advanced)" box does not clamp to 0.29, the range the game accepts.
6. MAActionNation labels (Player's side 6 / Enemy 5 / Neutral 0): fact `nations` marks the mapping as inferred.
7. MAActionSound IsQueued / DelayBeforePlay and MAActionMusic MusicEvent (play/stop/swap/intensity) have code facts but no UI control.
8. Counter: fact exists (CheckType compares the count) but the UI cannot add the reference that says which trigger is counted.
9. Attach, GameTime, PlayerVehicleType, Uber, Spider, plain MATrigger, MenuActivate, Point, NationRadius: generic Common-tier forms only; only structure/count facts exist (cinema-trigger-structure, matriggerattach-layout-plus20-bias, entry-zone-gen-layout, objective-state-core, nationtypetotest-is-live), no behaviour fact tied to the tab workflow.
10. Actions with a friendly name but only a generic form: PlayVoice (cue id has no picker; the old `voice` kind had one), AICommand, AIFire, AIScan, Camera, Lights, PlayAnim, PopupMenu, ChangeHUD, ChangePlayerVehicle, AttachDetach, Attribute, DropShip, MoeEFX, Response, CheckItGoal, Uber. Facts exist for Lights, AIFire, DropShip, PlayVoice only.
11. Action target as a **set**: Show/AI/Nation/Remove use only ActionEntity (single object). Retail pattern A uses AISet/ActionSet; the UI has no set picker for them (Properties "Target set" is the only way). Destroyed "by set" (DestroySet, TypeOfCheck 2) likewise.
12. The trigger form hides random re-arm (UseRndReset, RndResetTimeMin/Max), MissionVariable gate, AllowClientActivate, ResetIfHaveInvalidCheck (Advanced tier, Properties only), though the re-arm and variable-gate facts are code-confirmed.
13. Percent combine (CombineMethod 3, MinCombinationPercent) for Destroyed/Circle/Box: shown as "Other (3)", not selectable.
14. Game-side start of AI events: the wiki records that the code that runs a trigger's actions/events is **not found** (`action-dispatch-runner2`, `matrigger-fire-1452d4-walkers-and-builder-145582-latent-bug`); everything about events starting behaviours rests on retail data and in-game proofs.
15. Open tab items: T2 (no "added by you" mark on triggers), T3 (generic names for new triggers).

#### Not creatable

Retail classes with no creation path in this tab (retail inventory sec. 3, dictionary entries, and the `build_part_kinds` mechanism, protolib.cpp:23-110; none of this was run in a live editor, so treat as inferred):

- **Trigger classes**: MATriggerHeight, MATriggerFlagStatus, MATriggerStatCompare have no instance in the retail inventory counts, so no prototype can be copied. MATriggerNationRadius and the Checkpoint triggers (30 retail) are positioned: "New trigger > Other kinds" skips positioned classes (AT:632); only MATriggerMenuActivate and MATriggerPoint have palette entries (app_add_part.cpp:219-220); whether the palette lists NationRadius/Checkpoint is **unknown**.
- **Action classes** absent from the retail count list (no prototype to copy): MAActionAICommand, MAActionCamera, MAActionPopupMenu, MAActionMoeEFX, MAActionAddCargo (the wiki says "never used" in retail), MAActionCheckItGoal, MAActionLobbyArea, MAActionSoccerGoal. (The harvest also scans multiplayer worlds, so some may exist there.)
- **Spawner link**: MASpawner `TriggerEnableID` (pattern B, 157 of 167 campaign spawners) cannot be authored from the Triggers tab; no control points a spawner at a trigger.
- **Orders**: only MAPatrol, MADefend, MAFollow, MAAttack can be created. Retail MAEvent count is 360 against 341 for those four, so about 19 events carry other or no behaviours; they show as "order" and cannot be made here.
- **Counter source / Logic-style reference lists**: only Logic and Destroyed have a reference list UI; any other class that relies on MoeEntityReference children (Counter) cannot be completed in the tab.

#### Surprises (editor vs wiki)

1. **Stale wiki description of the compiler.** `editor-workflow` ("Triggers compile to native MATrigger and MAAction trees in the group 'Editor Triggers'") and `editor-trigger-actions-map` describe the old model. The current tab edits native objects directly; the "Editor Triggers" group only appears for legacy files and is renamed "Triggers" on load. the editor notes vocabulary ("Give a unit orders", "Change a unit's side") likewise refers to legacy labels no longer in the live UI.
2. **MAActionAI label says "spawners".** Label "Switch units, spawners or triggers on or off" and `editor-trigger-actions-map` ("enables triggers, units or spawners"), but `reinforcements-spawner-pattern` says spawners are enabled via the spawner's own `TriggerEnableID` = trigger uid, with the spawner `Enabled 0`. No fact shows an MAActionAI enabling a spawner.
3. **Swap-set "Swapped in at start" and "Its units appear/leave the level".** The UI implies a load-time hide; `swap-set-linked-members-visible-at-start-in-game-contradicts-hide-rule` shows linked members visible at start, and item (4) of `what-is-visible-at-mission-start-.` (hidden unless bSwappedIn) is only "contested".
4. **Broadcast caption.** The UI offers "Speaker or title (optional)"; `broadcast-caption-missing` (verified-in-game) says the caption is not displayed.
5. **Checkpoint template promise.** Tooltip "If the player dies after reaching this circle, the mission restarts from here" versus `checkpoint-serialization` (restoration unproven).
6. **"Repeat" wording.** Tooltip says "Fire every time the condition is met"; `trigger-rearm-and-random-reset` shows TriggerAutoReset clears the has-fired byte every update, so a still-true condition (player standing in a circle) can re-fire repeatedly rather than once per entry. This is an inference from the re-arm code, not verified in game.
7. **"The player" shape filter.** Writes TypeOfCheck 3 + PlayerEntitesOnly 1; `tree4-uc-radius-trigger-correction-18-11z-typeofcheck-3-never-fires` says this never fires in UnderCover MP with the on-foot avatar. The UI only has a code comment (AT:793-795), no warning on MP maps.
8. **"Used by" key set is narrower than the reference-key list.** `entity-set-structure-.` names AISet, ActionSet, DestroySet, RadiusSet, EntitySetUID, TriggerEnableID, m_wptGroupUID as reference keys; `used_by` (CT:1205-1243) checks only ActionEntity, MarkerUID, cinemaID, ReferenceUID, TriggerID, Defend/Attack/FollowUID, set members, dwEntitySwapSet, dwSwapSet. Deleting a set that an AISet or RadiusSet uses warns less than it should (AS:127).
9. **WaypointID convention.** The editor writes the FIRST waypoint uid (matches `ai-orders-structure`) while retail cinema path groups were measured as LAST (`cinema-path-pattern-.`; `editor-ai-paths-as-real-objects-.`: "retail11 did not reconcile"). Unresolved.
10. **Combine method labels.** The Destroyed UI uses 2 = all / 1 = any (matches the 2026-10-24 correction); the old catalog text (t04_scenario.json:6218) had them swapped and the editor notes the relabel. No remaining editor conflict, but the dictionary text should be checked.
11. **Timer fields.** The wiki records TrgTimerDuration = seconds/60 (minutes); the editor keeps both in step, so a retail timer edited via Properties alone could leave them inconsistent (a footgun, not a disagreement).

### Cutscenes, Messages, Options, Level tree, File menu, New scenario, Test

Read-only code and wiki read, nothing run.
Code refs are relative to `editor/src/`. Confidence column: "C" = editor behaviour confirmed in code; then the wiki fact's own confidence. Very long fact slugs are abbreviated with "." (search by prefix).

Common wiring:
- A scenario is one `.ma2map` MGF v4 archive (`ma2map-container`), written by `ScenarioIO:build` (core/scenario.cpp, build starts ~1840, save ~2074). Contents: `scenario.ini`, `world.wdf`, `templates.wdf`, `preview.tif`, `editor/project.json`, `Terrain/Scn<ID>_*.tif`, `Pathfinding/Scn<ID>_*.map`, `Audio/<n>.wav`, `terrain_layers.bin`, plus `[Assets]` files.
- The game's index copies everything except `scenario.ini`, `world.wdf`, `templates.wdf`, `preview.tif`, `editor/*`, `audio/*` (`index-excluded-names`).
- Local text id `0x00F00000 + n` (n = `[Strings]` key) is remapped by the game (`world-remap-text-cue`, `ma2-scn-text`, `scenario-text-count-limit`).

#### Gaps (controls whose game effect no wiki fact explains)

1. `MAFreeCameraController.bSkipTo` (Shots tree): no fact; `cinema-stop-and-advance` lists its effect as open.
2. `MACameraProperty.Offset` (eye and focus steps), `Endy` / `EndWidth` / `EndHeight` (screen-size step), `startRGB` / `startAlpha` / `endRGB` / `endAlpha` (colour filter): only step template names are known. Only `flags` is documented (`camera-path-duration-flags`).
3. `MAPath.useSpline`, `smoothIn`, `smoothOut`, `duration`: structure is documented (`cinema-path-pattern.`), but the game's interpolation for MAPath eye paths is not (the Catmull-Rom fact covers MACameraPan).
4. How the game aims the camera at `focusUID` (versus the path tangent): the cinema-camera fact lists the look rule as open.
5. Deleting a cutscene that a trigger still uses: no fact on what the game does with a `cinemaID` that does not resolve.
6. Briefing "Title" and "Briefing" text: no fact shows custom ids render on the briefing screen (`briefing-screen-open` only says the screen is skipped).
7. "Speaker or title (optional)" and "No caption" on "Show a message": the editor offers them, the game never shows the caption (`broadcast-caption-missing`, open game bug).
8. Objectives: nothing explains what happens if the copied MARoot has fewer than 30 `ObjectiveItemDesc<i>` keys (the editor sets only keys that exist, triggers.cpp:556-566; `NumObjectiveItems` is constant 30 in the game, `maroot-objectives-keys`).
9. "Add part": no fact lists which classes are safe under which parents.
10. "Duplicate" of units, AI orders (`MAEvent`) and triggers: game effect beyond entity-set membership not documented.
11. Save As / Test with an untitled scenario: fact `editor-test-f5-saves-untitled-scenario.` (code-read-not-run) conflicts with master code (see Surprises).
12. "Add part" and "Duplicate" of classes whose models are not in the base archive: `palette-sweep-in-game.` shows an 80-object batch failing on heap, but no fact gives a per-object rule.
13. `--quick-test` on the game side: no single fact lists everything it does (only the Return key workaround and idle-player level restart are documented).
14. Cutscene "Preview" fidelity versus the game's shot player (letterbox bar size 11 percent, linear interpolation): no fact compares.

#### Surprises

1. Preview fallback shot length is 5 s when `CameraDuration` and path duration are 0, but the game's `CameraDuration` default is 8 s (`camera-fov-and-shot-length`).
2. The "Game started" popup tells Mission testers the campaign intro movie plays first, but `custom-scenarios-no-spintro` says Custom Scenarios mode suppresses SPIntro (verified in test42). The editor text may be stale (the older `briefing-screen-open` fact said the intro played).
3. The Briefing title and text the Messages tab writes are never shown for a single custom mission: the game skips the briefing screen (verified-in-game), although `[Mission]`, `[Strings]` and MARoot ids are all written.
4. `editor-test-f5-saves-untitled-scenario-to-scenario-folder-as-name-ma2map` says Test saves silently to `<Name>.ma2map`; in master `cmd_save` with no file opens the Save dialog (app.cpp:1447-1453). Not merged, or changed since.
5. There is no Export. Save is the export; the game finds the file by scanning the scenario folder (Scenarios.ini). Test is a plain `--scenario` launch plus a menu walk inside the game.
6. "New cutscene" is built only from the retail Mission_05 data (`retail_world("Mission_05")`); without the disc data it fails with "the retail Mission_05 is needed as the model".
7. "Add shot" copies only the LAST controller (about 19 objects), moves it 25 m +X, and the Description gets " 2" appended each time; there is no reorder. "Delete shot" keeps pieces another shot still uses.
8. Objective text goes to three places on save: `[Strings] 60100+i`, `ObjectiveItemDesc<i>`, and ASCII text cut to 60 chars in `ObjectiveEditorName<i>` and `mfname<i>`.
10. Test refuses while any `MechAssault 2.exe` is running, because the game reads new or changed scenarios only at start or hub/menu rescan.
11. Cutscene Preview hides helper markers on purpose ("the game draws no helpers").
12. Mission tests pass no `--mode`, `--bots` or `--skill`: only Multiplayer maps get the Players-tab Testing settings.
