### Editor audit 2026-11-14 (hands-on, editor 4a3e3b0f, game 1.0.9 rc33)

Seen in the editor and the game during the editor audit. Full entries with repro steps: the audit notes` (ids in brackets). Appended to this page only (not yet in the facts store).

Placement and saving
- A road piece is created at the un-rounded ground height + 0.15 m; a base at the drawn 8-bit ground + 0.08 m (+0.02 m mesh). On "10.0 m" flat ground: road y 10.15, base y 10.18. The game draws the base over the road wherever they touch. Two overlapping bases or crossing roads get the same height and z-fight in editor and game.
- On a slope a road or base is created level at the highest ground under it (road 14.5 m, base 7 m of air). Sheets are single-sided: invisible from below in the game.
- First save and reopen: flat ground 10.00 becomes 10.12 m, slopes move up to 0.24 m either way, objects keep their y. Later saves do not move heights again. A road ends 0.03 m above the ground instead of 0.15.
- Editor: `Terrain:height_at` is now the game's ground (saved 8-bit steps, cells split on the (gx,gz)-(gx+1,gz+1) diagonal); the fine float layer is the brushes' private store. Retail NewRiverCity grid nav nodes at terrain+2 m: 1201/1201 with the triangle ground (1133/1201 with the old bilinear fine ground), so the game's ground is the drawn triangles. A 0.5 m step needs range -20.107.5 (127.5/255); new maps use it, so flat ground reads 10.00 and survives save and reopen unchanged.
- Colour map: the green channel keeps dropping on partly texture-blended texels with every save (22 levels after 5 saves) [S-drift].
- Undo history is 40 steps, dropped silently; every Q / E press is one step.

Missions in the game
- Cutscene length = the sum of its "Shot length" values (within 0.4 s); a shot's path time is flight time only, then the camera holds. Starts at 0, 1 or 5 s all work. Space skips. Enemies keep firing during it (armour unchanged). Units already patrolling keep moving through it [P5 pass 6, S-trig].
- Briefing title and text are never shown, on the quick-test path or the Custom Scenarios menu path. Lose or death: blue tint, LOADING, silent restart (from the checkpoint if one was saved), looping. Win: blue tint, LOADING, hub menu, no result screen.
- Triggers that fire in the game: timer, player inside a circle or box, "another trigger has / has not fired", loop (repeats about every 7 s), enable / disable another trigger (a timer counts from the enable), remove unit (counts as destroyed), destroyed any versus all, hide / show unit, teleport player, enable unit, complete objective, checkpoint, message, reinforcements with an attack order, sound and voice cue.
- "Player OUTSIDE a circle" never fires (four setups) [S-trig]. Messages fired at the same instant replace each other. A unit left on Neutral never follows a patrol order; a unit on the player's side does (Hackman about 14 m/s, Atlas about 7 m/s, loops for ever) [S-trig, scripted movement check].
- Multiplayer: a mode the map does not list falls back to Team Destruction (log: "mode X is not one of <id>'s modes, using TeamDestruction"). `--bots 0v0` cannot start a team match; use `0v1`. Open: Base War on a from-scratch map (New dialog kit) ended at about 5 s with "Blue Team Wins!"; Capture the Flag 2v2 bots froze about 48 s in after taking the flags on a retail copy and a from-scratch map (not compared with unedited retail) [S-mp].

Harness
- The game log has no trigger or cinema lines; `RECOMP_SCENARIO_AUTOSTART=0` gives the real menu walk; the MCP server keeps only the newest ~30 game frames.
- Editor automation: mouse commands ignore `mods`; hold modifiers with `key ModShift|ModCtrl|ModAlt action=down/up` (a LeftShift down with mods leaves it stuck). In-app "Please confirm" popups are not answered by `dialogs`. A full `dump` is about 1,700 tokens, an unfiltered `items` about 8,000. A Python script can drive the pipe directly once the editor was started through MCP.

### Editor: what can be cut, and collision of a cut model

- Collision of an MGMODEL is the `<bv_obb>` boxes inside the root node's `<bounding_volume><bv_composite>` (Env_WideBridge02: 10 boxes, Env_MedWall_Span: 3; node transform identity in every model seen, so origin / lengths are model space; box axes are (-1,0,0), (0,0,-1), (0,1,0) = x, z, y with `lengths` the half extents along them: deck box x -0.36 +- 12.5, z -43.3 +- 43.85 = -87.15.0.55, y -1.15 +- 3.42). The cut model's boxes are clipped one by one (`crop:clip_volumes`); a box entirely outside the kept rectangle becomes a 5 mm box inside it. Before this the save refit every box to all kept vertices (one solid block). [code-confirmed, fmt_test T1.2]
- The save's cut test (`crop:cuttable`): refuses a model with `<shadow_mesh`, a skinned vertex layout (flag 0x80000) or an unknown layout, or a missing file. Census of every wall / bridge / base template and road piece: 0 refused for shadow volumes or layout; every refusal (54 of 138) is a template whose model is not on the disc (cut content: Env_Fence_Small, Env_Guardrail, Canal_Wall_INT / HLF, 15x15 parking lot, 20 big Bd_/Bb_ bases,). [runtime-observed, editor census 11-15]

### a cut road piece can run the game out of memory at level load

- Symptom: the level load dies with `xbox_HeapAlloc: out of memory (requested 29360192, used 49983552/50855936)` / `Memory.cpp(664) HeapAlloc Failed`. The heap log shows two extra blocks (7 MiB then 14 MiB) and then a 28 MiB request: a buffer that doubles without end while the level loads. A map with the same road whole (retail path) loads; no block above 8 MiB is allocated.
- It is NOT the side cut and NOT the clamped lane points: the same cut `.road`, node, mesh files loaded when named `._c3EBE4CA0` (two maps) and crashed when named `._cE95D94BD`, `._cA1B2C3D4`, `._c3CEB3FFD` (same bytes, tag text replaced everywhere, same-length names). Moving the files to a new folder (`roads/ma2se_c/`), a fresh save folder, or nudging a duplicate lane point did not change it. The cause is in the game's handling of the new file names / keys (not found); a cut road piece must be treated as unsafe until the game side is understood. The editor lays road pieces whole and Check scenario reports a cut one as an error. Bases, walls and water cuts loaded in every game test so far (a handful of names).

### cause of P1-08 found (bare LF line ends), road cuts back on
- The game's INI reader (mgIO `IniFile`, file parse at `0x0025F000`, line split loop `0x0025F0B5`) ends a line ONLY at `\r` (writes a NUL there and skips 2 bytes). A text file with bare `\n` ends is one long line: only its first section survives. Retail `.road` / `.node` / `.mesh` use `\r\n`. The editor's `crop:make_road` wrote `\n` only (and `make_model`'s rewritten `mesh =` / `vertices =` / `faces =` lines too). [code-confirmed + verified-in-game]
- Then `.road` parse `0x000D5508` finds no `[attachments] nPoints`; its count (local `[ebp-8]`) is never initialised and holds the stack left by the RoadDefinition hash (`0x0001E740` -> tolower `0x00309464` pushes the running CRC): the case-insensitive CRC32 (init -1, no final xor) of the RoadDefinition text minus its last character. Read in game with RECOMP_PEEK: nPoints = `0x2BBD80C9` = that CRC of `roads\country\MA2SE_longStraight_cE95D94BD.roa`, i = 0x40000 when the 28 MiB attachment vector (56-byte entries, push_back `0x000D602F`) failed. Negative -> no loop, map loads (road with no attachments, no model); positive -> loop until out of memory. Rule matches all 4 named cases (3EBE4CA0 neg loads; E95D94BD, A1B2C3D4, 3CEB3FFD pos crash). [verified-in-game]
- Fix: cut `.road` / `.node` / `.mesh` written with `\r\n` (fmt_test checks it); every save rewrites the cut files, so an old map is fixed by saving it; Check warns while an opened file still holds a bare-LF cut road. Game side (not done, for the game clue): initialise nPoints to 0 in `sub_000D5508` before the `nPoints` read at `0x000D5594` (same pattern worth checking in the `[Roads]` parser `0x000D5C80`). Any other editor-written INI-style text the game parses must use `\r\n` too.

### Editor: framing a shot; what the PC Release game did with an editor-built cutscene (probe 11-16)
- Editor side: the game's Field of view (MAFreeCamera key D186B2CA) is read as the HORIZONTAL angle across the 2.35:1 picture band (wiki t45: a letterboxed shot keeps the 4:3 horizontal extent), so the editor camera's vertical angle is `tan(v/2) = tan(h/2) * view_h / band_w` (`game_fov_to_editor`, core/cutscene.h). This relation is taken from the projection constants, NOT yet confirmed by an in-game pose match (see next point).
- Probe (Mission_05-based map, one 8 s shot started at 0 s by "Play at mission start", `--quick-test`, frames every 250 ms, 1280 x 960): the camera did NOT show the authored pose. Eye (493.7, 17.9, 527.4) looking at (493.7, 10.1, 571.7) as a still shot (two path points 2 cm apart) and as a 20 m moving shot gave the SAME fly-through: far view toward the placed building, closing on it, passing it, ending on the horizon and sky, then a fade to black. A map with the same cutscene but no trigger playing it showed no cutscene (brightness flat), so it is this shot that plays. Cause not found (path points, focus marker and the controller's Camera object are all in the file): possible readers are the cinema's own camera state or the path's useSpline / smoothIn / smoothOut / WaypointSpeed 0 fields.
- Fades: black fade-in over the first ~1.25 s and fade-out over the last ~2 s of the shot are present in the game with BOTH type-4 colour-filter steps ("Filter Begin" / "Filter End": startRGB 0, alpha 1 -> 0 at start 0; 0 -> 1 at start 2, flags 1) deleted from the shot, so those steps are not what draws the fades; the editor keeps the per-shot fade ticks hidden (D21).

### why editor-built shots did not play at their pose (cause found, fixed in the editor)
- **A cinema path starts at its waypoint group's OWNER.** MAPath start `sub_0015705D` (called by the eye step 0x1C92CA / 0x1C9B78 with entity 0) clears the point list, resolves `m_wptGroupUID`, and when the group's tree parent (`[group+4]`; node layout +4 parent, +8 next sibling, +0xC first child) IsKindOf MAEntity (class id `[0x4EAEA8]`) with flag bit 18 of `[parent+0x1C]` set, pushes the PARENT's position (vt+0x60) as point 0, then every MAWaypoint child in order (0x12F0F6 / 0x12F014). Retail relies on it: Mission_05 "IcarusDead flyby focus 1" MADummyObj (1719, 90, 490) is the start of its 3-waypoint flyby; Mission_02 camera "1" (1019, 80, 1388) starts its "1 wpt" path. [code-confirmed + verified-in-game]
- **The look is focus + Offset.** Focus step 0x1C9892: look = focus object position (vt+0x60) + the step's `Offset` vec3 (focus property +0x50; Mission_05 template Offset (0, 10, 0), Mission_02 (0, 7, 0)). [code-confirmed]
- Cause of the editor change "same fly-through for a still and a moving shot": the editor's shots are cloned from Mission_05's IcarusGoBoom, so the eye path's group sat under the template's flyby MADummyObj (left at its template offset, ~60 m up and ~150 m away); the game flew from that marker to the authored points, looking 10 m above the focus marker (horizon at the end).
- Editor fix: reader = game rule (owner point first, look + Offset); every authored view (Frame it / Use this view / Start / End = this view, Add shot, rebuilt eye path, Draw a path on the map) moves the group into the cinema's "Paths" MAGroup (no position: nothing prepended; the empty flyby marker is removed) and Use this view / aim zero the focus Offset. Game proof (PC Release, `--quick-test`, 500 ms frames): a still shot holds the authored view for its whole length (eye (470, 25, 470), the player's mech at the focus centred as in the editor's Frame it band); a moving shot flies from its start view to its end view. Old maps saved before CAM1 still fly from the marker until a shot is re-framed (the editor now previews that honestly).

### Editor: timed cutscene events in a custom scenario (game-proven 2026-11-16)
- **A shot's `triggerInit` fires when the shot starts and runs its actions in a custom scenario.** Probe (two 8 s / 5 s shots, 500 ms frames): a message under shot 1's start trigger shows at 0 s, under shot 2's at 8 s, the last shot's `triggerExit` message at the total (13 s, +-0.5 s). [game-proven]
- **A cue timer works as the editor builds it:** a `MATriggerTimer` with `TriggerEnabled 0`, `TriggerAutoReset 1`, `TrgTimerDurationSeconds` = o, switched on by an `MAActionAI {ActionEntity = timer, EnableAI 1}` under the shot's start trigger, fires its actions at shot start + o (message and own-clip cue at 9.0 s for shot 2 + 1 s, +-0.5 s); its last action `MAActionAI {ActionEntity = timer, EnableAI 0}` stops the repeat: the clip's `action cue` trace line appears once over the 8 s shot. [game-proven]
- Messages queue (), so a second message shows after the first has run its `TimeDisplayedFor`; probe messages used 0.9 s to read as a clock. A friendly unit given a walk order (MAEvent TriggerID = the cue timer, MAPatrol with TraverseType 1) is a normal AI order; the cinematic fade between shots is the game's own.

### Editor: reinforcements on a delay, mission clock, Neutral units (game-proven 2026-11-16)
- **A spawner whose `TriggerEnableID` is a plain `MATriggerTimer` (Enabled 0, TrgTimerDurationSeconds N) brings its unit in N seconds after the mission starts**; a Scout Mech set to 45 s appeared at about 45 s and (with an Attack-the-player order whose start trigger fires at the mission start) fired at the player on arrival. Objectives completed by timers (`MAActionMissionVariableSet`) advance on time; a "Win: every objective done" logic trigger over them ended the mission at the last delay (60 s). A message timer showed "THIRTY SECONDS" at 30 s. [game-proven, 1 s frames]
- **Neutral (Nation 0) units have no AI**: orders on them never run (S-trig D1). The editor refuses to create such an order without moving the unit to a side first (Player's side 6 / Enemy 5), flags existing ones in Check, and `add_order` still adds the wake action for AI-off units.
- "Lose the mission if the time runs out" = one `MATriggerTimer` named "Countdown" with `TrgTimerDisplayOnHUD 1` and a `MAActionGameCondition` GameCondition 1.

### Editor: a reinforcement's orders start on its arrival timer (game-proven 2026-11-16)
- A unit inside a spawner (`TriggerEnableID` = a delay timer, spawner Enabled 0) given an order whose `MAEvent.TriggerID` is **that same timer** (not a mission-start timer) walks / patrols on arrival: a Cougar set to arrive after 12 s on a flat mission with a Walk-a-path-once order (MAPatrol, path TraverseType 1, 4 points) was absent until the timer, then walked across the view and off the route (frame sheet, 1 s frames). With the order on a mission-start timer the unit is not yet spawned when it fires, so a walk or patrol never runs; only the default fight-the-player AI of an Enemy shows.
- Editor rule: orders given to such a unit use the arrival trigger; changing "Arrives" moves them (a start timer "Orders: X" that is emptied is deleted; "At the start" gives them a new start timer back). The unit's wake-up action (`MAActionAI` EnableAI 1) moves with the orders.
- Retail cue pickers: 23 retail sound / music / voice cues sit beside an `MAActionBroadcast` whose `BodyTextID` is a game text; the editor shows those words ("subtitle - Mission 05") and groups cues by mission.

### a cutscene played a second time (game-proven 2026-11-16, PC Release 1.0.9, 500 ms frames)
- **Colour filter steps stick after a play in a cutscene of several shots.** A 3-shot editor intro (8 + 5 + 5 s, the Mission_05 template's type-4 "Filter Begin" / "Filter End" steps in every shot) replayed by a 30 s timer: the replay is pure black (mean luma 0.0) for shots 1 and 2, shot 3 shows without fades; with every type-4 step at startAlpha = endAlpha = 0 both plays show every shot (hard cuts, no fades). A 1-shot cutscene replays with a picture (V3). Cause in the game not traced (controller advance vs Stop; MACinema code 0x14F2xx-0x1567xx is not in the game source tree); the filter step object is `sub_001C55AD` (show at start alpha when start = 0), `sub_001C5693` (interpolate start -> end colour / alpha, hide and free the quad after its window), `sub_001C57BC` (start: quad on the view, `+0x10 = clock - +0x10`). Fields: +0x2C.0x2E start RGB, +0x30.0x32 end RGB, +0x34 / +0x38 start / end alpha, +0x40 quad. [verified-in-game; code addresses code-read]
- **Shot 1's start trigger is not fired again on a replay of a several-shot cutscene** (inferred): AI-off under shot 1's `triggerInit` held the enemy on the first play but not during the replay (it fought through it); the same actions under the trigger that plays the cutscene held it on both plays. The last shot's `triggerExit` fires on every play (release after the replay seen; V3 HANDBACK). The cinema fires shot triggers through `sub_001452D4` with force = 1 (0x1D1551 pushes 1): past the fired flag and TriggerEnabled.
- **A timer switched off before it fired** is suspected to keep its old start (an interim build that stopped the safety timer from the end trigger released the enemy early in the replay); a timer that fired and switched itself off restarts on the next switch-on (cue timers, D22). Editor rule: the hold's safety timer always runs out (Repeat on) and switches itself off.
- Editor: hold under every playing trigger, release under the last shot's end and the repeating safety timer (no once-only Logic); colour filters at alpha 0 in the copy for a cutscene of 2+ shots that can play twice (2+ playing triggers or one with Repeat), `[Generated] FadeN` restores them on open; the "Countdown" HUD clock starts after the intro (once-only Logic on the intro's end).
- Open: an intro played by a 0 s timer did not hold a Cougar 60 m ahead on the first play (it fired during shot 1); with a 3 s intro it was held.

### the 0 s intro hold (game-proven 2026-11-16, PC Release 1.0.9)
- Two Military Rommel tanks 32 m / 62 m from the player, 3-shot intro (18 s) played by a 0 s timer. With the cutscene's hold set to "Nobody" the tanks fire in shot 3 (thin beams from the tanks to the Mad Dog, ~14-18 s ); with the default hold (enemies) there is no beam in any shot, on the build and on the build alike. So an AI-off given at second 0 did hold these tanks; the Cougar case from is not reproduced with tanks (no tank fires during shot 1 even unheld).
- Editor: a cutscene played by a timer of one second or less also gets "[gen] <cutscene> - hold again", a timer of start + min(0.5 s, half the cutscene) that gives the same AI-off a second time while shot 1 plays (insurance for units whose own AI starts a moment after the mission does).

### side change on an empty unit, Defend order (game runs 2026-11-16, PC Release 1.0.9)
- **A side change needs a crewed unit** [verified-in-game] The editor's Neutral 'Mech / vehicle is EMPTY (StartAbandoned 1, AttackPilot 0, m_bAIEnabled 0, MAOwnerController). MAActionNation 5 + MAActionAI EnableAI 1 on it turns it red on the radar but it never moves or fires (F1-T1 row 6, F-V3-3). Retail units that change side are saved Nation 0 but CREWED and asleep (StartAbandoned 0, m_bAIEnabled 0): Mission_02 'End Uller 1/2' (set 132794, TL - in indust area: EnableAI on the set + Nation 5), Mission_03 Elementals / troopers / turrets (TL - UpperGate: Nation 5 then EnableAI on set 156815), Mission_04 Raptors (TT Hack Gates 2). Proof: F1-T1 mapD with the Hackman given that crewed form (StartAbandoned 0, AttackPilot 1, owner controller removed, AI off) + the same Nation 5 / wake trigger at 8 s: the Hackman jumps at 9 s, fires at the player at 10 s and keeps fighting. Editor: "Wake it too" now also crews an empty unit (ScenarioIO:crew_for_side_change); Check flags a side change on an empty unit.
- **Defend runtime (code-confirmed, recomp_0046.c / 0040.c)** MADefend runtime fields sit at obj+0x78 DefendUID / +0x7C Radius (serializer `this` = obj+0x20). Load-time link check sub_000D4AF9 zeroes DefendUID unless the target IsKindOf MAEntity and flags a MACorporeal marker +0x85 |= 8. Begin-order (AI vtable slot 5: MAMech sub_001B3B9B, MATank sub_001B8D08) sets campaign-AI mode 2, ai+0xD8 = DefendUID, ai+0x94 = 1 (active) if sub_00185C52 resolves it, ai+0xDC = Radius; the Mech version also clears ai+0x9B. Tick (slot 6: Mech sub_001B3C09, tank sub_001B8D6F) re-validates and runs the mode dispatcher sub_00183FF7; mode 2 (sub_00184376) moves only while a path handle ai+0x178 exists. The Mech tick aims via sub_0016B0FF (entity uid at AI singleton [0x524A70]+0x1C) and sub_0018B106. The only Radius reader found is the Mech weapon clamp sub_001B42E5 (engage range = Radius x const), not a stay-inside test. Who requests the mode-2 path toward the marker is not found.
- **Editor Defend moves nobody on a new flat map** [verified-in-game] Friendly Hackman, Atlas, Cougar and a Manticore tank, defend markers (NULL MACorporeal 32093) 100 m to the side, Radius 60 and 150, AI on or woken at 0 s: no unit moved in 85 s or in 5 min (map). The F1-T1 C7 maps had their markers 5-6 m from the units (not evidence either way); the older M08-copy tank proof (tank drove 60 m) is not reproduced here. A Mission_08-copy run could not be judged (jungle hides the units). Open for the game clue.

- Ramp slopes: ramps of 36, 64, 79, 90, 109 and 148% (rise/run) up mesas were all climbed to the top; a 171% ramp (28 m over 16 m) was not (the 'Mech stands at the foot, tilted). So the player's 'Mech limit is between 148% and 171% (tan 60 deg = 173%; not proven in code). The bot planner's limits (read from the bot source, v35-edgame `kit/source/game/src/bots`): 'Mech grid TG_STEP_HEAVY 1.1 m per 2 m cell = 55% (ma2_bot_nav.c:142, tg_steps:255-282, built at:412; PATH_WALK_GRADE_HEAVY ma2_bot_path.c:284); tanks add slope_max 55 (ma2_bot_ctrl.c:2337, used at ma2_bot_path.c:152); Battle Armor and pilots plan on the light grid, TG_STEEP 0.80 = 80% (ma2_bot_nav.c:137,411); hover has no limit of its own (not measured). The editor tiers are kSteepBot 0.55 (yellow: bots won't route over it), kSteepClimb 1.50 (orange: too steep for 'Mechs, the player can't climb it) and kSteepWall 1.70 (red: a wall).
- **CORRECTION 2026-11-17 (see `t60.v4-171-block-not-reproduced`, proof `reach\proof\V4-VS-M2.md`):** the bullet above is wrong about the player's limit. A rerun on rc33 and v35-edgame had the Atlas climb V4's own 16.5 m / 28 m (169%) ramp and a 66 m single-cell face (825%); V4's map was never saved (likely a frame-reading or setup artifact). The steep tiers (kSteepClimb 'player can't climb', kSteepWall) are not a verdict on the player. Object faces were not tested.



### Facts

- **Sun direction consumer: menv-fog-setter-args says "DirectionalLightDirection is never read by name (sun direction has no consumer, open)", while m15-model-v0-sun-has-extr** [code-confirmed] Sun direction consumer: menv-fog-setter-args says "DirectionalLightDirection is never read by name (sun direction has no consumer, open)", while m15-model-v0-sun-has-extra-factor (verified-in-game) shows models light with c13 = DirectionalLightDirection, and menv-sun-colour-direction infers the offset. The editor's Sun sliders and lightmap bake assume the field is used. *How:* Editor vs game/wiki disagreement found in the t16 survey; fix the editor or the stale fact. Table row: see page t16_editor_to_game, section Map, Terrain, Paint, Water, Plants, Environment, View.

<a id="t18_ctf_vtol_1104"></a>

## Bot CTF VTOL flag runs: route, boarding, opening pair (2026-11-04)

## Bot CTF VTOL flag runs: route, boarding, opening pair (2026-11-04)

After d23e814 (v13l), runs started but none reached the flag. 2cff8b2 fixes the causes below. Facts are in pack `t18_ctf_vtol_1104`.

### Why the VTOL "could not climb" and shuttled by its base

- **Implicit `clampf2`.** BeelineVary's bow called `clampf2` before its definition. MSVC compiled it as an implicit `int` function, so every bow point landed about 35 km off the map. The only hint was warning C4142. It is now defined before `vtol_direct_path`.
- **VtolEdgeAll bend pile-up.** A bend pushed out of the 25 m edge band could land on the same spot every time. It was then inserted 12 times (path n = 15), and after the craft passed it, each 0.5 s replan put it back behind the craft. EdgeBendAhead refuses bends more than 60° off the leg, or within 10 m of either end.
- **The climb was a symptom.** ModClimb's demand flickered because the route ahead flickered. Note that `comp+0x90` in a .botrec always reads 0, because it is sampled after the input pass, so it says nothing about the hook.

### Why the enemy pilot never boarded its VTOL

- **Entry zone geometry.** The NRC VTOL's entry zone (r 4.1) is centred 3.0 m ahead of the hull and 1.9 m up. The game offers the craft (player+0x428) only from the sides, 4.7–5.8 m from the hull centre at ±27–45° off the nose. A pilot in front of the nose, or pinned under the wing, gets no offer.
- **The measured hull rejects every spot.** The hull is a sector maximum and reads 6.6 m (the wing) toward the zone. So every candidate spot was "inside the hull", and the aim stayed on one blocked line.
- **WedgeRetry never stepped back.** `pilot_escape` had a 5 m reach, but the hull centre was 7 m away.
- **The fix is RimSlide.** It steps the pilot round the zone toward offer spots learned that match (mirrored to both sides, transferred between copies of the same model). It does this both at the rim and inside the zone after 1 s without an offer.

### The opening push (CtfPair)

- **One pair per team.** In the first seconds each team names one VTOL pilot and one BattleArmor pilot, the pair that reaches them soonest. Everyone else is steered to the 'Mechs.
- **The run starts at once.** It begins when the partner is in its suit, with no random roll. The BattleArmor holds until its VTOL is near; the hold must stand down, or the 0.05 ride margin never beats it.
- **The player can take a role.** If the player takes the VTOL, the bot BattleArmor waits for him but lets go if he flies off: 250 m away, 80 m beyond his nearest approach, or 30 s. If the player takes the BattleArmor, the bot VTOL holds 25 s for him.
- **The pair ends early when needed.** It ends when the run is on, when a paired bot takes another ride, or at 60 s. After that the normal emergent picking runs.
- **Start-up timing.** At t = 0.0 the world view can have no vehicles yet, so the pairing retries for 8 s.

### Results and what is left

A/B tests on NRC CTF Elite, no hooks:
- **v13l:** 0 of 5 runs reached the flag, 0 captures.
- **v13n–p:** 9 runs reached the flag, 3 captures, 0 wedges.

Still open:
- The NRC red BattleArmor pilot's ground route circles its suit.
- The VtolTwoRiders hold at pickup costs 5–8 s.
- The cruise drops to 15–30 m/s under fire.



### Facts

- **BeelineVary bow point ~35 km off the map: clampf2 used before its definition (implicit int)** [code-confirmed] In ma2_bot_ctrl.c, ctrl_plan's FlagBeeline bow (BeelineVary) called clampf2 about 600 lines before its static float definition. MSVC C compiled it as an implicit int clampf2, so the bow offset was garbage and every flag-run bow point landed ~35 km off the map (vl2 bot 5 at t=12.6: path pt[13] = -27174,-21748). The only build hint was warning C4142 'clampf2: benign redefinition of type'. VtolEdgeAll then inserted its 12-bend cap on that leg at every 0.5 s replan (path n=15: the 'beeline rejected, n=15' symptom), and the VTOL with its rider shuttled ~50 m by its base for 25 s. Fixed by defining clampf2 above vtol_direct_path. *How:* Treat C4142 / C4013 in the bot sources as errors: an implicitly declared float helper returns garbage. Check a VTOL route's points (botrec at T --full: bot.ctrl.path.pt) before tuning climb logic.
- **VTOL+rider 'cannot climb' on NRC CTF was the broken route, not the flight model** [code-confirmed] The 11-04 report 'a VTOL with a rider holds 39-56 m while vt_alt / vt_need want 88-110 m' (vl2 bot 5, t=16-57): ModClimb's demand (vt_lift_demand 30) came and went in 0.1-1.5 s bursts because vt_manual_need samples the route ahead, and the route was 13 ping-ponging bend points plus an off-map point. At t=29 the same craft climbed at +13 m/s with the demand held. The recorded comp+0x90 reads 0 almost always, even while climbing: the recorder samples it after the flyer tick's input pass has rewritten it, so it is not evidence that the hook failed. *How:* Before suspecting the climb hook, check the path (n, pt[]) and whether vt_lift_demand is steady; comp+0x90 in a .botrec is not a view of the hook's write.
- **Where the game offers the NRC CTF VTOL to a pilot (player+0x428)** [verified-in-game] Both New River City CTF VTOLs (A at 1325.3,729.2 yaw 0.436; B at 332.2,1209.2 yaw 0.89) have their entry zone (r 4.1) centred 2.95-3.0 m straight ahead of the hull centre along the yaw (bearing atan2(dx,dz) = yaw) and 1.9 m above the ground, so the reach at a pilot's feet is ~3.63 m. Observed offers (player+0x428 = the VTOL's UID): 5.81 m out at +27 deg off the nose (vl2 bot 5 at 1329.9,732.8), 5.10 m at -39/-40 deg (vi2, vl1 bot 0), 5.07 m at +45 deg (vh2). The zone centre itself is under the hull. A pilot at +15 deg, 6.98 m out (1329.8,734.6) is pinned by the wing and never offered (vl1 bot 5, 7 s). *How:* Aim boarding pilots 5-6 m out, 27-45 deg either side of the nose; RimSlide learns these spots per model at run time.
- **The measured hull (sector max) puts a VTOL's whole entry zone inside the hull** [code-confirmed] Ma2VehicleView.ext is the furthest collision hit per 22.5 deg sector at pilot head height. For the NRC VTOL the sectors toward its entry zone read 6.6 m (the wing), so hull_at rejected all 25 candidate spots of ctrl_board (the centre, 8 at 0.55 r, 16 at 0.85 r) and the aim fell back to the fixed far-side point ep + u*(zr-0.4) = 1327.9,734.9. Every WedgeRetry try reused that aim (its skip list filters candidates, not the fallback). *How:* Do not trust hull_at near a VTOL's wing for standing room; use the game's offers (learned spots) or a slide round the zone.
- **WedgeRetry retries never stepped back from a VTOL (pilot_escape reach 5 m)** [verified-in-game] ctrl_board's WedgeRetry called pilot_escape(c, w, me, retry ? 5: 12). pilot_escape only backs off from the nearest unoccupied hull whose centre is within `reach`; a pilot pinned by a VTOL's wing stands ~7 m from the hull centre, so retries 1-2 did nothing (vl1 bot 5: esc_until 0 from t=10.7 to 17.5 on the same spot) and only the give-up (12 m) moved it. The retry reach is now max(5, hull_r + 3) (RimSlide switch). *How:* pilot_escape's reach is a centre distance, not a gap: size it from hull_r for long hulls.
- **RimSlide: boarding pilots slide round the entry zone and go to learned offer spots** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_BOT_RIM_SLIDE / [Bots] RimSlide (default on), ma2_bot_ctrl.c ctrl_board. Pressed at the zone rim (no 0.4 m headway in 1.2 s), the pilot walks 34 deg round the zone centre and in to 1.2 m inside the reach (1.8 s a step, up to 6 steps, flips direction once if a step gets nowhere): first toward the side nearer a learned offer spot (else the side with more measured hull room), and straight to a learned spot within 3.5 m. offer_learn records every offer a bot pilot gets on a non-BattleArmor vehicle as (zone r, zone distance ahead, bearing off the heading, distance), per match, mirrored for the other side. Logs [BOT-RIMSLIDE]; [C7] rimslide: steps, flips, learned, side_learned, to_learned. *How:* If a bot pilot stands outside a VTOL zone for seconds, check [BOT-RIMSLIDE] lines and whether a spot was learned that match.
- **CtfPair: the opening CTF push pairs one VTOL pilot and one BattleArmor pilot per team** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_BOT_CTF_PAIR / [Bots] CtfPair (default on), ma2_bot_brain.c pair_update / pair_veh_value / pair_eval (playtest 11-04). In the first 20 s of a team CTF match each team picks the free VTOL nearest a teammate on foot (120 m), the free BattleArmor nearest it (150 m), and the two bots on foot that reach them soonest together (cost 2 x the later arrival + the sum). The paired pilots get +6 for their vehicle, everyone else -6 for both (CtfVtolPick, CtfBaPick and the partner-ask bonus are off meanwhile), so the rest take the strong 'Mechs. frun_consider starts the run as soon as the paired BattleArmor is in its suit (no p_try roll, no lone cover, no ask); the BattleArmor holds where it stands (OP_HOLD 2.2) until the VTOL's pickup or muster ride outbids it. The player counts: or heading for (human_claim), the VTOL -> the bot pilot is freed and the bot BattleArmor waits for the player's VTOL and latches on by BaBoardPlayer; it gives up at 250 m, 80 m beyond the nearest approach, or 30 s ('the player flew off'). In the BattleArmor -> the bot VTOL's muster holds 25 s for him. The pair ends when the run is on, the player is aboard, a role is lost, or after 60 s; the emergent picking runs for the rest of the match. Logs [BOT-PAIR]; [C7] ctfpair: assigned, human_vtol, human_ba, vtol_waits_n, ba_hold_n, run_started, player_flew_off, ended. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_CTF_PAIR=0 gives the old emergent opening for comparison.
- **VtolEdgeAll piled one bend 12 times and put it behind the craft at every replan (EdgeBendAhead)** [code-confirmed] vt_route_keep (VtolEdgeAll) inserts a bend wherever a leg dips into the 25 m edge band, pushed out by vt_keep_in along the edge field's slope, and re-checks the new leg a -> bend. Near New River City's blue base the push always landed on the same spot (349.99,1169.79): the leg up to it still dipped, so that point went in 12 times (the cap; path n=15), and once the craft had passed it each 0.5 s replan put the bend back behind it. The flag-run VTOL with its rider shuttled round its base for 70 s (vm1 11-04, bot 0, t=22-91), even with the bow fixed. EdgeBendAhead (RECOMP_BOT_EDGE_BEND_AHEAD / [Bots] EdgeBendAhead, default on) refuses a bend more than 60 deg off the leg's heading, past 95 % of the leg, or within 10 m of either end; the leg is then left as it is ([C7] vtedgeall: bend_off_leg). *How:* A VTOL circling near its start with path n = 3 + 12 is this; check bends= in [C7] vtedgeall.
- **Standing 'inside' a VTOL's entry sphere in front of its nose gets no offer** [verified-in-game] vn1 11-04: bot 9 stood 3.46 m from the NRC VTOL's zone centre (within the 3.63 m reach at the feet), -19 deg off the nose and 6.1 m from the hull centre, for 3 s; player+0x428 never named the VTOL, ctrl_board marked it enter_failed and the bot took a tank, so its team made no opening run. Offers seen were all from the sides (+-27-45 deg, 4.7-5.8 m from the hull centre), so the offer is not just the sphere distance (something in front of the nose, the gun or the hull's own shape, is in the way: inferred). RimSlide now also steps inside the zone after 1 s without an offer (to a learned spot within 3.5 m, else 34 deg round); [C7] rimslide: inside_steps. *How:* Being inside entry_r is necessary, not sufficient: check player+0x428, and move to the sides of a VTOL's nose.
- **At match time 0.0 the bots' world view has no vehicles yet** [verified-in-game] On New River City CTF the first brain tick (t=0.0) can see no vehicles (vm2 11-04: CtfPair found 'no free VTOL by the spawn' for both teams at t=0.0, while vm1 paired both at t=1.8). Start-of-match logic that looks at vehicles must keep looking for the first seconds (CtfPair retries until 8 s). *How:* Do not make a once-per-match decision from the first tick's vehicle list.
- **A held BattleArmor goal outbids the VtolMuster ride (ride_margin is 0.05)** [verified-in-game] The muster ride is scored max(1.6, objective + ride_margin + 0.3), and ride_margin is 0.05 except for a flag carrier. A BattleArmor whose running goal is an objective (with the goal hysteresis) therefore stays on it: with CtfPair's OP_HOLD 2.2 the paired BattleArmor stood 9 s beside its VTOL hovering 7.6 m over it (vm1 11-04, t=12.6-21.7). The hold is now dropped once its VTOL is up within 90 m (the player's within 30 m). *How:* Any new objective-level goal for a BattleArmor must stand down near a waiting VTOL, or the ride never wins.
- **NRC CTF Elite A/B: v13l vs the route + boarding + pair fixes** [verified-in-game] New River City CTF, Elite (RECOMP_BOTS_SKILL=3, 5 v 6), no test hooks, 240 s, sweep_cell.py NAME 6 4 240. Baseline v13l 9b9e4818 (vl1, vl2): opening runs started 9.4-13.1 s but no run reached the enemy flag (0 of 5; inbound flights of 47-70 s ended 'too badly damaged' or 'someone else has their flag'), 0 captures, 8 boarding wedges (enemy VTOL pilot gave up in vl1), VtolEdgeAll 710-3986 bends a match. 2cff8b2 builds v13n a125c86e / v13o 3d951abd / v13p c518e914 (vn1-2, vo1-2, vp1-2): 9 runs reached the flag (inbound 9, 18, 19, 19, 21, 33, 36, 57, 57 s), 3 captures, 0 wedges; with v13o+ both teams' opening runs started at 7.5-13.4 s in 6 of 8 team-matches; the 2 misses were NRC's red BattleArmor pilot whose route circled the suit 5 m away and took a 'Mech (separate follow-up; CtfPair now hands off at once). Slow inbounds left: a 5-8 s VtolTwoRiders hold at pickup and 15-30 m/s cruise under fire (vp2 bot 8). *How:* Repeat with the same recipe to compare; frun / ctfpair / rimslide / vtedgeall [C7] lines and [BOT-FLAGRUN] / [BOT-PAIR] / [BOT-RIMSLIDE] in stderr.txt.
- **VtolEdgeAll's carrot keep-in parked the blue VTOL in its base corner** [verified-in-game] The VtolEdgeAll keep-off widens with height (vt_keep_m: 25 m + (height over ground - 20), up to 55 m; 53 m at 48 m up). By NRC's blue base, a map corner, vt_keep_in pulled every carrot ahead back to 1-4 m from the craft ([BOT-VCRAWL] dest=1-4 m, vtedgeall.dest_in_s every frame), so the flag-run VTOL hovered with its rider for 90 s and the run timed out (r1 11-04 bot 4, t=18-102). EdgeBendAhead now refuses a kept-in carrot within 10 m of the craft or over 60 deg off the original ([C7] vtedgeall: dest_in_refused_s). With v13s blue's inbound was 27-29 s. *How:* A VTOL hovering by the map edge with a carrot a few metres off is this; check dest_in_s / dest_in_refused_s.
- **MaxVTOLHeight (MAFlyer actor+0x4E0) caps stick-flown VTOLs at the terrain height + (cap - ~6.6 m): 48 m on NRC, 28 m over Bogged Down's bog; MoveTo can exceed it and is pulled back down** [verified-in-game] MAFlyer actor+0x4E0 = MaxVTOLHeight (property loaded/saved by sub_111D6C and sub_10F59C; default 55; actor+0x4B4 also reads 55 and is copied to the FlyerAI at ai+0x18C by sub_110EE9). No runtime code was found that compares against +0x4E0 directly, so the cap rule is measured: with the stick climb (ModClimb comp+0x90 = +30) held, bot VTOLs level off at the terrain height-map height under them + ~48.4 m (55 - 6.6): 48.0-48.7 m over NRC's flat terrain (~0) round the blue base (r1, 306 samples), 28.2-28.4 m over Bogged Down's bog (terrain -19/-20; vv2 t=66-69 at 600-720,1340-1430, vu2 at 916,1326), ~46 m over its plateau. The surface_height (walk grid / buildings) does not matter; terrain_height does. Crossing from the plateau to the bog the ceiling falls ~20 m at once and the game pulls the craft down at 21-27 m/s (with the stick climb held or not): a rider ~9 m under it hits the plateau rim -- the Bogged Down knock-offs at 916-933,~1240, at first taken for collisions with buildings. MoveTo (the FlyerAI) climbs past it (95 m, r1 t=42-48) but once the stick demand is on again the craft is pulled back down at about -30 m/s (95 -> 43 m). StickCeil (RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_STICK_CEIL / [Bots] StickCeil, 6f1d1cf) keeps vt_ceil_agl = +0x4E0 - 6.6 (lowered only by a learnt plateau, measured over the terrain and within 5 m of that), vt_ceil_at(x,z) = terrain_height + agl: the lane A* (ag_shut) shuts a cell whose own ceiling is below the tallest surface of it and its 8 neighbours + clearance (13 m with a rider), the straight leg is refused where any 25 m+ sample's ceiling is under its surface + 20 (ground_ceiling, [C7] stickceil leg_refused), the cruise and MoveTo altitude are capped at the ceiling under the craft. *How:* Plan stick-flown VTOL legs under cap - 6.5 m; with a rider, the rider hangs ~8-9 m under the craft.
- **Per map: what stands above a ridered VTOL's reach (ceiling minus the rider's hang), so its flag run must go round** [verified-in-game] With a BattleArmor on the claw the lowest point is ~9 m under the craft, so anything above (terrain + 48 - 9) blocks the run: ~39 m on NRC, ~19 m over Bogged Down's bog. New River City: the towers beside the blue base (from ~322-340,1198-1211 toward the red flag 1077,797 the surface ahead reads 75-76 m, need 95 m; [VTCLIMB] vs1/vs2) -- blue's straight leg is refused (ground_ceiling) and the lane route goes round; on the red side the way toward 805,1423 reads 51 m from 1323,727. Bogged Down: the middle -- the plateau (rim 20-25 m) falls to the bog (terrain -20) where the ceiling is ~28 m, so a ridered VTOL may not cross from the plateau out over the bog near the rim (916-933,~1240; RiderRay hits at 19 m: 851,1334 and 689,1364, vw1); its middle buildings are destructible (dynamic colliders: a static-only ray misses them). NRC RiderRay hits at 39 m: 1141,1104; 852,1370; 969,868; 1090,866; 810,1337 (vw2). Walk-grid surface heights (surface_height, g_ag.hg) do not see every roof; RiderRay casts collision rays (static + dynamic) at the lowest ceiling along the leg - 9 m and learns hits as shut airspace. *How:* If a ridered VTOL loses its rider over a town, look for [BOT-RIDERRAY] lines and compare surface_height with the real roofs.
- **RiderRay: ridered VTOL legs are checked with real collision rays at the rider's lowest reachable height** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_RIDER_RAY / [Bots] RiderRay (on), ma2_bot_ctrl.c vt_rider_ray_shut. With a rider and a known ceiling, a collision ray (ray_cast_as, self = the craft, static and dynamic layers) runs from 12 m ahead along the leg at the lowest vt_ceil_at along it - 9 m: in vtol_direct_path over 400 m (a hit refuses the straight leg, why ground_riderray) and in flight twice a second along the next leg (speed x 4 + 40 m, at least 80; a hit forces a replan). A hit is added as learnt shut airspace (airblk_add, 25 m), which the lane A* (ag_shut) and the straight-leg check already avoid. [C7] riderray: casts / shut / replans; [BOT-RIDERRAY]. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_RIDER_RAY=0 to compare.
- **RunRepick and RunCommit: a flag run is not dropped for a knocked-off rider, and takes no side trips** [verified-in-game] In a playtest (11-04) a VTOL and its BattleArmor on a flag run broke off to fight. In rec 2026-11-04 the run itself flew straight; the detour came after the rider was knocked off over Bogged Down's middle buildings: the run ended ('let go short'), the lift then ferried the BattleArmor to its own guard point and a support goal turned the VTOL on the player. RunRepick (RECOMP_BOT_RUN_REPICK, on): a rider that comes off on the way more than 150 m short is fetched again and the run goes on (twice a run; then it ends as before). RunCommit (RECOMP_BOT_RUN_COMMIT, on): while a run is at pickup or inbound, its VTOL and BattleArmor score no support / attack / cover / power-up goals (they still fire on the way; damage still ends the run). [C7] runrepick: repicks; runcommit: side_goals_dropped. *How:* A run member wandering off mid-run: check [C7] runcommit and frun phases.
- **DropLatch: a rider's decided drop is carried out even after its order changes** [verified-in-game] A riding BattleArmor lets go only in the ride order (MA2_ORD_IDLE, ma2_bot_ctrl.c, o->detach -> ba_release, retried each 1 s). At a flag run's FR_GRAB the BattleArmor's goal turns to the grab objective (a TRAVEL to the flag) within ~0.4 s of order_ride deciding 'flagrun-drop', so the release never ran: it hung on 7 s while its VTOL went to 94 m/s and fell 85 m past the flag (au3_64 bots 0/4, t=35.7-42.9). DropLatch (RECOMP_BOT_DROP_LATCH / [Bots] DropLatch, on): a per-bot latch keeps releasing for 3 s after a detach was ordered, whatever the order now is ([C7] droplatch: releases; [BOT-LIFT] '. (the drop it decided, order now N)'). Proven vx1 t=31.8, vx2 t=32.3 / 156.1. *How:* A rider dropped late / past its target: check droplatch releases.
- **EjectSink: an ejecting bot VTOL sinks with the -30 demand (the stick's vertical does nothing under ModClimb)** [verified-in-game] The VTOL exit (MA2_ORD_EJECT) pushed the stick full down and held Y, but under ModClimb the stick's vertical axis does not move the craft (a player sinks with Ctrl = comp+0x90 -30) and holding exit does not set it down from high up: a swap-eject VTOL hung 48 m over the Bogged Down base for 6 s, y flat, then the 'stuck high' lift-off retry climbed it to 71 m (au3_60 bot 10, t=100.1-106.4). EjectSink (RECOMP_BOT_EJECT_SINK / [Bots] EjectSink, on) sets vt_lift_demand -30 down to 3 m over what is under it (+30 during the retry lift), counts sinking as headway for the stuck test, and clears the demand when the order stops being an eject. [C7] ejectsink: sink_s. Proven vx2 (from 28.5 m).
- **Fixed: on Bogged Down a ridered VTOL crossing from the plateau to the bog met obstructions above the rider (route ray-checked before flying)** [verified-in-game] With the terrain-relative ceiling the plateau (terrain ~20) allows ~68 m and the bog (terrain -20) ~28 m, so a rider ~9 m under the craft is at ~19 m over the bog -- below the plateau rim (20-25 m) and whatever stands at ~19 m near 854,1332 / 886,1325 (RiderRay hits, vx2). In vx2 red's lane route (via 830,1290) crossed there, RiderRay learnt the hit (25 m circle) at t=19.6, but the replanned lane route (20 m cells, pulled tight) still passed it; the craft was dragged from 47 to 25 m as the terrain fell, stalled at 877,1317 and lost the rider; RunRepick fetched it twice, then the run ended. Next: give learnt shut air a cell-sized margin in ag_shut / the tightening, or route the crossing where the terrain slopes down gradually. FIXED 2e1bed5: every leg of a ridered lane route is now ray-checked at the rider's lowest reachable height before it is flown (hits -> shut air, replan, 4 tries; [C7] riderray route_replans), and shut air reaches 0.75 cell further for ridered routes. Bogged Down CTF Elite v13z 49a5df94: red's opening run reached the flag in both matches (20 / 22 s), no rider knocked off (route_replans 1 / 8).
- **A VTOL's first route could be planned before StickCeil knew the ceiling (NRC blue base stall)** [verified-in-game] StickCeil set vt_ceiling only in vtol_prepare's twice-a-second refresh; ctrl_plan could plan a flight's first route before it, with no ceiling, so New River City's blue flag run took the lane over the towers beside its base (a 92 m need) and pressed at its 48 m stick ceiling for up to 90 s (ze2 / zc2 / zd1 / zb2 11-04; whether it happened depended on call order, which is why v13w crossed once). Fixed in 31ecd56: the ceiling is seeded in ctrl_plan before any VTOL plan ([C7] stickceil seeded_at_plan). Also: the straight-leg ceiling check now samples every 6 m from 8 m out (12 m from 25 m let a 74 m tower beside the pad through), RiderRay casts in 60 m pieces at each piece's own ceiling (one ray at a long leg's lowest ceiling shut every exit), from 4 m out (from 12 m it began past the wall it was pressed against), and learns 18 m circles (25 m + a cell closed NRC's 30-40 m streets). Diag [BOT-VDIRECT] (RECOMP_BOT_DIAG) prints what a ridered straight leg was taken on. *How:* A VTOL stuck at its start pressing at ~48 m: check stickceil seeded_at_plan and [BOT-VDIRECT].
- **ExtractHpSync and DropSooner: flag-run extract and drop timing** [verified-in-game] The carrier lets go of a VTOL under 30 % hp (order_ride) but the run's extract held on to half the give-up hp (Elite 14 %) and kept sending it back to ride: it re-boarded and dropped for 25 s, 64 m from its own stand with the flag, while the VTOL hovered 8.5 m over it 'air shut' every way (au5_60 b1/b2, t=50.3-75.7). ExtractHpSync (RECOMP_BOT_EXTRACT_HP_SYNC, on): off the claw with the VTOL under 30 % the run ends and the carrier walks the flag home ([C7] frun ends_carry_hp); a carrier does not board a VTOL that weak. DropSooner (RECOMP_BOT_DROP_SOONER, on): held within 30 m of their flag 4 s (was 10) without getting low, the rider lets go (b2 hovered 11 s over the stand, 1000 -> 400 hp). The au5_60 5 s release delay was a build without DropLatch (v13au2 predates it).
- **RunNeedsHome and GrabNoRide** [code-confirmed] RunNeedsHome (RECOMP_BOT_RUN_NEEDS_HOME, on): frun_consider starts no run (no partner ask, no lone cover) while our own flag is carried -- a capture needs it on its stand (au16_61 runs 4/5 could not score; run 5's VTOL died re-picking). [C7] frun no_run_flag_away (3 / 7 in zi1 / zi2). GrabNoRide (RECOMP_BOT_GRAB_NO_RIDE, on): in FR_GRAB a dropped BattleArmor is not offered the VTOL hovering low over it as a ride (drop/ride flapped 3 times, 8.5 s, au16_61 run 3); [C7] grabnoride rides_dropped. CORRECTION 2026-11-14: its premise is wrong in MechAssault 2 (a capture counts with our flag away); RunNeedsHome now applies only with CapAnyway off (t47.ctf-capture-own-flag-away).
- **Open: some ridered stick flights hold ~20 m/s at full thrust** [verified-in-game, open-question] NRC zi2 11-04 (v13zh): both opening flag runs flew the stick branch with forward thrust 1.00 sent (cmds 4:1.00) yet held ~20 m/s at 26-31 m up for 20 s (closing ~14 m/s), against 40-90 m/s in other runs the same day; no bot code scales thrust (vtol_stick's thrust_max is not on this path). They cruised low (vt_mneed 13.7 below the craft: no climb asked) while fast runs cruised near the 46-48 m ceiling -- whether the flight model's top speed depends on height (or something else) is not known. *How:* Compare the craft's comp speed fields between a slow and a fast stick flight at full thrust.
- **CarryHoldOn: a flag carrier holds on to a damaged VTOL down to 15 %** [code-confirmed] order_ride's carry branch let go of a VTOL under 30 % hp (the plain-lift rule) even when riding home with their flag: the carrier fell mid-map, 420 m from home, and died on foot with the flag (ad1_64 b9 t=46.8, b7 t=221). CarryHoldOn (RECOMP_BOT_CARRY_HOLD_ON / [Bots] CarryHoldOn, on; 0189785): carrying, the rider holds on to 15 % (the run's extract give-up, half of Elite's 28 %); carry_let_go_hp is shared with ExtractHpSync and the carry boarding gate so they cannot disagree. [C7] carryhold: held_s.

## Bot behaviour audit, pass 2: MechAI goto idle, backtrack halt band, dodge on retreat, VTOL swap loop (2026-11-04)

### Facts

- **MechAI goto (mode 6, awake) idles: turn in place (anim 18) then anim 0 with forward speed comp+0x98 = 0, carrot 20-30 m ahead** `001843C1`, `0018A38E` [verified-in-game] A walker in MechAI goto mode 6 with ai+0x90 = 1 sometimes turns to its carrot in place (ai+0x360 = 18, comp+0xB0 = +-90 deg/s, comp+0xA0 = target yaw in degrees) and then stays at anim 0 with comp+0x98 (forward speed) = 0 while the carrot is 20-30 m ahead and it faces it. The game's mode-6 handler sub_1843C1 calls MoveTo , when MoveTo returns 'arrived', sets speed 0 (sub_2AD5C0). Seen: au3_20 bot 3 7 s on a mound after a hop, au3_60 bot 4 7 s on level ground (871.9,4.1,1596.5), au3_20 bots 2/5 4 s each; ~39 s over 4 Elite matches. Not the cause: MoveTo's overshoot test dot(dest-pos, dest-ai+0x188) (ai+0x188 is 0 for fresh 'Mechs and the sign does not predict moving, 87 vs 89 %). The exact gate in MoveTo (sub_18A38E -> 185D6E / 186362 / ai+0x2C 1B1075 / 179E58) is not decoded. Distinguish from a body pressing a wall: there comp+0x98 stays set (22.5) and anim is 2 (au4_20 bot 0). *How:* GotoWalk (ma2_bot_ctrl.c, RECOMP_BOT_GOTO_WALK / [Bots] GotoWalk) drives such a body with body_walk_direct for up to 2.5 s when it is still 1 s, facing (25 deg) a carrot 8 m+ off and comp+0x98 < 0.5. Read comp+0x98 and ai+0x360 before blaming the planner for a standing walker.
- **Backtrack to a crumb 5-10 m off stood the whole 4 s (MoveTo halt band); AiKick is off during backtracks** [verified-in-game] The stall watchdog's backtrack steered at the breadcrumb itself; MoveTo halts 5-10 m short, so a crumb 6.7 m off was 'arrived at' and the 'Mech stood facing it at anim 0 until back_until (au3_00 bot 0, t=191.0-194.8). AiKick and FastStall are suppressed while back_until runs. BackCarrot pushes the steer point to kind_min_carrot along the same line (arrival test still 3 m from the crumb). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_BACK_CARROT / [Bots] BackCarrot; [C7] backcarrot pushed_s. Any new steer target closer than ~10 m for a MechAI body needs the same push or a direct walk.
- **Shuttle stall fired on a fresh retreat from samples taken during a peek fight** [verified-in-game] The 12 s / 11 m shuttle test kept its samples across goals: a peek-hide/peek-shoot fight (goals <= 25 m, where the test never fires) filled them, and 0.8 s into a retreat goal 37 m off, running at 10 m/s, it declared a stall (au3_00 bot 0, t=190.77) and backtracked. ShuttleReset clears the samples whenever the goal is within 25 m (not on every goal change: retreats re-pick their point every few seconds and that would blind the test). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SHUTTLE_RESET / [Bots] ShuttleReset; [C7] shuttlereset n.
- **Travel hop along a leg landed on a 17 m mound (hop_ok only checked structures)** [verified-in-game] hop_ok sampled the hop line every 8 m for structures (surface > terrain + 3) only. au3_20 bot 3 hopped a leg at y -12 (t=12.9, jet dir -31.5 deg = ai+0x244/+0x24C; ai+0x250 end time, +0x254 start time, +0x258 strength) and landed 20 m on at y 5.1 on raised terrain, then idled (see audit-mechai-goto-idle-signature). JumpLand also refuses a hop where the ground top on the line rises 4 m+ over the body. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_JUMP_LAND / [Bots] JumpLand; [C7] jumpland refused (216 refusals in a 240 s Bogged Down TD match).
- **Missile dodge threw retreating bots back toward the enemy (side chosen = own side of the missile line)** [verified-in-game] The incoming-missile dodge jets perpendicular to the missile's course on the side the bot stands. With the attacker on the flank, that side points back along the retreat: au3_20 bot 9 dodged 5 times in 17 s (209.9-226.7), each jet NW while retreating SE, net 19 m, died. DodgeFlee: while the goal is G_RETREAT and the point is 5 m+ off, the dodge takes the perpendicular that agrees with the way it is going (homing missiles: either side leaves the course). Recording: 3 of 4 retreat dodges flip. DodgeBurn (0.7 s burn) shortens each throw as well. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_DODGE_FLEE / [Bots] DodgeFlee in ma2_bot_brain.c brain_tick_body; [C7] dodgeflee flips.
- **VTOL swap loop: the 2 s after an eject order fell into swap-go, flying the craft back at the ride (116 s)** [verified-in-game] order_swap: for a VTOL, 'now < next_eject' skipped the set-down branch and fell into 'else if (hdist > 12) swap-go' (walk-to-entry), so exit was let go and the craft flown back at the 'Mech; au3_60 bot 10 cycled swap-land/go/eject ~50 times 73.6-189.7 at 40-72 m and was shot down. Also: Y held with stick down at 68 m (48 m AGL) did not descend in 6 s, and the ctrl eject's 'stuck high' lift-off retry climbs (y 50 -> 71). SwapUnstick (4 m in 10 s) never tripped because the craft kept moving. Fixes: SwapHold (VTOL in the eject window keeps the exit held) and SwapHeadway (no 2 m gain in entry distance + height over the ride in 20 s = give up; trips at 97.4 on the recording). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_SWAP_HOLD / SwapHold, RECOMP_BOT_SWAP_HEADWAY / SwapHeadway; [C7] swaphold frames, swapheadway giveups. Open: why the exit hold does not set the VTOL down there (VTOL flight owner).
- **A BattleArmor standing on a roof under body_stop with ai+0x240 = 1 can be the hold-high post, not a stall** [verified-in-game] au3_20 bot 8 stood 7.3 s on a roof at (865,21,1092) (176.4-183.8) in AI mode 7 (S drive) with the jet flag set: the brain's 'hold-high' post, firing at full hp, then moved on. Reviewer flagged it as the idle bug; it is normal. *How:* Check the brain tag (desc 'hold-high') and v.firing before treating a still roof BA as stuck.
- **CtfPair BA pilot swapped into a free Mech once its VTOL came within 30 m (PairKeep)** [verified-in-game] When the pair's VTOL closed to 30 m the pair hold released and G_SWAP (1.25, a free 'Mech 40 m off) outbid the ride; the BA ran up a ramp and back for 10 s. pick_swap now returns -1 for the pair's ba_pl while the pair is active. BRT(g_pair) is in the recorder tables. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_PAIR_KEEP / [Bots] PairKeep.
- **BattleArmor knocked onto a roof stood with the walker bit clear (BaRoofLand)** [verified-in-game] BaLand gave comp+0x145 bit0 back only on terrain or a known surface; a BA put down on a 42 m NRC roof stood until AiKick. ba_land_release now also releases a BA standing still (ai+0x240 = 0, |vy| < 0.5) at one height for 0.25 s: prove_roofland.py releases at 39.81 on the recording. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_BA_ROOF_LAND / [Bots] BaRoofLand (BotCtrl bal_t/bal_y/bal_n).
- **Missile dodge burned 2 s and threw a flag-run BA 40 m back onto a roof (DodgeBurn 0.7 s)** [verified-in-game] au3_64 bot 4 at t=43.2-46.8 (order.dodge dx .96 dz -.27): 0.7 s into the burn it was already 8 m clear of the missile line (3 m needed) at y 2.4; the full 2 s carried it 40 m back and 20 m up onto a roof. The dodge burn is capped at 0.7 s. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_DODGE_BURN / [Bots] DodgeBurn. botrec diff --stream bot finds order.dodge changes.
- **Base War: bots attacked/guarded the 2000-hp indestructible VTOL bay instead of the 24000-hp plant (BaseWarCore)** [verified-in-game] obj_basewar added only 150 m to small team buildings. On Deliverance the bay (1348,15,313 / 835,28,1737; saved Indestructible=1) stands ~490 m in front of the plant (1834,5,248 / 352,5,1804), so attackers took it as their order point; defenders guarded the nearest own building = own bay roof (y 28, no_path). au5_91: 786 bot-s attack orders on bays + 406 s guarding own bays. BaseWarCore: while a plant-sized building (>= 50 % of the biggest) stands, smaller ones are no target, and defenders guard their own biggest. au7_91: 0 s. Still open: attack runs rarely reach the plant (1.5-2 km trek; attackers stay 1000-2100 m off). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_BW_CORE / [Bots] BaseWarCore in ma2_bot_brain_obj.c; [C7] bwcore skipped_small.

<a id="t20_campaign_picker_centre_1105"></a>

## Mission picker barrel: Custom Scenarios shift and Campaign centring (2026-11-05)

## Mission picker barrel: Custom Scenarios shift and Campaign centring (2026-11-05)

### Overview

Campaign and Custom Scenarios use the same retail mission picker (menu vtable 0x48F3E0). On Custom Scenarios the PC port draws a Scenario Editor button to the left of the level selector (the "barrel"), so the barrel is moved 50 640x480 units right to make room. Campaign has no Editor button, so its barrel must stay in the retail, centred position.

Before 2026-11-05 the shift was only ever applied, never taken back. Because the Campaign picker reuses the barrel widget, it stayed shifted right after a visit to Custom Scenarios. The fix makes the shift reversible.

### Key code

| Function | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ma2_pc_menu_pulse | Sets the offset each pulse: 50 on 0x48F3E0 in Custom Scenarios mode, else 0 | pc_native_settings.cpp:518 |
| ma2_barrel_offset / g_barrel_dx | Holds the current offset | ma2_bots_ui.c:518 |
| shift_widget | Moves one widget's +0x4C and +0x5C x to base + offset; remembers base and applied offset (g_shifted[16]) and restores when the offset drops to 0 | ma2_bots_ui.c:523 |
| shift_barrel | Shifts the barrel and its non-arrow text children; skipped when the offset is 0 and nothing is still shifted (g_shifted_live) | ma2_bots_ui.c:542 |
| ma2_scn_hub_action | Ends Custom Scenarios mode on any other hub item, so Campaign gets offset 0 | ma2_scenario.c:2226 |

### Bugs and fixes

- **Campaign level select off centre (fixed 2026-11-05, the game source tree on top of e4a03a9).** shift_widget only added the offset, and shift_barrel returned early when it was 0, so the reused widget kept +50. Each tracked widget now stores its applied offset and is moved back to its base x when the offset changes.
- **Builds.** v13au28 (A046C9FC.62E4) does not have the fix. The PC Release exe 1446948D.8800 (11-05) is v13au28 plus the fix.

### Test

Open Custom Scenarios (selector shifted right, Editor button on the left), back out to the hub, then open Campaign. The selector must be centred.

### Open questions

- Not yet confirmed in-game after the fix.



### Facts

- **The mission picker barrel moves 50 units right only on Custom Scenarios** `0048F3E0` [code-confirmed] ma2_pc_menu_pulse calls ma2_barrel_offset(50) on every menu pulse when the menu vtable is 0x48F3E0 (the mission picker) and Custom Scenarios mode is on (ma2_scn_custom_active), and ma2_barrel_offset(0) everywhere else. The 50 640x480 units make room for the Scenario Editor button drawn to the left (EDITOR_X0.X1 = 65.113). place_one -> shift_barrel moves the barrel title and its text children (the description); the arrows are re-placed from the barrel every frame. — pc_native_settings.cpp:518
- **Bug: Campaign level select stayed shifted right after visiting Custom Scenarios** [code-confirmed] The Campaign mission picker's level selector was off centre, shifted right as if the Editor button were there. Root cause: shift_widget only ever added the offset, and with the offset back at 0 shift_barrel returned early, so nothing moved the widgets back. The Campaign picker reuses the Custom Scenarios barrel widget, so it kept the +50 x at +0x4C and +0x5C. Fix (the game source tree, ma2_bots_ui.c, on top of e4a03a9): each tracked widget stores its base x and the offset applied (g_shifted[16]: w, x[2], dx); when the offset changes, including back to 0, x is rewritten to base + new offset. g_shifted_live counts entries still offset, so with offset 0 shift_barrel does nothing unless a shifted widget needs restoring. A widget whose +0x4C no longer equals base + applied is treated as new and re-based. *How:* Open Custom Scenarios (selector shifted right, Editor button on the left), back out to the hub, open Campaign: the level selector must be centred. — ma2_bots_ui.c:523
- **Custom Scenarios mode ends when any other hub item is chosen** [code-confirmed] ma2_scn_hub_action calls ma2_scn_custom_leave for every hub action except 8 (Custom Scenarios), so the Campaign picker sees ma2_scn_custom_active == 0, gets barrel offset 0 and shows no Editor button. The mode is not ended when the hub is merely rebuilt (quitting a custom mission passes through the hub on the way back to the picker). — ma2_scenario.c:2226
- **Centring fix shipped to PC Release on 2026-11-05 (exe 1446948D.8800)** [documented] build-\mechassault2_recomp.exe with the shift_widget restore was built (only ma2_bots_ui.c recompiled) and copied to PC Release as 'MechAssault 2.exe' with mechassault2_recomp.map. SHA-256 1446948DD3B1E970A832F2DF19DAB7E012EEA1979CAF26CC8D4D1517E45A8800. It is v13au28 (A046C9FC.62E4, a test folder, 11-05, the Bots audit build) plus this fix; v13au28 itself does NOT have the fix. Not yet checked in-game at the time of writing. — ma2_bots_ui.c:523

## Side-balance sweep round 2 (11-07): open items closed

### Facts

- **CTF Going Commando: 0 grabs because a retreat jet hop carried BattleArmor over the flag** [verified-in-game] On Going Commando (all BattleArmor) bots did reach both flags (bs62b b0 22 m from blue at 196.2 s; bs62a b7 12 m from red at 53.8 s) but crossed them 6-7 m up at 25-30 m/s: a retreat order 0.5 s earlier started a 2 s jet hop (ord 5, jump command held), the brain switched to the grab (FlagTouch walk) and the burn carried on over the flag. 20-30 m out a power-up (1.25) or retreat (1.20) also out-scored the grab (1.15) because the 2.6 commit started at 20 m. Fixes in 6cbb7a9: TouchJetCut (a touch order inside 30 m ends a running jump: ai+0x240 = 0, actor+0x268 bit 15 and thrust +0x4E4/+0x4E8 cleared) and GrabReach (commit from 30 m). Proof runs: 1 and 7 grabs (rc2 0 and 0), a capture each side. *How:* audit/gc_jet.py SRC REC BOT T0 T1 [STEP] prints pos/vel/cmd/drv/order per step; gc_near.py lists frames near the enemy flag.
- **Going Commando: APU MMIO crash at guest 0x3A8A02 and a sim freeze, both in the first minute** [verified-in-game] 4th sighting of the DSOUND APU MMIO read at 0xFE000268 (guest 0x3A8A02, edi=0xFE000264), every one on Going Commando (bs62a, gc6b first try at 44 s). A separate try (gc6a) froze at 51 s game time: the process stayed alive, only [PC-UI] and [KERNEL] summary lines after, no CRASH line. Neither run had the new touch jet cut near the event. Logs: NOTES audit/balance/crash/.
- **Base War Deliverance: the middle follows head count (the idle sweep human = 5 v 6)** [verified-in-game] Kills by tenth of the plant-to-plant line (audit/killfrac.py): with the idle test human on team 1 (bs91a, bw7a) the fights land in team 1's half (tenths 1-4); with it on team 2 (bs91b, bw7b) in team 2's half (4-9). bw7b (team 1 with six bots) won 1735-0. Scores come from a few lone runs: bs91b team 2's 1395 = one BattleArmor at team 1's plant 306-321 s. Attackers past the middle were alone 85-100 % of the time (bw_push.py); BwGroup (6cbb7a9) stages them at the main lane's 45 % point for up to 12 s. *How:* audit/killfrac.py STDERR x1 z1 x2 z2; bw_push.py; bw_hits.py.
- **Base War Deliverance: the rc3 objective stands (59 s vs 32 s) are guards standing at posts, same total** [verified-in-game] All long stands in rc2_91 and rc3_91 are defenders at their guard posts (objective, ord 2). Total defender still time is the same (296 vs 301 bot-s, threatnear.py); nobody reached either plant in either 240 s run (enemy bot-s within 400 m: 16 and 7), so it is split into more >= 1.5 s pieces, not more standing. *How:* audit/longstand_bybot.py; threatnear.py.
- **Base War Bogged Down: team 1 wins on damage per close 'Mech-second, no pathing fault** [verified-in-game] Team 1's 'Mechs get to 63-68 m of team 2's plant and stream damage (66-110 per tick): 151 and 91 hp per second with a 'Mech within 150 m; team 2's 'Mechs stood at 140 m in run a (13 hp/s) and 69 m in run b (60 hp/s) (bw_close.py). Team 2's damage is mostly BattleArmor (5183 of 7287 in bs90a). Vehicle picks are even, line-of-sight blocks to the plants the same both sides (BOT-OBJFIRE no-line 18/19, 17/12). Below the 2x flag. *How:* audit/bw_close.py, bw_bykind.py.

There is also a way out to the south-east (iw11b b6 left at about 135 s). *How:* audit/pocketbail_check.py STDERR. simulates PocketBail offline.
- **Snatch It Ill Wind: team 2's short way to the cores needs 3 m clearance; big 'Mechs loop south** [verified-in-game] RECOMP_BOT_PATHTEST (grid planner) from team 2's base 1218,1475 to the pile 719,1296: r=2.5 585 m, r=3.0 559 m, r=3.5 743 m, r=4.0 747 m (south loop via 1044,1222 and 832,1148). Team 1's base to the pile is 450-500 m at r=4. The pile back to team 2's base is 574 m at r=4 down a one-way drop at 750,1386. A 'Mech plans with 0.6 x its hull (2.6-4.0 m), so small 'Mechs, BattleArmor and pilots already take the short way; the gap at team 2's base exit (1146,1492 -> 1130,1476) is 6-7 m wide. Check It attackers pair up on the two nearest terminals; Snatch It attackers pair up and count cores in the other base as near as free ones; Base War flex players guard the plant. ck11a: the behind side concentrated on terminals 1 and 3. *How:* audit/ck_targets.py SRC REC.

The sweep's test human idles, so its side plays 5 v 6: the 6-bot side won 26 of 36 decided rc4 runs (rc2 15 of 29). With two runs a cell, the 'same side wins both' flag fires on any cell where the 5-bot side wins one run: 5 new rc4 flags (Snatch It On the Rocks and Rush Hour, Check It Ill Wind and Killing Fields, Base War Rush Hour) are that. Carried over and measured as map design: Snatch It Ill Wind, Base War Bogged Down and No Man's Land. *How:* audit/balance/compare.py bs rc4_ prints the before/after table; table.py PREFIX OUT TITLE.

The bot asked for the bail-out every 15 s to the end. 96990bd WedgeFight: after two bail-outs from the same hull it fights from there. ec66392 PocketMark: when PocketBail fires for a tank, its spot (5 m) becomes a learned obstacle (rc5 test: one wedge, no second tank). *How:* grep BOT-POCKETBAIL / BOT-TRAPPED; C7 trapbail wedge_fight, pocketbail marked.

## Objective-reach audit (11-08): tank slope, vehicle spawn pins, Check It walks

### Facts

- **Ill Wind team-2 tank exit: a 30-37 deg face open on the light grid, plus a drop link down it** [verified-in-game] HPROBE along 1205,1420 -> 1165,1376 shows y 14.8 -> -6.9 with slope 47-76 (rise/run x100) and light-grid clearance 4-9 m (heavy 0): the light grid (wall at 0.8) left it open and the tank planner (light grid) routed down it; every team-2 tank bounced at 1195-1209,1412-1425 until PocketBail. Limiting tank cells to slp<=55 in passable was not enough: the drop-link search still added a 6 m 'drop' 1190,1402 y9.5 -> 1190,1388 y3.7 over the face because the cells in between were not blocked, only steep. Fix 12882a1 (TankSlope): ma2_path_set_slope_max(55) for tanks and no drop link across a non-blocked cell steeper than the limit. The real exit is the 16-22 deg ramp at x 1200-1204 (slope 29-41). After: tanks 2-11 s in the exit box (25-38 s before), no bail there in the rc10 matrix. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_HPROBE="x0,z0,x1,z1,step|." prints terrain/surface/clear/heavy/slope per point at nav build; RECOMP_BOT_PATHTEST_SLOPE=55 applies the tank slope limit to PATHTEST queries.
- **A vehicle respawns on whatever stands on its spawn spot (VTOL on a tank, Ill Wind team 1)** [verified-in-game] rc9_63b: a VTOL (02146130) appeared at t~54 at 331.2,17.8,976.6 on a tank crossing that spot (BOT-CONTACT d=2.5 m, hull 6.7); the tank did not move to two decimals for 15 s until PocketBail; again later in the run and at the 'Mech spot 338,959. The game's vehicle generator does not keep the spot clear of a ground vehicle (wiki: MACrateGenerator occupancy scan 0x152B32, radius unknown). Fix 687e095 (VehPad): where an unoccupied vehicle actor is first seen is a spawn spot (radius = measured hull, 9 m VTOL); an empty spot within 80 m is a planner obstacle for tanks. Ill Wind team-1 base bails: rc2 4, rc4 4, rc6 1, rc10 0. *How:* [BOT-VEHPAD] lines list the learned spots per map; [C7] vehpad plans.
- **Check It No Man's Land terminal 634,74,1227 is on a mesa reachable only up its east face** [verified-in-game] Pilot PATHTEST with slope<=55 has no route (gap 82 m); a 'Mech route ends 89 m short. Without a slope limit the pilot route goes up the west face (30 deg at 505,1240 then 43 deg at 521-524,1256-1260), which a pilot cannot walk: FootFallback pilots stood at 505-509,1237-1242 for the walk's 40 s (rc6_73b, rc10_73a b1/b2). A BattleArmor reached it by walking 583,55,1177 -> 604,74,1192 (rc10_73b, after a VTOL lift); another churned at the foot 153 s (p30_73a b1). Claimed in 2 of 8 matrix runs. Fix 78aef13: WalkProgress (walking pilot no 5 m closer in 10 s -> skip 25 s) and ClaimProgress (any claim no 10 m closer in 30 s -> skip 25 s). *How:* Same probes: RECOMP_BOT_HPROBE / RECOMP_BOT_PATHTEST on mode 7 map 3.
- **Killing Fields terminal 2: FootFallback pilots can freeze against their own hull on getting out** [verified-in-game] rc11_72b b3/b5, p31_72a b0: right after the eject at the platform foot (456-479,1191-1263) the pilot logs AiKick and FROZEN (no 0.5 m in 3 s) with the carrot 8-10 m off; WalkProgress now ends that walk after 10 s (was 40 s). Terminal 2 is still claimed 1-2 times per run. *How:* grep "getting out to walk|made no progress" in stderr.
- **On the Rocks CTF 1509-1514,1503-1506: tanks pinned by something not on the nav grid (open)** [verified-in-game] rc4_65b (8 bails, one tank), rc10_65a (2): the hull stops dead (position equal to 2 decimals for 14 s, pivot does nothing). HPROBE: terrain = surface, slope 32 (18 deg), light clearance 43 m; PATHTEST routes straight off it; no vehicle or objective within 25 m. So a collision shape neither terrain_height nor the surface rays ; the eject is refused (no room) and WedgeFight keeps it there. Needs the static-prop collision data.
- **Objective-reach matrix numbers (rc2/rc4/rc6/rc10, same analyser)** [verified-in-game] 22 cells x 2 per build (rc2 20). no_route: rc2 34/1092 s, rc4 30/859 s, rc6 12/457 s, rc10 9/174 s. gave_up: 5/204, 6/442, 2/76, 2/108. open_stall: 6/262, 6/471, 4/246, 3/167. [BOT-TRAPPED] bails per 44 runs: rc4 16, rc6 9, rc10 7. Crashes 0 in all. Per-cluster table in NOTES OBJECTIVE-REACH.md. *How:* audit/objreach.py SRC REC TXT --json OUT; objreach_table.py OUT.md; cluster_table.py.

## Objective-reach pass 2 (11-08): exits, faces, jet-ups, tank embeds

### Facts

- **sub_DD890 sets a body position (eax = actor, ecx = Vec3*): moves pilots, not tanks** [verified-in-game] The teleport action's per-player call. If actor+0x90 (PhysicsInfo block) is non-zero it only copies the position there; otherwise it calls the body component (actor+0x8C)+0x40 vtable slot 1, thiscall(pos*). Test (RECOMP_BOT_TEST_TELEPORT): a pilot rose 4.9 m in 0.07 s and fell normally; a tank (actor+0x90 = 0, component path) did not move at all, and embedded tanks were not freed. A tank's physics position is set elsewhere (open). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_TEST_TELEPORT="bot,t,dy" (bot -1 = first bot in a tank) logs the position then, +0.5 s and +2 s.
- **Embedded tank signature: x/z velocity exactly 0, position fixed, vel.y swinging** [verified-in-game] After a hard landing (flying off a crest at cruise 18-20 m/s, or hit hard) a tank can stay embedded for the match: x/z velocity exactly 0, position equal to the cm, vertical velocity swinging -4.+75 m/s (0 in about half the samples), pivot and eject refused. Seen at On the Rocks 1023,58,1357 and 1499-1537,1463-1553 (about once per run, CTF and Snatch It) and CTF Bogged Down 874,972. No collider there (FPROBE). The bots detect it (1.5 s, vel.y swinging in a third of frames) and mark the spot (EmbedMark); they cannot free the tank.
- **Tank speed: 18-20 m/s cruise; me->vel spikes are single frames** [verified-in-game] Measured from positions at 1 s cadence no bot tank exceeded 20 m/s in the rc14 matrix; the instantaneous velocity (Ma2PlayerView.vel) shows 30-53 m/s spikes on rough ground. sub_2AD5C0 forward speed is a percent of the body's own top speed, above cruise for tanks.
- **A pilot leaving a 'Mech is held ~2.4 s by the game, then can be wedged inside the hull** [verified-in-game] Pilots appear 2-2.7 m from the 'Mech centre inside its 6-6.5 m hull; no input moves them for ~2.4 s (exit animation). EjectStep (travel leg, first 0.5 s) fired 0-2 times a match; a push 120 deg off the way out walked one in under the 'Mech (0.9 m from centre) where nothing moves it. ExitUnwedge: from 2.2 s to 7 s, within 4.5 m of that hull, walk 7 m out at 0/+-45/+-90 deg, 1 s each. Result: 43 of 44 exits walked off, median 2.6 s.
- **Check It No Man's Land terminal 634,74,1227: only a BattleArmor gets up (east face)** [verified-in-game] Every recorded claim (5 runs) came from a BattleArmor climbing the east face 562,39,1182 -> 597,72,1198 and getting out on top. The east face is slope 82-117 (39-50 deg, a wall on the grid); the west face stops pilots at its foot (505-512,1236-1248) although the grid reads 30 deg. FootPrecheck plans the walk as a pilot (radius 0.6, drop 10, learned pilot faces) and stays in when it ends > 8 m short; PilotFace learns a failed face (stall or 8 s shuttle under a waypoint 2 m+ up) as impassable for pilots 30 m round.
- **Jet-up and drop give-ups: judge by landing, not by a 1 m rise; replans restarted them** [verified-in-game] A jet-up counted as climbed after any 1 m rise (a hop) and a 2.4 m drift restarted its clock: a BA retried a 9 m up-link for minutes (rc10_93b b2, Base War Rush Hour hill 1040-1150,1600-1690). JetUpLanded: landed = within 2 m of the landing height and 8 m of it; tries keyed on 6 m. Drops: each replan along an edge moved the try 8-10 m and restarted the 5 s give-up (rc10_83b b9, four tries); DropEdgeRun fails an earlier try that lasted 2.5 s+ when a new one starts within 15 m / 15 s.
- **C7 diagnostics table filled at 256 pieces** [verified-in-game] Pieces first used late in a match (StuckHull) got no slot: they ran but were neither logged nor counted ('[C7] table full: pieces 256'). Raised to 384 (34d026e).
