## Film review + arrival parity (11-08): moment-by-moment bot play judged against human play

### Facts

- **How bot play is reviewed: play-by-play film of every bot with its surroundings (audit/film.py)** [verified-in-game] Review standard: each bot is judged at each moment against what a skilled human player would do in its place, not by totals or a checklist. audit/film.py TOOLS REC [--bots] [--t0 --t1 --step] prints one line per bot per step: team, body, hp, speed, goal/role/op/note, target (dist, hp), weapon groups that fired in the last second, heat, defence state, Alpha, the 3 nearest enemies (dist, bearing, hp, what they do: CARRYING / CLAIMING / ->whom), 2 nearest mates, objective state, power-ups within 40 m; events (deaths, kills, body changes, 15 %+ hits) inline. audit/moments.py and audit/qsweep.py only point at moments worth watching. Notes go to *How:* python -I film.py <src_parN>/tools --t0 20 --t1 80 --step 4 (use the tools of the build that recorded it: struct layouts change).
- **JetUpLong: jet up-links reach 28 m (PATH_HOP_LONG), not 10 m; capped jet searches get the HopOut pass** [verified-in-game] ma2_bot_path.c up-links scanned PATH_UP_REACH 5 cells, so a 15 m bank 12 cells deep (Ill Wind, under the Snatch It cores, 716,1384 y2 -> 716,1360 y17) was never a jet-up: team 2 jet 'Mechs planned 838 m round vs 705 m with the long reach (team 1 501 m). The long reach widens pass 1 on city maps until it hits the expansion cap before running dry, which stopped the HopOut pass (the only one that lands on a deck): Rush Hour T2 to the y55 core deck ok=1 564 m -> ok=0. Fix: a capped jet search 10 m+ short also gets HopOut, and jet bodies cap pass 1 at 160k (80k for a goal on a built top). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_JET_UP_LONG=0 / [Bots] JetUpLong=0 for the old reach. [C7] jetuplong: links, hop_after_cap, capped, capped_deck. PATHTEST 'len=' excludes the first leg (start -> pt[0]).
- **MechClimbJet / ClimbProgress: a jet 'Mech or BattleArmor that stops getting nearer a higher route point jets at it** [verified-in-game] Jet 'Mechs slid back down 0.41-0.52 slopes for 70 s (Ill Wind y -18 basin exit ramp 762,1414 -> 720,1414) and a BattleArmor circled 25 s under On the Rocks' y78 core plateau: BaUnstick only fires when still. ma2_bot_ctrl.c now jets (body_jump_up, <= 30 m) at the next route point when it is 2 m+ higher and the body has not got 2 m nearer it in 2.5 s (or not moved 0.9 m in 1.2 s). Slope stall share by slope (slp = rise/run x100): 6-41 ~10-20 %, 42-47 21 %, 48-53 30 %. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_MECH_CLIMB_JET=0 / [Bots] MechClimbJet. [BOT-CLIMBJET] diag. [C7] mechclimbjet: jets, jets_ba, progress.
- **Objective hunters named no target: 'enemy within 20 m of the looked-at spot' (HuntTarget / CarrierFire)** [verified-in-game] obj_order set a hunt's target to obj_enemy_near(obj_pt, 20 m); obj_pt is the look at the carrier, refreshed every 1.5-5 s by skill, so a 20-30 m/s carrier was 20 m+ away and the hunter had NO target (CTF Bogged Down: carriers passed hunters at 17 m and 37 m). The travel order also fired only at the brain's own threat target (Rush Hour: four 'Mechs at 70-150 m let a core carrier pass, 2 shots in 7 s). Fixes: HuntTarget names the visible carrier directly; CarrierFire fires at it in reach; TravelFire fires any order target seen in reach; HeatPush skips the BurstFire vent pause on a carrier or a target under 30 %. *How:* Switches RECOMP_BOT_HUNT_TARGET / CARRIER_FIRE / TRAVEL_FIRE / HEAT_PUSH. [BOT-NOFIRE] (RECOMP_BOT_DIAG) names why a target in reach went 1.5 s unshot: order fire=0, heat, no_los, ally_in_line, cadence/aim, range, defended, vtol_nose, blast_hold.
- **Target jamming (defence type 3) had no use rule: bots never switched it on** [verified-in-game] shield_logic (ma2_bot_brain.c) handled shield / absorber / AMS (heavy fire), camo (retreat/cover) and the anti-BA 'Mech shield, but not MA2_DEFT_JAM. 'Mechs with jamming died under 2-4 attackers with it ready. JamUse: jamming goes on under heavy fire (skill-scaled dps, hit < 1 s ago), and any non-camo defence goes on as a last stand under 35 % hp, hit in the last 1.5 s (Regular+). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_JAM_USE=0 / [Bots] JamUse. [C7] jamuse: on, last_stand.
- **Weapon upgrades are class-specific (Energy / Ballistic / Missile); the bot view knew only 'weapon'** [inferred] Templates 'Energy Weapon' / 'Ballistic Weapon' / 'Missile Weapon' set PowerupWeaponFireClass0/1/2 = 1; the game gives one only to a body with a weapon of that class below its top level. Ma2PickupView had only armor (0 = weapon), and wpn_room meant 'some class has room', so bots walked onto upgrades of a class they could not raise (BA b9 circled two for 3-5 s each). Interim: PuRefusedKind (2 s on it, then no weapon upgrades for that body). Proper fix in progress: read the class flags (offset being located with RECOMP_BOT_PU_DUMP [PICKUP-DUMP] +0x180.+0x1DC) and match per class. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_PU_DUMP=1 with RECOMP_BOT_DIAG prints each pickup's dwords once.
- **ChargeCool and VtolAirDuel: no heat pause when cool; short hover bursts against aircraft** [inferred] ChargeFire paused every heat weapon through each charge-weapon charge even at 5 % heat (a group silent 7-25 s at 44-127 m): now only at heat >= 50 %. VTOL attack phase 1 (stop, face, fire) lasted 1.5-3.5 s; two VTOLs fighting each other sat at ~1 m/s for 10 s+ in three matches: against an aircraft the burst is 0.7-1.3 s, then a new spot. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_CHARGE_COOL / RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_AIR_DUEL. [C7] chargecool: fired_through; airduel: bursts.
- **RunFocus, DeckScreen, TankBlastSwerve, SnatchRush, DropShort** [inferred] RunFocus: a grab / hunt / carry runner is not pulled off by a target > 120 m unless hurt (< 40 %) or under fire (> 15 dps) - it shoots on the move. DeckScreen: Snatch It bodies that cannot reach a raised core pile screen a third of the way from the pile to the enemy base. TankBlastSwerve: a tank escaping a death blast swerves along its heading / tangent (a point behind it was a pivot on the spot and death). SnatchRush: guards play the opening while their base holds no core. DropShort: a drop leg that lands 4 m+ low, 8 m+ short and still for 2 s replans and forbids that drop 10 min. *How:* Switches RECOMP_BOT_RUN_FOCUS / DECK_SCREEN / TANK_BLAST_SWERVE / SNATCH_RUSH / DROP_SHORT.
- **Open items from the 11-08 film review** [verified-in-game] (1) CTF Bogged Down T2 two-rider VTOL crawls 5-15 m/s at y46 out of its base (also rc10_60a). (2) A VTOL carrying the flag-holder BA flies off to repair at 12 % and strands the carrier. (3) 'Mechs queue single-file in streets (choke-follow + yield). (4) Bodies pinned on unseen obstacles at deck corners (Rush Hour 1165,1429). (5) Tanks pivot on the spot 12 s among checkpoint clutter (Check It Deliverance). (6) Ill Wind Snatch It stays ~1.4x map-uneven (sea inlet). *How:* Film the named runs to see them.
- **Weapon power-ups carry their fire class: entity +0x1B4 / +0x1B8 / +0x1BC = class 0 / 1 / 2 (PowerupWeaponFireClass0-2)** [verified-in-game] RECOMP_BOT_PU_DUMP run (CTF Deliverance, 11-08): every weapon upgrade sets exactly one of the dwords +0x1B4/+0x1B8/+0x1BC to 1; armour packs have +0x1B0 = armour and none set. Player 00F85DA0 took the +0x1B4 crate then the +0x1B8 crate and its arsenal class 0 then class 1 rose (arsenal +0x7C+4c, 56.6/56.7 s). So crate class c raises arsenal class c. Bots (PuClass, par12): Ma2PickupView.wclass, Ma2PlayerView.wpn_room = bit per class with room; a bot wants only crates whose class it can raise. Arsenal tops seen: 'Mechs c0/c1/c2 2/2/2 or 2/2/0; BattleArmor only c2; kind-3 c0+c2. *How:* Read MEM32(e+0x1B4+4c)==1 for the class; armour = MEM32(e+0x1B0).
- **Check It: a pilot that gets out with an enemy combat body within 150 m dies (13 of 14), and the 40 m get-out left a 40 m walk** [verified-in-game] Film review A_70a-A_73a (par10): 13 of 14 bots that ejected to work a terminal with an enemy 'Mech/tank/BA/VTOL within 150 m died 2-7 s later without claiming; 30 of 44 ejects came at the 40 m threshold. Fixes (par13): EjectClear (stay in and fight while an enemy combat body is within 150 m of us or the terminal; C7 ejectclear held_s) and EjectClose (get out at 12 m, or inside 40 m once the vehicle gains no 1 m in 2.5 s; C7 ejectclose early/near). Switches RECOMP_BOT_EJECT_CLEAR / _EJECT_CLOSE, [Bots] EjectClear / EjectClose. *How:* ma2_bot_brain_obj.c obj_order, before the MA2_ORD_EJECT.
- **VTOL stall watch counted +-10 m wobble as headway; VtolHeadway measures getting nearer the route goal** [code-confirmed] A_64a (CTF map 4, par9): T1 VTOL with a BA rider hung 23 s at its stick ceiling (48.7 m) under a 89 m climb need; the old watch (2.2 m drift = progress) never tripped. VtolHeadway (par14, ctrl.c vtol_prepare): 60 m+ from the route goal, not in a firing hover, no 15 m nearer in 10 s -> airblk_add 30 m ahead + replan. C7 vtheadway shut; RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_HEADWAY / [Bots] VtolHeadway. *How:* Diag line [BOT-VTOL] headway:
- **A 'Mech that goes down while its pilot ejects blows ~5 s after 0 hp, not 2.2 s (EjectBlast)** [verified-in-game] Film 11-08 (par13-15 sweep): when the hull reaches 0 hp during its pilot's eject (low-hp eject, Check It eject), the death blast comes 4.5-5.0 s after 0 hp (A_90a 48.3 -> 53.4; c13_70a 65.1 -> 70.1 killing three 'Mechs; A_74b, A_85b, c13_72a x2). Plain kills stay at 2.2 s. The ejected pilot shows as an alive pilot 2.7-2.8 m from the hull within ~1 s. EjectBlast (core blasts_update, RECOMP_BOT_EJECT_BLAST / [Bots] EjectBlast, default on, par16): an alive pilot within 8 m of a downed 'Mech in its first 2 s holds that blast's window to 5.8 s (was 2.6 s, after which BlastWary let defenders walk back ). Ejected pilots are locked 2-6 s beside the hull (all 88 ejects); ~75 % die within 10 s, but riding to 0 hp kills the pilot every time, so stays. [C7] ejectblast: late.
- **SlopeStuck: a goto that holds a target yaw it never turns to is walked out** [inferred] After a drop a walker's MechAI goto can stand with comp+0x98 (forward speed) 0, comp+0xB0 (turn rate) 0, ai+0x360 0 and its target yaw comp+0xA0 17 deg off the facing while the carrot is 120 deg off (A_205a TD b6 fell 61 -> 47 m at 71.5, stood 7.5 s). SlopeTurn only treated the target yaw as held within 10 deg (0.17 rad), so GotoWalk's 1 s clock reset every frame. SlopeStuck (RECOMP_BOT_SLOPE_STUCK / [Bots] SlopeStuck, default on, par17 99a7728e, commit 4b8ab9d): off > 25 deg with no turn rate also counts as held. 30 post-drop stands of 3-17 s in the par13-15 sweep. [C7] slopestuck: held_s.
- **The engage 'fight wedged' watchdog never fired (engaged cleared every frame); WedgeLive + BoxWedge** [inferred] In ctrl_do_engage's 'Mech/tank branch ctrl_release_attack sets c->engaged = 0 right before 'if (!c->engaged) reset eng_pos/eng_wt', so the 6 s no-headway clock reset every frame: '[BOT-CTRL] fight wedged' fired 0 times in 56 par15 sweep matches and ctrl_engaged counted an engagement per frame (s17_205a b5: 140/s, BOT-SUM engagements in the thousands). WedgeLive (RECOMP_BOT_WEDGE_LIVE / [Bots] WedgeLive, par19 ab85ca09) keeps the flag across the release. BoxWedge (RECOMP_BOT_BOX_WEDGE, par18): a stand that is only ctrl_fight's 'boxed in: stand and shoot' (no ring step passes fight_spot_ok) for 6 s+ no longer counts its shots as headway (s17_205a TD b5 stood boxed 43 s at 1010,28.6,1668 firing at 160-260 m, 96 -> 45 %). engage_wedged makes the brain find a firing spot. [C7] wedgelive: wedged; boxwedge: wedged.
- **LmsGhostRoam: LMS ghosts were still 'investigated' and stomped** [inferred] In LMS / Team LMS an eliminated player stays in the player list as an alive 10-hp pilot with deaths >= 1, parked at its spawn (A_400a: T2's at 886-920,1449-1458). LmsGhost skipped them as targets and LmsOutCount as opponents, but pick_roam_raw's freshest-memory 'investigate' and the stomp surprise still chose them: b1 sat on the ghosts 140-180 s (stomped one) while the last live T2 pilot was 800 m off. LmsGhostRoam (RECOMP_BOT_LMS_GHOST_ROAM / [Bots] LmsGhostRoam, par20, commit f5edd0e) skips them in both. [C7] lms: ghost_roam_skipped.
- **HeatJet: 'Mech travel hops wait while hot near enemies** [inferred] Each 'Mech jet hop adds about 20-35 % heat. On hilly maps with jet-up routing (custom cu1 = Bogged Down base) bots hopped into fights already at 80-119 % and could not fire (cu1_bw b10 / b1: 471 / 107 damage in 150 s). HeatJet (RECOMP_BOT_HEAT_JET / [Bots] HeatJet, par21, commit c41dece; heat_jet_hold in ma2_bot_ctrl.c) holds the cruise hop and route hop while heat >= 65 % with an enemy within 350 m; up-jets, stall and escape hops are unchanged. Mech time at heat >= 100: 15 -> 9 % (cu1 Base War), 6 -> 4 % (Rush Hour Base War). [C7] heatjet: held.
- **Bots play every mode on editor-made maps; how to launch them** [inferred] All ten modes armed and played with bots fighting; quick-test closes the game at Game Over, so LMS-type runs end early. Two engine-side faults showed up: the DSOUND 0xFE000268 crash (LMS, 4 s) and a sim-thread freeze (Not It, 30 s).
- **Awake MechAI goto parks a 'Mech ~10-15 m short of a touch point; TouchStall walks it in** [documented] 11-09: body_steer (awake MechAI in goto mode 6, drive tag A348) stops a 'Mech 10-15 m short of its point and stands at 0 m/s. TouchStride hands a lined-up 'Mech 8 m+ from a touch point (core, flag, power-up) to that navigator, so near a Snatch It core it stood still, or went stop-go as the bearing drifted past 0.35 rad (B_803 b2: 4 s at 10.4-11.2 m from the core under fire). TouchStall (ma2_bot_ctrl.c ctrl_exact_walk, default on, RECOMP_BOT_TOUCH_STALL): handed off, under 1.5 m/s for 0.5 s within 16 m -> direct walk for the rest of that point. The 16 m limit keeps the start-of-match wait far out from latching the slow direct walk (~7.5 m/s). par23: 6 and 8 fires per Snatch It match; B_803 OBJECTIVE-IGNORED 8 -> 0 in t23_803.

<a id="t25_dsound_defer_guard_1109"></a>

## DirectSound deferred-list double insert (audio-thread crash at 0x3A8A02)

### Facts

- **Audio-thread crash at guest 0x3A8A02 / read 0xFE000268 = a voice queued twice on the DirectSound deferred list** `003AD1A5`, `003AD345`, `003AACE7`, `003A65A0` [verified-in-game] Root cause of the recurring audio-thread access violation (guest stack 0x3A8A02 <- 0x3AAD59 <- 0x3C4C70 <- 0x3AB348 <- 0x3AB3C5; edi=ecx=0xFE000264, esi=0x00980334 = DSound core, ebx=core+0x4A0). sub_3AD1A5(voice, 1) (called by the APU interrupt release 0x3AAEE1) unlinks a finished voice from the active list (+0x4C) and tail-inserts its entry +0x54 on the core's deferred list +0x4A0 (0x3AD345, with ma2_audio_deferred_retain taking one ref). On the Xbox the DPC drains that list straight after the interrupt; here the DPC runs on another host thread, so a short voice can be restarted and finish again while its +0x54 entry is still queued. The second tail insert self-links the entry while the list head still points at it; RemoveEntryList sub_3A65A0 returns a self-linked entry unchanged, so the drain loop sub_3AACE7 calls the voice's poll (vtable 0x4535B0 slot 6 = 0x3AECB7) and Release (sub_3A666A) on the same voice again and again until it is destroyed. The base destructor 0x3A79F7 resets the vtable to 0x453448, whose slot 6 is sub_3A89C5, a stdcall API wrapper called thiscall-style, so it reads its object argument from stack garbage (0xFE000264) and Release faults reading 0xFE000268. Proven live: the dsfix build's list walk logged '[AUDIO-DEFER] voice object 00BFBCA4 . finished again while still queued (position 0)'. 00BFBCA4 is the edx value in the d5_62b crash block. SHIPPED: PC Release par24 (48831dc, exe sha256 28c3eb44.) since 2026-11-09. Switch: t28.audio-defer-guard-env. *How:* Fixed in branch dsound-defer-fix (commits 0163bba + b984562; Test exe 'MechAssault 2 v13-1.0.2-dsfix2.exe' 1829d633). ma2_audio_defer_insert_ok (apu\ma2_audio_guest.inc, hooked at loc_003AD345 before the retain) walks the deferred list and skips the insert when the voice's entry is already a member: the queued entry already runs the voice's state poll. Safety net ma2_audio_defer_drain_ok (loc_003AAD51) resets a head that points at a self-linked entry, and never calls into an object whose vtable is the destroyed base 0x453448. grep stderr for [AUDIO-DEFER]. RECOMP_AUDIO_DEFER_GUARD=0 turns both off. A crash with this stack in a build that has the guard means some other path corrupts the list. Proof 11-09: 18 hidden runs on the guard builds (cu1 LMS x8, cu1 Not It x6, Going Commando cell 6/2 x4), 0 crashes; the insert guard fired 7 times in 6 runs (each one the crash setup); the drain safety net never fired. 6 runs instead hit the separate ACTIVE-list freeze (APU thread looping KeInsertQueueDpc, esp 0x7FFFC4), fixed by ActiveGuard 5a2b21c on branch hang-watch, which is built on top of this guard.

<a id="t26_dsound_active_guard_1109"></a>

## DirectSound active-list re-insert (game freeze in BA death blasts)

### Facts

- **Game-thread freeze during BattleArmor death blasts = DirectSound DPC spinning forever on a self-linked active-list entry while holding the DSound lock 0x3C4598** `003AE5C7`, `003AE754`, `003AACE7`, `003AAD1D` [verified-in-game] The game thread holds the XACT critical section 0x3E869C (taken in sub_3DDE80) and blocks at 0x3DDECB in the XACT raise lock sub_3DDEAD -> ma2_xact_raise_lock, waiting for the DirectSound API lock 0x3C4598. That lock is held by the DSound DPC thread (kernel_run_dpc -> sub_3AB3BC -> sub_3AB320, which holds 0x3C4598 for the whole run), sampled 3/3 times inside the drain sub_3AACE7 / voice poll sub_3AECB7: it is not blocked, it loops. Mechanism: the voice start sub_3AE5C7 head-inserts the voice entry (voice+0x4C) on an active list (core+0x488/+0x490/+0x498) at loc_3AE754 without checking that it is still linked. On the Xbox the APU interrupt release 0x3AAEE1 -> sub_3AD1A5 always unlinks a finished voice first; here the ISR try-locks 0x3C4598 and skips the release when the lock is held, and the stop-wait sub_3AE0D2 gives up after 0.5 s, so a restarted voice can still be on the list. Head-inserting an entry that is already the head self-links it (Flink=Blink=self) while the head still points at it. Phase 1 of sub_3AACE7 treats a self-linked current entry as 'list changed under me' and restarts from the head (loc_3AAD1D), which is that same entry again: an endless walk with 0x3C4598 held, so every other thread that needs the DSound lock (the game thread via XACT) waits forever. The APU thread keeps calling KeInsertQueueDpc (ordinal 119) at esp 0x7FFFC4 throughout. Proven by the hang watchdog: [CS-WAIT] tid=<game> waits on 0x003C4598 at guest 003DDECB; held by tid=<DPC thread>, with the DPC thread's guest stack in sub_3AACE7/sub_3AECB7 (runs h3_cu1 t=9.21, h3_cu2 t=10.21). Separate , but the same race family as, the deferred-list double insert (dsound-defer-double-insert). SHIPPED: PC Release par24 (48831dc, exe sha256 28c3eb44.) since 2026-11-09. Switch: t28.audio-active-guard-env; the hang sampler is t28.cs-wait-hang-sampler. *How:* Fixed in branch hang-watch (commit 5a2b21c on top of DeferGuard 0163bba and diagnostics e47a885; b984562 cherry-picked as 48831dc; clue fast-forwarded to 48831dc for release candidate par24). Test exe 'MechAssault 2 v13-hang5.exe' (a test folder, md5 be6011a3). Switch RECOMP_AUDIO_ACTIVE_GUARD (default on, =0 off), code in apu\ma2_audio_guest.inc. ma2_audio_active_preinsert (hooked at loc_3AE754 in recomp_0096.c) unlinks the voice entry first when it is still linked and its neighbours point back at it, logging '[AUDIO-ACTIVE] voice object X (hw voice N) started while still on an active list; unlinked first'. Safety net ma2_audio_active_repair (hooked at loc_3AAD1D in recomp_0095.c) runs only when the list head points at a self-linked entry and rebuilds the Flinks from the Blink chain (cap 1024, empties a looping chain). Diagnostics: RECOMP_BOT_STALL=1 makes the bot stall monitor print the game thread's guest registers and code-range return addresses, plus [CS-WAIT] lines (kernel_rtl.c xbox_cs_waiters_dump) naming every thread blocked in a guest critical section, the lock VA, the waiter's guest site and the owner's tid and taking site. A frozen run shows [BOT-STALL] freeze with menu pulse stopped; Game Over shows idle bots with 'menu pulse 0 ms ago'. Proof (2026-11-09, hang5 exe, RECOMP_BOT_STALL=1): 19/19 runs with 0 freezes. 10 LMS on the custom map b3_allmodes_rides (60 s, skill 3; pre-fix baseline about 2 freezes in 7) and 9 Not It (6 custom map + 3 retail par 5/4, 150 s; pre-fix hang3 baseline 2/2 froze at t=9-10). The guard fired in 10 of the 19 runs: [AUDIO-ACTIVE] 21 times (all 6 custom Not It runs, 1-4 each; LMS runs 1, 2 and 5; retail ni2), each one a re-insert that used to freeze the game. [AUDIO-DEFER] fired 7 times. No [CS-WAIT] lines. h5_lms8 ending at t=39 was a normal LMS Game Over, not a freeze.

<a id="t27_pink_placeholder_mtb_refs_1109"></a>

## Pink pole-and-cube placeholder in custom scenarios: templates named inside .mtb files

### Facts

- **The pink placeholder (40 m pole + 10 m cube) is drawn when an object's build fails, not only when its model file is missing: B4720 passes false to vtable slot 0 (sub_D8221), which attaches the marker built by sub_D8391** `000D8221`, `000D8391`, `000B4720`, `000B47B7` [verified-in-game] sub_B4720(entity, flag) builds a world object: ok = vt+0x38 (resolve; MABuilding = sub_129490) then vt+0x2C (init; MABuilding = sub_127ED7, which first calls MACorporeal model load sub_D7B3D), then calls vtable slot 0 = sub_D8221(ok). sub_D8221 stores ok in entity+0x1C bit 0x800 (sub_B2790) , when ok is false, attaches a shared debug mesh made by sub_D8391 to entity+0x94: an untextured 4-sided prism 1 m wide and 40 m tall (globals 0x50C8C0, height = float 0x471450 = 40.0) plus a 10 m cube (0x50C8C4), colour 0xFFFE6BE8 (pink), placed at the entity position + 40 m. That is the 'pink pillar', 'pink cube on a pole' and 'pink Battle Armor'. MABuilding resolve sub_129490 creates its DestroyedBuilding template (+0x1B8) with sub_161D77 and runs sub_B5E80 (tree walk sub_B2B70 calling each node's resolve) over it; any failure down that chain (destroyed building, its collapse sequence, or an object its .mtb names) clears the result, so a building whose OWN model loads fine still draws as the pink pole. The instance's TemplateID decides; a different Corporal3DObj on an OverrideTemplate=1 instance and the instance's DestroyedBuilding value are not used (game-tested 11-09). *How:* To find why an object is pink: log sub_D8221 calls with arg 0 (caller 0xB47B7) and the steps of the class's resolve/init. RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE shows the marker as an untextured 'prim 5 n 24' plus 'prim 5 n 36' draw.
- **mtb files name templates (TemplateID of embedded objects, DestroyedEffect, MAEffectID); the editor's [Assets] closure did not follow them, so e.g. Dante office 18 (v2 and plain) drew as the pink pole on Bogged Down (FIXED editor d34766e)** [verified-in-game] A model's .mtb is a WDF of its pieces and the pieces can carry entity properties: TemplateID (objects embedded in the .mtb), DestroyedEffect and MAEffectID (rubble/dust/explosion effects). Survey of all 716 .mtb on the disc: 93 DestroyedEffect, 87 TemplateID and 149 MAEffectID values are GlobalEntities UIDs. City Fight case: placed BldCom_DAN_Office18_v2 (0x1ECB2) -> DestroyedBuilding v2_WS (0x1ECAE) -> v2_WS_CS (0x1ECAF), whose BldCom_DAN_Office18_WS_2_CS.mtb gives 12 chunks DestroyedEffect = 0x1E0DE 'BD_Debris_Crash_LG_01 - CRASH MODIFIERS ONLY!' (files SpecialEffects/BuildingDestruction/BD_Debris_Crash_LG_01/BD_Debris_Crash_LG_01.MGMODEL + .mtb, and BD_Debris_Crash_LG_01.mgparticle). Bogged Down and common.mgf lack them, the editor never shipped them, the game logged failed lookups for that .mtb/.MGMODEL/.mgparticle, the building build failed and drew the placeholder. All files of the building itself were found (lookup trace at sub_25D60 call sites). Shipping those 3 files (manual [Assets] edit, then the fixed editor's re-save) makes the building draw (shots in NOTES NOTES pink-shots). Office15/19 work on Bogged Down because their .mtb references (RubblePile_02, BD_DustCloud_LG) are in boggeddown.mgf. *How:* Editor fix d34766e: TemplateCatalog:mtb_refs reads a template's CorporalMTB (else <model>.mtb) and closure follows TemplateID/MAEffectID/learned reference keys found there; fresh_templates also ships closure templates known to the Base whose model the Base/common lack. Old saves need a re-save in the fixed editor (the game runtime is unchanged). Sweep: fmt_test.exe --game <install> --mtb-sweep OUT.tsv -> 102 of 918 palette templates reach templates only through .mtb references and would have drawn the placeholder on at least one of 36 Bases (Office18/v2/WS and Office07/WS on 32 Bases incl. Bogged Down; 24 templates on Bogged Down). DestroyedEffect path verified in game; MAEffectID/TemplateID paths are inferred from the same code (not each tested in game). UPDATE 11-09 evening: the turret path is proven too (Dual Laser Turret's .mtb names Expl_Tur_02; missing it failed the turret on Mission_08). Sweep with code-required files: 216 of 918 palette templates affected before, 0 after; editor d062003f in PC Release.
- **Every MABuilding needs 4 hard-coded effect files (BD_Holefire_Loop_01, BD_WindowShatter, BD_HoleDamage .mgparticle, BD_HoleDecal.mat); on a Base without them any placed building draws the pink placeholder** `00129490`, `004B0030`, `004B0034`, `004B0038` [verified-in-game] MABuilding resolve sub_129490 checks \SpecialEffects\BuildingDestruction\BD_WindowShatter.mgparticle (ptr 0x4B0034), BD_Holefire_Loop_01.mgparticle (0x4B0030), BD_HoleDamage.mgparticle (0x4B0038) via sub_16BA65 and \SpecialEffects\Effects_Decals\BD_HoleDecal.mat (0x4B003C) via sub_16BC28; any miss clears the result. Game-observed 11-09: BldCom_DAN_Office15 placed on a Mission_08 copy draws the pink pole even with every .mtb-referenced file shipped (pinkfix editor 85b87342); the only failed lookups are these 4 paths (Mission_08 has no buildings). The editor's [Assets] closure does not know these code-named paths. *How:* FIXED editor dcdcad4 (TemplateCatalog:code_required, published to PC Release 11-09 as editor d062003f): ships the 4 files plus their closure when Base/common lack them (Mission_08, Mission_06b, In Your Face). XBE survey: no other class needs a code-named file that some Base lacks. Game proof: Office15 + Dual Laser Turret on a Mission_08 copy, 2 failed objects -> 0.

## Public-release polish (2026-11): what changed, which fact says so, which build has it

### Overview
This topic collects the changes made while preparing the public release (version 1.0.2). Two groups: changes of
2026-10-21.11-09 that were already in the published PC Release (par24, 48831dc, exe 28c3eb44) but had no
fact, and the release-polish work of 2026-11-10 in the r26 branch (game), the editor repository and the installer kit.
The r26 items are code-complete and mostly proven in a hidden test run; they are NOT yet published. Each row below
names the fact (merged id = `t28.<id>`), the commit and where it shipped. Every fact also has a how_to_use line with
the switch and the proof. Corrections to older facts are in (BattleArmor walk, frame limit,
tank step, FPU shipped note, status clean-up).

Reading the status words: "par24" = in the published build; "r26" = in the r26 source branch, not yet published;
"editor" = editor repository after dcdcad4; "kit" = installer kit history after 7e85a1e.

### Facts

- **Bot BattleArmor ran on the spot after a jet: the jet clears walker bit comp+0x145 bit 0 and nothing set it back (BaLand, BaWalk)** [verified-in-game] BattleArmor walking works: a bot walks 11-15 m/s (measured on Bogged Down CTF) and a player's BattleArmor walks 15 m/s. The older fact that a BattleArmor MoveTo moves 0 m/s because walking is animation driven is wrong. A jet clears comp+0x145 bit 0 (comp+0x144 bit 8, the walker's hold on the body). For an AI-driven BattleArmor nothing set it back, so after its first jet the bot played the run animation on the spot and moved only by more hops. BaLand sets the bit back once the BattleArmor is down (ai+0x240 clear for 0.25 s). The code that restores the bit for a player's BattleArmor was not found (sub_119521 and sub_17D401 belong to other classes). *How:* Fix a8eab5c (2026-11-03), in PC Release since exe 24452d6b and in par24 (48831dc). Two switches, both on by default: BaLand (RECOMP_BOT_BA_LAND / [Bots] BaLand) and BaWalk (RECOMP_BOT_BA_WALK_FIRST / [Bots] BaWalk): walk first, travel hops only 90 m or more from the goal and ending 40 m short, a strafe hop every 9-14 s in a fight, a dodge hop every 7 s. Measured old vs new: walking 41 -> 66 % of ground time, standing 51 -> 23 %. Diagnostics: RECOMP_BOT_BA_ANIM_DIAG and RECOMP_BOT_BA_ANIM_DUMP. A roof landing needed a later fix (t19.audit-f2-baroofland). The hop workarounds BaUnstick, BaDipHop and BaHackHop were built on the 0 m/s premise and may now do more than is needed. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:5449
- **Missing voice lines: a streamed wave that fits in one XACT packet never played; XwbDefer completes wave-bank reads 4 ms later** `003E2BE1` [verified-in-game] Cinematic and mission voice lines went missing (for example '[text omitted]'): every streamed wave that fits in one 18,432-byte XACT stream packet, about 1.2 s or shorter (148 of 997 Voice_English waves and 48 SFXStream waves). XACT Play returned S_OK and the packet was read, but the stream never started. Cause: our NtReadFile completed the read inside the call, so XACT's packet fill sub_003E2BE1 saw 0 bytes left (its end-of-data path) during Play, before the stream had started; on an Xbox the disc read completes later. Fix XwbDefer (kernel_bridge.c): a read on a streaming wave bank handle (WBND header at offset 0, async handle, no event or APC) returns STATUS_PENDING and completes 4 ms later on a worker thread. The mission '[text omitted]' went from 27 of 37 lines to 37 of 37. *How:* Fix c036eb4 (2026-10-31), in PC Release par24 (48831dc). RECOMP_XWB_DEFER_MS sets the delay; RECOMP_XWB_PAD=0 turns the fix off; RECOMP_XWB_PADLEN=1 selects the older padding work-around (bad: its 1.5 s silent tail cut off the next line). Traces: RECOMP_IO_TRACE ([READ] h=), RECOMP_APU_VOICE_TRACE, RECOMP_SND_TRACE ([SND-PLAY] / [SND-RET]). Test recipe: RECOMP_TEST_MISSION_INDEX=4, then Enter five times. Do not add fprintf probes at XACT function entries in recomp_0098.c: that crashed every time (cause unknown). — kernel_bridge.c:3909
- **VTOL climb: flight component comp+0x90 is the climb demand (+30 Shift, -30 Ctrl); only human input fills it, so bots set it in a hook (ModClimb)** `00113964`, `00113478`, `000E9A5F`, `00113A6B` [verified-in-game] A stick-flown VTOL holds a fixed height and rises only when the ground pushes it. A player climbs with Shift (left stick click) and sinks with Ctrl: the flight component (actor+0x8C) has comp+0x90 = +30 while Shift is held, -30 with Ctrl and 0 otherwise (W+Shift for 4 s = +29 m at full speed). The flyer tick sub_113964 fills comp+0x90 every frame in its input pass sub_113478 from the human-only input object, so for a bot it was always 0 whatever command the bot sent. Fix ModClimb: the hook ma2_bot_vtol_lift(actor) at loc_00113A6B, between sub_113478 and the flight step sub_E9A5F, writes the bot's demand (vt_lift_demand = 30 when a surface is within climb distance). MoveTo also climbs, but it stops or crawls the craft (it settles 2 m short), so it is not used for climbing. *How:* Fix 37bfc0e (2026-11-01), in PC Release par24 (48831dc). Switch ModClimb / RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_MOD_CLIMB. The hook is a hand edit in the generated files recomp_0027.c and recomp_fast_0027.c: reapply it if they are regenerated (the installer kit carries it as a post-FastCode patch, t28.installer-kit-1109-post-fastcode). Code: ma2_bot_ctrl.c, ma2_bot_vtol_lift (line 2630) and vtol_manual. Test hooks: RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_VTOL_CLIMB, RECOMP_TEST_VTOL_CMDS, RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_PROBE. The height cap that applies on top is t18.ctfvtol-maxvtolheight. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:2630
- **VTOL stuck at about 0.4 m/s at 144 fps and above: horizontal drag sub_19236B snaps speed to 0 below 0.707 m/s before thrust adds a*dt (VtolSnapFix)** `0019236B`, `00192724`, `001922B8`, `004BB174` [verified-in-game] At 144 fps and above a VTOL under thrust could stay at about 0.4 m/s. The flyer's horizontal drag sub_19236B sets the horizontal speed to 0 when it is below 0.707 m/s. The thrust sub_192724 runs after it and adds a*dt (a is about 95), so with a small dt every step falls under the snap again. Fix ma2_vtol_snap_keep (recomp_manual.c): the snap is skipped while the commanded velocity (body+0x8C / +0x94) passes the gate constant at 0x4BB174. The velocity pipeline is sub_1922B8 (drag, vertical, turn, wobble, thrust). comp+0x8C / +0x94 hold the commanded velocity, not the thrust input. *How:* Fix 7db3064 (2026-11-04), in PC Release par24 (48831dc). RECOMP_VTOL_SNAP_FIX=0 gives the original behaviour. The Unlimited frame limit was removed the same day for this reason (t28.frame-limit-no-unlimited-default-144). Brake test script: RECOMP_TEST_HCLIMB_SCRIPT. — recomp_manual.c:1376
- **Frame limit: Unlimited was removed; presets 30 to 360, default 144, an ini value of 0 reads as 144** [code-confirmed] Since c3bee9c (2026-11-04) the Settings row 'Frame limit' cycles 30, 60, 90, 120, 144, 165, 180, 240 and 360 FPS; there is no Unlimited. The default is 144. At start a FrameLimit of 0 or less (an old ini that had Unlimited) is set to 144 and a value from 1 to 29 is set to 30. A saved value that is not a preset (for example 75) counts as 144 the next time the row is moved (Left 120, Right 165). First run picks 60 on integrated graphics and on a mid-range laptop, otherwise 144. Reason: uncapped step rates broke the VTOL thrust (t28.vtol-stick-snap-high-fps). *How:* Code: pc_native_settings.cpp line 652 (preset row) and line 937 (0 -> 144, under 30 -> 30); main.c line 205 (default 144, range 0-1000, env var RECOMP_FRAME_LIMIT); pc_firstrun.h line 16. A hand-edited value from 361 to 1000 is still honoured (area B finding B-16). The installer kit's default pc_settings.ini has FrameLimit=144 since the 2026-11-09 repack. In PC Release par24 (48831dc). — pc_native_settings.cpp:652
- **NavCache: the bots' static obstacle grid is kept on disk, on by default since 1.0.1 (bots ready at t=0 on a cached map)** [code-confirmed] The static part of the bots' obstacle grid is saved per map and game mode in %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\NavCache and loaded in the next match, so bots are ready in the first frame (Going Commando CTF: 896 ms build -> 22 ms load, first decision at t=0.0 instead of 0.9 s). The key holds the map archive and its size, the game mode, the grid extent, terrain and prop fingerprints, NAV_CACHE_VERSION, the grid constants and the build stamp; any mismatch or read error gives the normal build and the file is rewritten. Stock maps only: no file is written for an editor scenario. At most 24 files are kept (NAVC_KEEP, newest by write time, about 8-17 MB each). A cached grid equals a fresh build byte for byte on 8 maps; on Going Commando two fresh builds already differ by 1-3 cells (swaying MechTopples trees). *How:* Default ON since 46cfe22 (2026-11-03); it was added OFF in 8f91605 for 1.0. In PC Release par24 (48831dc). Off: RECOMP_BOT_NAV_CACHE=0 or [Bots] NavCache=0. RECOMP_BOT_NAV_CACHE_VERIFY=1 builds the grid anyway and compares: '[BOT-NAV-CACHE] verify map=<m> mode=<g> identical=1/0'. Counters: [C7] navcache hit / miss / write / reject. The build stamp in the key means each new exe rebuilds its files once. Disk use is area D finding D-11. This is not the older BotNav\gen_<fp>.map graph cache (t01b.nav-cache-path). — ma2_bots_core.c:1668
- **RECOMP_BOT_STALL=1 also prints [CS-WAIT] lines: which thread waits on which guest critical section and who owns it** [code-confirmed] With RECOMP_BOT_STALL=1 the bot stall monitor reports a game thread that has stopped ticking the bots ([BOT-STALL]). Since e47a885 (2026-11-09) it also prints [CS-WAIT] lines from xbox_cs_waiters_dump (kernel_rtl.c): every thread blocked in a guest critical section, the lock, the waiter's guest site, and the owner thread and where it took the lock. This is how the BattleArmor death-blast freeze was traced to the DirectSound DPC (t26.dsound-active-reinsert-freeze). A real freeze shows [BOT-STALL] with the menu pulse stopped; a finished match (Game Over) shows idle bots with a recent menu pulse. *How:* Set RECOMP_BOT_STALL=1 for any freeze report, then read the [BOT-STALL] and [CS-WAIT] lines in the game log. In PC Release par24 (48831dc). It is a diagnostic only: without the env var nothing is printed. — kernel_rtl.c:609
- **RECOMP_AUDIO_DEFER_GUARD (default on, 0 = off): DirectSound DeferGuard, no second deferred-list insert for a queued voice** [code-confirmed] DeferGuard fixes the audio-thread crash at guest 0x3A8A02 (read of 0xFE000268): a voice queued twice on the DirectSound deferred list. It is on by default; RECOMP_AUDIO_DEFER_GUARD=0 turns both of its checks off (the insert check and the drain safety net). Full cause and hook sites: t25.dsound-defer-double-insert. *How:* Commits 0163bba and 48831dc (2026-11-09), in PC Release par24. Code: apu\ma2_audio_guest.inc line 136. Log tag [AUDIO-DEFER]. — ma2_audio_guest.inc:136
- **RECOMP_AUDIO_ACTIVE_GUARD (default on, 0 = off): DirectSound ActiveGuard, no second active-list insert for a still-linked voice** [code-confirmed] ActiveGuard fixes the game freeze in BattleArmor death blasts (seen in Not It and Last Man Standing): a voice inserted a second time on the DirectSound active list made a self-linked entry, and the audio DPC walked it forever while holding the lock the game thread needed. It is on by default; RECOMP_AUDIO_ACTIVE_GUARD=0 turns it off. Full cause and hook sites: t26.dsound-active-reinsert-freeze. *How:* Commit 5a2b21c (2026-11-09), in PC Release par24 (48831dc). Code: apu\ma2_audio_guest.inc. Log tag [AUDIO-ACTIVE]. To look at a freeze: t28.cs-wait-hang-sampler. — ma2_audio_guest.inc:216
- **quick-test (RECOMP_QUICK_TEST=1): skips every movie up to the first in-match frame and closes the game when the match is left** `00481EF8`, `001F84DE`, `0048BAC8`, `002439B7` [documented] quick-test (or RECOMP_QUICK_TEST=1) is the mode the editor's Test button uses (a Preferences option, on by default). - **Scenario [Assets] build opens one retail archive at a time: the 32-archive limit is gone** [documented] A scenario's [Assets] rows are built by build_resource (ma2_scenario.c). The name-hash seed changed with the fix, so short resources made by older builds are rebuilt. *How:* Code: ma2_scenario.c line 818 (qsort by_archive). - **The Custom Scenarios picker lists the Name stored inside the .ma2map, not the file name: two files with the same Name look identical** [code-confirmed] The Custom Scenarios picker shows each scenario's [Scenario] Name from inside the .ma2map file, not the file name (ma2_scenario.c reads Name at line 613 and returns it as the entry's title text at line 2254); the multiplayer New Game map list is matched by the same Name (line 1659). Only the 8-character Id has to be unique: a second file with the same Id is skipped and logged as 'duplicate Id' (line 974). Before the fix: give each scenario its own Name in the editor. — ma2_scenario.c:613

<a id="t28_vtol_ferry_speed_1110"></a>

## VTOL ferry crawl: stale AI forward speed in the body integrator (2026-11-10)

## VTOL ferry crawl: stale AI forward speed (2026-11-10)

### Overview
A flying VTOL's body velocity is written each step by the generic integrator sub_002AD940 as
`flight-model velocity (comp+0x10C) + heading x ground speed` (sub_002AD800). The ground speed ramps toward the
forward-speed target comp+0x98 that the AI MoveTo sets (sub_002AD5C0). The stick flight model never clears it, so a bot
craft handed from AI MoveTo to the stick kept whatever MoveTo last asked: a rider pick-up hover left -53.4 m/s (red ferry
crawled at 6 m/s) or +43 m/s (blue ferry overspeed 100+ m/s). The 11-04 "height ceiling" explanation was wrong.

### Key code
| address / function | what it does |
|---|---|
| sub_002AD940 | body integrator; SetVel at 0x2ADAB9 |
| sub_002AD800 | ground term: heading (sub_002AD120) x speed ramped by sub_002ACCA0 |
| sub_002AD5C0 | SetForwardSpeed: pct x comp+0xBC x 0.01 -> comp+0x98 |
| vtol_stick_take (ma2_bot_ctrl.c) | stick takes the craft, zeroes comp+0x98 (StickSpeed0) |
| vt_edge_recover (ma2_bot_ctrl.c) | EdgeStickOut: no MoveTo while the stick already flies out of the edge band |

### Env vars / switches
RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_STICK_SPEED0, RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_EDGE_STICK_OUT (both on), RECOMP_TEST_VTOL_VELWATCH=<n> (write watch).

### History
Fixed in v26-vtol b91f768 (2026-11-10), proven on botrec 2026-11-10 and in NRC/Bogged Down CTF runs.



### Facts

- **Bot VTOL ferry crawl/overspeed = stale AI forward-speed target comp+0x98 added to the stick flight velocity** `002AD940`, `002AD800`, `002ACCA0`, `002AD120` [verified-in-game] The body integrator sub_002AD940 (reached from the comp step sub_002AEC20 when comp+0x140 == 0) stores the body velocity (state comp+0x40, SetVel 0x2B2810 at 0x2ADAB9) as slot5(dt) + the flight model velocity comp+0x10C. slot5 = comp vt+0x14 sub_192A72 -> sub_176A4E -> sub_002AD800, which (with comp+0x144 bit 8 set, as on every flying VTOL) returns heading(yaw, sub_002AD120) x a ground speed: sub_002ACCA0 ramps the current speed comp+0x5C (state +0x40 slot +0x18 = [+0x1C]) toward the target comp+0x98 (state +0x7C [+0x1C], written by SetForwardSpeed sub_002AD5C0 = pct x comp+0xBC x 0.01, clamped to +-comp+0xC0) at comp+0xC4 per second. An AI MoveTo (bot body_moveto) sets comp+0x98; the human/stick flight model never clears it. Fix (v26-vtol b91f768): vtol_stick_take zeroes the target through sub_2AD5C0 whenever the stick takes the craft. *How:* [C7] stickspeed0 zeroed; switch StickSpeed0 / RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_STICK_SPEED0 (default on, 0 = old behaviour). botrec: g('comp',0x98,'f') and g('comp',0x5C,'f') on the craft; [BOT-VTOL] stick takes . (RECOMP_BOT_DIAG). — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:2822
- **Proof of the VTOL forward-speed fix: recording state and live NRC/Bogged Down CTF runs** `002AD5C0` [verified-in-game] Recording 2026-11-10 bot 3 (red ferry): 815 of 857 frames from 12.04 s are stick-flown (branch S, comp+0x144 bit0 clear) with comp+0x98 = -53.4, so vtol_stick_take fires from 12.04 s and the integrator term ramps to 0 within 0.8 s (70 m/s^2). <a id="t29_lens_flash_freeze_1110"></a>

## Explosion lens flash and the screen haze fix (R26 tint)

## Explosion lens flash and the screen haze fix (R26 tint, 2026-11-10)

### Overview
Explosion and hit effects carry a `MAModSubObjectLensFilter` sub-object. When the effect comes into a view, the
game shows a full-screen colour quad (a filter object, class vtable 0x463D74) on that view's overlay list and fades
it: white, StartAlpha 0.2 at 0.6/s for a mech death (Expl_Mech_01, starting 2.2 s after the blast timer), 0.2 at
3/s for a BA mortar hit, 0.5 at 2.0/s for some other hits. The quad is drawn after the 3D scene and glow, before
the HUD.

The quad's visible flag and alpha are written only by the sub-object's per-frame update (sub_0013FC88). If that
update is skipped while the effect still exists, the flash stays on screen at constant strength: the uniform

### Key code
| Address | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| sub_0013F4BD | LensFilter ctor (vtable 0x471E18) | recomp_0032.c |
| sub_0013F5D3 | creates the filter per view; colour = Color + StartAlpha; hidden | recomp_0032.c |
| sub_0013FC88 / sub_0013FD69 | per-frame update: in view, fade and show; else hide | recomp_0032.c |
| sub_0013F832 | release: removes the filters | recomp_0032.c |
| sub_000AFCB0 | filter draw (untextured or textured quad, colour bytes clamped to 0x80) | recomp_0018.c |
| sub_002B1270 then sub_00107DA3 | modifier update gate (slot 25, then slot 24) | recomp_0070.c, recomp_0026.c |
| sub_00107F63 | range test: view distance against max(600, camera vt+0x38) | recomp_0026.c |

### Added code and hooks
- recomp_manual.c: ma2_lens_shown, ma2_lens_draw_check, ma2_lens_forget (the fix); ma2_lens_test_skip (test
hook); ma2_lens_trace_update, ma2_lens_trace_draw (diagnostics).
- recomp_0032.c: calls in sub_0013FC88 (three show sites, including sub_0013FD69) and at sub_0013F832 entry.
- recomp_0018.c: call at sub_000AFCB0 entry. Reapply these hooks if the recomp sources are regenerated.
- nv2a_pb_exec.c: cover_trace (RECOMP_COVER_TRACE).

### Env vars and test hooks
RECOMP_LENS_TRACE=1, RECOMP_TEST_LENS_FREEZE=<s>, RECOMP_LENS_FREEZE_FIX=0, RECOMP_COVER_TRACE=1.

### Bugs and fixes
- Frozen lens flash = screen haze. Fixed in v26-tint 9896cc8 (exe sha256 d64c14b6.): a lens quad its update did
not show in this frame or the one before is hidden. Proven with RECOMP_TEST_LENS_FREEZE=6 (before: constant haze,
frame 1st-percentile luma 125 for about 3 s; after: hidden two frames later, scene normal) and a regression run
(natural flash 0.486 to 0.014 in 0.24 s, no hide events; black fades unchanged).

### Open questions
- Which gate skips the update in natural play: the range test with the stale x87 far value, the view mapping, or the
timing window. RECOMP_LENS_TRACE logs '[LENS] STALE' with the fields when it happens.



### Facts

- **MAModSubObjectLensFilter is the explosion screen flash: a full-screen colour quad shown when the effect comes into view** `0013F4BD`, `0013FC88`, `0013F5D3`, `0013F832` [code-confirmed] MAModSubObjectLensFilter (ctor sub_0013F4BD, primary vtable 0x471E18, object 0x108 bytes) is a sub-object of explosion and hit effects. On its first active update sub_0013F5D3 creates a filter object (class vtable 0x463D74, ctor sub_000AFBA0, 0x40 bytes) per view and puts it on the view overlay list (view+0x164). The view draws it after the 3D scene and glow pass and before the HUD with sub_000AFCB0: an untextured pre-transformed 640x480 quad, blend SRC_ALPHA/INV_SRC_ALPHA, z LEQUAL, fog on. Saved fields (sub_0013F8FB): StartAlpha, EndAlpha, DeltaAlpha, CurAlpha, Color, Texture. Runtime: colour RGB +0xBC.+0xC4, StartAlpha +0xD0, DeltaAlpha +0xD8, CurAlpha +0xDC, single-view filter +0xCC, per-view {view, filter} pairs [+0xFC, +0x100). *How:* RECOMP_LENS_TRACE=1 logs every lens update and drawn flash. — generated recomp_0032.c (made at install time, not in the repository):4690
- **The lens flash fades only inside its own update sub_0013FC88: visible and CurAlpha -= dt*DeltaAlpha while the effect is in view** `0013FC88`, `0013FD69`, `0013FF21`, `0016B25E` [code-confirmed] sub_0013FC88 (vtable slot 24, called through sub_002B1270 only when slot 25 sub_00107DA3 allows it) returns early when the sub-object has no owner or its timing window (sub_002B0B20: StartTime +0x64, Duration +0x68, TimingFlags +0x70) is closed. Otherwise, per view (pairs list; view to camera via sub_0016B25E then [+0x154] vt+0x44), sub_0013FF21 tests the owner against the camera (vt+0x4C, plane mask 0x3F): in view, CurAlpha -= dt (double 0x4E2428) * DeltaAlpha, the colour is copied to the filter (sub_000AFC50) and filter+8 = 1; out of view, filter+8 = 0 with the alpha held. The filter flag and alpha are written nowhere else, so a skipped update leaves the last state on screen. — generated recomp_0032.c (made at install time, not in the repository):4690
- **Retail lens flash values: white, StartAlpha 0.2 fading at 0.6/s (mech death Expl_Mech_01, starts 2.2 s ) or 0.2 at 3/s (BA mortar); no texture** [code-confirmed] Lens filters exist in explosion and hit .mtb files of every MP and campaign archive (14 in boggeddown.mgf: Expl_BD_LG_01, Expl_BattleArmor, Expl_Mech_01, Expl_Tur_01/02, Expl_VE_*, BA_Mortar_Hit*, AlphaStrike_Hit*, LavaGun_Hit). Expl_Mech_01: Color FFFFFFFF, StartAlpha 0.2, DeltaAlpha 0.6, EndAlpha 0, Texture empty, StartTime 2200 ms, TimingFlags 1. BA_Mortar_Hit: StartAlpha 0.2, DeltaAlpha 3. Runtime traces also show flashes starting at 0.5 with delta 2.0 (colour 1,1,0.88). A normal flash is gone in 0.25-0.33 s. *How:* Class key .mtb WDF = crc32('MAModSubObjectLensFilter') ^ 0xFFFFFFFF = 8A67F057. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Screen haze bug: a frozen explosion lens flash; fixed by hiding a lens quad its update no longer shows (R26 tint 9896cc8)** `0013FC88`, `0013FD69`, `000AFCB0`, `0013F832` [verified-in-game] The periodic grey-white haze is a uniform blend of the whole 3D scene toward near-white with alpha about 0.2, HUD clean, hard on and off, constant for 3.5 s. Fitted against the scene it matches the normal fading explosion flashes in the same capture (alpha about 0.19, same colour) except that it does not fade. Cause: the lens quad keeps visible = 1 and its alpha when its update stops running while the explosion effect still exists. Fix (v26-tint 9896cc8): sub_0013FC88/sub_0013FD69 mark a filter when they show it (ma2_lens_shown), sub_000AFCB0 hides a lens quad not shown in this frame or the one before (ma2_lens_draw_check, frame counter 0x4E2420), and sub_0013F832 forgets released filters (ma2_lens_forget). Screen fades (death/respawn black, blue loading tint) use the same filter class but are not tracked, so they are unchanged. *How:* A/B: RECOMP_LENS_FREEZE_FIX=0 restores the old behaviour. RECOMP_TEST_LENS_FREEZE=<s> skips one lens update for <s> s right after its flash shows (forced reproduction). — recomp_manual.c:1440
- **Which gate stops the lens update in natural play is not pinned down yet** `00107DA3`, `00107F63`, `00030440`, `0016B25E` [inferred, open-question] Candidates read from code: (1) slot 25 sub_00107DA3 (owner flags, damage-percent window , in multi-view mode, the range test sub_00107F63 that compares view-to-owner distance with max(600, camera vt+0x38); the stale-x87 reading of vt+0x38 was REFUTED 2026-11-10, see lens-range-test-far-distance-ok); (2) the per-view mapping sub_0016B25E returning 0, which leaves the filter untouched; (3) the timing window. Five instrumented runs (Team Destruction Bogged Down, Grinder In Your Face and New River City, 3840x1600, DrawDistance 100) showed only normal fades. The fix covers all three paths. *How:* RECOMP_LENS_TRACE=1, then look for '[LENS] STALE' (gate fields) or '[LENS] hide frozen' lines. — generated recomp_0026.c (made at install time, not in the repository):1
- **RECOMP_LENS_TRACE, RECOMP_TEST_LENS_FREEZE, RECOMP_LENS_FREEZE_FIX and RECOMP_COVER_TRACE** [code-confirmed] RECOMP_LENS_TRACE=1 logs '[LENS] upd' per lens update (alpha, delta, the 0x50C85C single-view flag, the views list from [0x524A5C]+0x1C and the {view>filter(visible alpha)} pairs), '[LENS] draw' per drawn flash or fade, '[LENS] STALE' when a drawn lens quad's sub-object has not updated for 0.15 s, and '[LENS] hide frozen' when the fix hides one. RECOMP_TEST_LENS_FREEZE=<s> freezes the first bright lens flash for <s> s (test only). RECOMP_LENS_FREEZE_FIX=0 turns the fix off. RECOMP_COVER_TRACE=1 (nv2a_pb_exec.c cover_trace) logs blended programmable draws whose transformed vertices cover the 640x480 target or straddle w = 0, at most 40 lines a flip. — recomp_manual.c:1395
- **Frame tail on MP maps: 3D scene, glow (8001/8001), lens flashes and fades (untextured, 302/303, fog on), then the HUD** [verified-in-game] Frame traces (RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE) on Bogged Down and New River City end the 3D pass with the glow chain (a 160x120 to 320x240 draw at 0x00002000, then a full-screen 320x240 quad with blend CONSTANT_COLOR 8001/8001, bc 00FFFFFF), then the view overlay list (lens flashes and screen fades as untextured pre-transformed quads, combiner prog 00000, final combiner fog lerp), then the HUD sprites. Earlier in the scene a 640x480 full-screen pass with blend DST_COLOR/DST_ALPHA (306/304, texture 80488000) runs every frame; its diffuse is (0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.506) in play and bluish (0.443, 0.455, 0.584, 0.2) in the menus. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Lens range test sub_00107F63 reads a real far distance (fld [builder+0x80]); the clue is refuted** `00107F63`, `0006D5A0`, `00139771` [code-confirmed] sub_00107F63 walks the view list (sub_00018F30+0x1C.+0x20) and calls vt+0x38 on MEM32(view+0x154), the camera builder (vtable 0x45DDD0, runtime-observed in RECOMP_CAM_SET). Slot 14 of 0x45DDD0 is sub_0006D5A0 = d9 81 80 00 00 00 c3 (fld dword [ecx+0x80]; ret), a real float return; only one other vtable (0x461008 region) holds it. sub_00030440 (mov al,1; ret) is a generic return-true used by 694 vtable slots and is not the slot reached here. The recomp keeps x87 in global g_fp_stack/g_fp_top in both the normal and __fast variants, so the callee's push reaches the caller's fst at 0x108003 regardless of the 'returns int_or_void' tag; caller bytes ff5238 d95508 d9450c . dff1 ddd8 7705 match the C. Range = max(arg, builder+0x80), in range if range^2 > dist^2 to owner+0xF0; the function returns 1 if ANY view is in range. It is only reached when sub_00018F10+0x69 == 0 or sub_0016282C fails (caller 0x139771), i.e. not on the normal single-view path. *How:* Do not chase stale x87 here; look at the other lens update gates (sub_002B0BB0 window, owner flags in sub_00107DA3, sub_0016B25E mapping). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

## Objective arrival parity (Snatch It Ill Wind bank, 11-10)

### Facts

- **Snatch It Ill Wind: team 2 was slow to the cores because its planner never went down the bank into the basin** [verified-in-game] Both bases are 510-535 m in a straight line from the core pile (718,1290 y 22), but team 2's base rim (1160,1450 y 15) stands over the y -20 basin behind a 35 m, 45-76 deg bank 40-48 m wide. Drop links reach 20 m and HopDown's 40 m leap ran only in the HopOut pass (a dry search), so team 2's first pass walked the north rim (708 m, stalls in the 924,1612 basin) or the south loop (850 m+). On the published 1.0.2 exe (86648cbb) team 2's first ground arrival was 20-72 s after team 1's (4 runs, ratio 1.47-3.16). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **BankDive: jet bodies get HopDown's bank leaps in the planner's first pass** [verified-in-game] ma2_bot_path.c: with BankDive on, a 'Mech with jets or a BattleArmor (drop limit 30 m+, g_up > 0) gets the dive legs (a jet leg down a blocked slope band of up to 40 m whose tops never rise above the start, onto bare free lower ground, cost run + 16 + 0.15 x fall) in the first pass, from natural ground only. PATHTEST Ill Wind team 2 base 1200,1470 -> pile: 708 -> 621 m; team 1: 538 -> 519 m. A 'Mech without jets cannot walk off that bank in the game (tried as a plain step-off: 'did not come down' at 6 rim spots), so it keeps the walk round. *How:* Default on; RECOMP_BOT_BANK_DIVE=0 or [Bots] BankDive=0 turns it off. [C7] bankdive: links. — ma2_bot_path.c:796
- **ChokeLeap: a bot leaping off a choke's mouth does not queue in the choke** [verified-in-game] choke_flow (ma2_bot_brain.c) made bots file in behind (FollowHold) or wait at a narrow choke even when their route leaves by a jet leg or step-off at its mouth: Ill Wind team 2's base exit choke (1135,1479 -> 1165,1487) is the top of the BankDive leap, and bots held 8-13 s behind a team-mate 2 m ahead. ma2_bot_leap_near (ma2_bot_ctrl.c) reports a drop/jet leg within the next 4 legs whose top is within 60 m; such a body skips the choke queue (tanks excluded). *How:* Default on; RECOMP_BOT_CHOKE_LEAP / [Bots] ChokeLeap. [C7] chokes: leaps (seconds). — ma2_bot_brain.c:2003
- **ClimbAhead: jet 'Mechs jet straight up steep climbs and replans no longer reset the climb clock** [verified-in-game] MechClimbJet/ClimbProgress restarted its no-progress clock whenever the next route corner moved 2 m, and replans under the Ill Wind basin exit ramp (0.41-0.52 slope) moved it every second: a team-2 'Mech milled 26 s before its first climb jet. Now only a corner 12 m+ away is a new climb, and a jet 'Mech jets at once when the ground 30 m (or less) toward the next corner is 6 m+ higher and steeper than 0.35. *How:* Default on; RECOMP_BOT_CLIMB_AHEAD / [Bots] ClimbAhead. [C7] mechclimbjet: ahead. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:4240
- **LeapTop: the steering carrot stops at a leap's top and a body at any upcoming top takes that leap** [verified-in-game] The drop and jet-up executors fire only within 8-12 m of the top of the leg being steered for, but path_carrot ran on along the leap leg (pulling the body across the corner to an edge that was not the top) and ma2_path_follow could skip the top corner. Now the carrot stops at a corner followed by a drop/jet leg, the follower never skips such a corner, and a body within 6 m of a leap top up to 3 corners ahead skips to that leap. Ill Wind team 2 bots had stood 3-12 s at the rim with path 0/9. *How:* Default on; RECOMP_BOT_LEAP_TOP / [Bots] LeapTop. [C7] leaptop: stop_s, skips. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:1200
- **JetTryFuel: a jet-up try is judged 6 s from its first burn, not from reaching the foot** [verified-in-game] the jet-up executor judged a try 6 s after the body reached the leg's foot, burned or not; after a climb burn the fuel is low and the next burn waits, so the try 'failed' and ma2_path_forbid_drop barred the spot for every bot for 10 min. Ill Wind's terrace jet-up (~690,1380, the only way from the basin to the core pile) was barred at 44-52 s in 4 of 7 runs. Now the 6 s count from the try's first burn (20 s if no burn could fire); BotCtrl.up_fire holds the burn time. *How:* Default on; RECOMP_BOT_JET_TRY_FUEL / [Bots] JetTryFuel. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:1200

<a id="t32_floor_model_1110"></a>

## Objective arrival floor model and measured movement speeds

### Facts

- **floor_model.py computes the optimal-human arrival time per map, mode, team and body class from the NavCache grid** [verified-in-game] The tool reads a bot-match .botrec (game type, pilot spawns, vehicles at kickoff, objectives) and the .navc grid the navigator builds at match start (sf, blk, hblk, slp; 2 m cells). It picks the .navc by height fit and runs a time-optimal Dijkstra from the objective cells for each body class (pilot, 'Mech with and without jets, tank, BattleArmor, VTOL). Walk edges go onto free cells or down steep cells. Jet edges are 6-40 m long, rise at most the measured climb per burn, and are used only where walking cannot do it. Boarding is a straight pilot walk at 12 m/s plus 2 s. Fuel is not tracked, so the result is optimistic. On Ill Wind Snatch It the floor gap is about 2-3 s for a 'Mech (T1 26.6 s, T2 29.3 s median), not the 8-10 s estimated before. *How:* python tools/floor_model.py TOOLS_DIR %LOCALAPPDATA%/MechAssault2/NavCache OUT.csv REC. speeds can be overridden with FLOOR_<PARAM> env vars. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **A 'Mech is not faster in the air than walking: airborne horizontal speed p50 18.3, p90 22 m/s** `0018ABB5` [verified-in-game] Measured over 317 'Mech hops (height above the nav surface more than 2.5 m) in Ill Wind recordings: airborne horizontal speed p50 18.3 m/s and p90 22 m/s; flat hops with a rise under 6 m ran at 16-20 m/s. On the ground the same 'Mechs move at p50 18.7 m/s and p90 27.5 m/s, with a per-body p95 of 25-33 m/s. The 30-45 m/s seen earlier was the slide down a bank. Jet-hop cruising across open ground saves a 'Mech no time. BattleArmor does gain: it hops at 24.5 m/s horizontally against a 13.6 m/s walk. The best 'Mech climb per burn is 24-25 m (mode of 17.8k [BOT-JETGAIN] samples); BattleArmor climbs 18 m. A pilot on foot runs at p90 12.1 m/s. *How:* Use these as the model speeds; do not add 'Mech jet-hop travel as a speed lever. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Ill Wind Snatch It: blue 'Mechs lose 6-11 s at the BankDive leap top and 5-12 s on the basin exit climb** [verified-in-game] Compared with the floor field (loss per 4 s window = elapsed time minus the drop in floor time to go), team 2's first-life 'Mechs lose time in two places. The first is 6-11 s in the 8-12 s after boarding, standing or turning at the top of the bank leap. The second is 5-12 s on the jet climb out of the basin to the core pile. The basin floor runs at floor speed. Team 1's best 'Mech per run loses only 0.9-1.2 s in total. Team 1's other 'Mechs lose 5-23 s at their own base exit, around 340-380,940-980. *How:* Fix generally (leap-top hesitation and climb-exit dwell). Re-measure with loss.py on new recordings. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

<a id="t33_arrival_parity_pass5_1111"></a>

## Arrival parity pass 5: leap stalls, step-off clearance, deep jet landings, floor tool fixes

### Facts

- **LeapStall: a jet body stalled 6-18 m short of a leap-down top jets from where it stands** [verified-in-game] The campaign MechAI goto sometimes will not walk the last 10-15 m of a gentle slope (grade ~0.33) down to the planner's leap-top cell: it turns on the spot with no forward speed. ## Arrival parity pass 6: the grid misses buildings over 40 m (TallSolid); MechAI goto stutter

### Facts

- **Collider faces are one-sided: a ray starting inside a building sees none of it** [verified-in-game] The game's collision ray query (sub_A10A0 + sub_8DF50) only hits faces seen from outside, and the terrain is not in that space. The bot grid probe cast down from ground+40 m, so any building taller than 40 m was open ground. Rush Hour has 4562 such cells (2 m grid); its 42-50 m block at 1118-1138,1322-1344 read as a 20 m corridor between two 7-9 m walls, and team 2 'Mechs stood 25-30 s at its face (Z_85a/b). FPROBE on D_85b1: a down ray from +100 m hits the roof at +42/+50, an up ray from +0.5 m hits nothing. TallSolid (commit adbf1ec): the first ray starts at terrain top + 160 m; if it meets something above ground+40, the 44 m ray gives the surface below and an up ray from that surface separates an overhead deck (underside hit: the low surface stays) from a solid (no hit: the roof is the surface). Movers, projectiles and water above keep the old ray. *How:* [C7] tallsolid cells/open; RECOMP_BOT_DIAG prints [BOT-NAV] tallsolid. RECOMP_BOT_TALL_SOLID=0 / [Bots] TallSolid=0 = old. RECOMP_BOT_FPROBE now also logs top (down from +100 m) and up rays per point; RECOMP_BOT_STALLPROBE=1 logs rays from stalled bot 'Mechs. — ma2_bots_core.c:1
- **The campaign MechAI goto can stutter (0.3 s step, 0.8 s stop) while facing its carrot** [verified-in-game] Q_81a1 b6 (Ill Wind Snatch It, team 2) right after boarding, 10.1-14.6 s at 1199-1188,1419-1421: drive A348 (body_steer to MechAI mode 6), yaw equal to the carrot bearing, yet it moves in 0.3 s bursts and stands 0.8-1 s between them (about 1 m/s in all). Each burst moves more than 0.7 m, which resets GotoWalk's 1 s still-timer, so walk-direct (W3515) only took over at 14.6 s; then 12-24 m/s. Nobody within 15 m (no crowding). This is ~3-4 s of team 2's post-boarding loss. Not fixed: a fix would judge progress over a 2 s window instead of a 1 s still-timer. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:3520

## Arrival parity pass 7: GotoWindow (goto stutter), Ill Wind Check It T1 variance, NavCache key ignores switches

- **GotoWalk also fires on poor headway over 2 s (GotoWindow), not only after 1 s stood still** [verified-in-game] The campaign MechAI goto can stutter: 0.3-1 s bursts of more than 0.7 m, then 0.5-1 s turning to the next carrot. Each burst restarted GotoWalk's 1 s still-timer. GotoWindow (commit deb9b44) keeps ground positions every 0.25 s in a 12-slot ring (BotCtrl gw_hp/gw_ht). A 'Mech or BattleArmor whose navigator gives no forward speed, has stood 0.3 s or more, has its carrot 8 m or more away, and has moved less than 0.5 x kind_cruise metres since the sample 2-3 s old (8 m for a 'Mech, 6 m for BattleArmor) walks direct. When the carrot is off the nose it uses the slow turning step. A fire or a failed walk clears the ring. Live H_81a1 (v13-v27p15): 18 fires in 180 s, and 49 of 50 GotoWalk walks moved. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_GOTO_WINDOW=0 / [Bots] GotoWindow=0 = old behaviour. [C7] gotowin: n. RECOMP_BOT_DIAG lines read [BOT-GOTOWALK] . kind=2 (2 s window) still . — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:3476
- **The NavCache key does not include grid switches such as TallSolid** [code-confirmed] The key is made of NAV_CACHE_VERSION, the trav params, the build stamp (__DATE__ __TIME__), the map archive and size, the mode, the extents, the terrain and prop fingerprints, and RECOMP_BOT_UNDERWATER. A run with RECOMP_BOT_TALL_SOLID=0 on an exe that already cached a map therefore READS THE TALLSOLID GRID from the cache. If that run misses the cache, it writes the old grid under the same key, and later default runs of that exe then use the old grid. To A/B any grid switch, add RECOMP_BOT_NAV_CACHE=0. The log then shows [BOT-NAV-CACHE] ready via=off. *How:* Always pair a grid-switch A/B with RECOMP_BOT_NAV_CACHE=0. — ma2_bots_core.c:1800

The floor on the TallSolid grid is unchanged: a tank reaches terminal 378,1371 in 26.8 s against 27.3 s before. The losses differ in kind from run to run. In RC_71b a T1 tank claimer stood 2.6 s at 267,1261, got no_path and was banned from 378,1371 for 25 s (ObjGiveUp), so the first T1 arrivals came at far terminals near 1050,1000. <a id="t35_lightning_units_1110"></a>

## Lightning flash: whole-scene flicker root cause and N.L-lit-only fix (R27 tint3)

### Facts

- **Root cause of the storm 'multiple shades' flicker: the PC lightning boost (B2) matched the sun colour by value in every draw** [verified-in-game] The B2 unit-lightning boost (10-26) added +0.9 to every vertex constant equal to the env sun colour (env+0x88) in every programmable draw while env+0x16C was on. The terrain shader (7-stage n738 program) passes that constant straight into V1 for its light map, billboards, bushes and stale constant slots (absolute c159 always holds it) matched too, so the whole 3D view pulsed 1.2-2.3x 3-6 times per strike. A/B with RECOMP_LIGHTNING_UNITS=0 removed every such step. It is PC-only and not an overlay, so the lens-flash fix 9896cc8 cannot cover it. *How:* Fixed in v27-tint2 0e4fd01; RECOMP_LIGHTNING_UNITS=2 reproduces the old behaviour. — nv2a_pb_exec.c:1
- **Fix: the lightning flash now lights only N.L-lit model draws (units), not terrain/sky/billboards** [verified-in-game] The boost now applies only to a sun-colour constant the current vertex program reads directly (no a0-relative read) and uses as a MAD operand, in a program that also has a DP3 against a constant (the N.L model lighting). 'Mechs, VTOLs, tanks and the skinned pilot (sun read at absolute c159) still flash; terrain (sun into V1 via ILU mov), bushes (no DP3), billboards and stale slots do not. Bogged Down 4 min same driver: uniform whole-screen probe steps during lightning 20 -> 0 (3 total, all fades), flash brightness median/p90 1.12/1.77 -> 1.07/1.42 (boost off: 1.03/1.34). Residual: static N.L-lit props (big swamp trees, landing pads) still brighten a little, because the sun constant is global (no per-object light set) and the shader cannot tell a prop from a unit. *How:* RECOMP_LIGHTNING_UNITS: 0 off, 2 old match-by-value, default N.L-lit only. Exe v13-tint3-fix1 sha256 0ada4c2db73245c847393f202bf70122975ba41ffa2a22fc3d9e526a06b616fd. Proof: int3 (traces, pair_b_45.png). — nv2a_pb_exec.c:1
- **The sun is applied from a GLOBAL light list per draw; the flash light (env+0x358) is never applied on PC** `000511C0`, `00052C20`, `0006D660` [code-confirmed] sub_000511C0 (per-draw shader constant setup) walks the global light vector [0x524ACC] via sub_00052C20, calling each light's vtable +0x30 = sub_0006D660 (directional light apply: c[base] = direction light+0x60, c[base+1] = colour light+0x14, base = [0x524ABC]+0x68 + 0x60). A probe saw only the sun light (and the menu light) in that list, flash on or off: the flash light at env+0x358 is never applied, so units cannot flash natively and the per-draw sun constant is the same for units and static props. Other sun-colour writers: 0x512A6 (8-dword block), 0x6FF62 (terrain), 0x5ADC2 / 0x55F13 / 0x608EA / 0x4F8FF. *How:* clue for a per-object fix: find who should add env+0x358 to the light list (or a per-object list) for dynamic objects only. — nv2a_pb_exec.c:1
- **RECOMP_LT_PAINT_FILE: paint the draws of chosen vertex programs to see what they are** [verified-in-game] Diagnostic (default off) in nv2a_pb_exec.c: the file lists vertex-program hashes (FNV of the program words, as printed in overlay-trace B/V lines); the sun-colour register of each listed program gets a colour (red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta, white in list order) so a screenshot shows what it draws. An entry '1' dumps every draw of one flip (B and K lines with the low constants). Found: EEB06244 = 'Mech, 2F421162/67E1ED8D = VTOL, 56E0CFFE = pilot (skinned), 428FCB07 = big trees, 9FE61736 = bushes, 82CD29E1 = terrain (Bogged Down). *How:* Needs RECOMP_OVERLAY_TRACE=1 and RECOMP_OVERLAY_TRACE_FILE; the file is re-read every 30 flips. — nv2a_pb_exec.c:1

### Facts

- **A jet leg already flown stays the route's next leg when the flight lands a few metres off its planned landing** [verified-in-game] After a jet flight the route's path.next can still be the jet leg just flown (drop 2) when the body came down 6-15 m short of / beside its planned landing at the same level: (needs the body within 8 m of the leg's foot) cannot fire, LeapStall(Up) scans from that leg and sees no rise, so nothing jets on and the goto walks the body to the old landing point first. Ill Wind Snatch It T2 at the basin exit ledge: P13_81b2 b6 landed 729,0.7,1401 at 40.97 (path 1/6 = basin jet leg to 722,1388) and jetted up the band only at 43.20; P13_81b2 b9 32.3 -> 33.74; P14_81a1 b5 33.7 -> 36.17 (landed_proof.py: 1.0-2.0 s each). *How:* LandedLeg (RECOMP_BOT_LANDED_LEG / [Bots] LandedLeg, default on): on the ground, next leg a jet leg whose landing is < 16 m off, within -2.+3 m of the body's height and 8 m+ from its foot -> path.next++. LeapNotWalk's jet-up reach follows LeapStallUpFar (24 m to the foot, 52 m to the landing). [C7] landedleg n; [BOT-LANDEDLEG] with RECOMP_BOT_DIAG. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:3413
