## Code research, first pass: bots and custom-map details

### Facts

- **On several missions the single-player start key StartVehiclesGeneric holds a different container from the other 17 StartVehicles* slots** [verified-in-game] Single player reads StartVehiclesGeneric (1F13DE84). On most missions all 18 StartVehicles* slots hold the same container. On Mission_11a the generic slot is 123726 (Avatar Ingame Container, an on-foot pilot) while the other 17 slots are 124035 (Mad Dog). The pattern repeats in the data for other missions: M13b generic 123726 vs 17x Rommel 124052; M04 generic 124038 (Owens) vs 17x on-foot; M17a and M17b generic 124001 (Battle Armor) vs 17x NovaCat; M01b generic 125894 vs 17x 124486; M02 generic 125894 vs 17x 124001. The game starts the player on foot on M11a, as the grey pilot. Only the M11a start was seen in game; the other missions are from the data. *How:* Open: a copy of M13b or M04 played in game to confirm the on-foot start. An editor that shows the 17-slot container as the player start will report the wrong vehicle.
- **On Mission_11a the intro cinema hands over from Foster Actor to the Uziels set at intro end** [documented] Mission_11a has two native swap sets, Swap Set Uziels (128588) and Swap Set Foster Actor (128587), both with bSwappedIn=1 at start. The trigger group TG - Intro End (under InGame Cinema 0 > Triggers) runs MAActionSwapSetOut on Foster Actor and MAActionSwapSetIn on Uziels, so the cinema stand-in is swapped out when the intro ends. *How:* Open: whether bSwappedIn=0 on a member set hides its members at load.
- **Env_SnowDust_01 snow emitter sits in node 'efx', which maps local +Y to world -X, and uses the VD_Tank_Smoke texture** [documented] Env_SnowDust_01 is attached to node 'efx' of the precip model. That node's rotation maps local +Y to world -X and local Z to world Z; the mtb Offset (0,-20,10) matches the editor position (20,0,10) under this frame. Velocity is 18 m/s up the node's Y axis, with a 7 degree cone and an 8 x 9.9 x 50 box in node frame. The texture is VD_Tank_Smoke 64x64 (RGB mean 120, alpha mean 52/255); ENV_snow 256x256 is nearly empty (alpha mean 0.6), so the flakes change little. The M10 slope lift is about nine overlapping smoke quads. *How:* Open: whether the game also yaws the precipitation frame with the camera (untested; the M10 pose forward is near +Z).
- **Translucent vegetation vertex light = Kd x (ambient + sun + sum of point-light colour x attenuation), with N.L = 1 on every term** [verified-in-game] For translucent-shading models (trees, bushes, Env_Deadbush, grass) the game's vertex light V0 is Kd x (ambient + sun + the sum of point-light colour x attenuation), with N.L = 1 for every term. M13a brush (Kd 2/3): d0 = 0.667(A+S) + p x lamp (0.36, 0.35, 0.28), with p between 0 and 0.72; unlit floor draws give A. M03 conifer (Kd 146): d0 = Kd(A+S) + lamp hue (1, 0.92, 0.53). This supersedes the earlier V0 = Kd x (A+S) reading and the rejected 0.86A + 1.29S fit. *How:* Open: whether the point-light term applies to other translucent classes (grass, Env_Deadbush on other maps).
- **Game terrain program 08421 on M13a combines colour map, detail mix, vertex specular and light map as out = 4 x colormap x mix x (V1.rgb x V1.a x T3.a + T3.rgb)** [code-confirmed] Decoded from the combiner words of the M13a ground trace: s0 r1 = t1; s1 r0 = t0.a x t1 + (1 - t0.a) x t2 (mix); s2 r1 = 2 x r0 x c0.a (0.5), so mix; s3 r1 = 2 x mix x t0; s4 r0 = V1.rgb x T3.a; s5 r0 = r0 x V1.a + T3.rgb; s6 r0 = 2 x r0 x r1. Result: out = 4 x colormap x mix x (V1.rgb x V1.a x T3.a + T3.rgb). V1 is the vertex specular (d1) and T3 is the per-frame light map (file ambient x static lightmap + pools). The micro pass samples detail texture 80A28000 at x15.6 and x112 tiling.
- **On M13a the editor's lit terrain term at the near ground (pixel 52,280) is 1.55x the game's, and the micro pass accounts for only 0.97 vs 0.85** [verified-in-game] Same-pose stage dumps (editor on master 0c0ee4c, game trace m13a_ground_g3): lit terrain before micro, editor 20.9, 22.5, 19.5 vs game 13, 15, 13 (1.55x); after micro (final), editor 20.2, 22.0, 18.6 (x0.97) vs game 11, 12, 11 (x0.85). So most of the near-ground error sits in the lit terrain term, not in the micro pass. Light map lm.r 0.816 and lm.a 1.0 on the editor side; the game T3 texel was not dumped. *How:* Open: the game T3 (815EB000) texel at the pixel, to split the 1.55x between the light map and the vertex-specular term. Whole-image pair ratio (ground 1.4x near, 1.1x horizon) is in the same summary.
- **MASpawner ParentID and SpawnID are 0 in every retail spawner; InitialID and InitialSecondID are odd/even 0xF80000xx pairs; the spawn tick does not test for a direct child** `00133C70`, `0013321F` [code-confirmed] In the retail dumps (Mission_05, 7 spawners; Mission_04, 19; catalog over 1202 spawners) ParentID and SpawnID are always 0. The link to the stand object is the entity-tree parent (Mission_05 spawner 141817 sits under the NULL MACorporeal 32093), not these fields. At runtime the spawn handshake at 0x133C70 stores a value from [edi+0x2C] into the ParentID slot (runtime +0xA4), so ParentID becomes a spawned-unit slot (medium); what SpawnID (+0xA8) does is unknown. InitialID and InitialSecondID are a per-spawner pair in the 0xF80000xx range (InitialID odd: 0xF8000001, 03, 05; InitialSecondID the even partner), at runtime +0xAC and +0xB0. The spawn tick at 0x13321F gates only on the Enabled bit (runtime +0x78 bit 0x01), the handshake bit 0x10 and the caps/timer; no direct-child test was found. Enabled is 0 on 205 of 1202 retail spawners. Catalog offset + 0x20 = runtime offset. *How:* Open: what [edi+0x2C] is at 0x133C70; what SpawnID and the InitialID gate do; whether a spawner whose child is deleted still spawns (needs an in-game trace). Direct-child norm: 1201 child instances for 1202 spawners (class counts, not per spawner).
- **The game shows ONE current objective (banner, HUD, radar, pause panel); the next appears only when the current one completes** `004EB23C`, `0021D6F7`, `001FC461`, `00169A49` [verified-in-game] Objective records live in a 30-record table (0x50E860, stride 0x64) read through one current index (global 0x4EB23C). The Objectives Display (sub_0021D6F7, vtable 0x48A4F0 slot 14) lists record i only when i == the current index; HUD_Text (sub_001FC461) shows the current record's text when it is enabled, not done and non-empty; the start banner (sub at 0x1F7D9D) and radar target markers (sub at 0x21DA39) also read the current record. Completion (sub_00169A49) marks every record whose mission variables are all set as done, but the index advances (sub_001699ED: next record not yet done) ONLY when the completed record is the current one; a later objective finished early is ticked silently and skipped. Retail missions are linear chains of 5-16 enabled slots (M02, M03: 'Intro Over' -> 'Steal Tank' -> 'Kill Stuff' -> .), never parallel lists. Proven in game on an editor-built mission (g3, d12_objective_order.ma2map): the start banner listed only 'FIRST: wait 8 seconds'; after its 8 s timer the pause panel listed only 'SECOND: survive 5 minutes'. A disabled (ObjectiveEnabledBool 0) current record shows nothing and stalls the advance (inferred from the walk, not observed). Editor: the Objectives section shows a hint saying the game shows one objective at a time. *How:* Editor tab: Objectives & Triggers > Add objective. Author objectives as an ordered chain; all user lines need EnabledBool 1 and a text. Do not expect objectives 2-3 in the pause list until 1 is done. Unknown: the start-banner and pause-panel builders themselves, the sub_00165164==0x10 / obj+0x69 branch of sub_0021D6F7.
- **Water wading is the type-map bit (8) plus MAEnvironment per-type values; no drown/swim code found; retail shallow water is ~0.3-1.6 m deep, editor default dig capped at 1.4 m** [verified-in-game] The game decides wading from the terrain type-map bit (8 shallow, 16 deep, 32 waterway) and MAEnvironment per-type values (Speed, Damage, Cooling, Mech may enter, Pilot in for shallow/deep/waterway); no code was found that drowns, slows or pushes out a pilot by water depth, and no swim state exists: the pilot follows the terrain bed. Retail data (all worlds with MAWater): type-8 cells lie median 0.3-1.2 m, p90 <=1.6 m below the plane (Bogged Down 0.9/1.2, flat MP lakes No Man's Land 2.9 m, Troubled Waters 4.4 m); type-16 cells 2-8 m (campaign only). The old editor default lake (min(pond_depth, 0.3 x short side)) was ~8 m with every cell below the surface marked 8, and an on-foot pilot sank fully. Editor fix: dug basin default capped at 1.4 m (kWadeDepth, water_ux.cpp dig_water_basin) with a 'Deep (only 'Mechs can wade)' tick for up to 8 m; Place water marks playable cells under the footprint as water ground (type map 8; moving/deleting water now clears old marks, 27ff6ab). GAME PROOF (g3, PC Release, UI-made wade_shallow.ma2map, default dig): the pilot wades thigh-deep, head and torso above the surface, no sinking. Deep (type 16): game-observed g3: a lake ~4 m deep with cells marked 16 lets the on-foot pilot walk in fully submerged and out the far side, no block, no damage in ~10 s (default MAEnvironment); a 1.2 m lake marked 8 is knee-deep. Editor now marks under-water cells deeper than 1.6 m as 16 ('Deep water' overlay) and warns that a pilot ends up below the surface. Shallow water reads faint from afar (thickness alpha ~ vertical depth/4, MEDIUM). *How:* Editor: Terrain > Water > Place water / Dig a basin. Keep wadable lakes 1-2 m deep; use the Deep tick only for mechs.
- **Player death restarts the mission by itself; retail missions have no lose-on-player-death trigger, and an empty Destroyed(IncludePlayers) trigger fires at load** `001FB241`, `000C8BDC` [verified-in-game] Runtime-observed: when the player dies the game restarts the level itself; a lost custom mission (Lose action, e.g. the Countdown template reaching 00:00) also silently restarts with no 'Mission failed' screen in Custom Scenarios. Retail missions have no trigger watching the player for this. Where retail does use MATriggerDestroyed with IncludePlayers 1 ('TD - PlayerDead' 261413, 'TD - Player Died' 155977/'TD - Player Is Dead' 156618) it carries a DestroySet (MoeEntitySet) + CombineMethod 1 + TypeOfCheck 2; the set is what makes it wait. An editor trigger with IncludePlayers 1 and NO set/units passes at once: Lose fires at load and the mission reloads forever; the 'Lose if the player is destroyed' template was removed and Check scenario flags the pattern as Must fix. Members of sets 261412/130400 are not in the dictionary (LOW). Engine death path (failed.ggf, sub_001FB241, health test sub_000C8BDC) has no caller found: general case LOW. *How:* Editor: Objectives & Triggers > Templates; Check scenario. No lose-on-death trigger is needed. Use the Countdown template for lose conditions.
- **A 0 s timer that starts a cinema did not play the intro in an editor-built mission; 1 s and 3 s do (retail Mission_05 uses 0 s)** `00148BB7`, `00156AD8`, `00155A99`, `004EB19C` [code-confirmed] An earlier 3 s timer cinema also played (G6). The editor wiring is field-identical to retail Mission_05 'TT - StartUp' (a 0 s timer), so the wiring is not the cause. Code (HIGH): the timer's first update only ARMS it (sets +0xBC armed and +0xB4 start time from the game clock at 0x4E2440); it fires on the next update when elapsed >= +0xB8, so a 0 s timer fires one tick after arming, not on the arming frame. MAActionActivateCinema returns silently if its cinema uid resolves to null; the cinema start sub_00155A99 is a no-op if a cinema is already active (byte 0x4EB19C set) and starts no controller when the Camera Controllers child list is empty. Best explanation (MEDIUM, not reproduced): the 0 s fire lands in the first ticks while load state is still settling or another cinema is active, Start returns silently and the fire is consumed; 1 s and 3 s let those frames pass. No 'mission started' gate on trigger updates was found. How retail Mission_05 avoids it is unknown (LOW). Editor: 'Play at mission start' and the 'Play the intro cutscene when the mission starts' template now write a 1 s timer. *How:* Editor: Objectives & Triggers > Templates > Play the intro cutscene when the mission starts; Cameras & Cutscenes > Play at mission start. Keep intro cinema timers at 1 s or more and start only one cinema at mission begin. Open: trace 0x4EB19C and the trigger tick at the 0 s fire; check TrgTimerDuration units (minutes vs seconds) and the 0x4E2438 vs 0x4E2440 clocks.

SHALLOW: Speed 100x52, 90x8, 75x3, 95x3; Damage 0x55, 100x7, 10x3, 200x1; Cooling 0x39, 8x21, 16x3, 4x3; Mech 1x54, 0x12; Pilot 1x54, 100x7, 0x4, 2x1. WATERWAY: Speed 100x63, 90x3; Damage 0x65, 1x1; Cooling 0x52, 4x11, 8x3; Mech 1x55, 0x11; Pilot 1x56, 0x10. 'Pilot in' is bimodal (1.0 vs 100.0); the scale (flag vs percent) is unconfirmed. Game-observed (g3, wade_deep.ma2map, default MAEnvironment): an on-foot pilot walks fully submerged through a ~4 m lake of type-16 cells, no block and no damage in ~10 s, consistent with the default/most common DamageDeep 0 and PilotDeep 1; this does NOT support the editor tooltip claim that deep water is 'Mechs only' (mech behaviour and the retail DamageDeep 200/125 worlds untested). Open: the sampler that reads the type-map bit and indexes these fields (the AI singleton reads CoolingWaterway; sub_001234D6 reads env+0x1C0, attribution may be wrong), whether MechDeep 0 blocks a mech, whether Damage is per second. *How:* Editor: Environment > Water values / Terrain > Water 'Deep' tick.
- **Retail developers prefix trigger names with a short code (TT, TD, TR, TG, TL, TB, TMA, TA, TC, TPVT, TGT, TUB, TNR, TSB) that maps almost 1:1 to the trigger class** [documented] Parsed from all 60 world WDFs (11,518 named MATrigger*, MAAction*, MAGroup, MoeEntitySet, instances). Code -> class (consistency): TT = MATriggerTimer (861/884, 97%; 'TT - Start', 'TT - StartUp'); TD = MATriggerDestroyed (451/451, 100%; 'TD - PlayerDead'); TR = MATriggerRadius (388/388, 100%; 'TR - Inside HUB'); TG = base MATrigger (370/387, 96%; 'TG - Intro End', 'TG - 2 start': trigger group / generic); TL = MATriggerLogic (297/297; 'TL - All enemies dead'); TB = MATriggerCuboidalVolume (121/122; box inferred); TMA = MATriggerMenuActivate (73/75; 'TMA - gate switch'); TA = MATriggerAttach (35/35); TC = MATriggerCounter (32/37; 'Counter - ' for 5 others); TPVT = MATriggerPlayerVehicleType (22/23); TGT = MATriggerGameTime (16/16; 'TGT - GameOver'); TUB = MATriggerUber (7/7); TNR = MATriggerNationRadius (4/4); TSB = MATriggerSpider (2/2). All MAAction* names start with 'Action - ' which is a class label, not a code (4,532 instances, 100%). MAGroup, MoeEntitySet, MAWaypointGroup, MASwapSet names are ordinary text (no codes). Exceptions: 23 MATriggerTimer names have no code, about 12 MATrigger names are default 'Trigger (Generic)_00006', separators vary ('TT-delay', 'TD -ship', 'TT_delay', 'TR Player in Uziel'), casing varies ('Intro end'/'Intro End'). Action names quote trigger names verbatim ('Action - Enable TT - delay stiletto intro'), so renaming a trigger would break such action text. The codes are developer convention; whether runtime code reads them is unchecked. Editor display rule: strip with a whitelist regex ^(TT|TD|TR|TG|TL|TB|TMA|TA|TC|TPVT|TGT|TUB|TNR|TSB)(\s*[-_]\s*|\s+) (case-insensitive) for trigger classes and ^Action\s*-\s* for MAAction*; do NOT use a generic [A-Z]{1,4} pattern. *How:* Editor: Triggers list/tab display names (prefix stripping) and new-trigger default names; keep the stored name unchanged.
- **The mission-variable table (0x4EB9E0) is read by the objective check AND by every MATrigger fire gate and MATriggerTimer, so deleting an objective's variable setter can break triggers** `001452D4`, `00148BB7`, `00169A49`, `001A94A1` [inferred] Readers (code-confirmed by a literal grep of 0x4EB9E0 over recomp_*.c): the objective completion check sub_00169A49 (recomp_0037.c:15436-15520; a record is done when every variable id at record +0x2C has a nonzero byte); the MATrigger base fire routine sub_001452D4 (recomp_0032.c:18049, read at 0x1453C3 /:18234), which takes a variable id from MATrigger+0x90 and fires only when table[id] == byte MATrigger+0x94 (ids <= 0 or >= 30 skip the check); MATriggerTimer sub_00148BB7 (recomp_0033.c:3971, read at:4031); and the save path sub_000F175D (recomp_0024.c:21776). Writers: MAActionMissionVariableSet sub_001A94A1 (recomp_0045.c:37), sub_0016990A (recomp_0037.c:15201), load sub_000F235C (recomp_0024.c:23326). No direct reads found in MATriggerLogic, MAActionGameCondition, MATriggerDestroyed or MATriggerRadius (literal grep only; indirect reads through a call to sub_001452D4 are not excluded, and the older claim that MATriggerRadius sub_00145D77 reads the table is not supported). Retail catalog: MissionVariable range -1.29, 2751 instances (~line 48821; the sample is -1 in most, 0 in a few), so non-negative ids DO appear on retail triggers. Not checked: whether a retail trigger's MissionVariable id equals an objective's ob<N>var<j> in a given mission (no per-object MATrigger dump for Mission_05). *How:* Editor: when an objective is deleted, keep the setter action's variable (just unlink the objective) instead of writing -1, unless the variable is proven unused by every trigger in the level: a trigger gated on that variable would otherwise never fire (or always fire).
- **An on-foot pilot completes a 'Destroy these' objective (4 demolition charges kill a Loki) and wins the mission; the objective check has no killer or weapon test** `00169A49`, `0050E860` [verified-in-game] Game-observed: new flat mission, player start On foot (pilot), one enemy Loki ~50 m ahead with AI off, Objectives > Add objective > Destroy these (the Loki), 'Win the mission when every objective is done' ticked. The pilot's fire key drops demolition charges; 4 charges destroyed the Loki, the objective completed and the mission was WON (return to hub). This matches the code read: the objective check sub_00169A49 (recomp_0037.c:15436-15520) tests only mission-variable bytes and never the killer or weapon. It also proves in game the full chain Destroy objective -> objective complete -> Win (reinforcement arrival remains unproven). The on-foot kill is slow, not impossible. *How:* Editor: Objectives & Triggers > Add objective > Destroy these. The on-foot start only needs a hint about how slow the kill is, not a block.
- **MABarrel.BarrelChargeEffectID 318 = MAEffect 'PPC L3 Charge' is the charge effect shared by most mech guns; Hammer, LRM, SRM and mortars have none** [documented] Retail data: BarrelChargeEffectID 318 = MAEffect 'PPC L3 Charge' is shared by Laser, Pulse Laser, Machine Gun, Autocannon, Gauss, Flamer and the Elemental/BattleArmor lasers; PPCs use their own (26265 L1, 697 L2, 318 L3); AlphaStrike uses 125299; Hammer, LRM, SRM, Guided Missile and mortars have 0 (no charge effect). So a mech charging any of the 318 guns shows the blue PPC-style arcs (retail behaviour, not an editor error). Hammer is BarrelClass 14 like LRM: a hold-to-charge lob missile (BarrelChargeRate 75, TimeToMaxLob 2.0, no lock). Loki loadout 32717 = SRM + Autocannon x2 + Pulse Laser. *How:* Editor: weapon/loadout display; no editor control changes this. When a render or effect audit sees PPC-style arcs on a laser/autocannon mech, it is the shared 318 effect.
- **Bowman Hammer makes no sound request while charging and one fire-cue request per release; silent charge is retail behaviour** `000D34C5`, `000D06BC`, `0008252B` [verified-in-game] Game-confirmed: holding the Bowman Hammer produces NO sound request during the charge and exactly one fire-cue request per release (chain 000D34C5 / 000D06BC / 0008252B). *How:* Audio/weapon audits: do not report 'no charge sound' for the Hammer as a bug.
- **Bot vehicle preference in the code: every 'Mech = 1.0, VTOL 0.55 + 0.05 x skill, BattleArmor 0.30 + 0.05 x skill; the game's m_nBattleScore is unused** [code-confirmed] Corrects bots-vehicle-value (which says tank 0.75, BA 0.70 + 0.08 x skill, VTOL 0.45 + 0.08 x skill). Current code: vehicle_pref(MECH) = 1.0 for every 'Mech, VTOL = 0.55 + 0.05 x skill, BattleArmor = 0.30 + 0.05 x skill (ma2_bot_brain.c:1096-1106, 1187, pick_swap 1240); the skill bonus makes Elites prefer VTOL/BA. The game's own strength rating m_nBattleScore (Templates.mgf, getter vtable +0x90, loader 0x464BEC) is not used: light 'Mechs 6 (Puma, Uller, Raven, Cougar, Kit Fox, Owens, Hackman, Corvus), 7 (Belial, Mad Dog, Stiletto, Raptor), 9 (Loki, MadCat, Bowman, Thor, Catapult, Hellbringer, Summoner, Timber Wolf, NovaCat), 10 (Atlas, Ragnarok, Star Adder, Prometheus, Blood Asp); Rommel/APC 4; VTOL - Player 4; BattleArmor/Elemental 3; PlayerTurret Gauss / Guided Missile 2; pilots 1. So a bot takes the nearest free 'Mech, not the strongest. *How:* Bots audit t3B-01 (proposed pref = 0.7 + 0.03 x score). Use m_nBattleScore as the game's own vehicle strength.
- **Bots no longer eject at low HP; a vehicle destroyed with its pilot inside kills the pilot (the bot respawns as a full-HP pilot at base)** [verified-in-game] Corrects bots-eject-rule ('eject below 12 % HP with an enemy within 80 m'): that rule is no longer in the bot code. Current exits: swap (HP <= 35 % AND a usable vehicle <= 70 m AND no enemy within 50 m), trapped/bail, and not-allowed kinds (ma2_bot_brain.c:1240-1270, 1660-1672). Runtime data (31 runs): 216 of 277 vehicle -> pilot transitions happen at hp < 0.15 (mech 115, VTOL 51, BA 28, tank 22) and the 'pilot' reappears at its base with hp 1.0 (E2E_1022 bot 10: MECH hp 0.00 at 724,1306 for 3 s, then PILOT at 955,827 = a respawn). In MP a vehicle destroyed with the pilot inside = the pilot dies; there is no automatic eject on destruction. Bots therefore ride every vehicle to its death. *How:* Bots audit t3B-02 (mode-gated bail-out proposed). Do not assume bots eject.
- **Bot reaction time is 0.90 / 0.55 / 0.30 / 0.12 s (Recruit/Regular/Veteran/Elite) and only delays committing to Attack and switching targets, not the first shot** [code-confirmed] t01b's 'Skill table' is right: reaction 0.90 / 0.55 / 0.30 / 0.12 s (c4 t4-B6 quotes Recruit 0.90 . Elite 0.12). The t01a bots-team-skill-table reaction values 0.60 / 0.44 / 0.28 / 0.12 are stale (Recruit 0.60, Regular 0.44, Veteran 0.28 are wrong; Elite 0.12 matches); its aim-error / QTE numbers were not re-checked. *How:* Bots audit t4-B6 (gate fire on mem_acquired). Quote reaction times from this fact.
- **Mixed 6v6 with one human on Red (cfg 5 Red / 6 Blue bots): Red bots Recruit x2, Regular, Veteran, Elite; Blue bots Elite x2, Veteran, Regular x2, Recruit** [verified-in-game] Data-verified: the human counts as an Elite of his side; the side facing the player gets its weakest place bumped one notch (E E V R R Rc); the other side keeps E E V R Rc Rc. Placement only runs when the hidden [Bots] AutoBalance ini key is 1 (default 1, no UI row; ma2_bots_ui.c:953,105). FFA has no 6-a-side cap (total 12 incl. humans). Grinder: bots capped to 1 (ma2_bots_core.c:381) but 'Off' (0 bots) is also allowed. *How:* Bots audit t3C-00/t3C-01/t3C-03.
- **[BOT-TEAMS] prints only nation 0 and 1 counts, but 6v6 teams sit on other nation ids, so the log cannot show side sizes** [code-confirmed] In FFA, [BOT-ROSTER] labels the FFA total as 'bots red=11 blue=0' next to the team config 'cfg red=5 blue=6' (cfg.ffa not printed; ma2_bots_core.c:400). *How:* When auditing a 6v6 from logs, count [BOT-PLAYER] created lines per team, not [BOT-TEAMS].
- **Bot boarding is healthy: 574 boardings in 40 runs, 100 % entered on the first Y tap, median 6.7 s** [verified-in-game] CanCarryFlag is 0 for 'VTOL - Player' and the tanks 'Manticore'/'Partisan', 1 for every MP 'Mech, BattleArmor, Rommel and the APCs (MEDIUM, Templates data). *How:* Baseline for judging boarding changes.
- **The bot stuck watchdog fires after 6 s without 3 m of progress (2.5 s on a boarding leg), not the design's 2 s, and recovers in several escalating steps** [code-confirmed] Code read: stuck = no 3 m progress in 6 s (2.5 s on a boarding leg) or 12 s 'shuttling' inside an 11 m patch; recovery: the spot 4 m ahead becomes a per-bot obstacle (90 s), ma2_trav_learn 30 s, re-probe + wall sweep; a second stall on open map adds a shared 'unseen obstacle' (r 2.5 m, kept for the whole match, side_prop_add ctrl.c ~1418); then backtrack 4 s to a breadcrumb; jet hop on 'Mech/BA; status.trapped after 4 stalls makes the brain bail out (eject, no_board 120 s). section 6 says ~2 s. Log lines ([BOT-DROP], [BOT-CTRL] no progress/shuttling, [BOT-BACKTRACK], [BOT-ESCAPE], [BOT-TRAPPED], [BOT-NAV] learned) print only with RECOMP_BOT_DIAG and [BOT-SUM] has no stuck counters. *How:* Bots audit t3A-01/t3A-05/t3A-06. Quote 6 s, not 2 s.
- **The bot planner links ledges DOWN only (one-way drops, <= 20 m); there are no jet-up links, so 'Mechs/BA never jet onto a ridge unless stuck** [code-confirmed] Code read: ma2_bot_path.c:176-190 and 355-385 build one-way DROP links down (<= 20 m reach, forbidden for 10 min per 15 m edge after a failed attempt); going up a ledge is never planned: jets up only as stuck recovery (ctrl.c ~1439) or a brain-picked roof (upjet). Design section 6 promises 'Mech/BA jump links. Also: moving vehicles are excluded from the static obstacle grid (obstacle_top: movers -> dyn) and handled as dynamic obstacles with path invalidation. Battle Armor causes 206 of 324 no-progress stalls in the 20-run s13 sweep (Go Commando 41 + 49, Rush Hour 59, In Your Face FFA 20), mostly single stalls in open ground; BA minimum carrot is 8 m (ctrl.c ~81, kind_min_carrot), inside MoveTo's known 5-10 m halt band (inferred cause). Confirmed on the current build (3D's Killing Field run): 76 of 80 stalls are Battle Armor, all single stalls, 80 backtracks. *How:* Bots audit t3A-03/t3A-04.
- **The bot nav graph is chosen by the loading archive, so a custom editor map built on one of 4 graph-shipping bases would load the base level's graph** [code-confirmed] Code + log: the graph source is picked from the loading ARCHIVE; a custom editor map reports its BASE level (3D's 6v6 log: '[BOT-NAV] map=boggeddown.mgf shipped=none', source=generated). Four bases ship a 'Mech graph: In Your Face, New River City, Rush Hour (= Mission16_Mech.map), Witch Cauldron (ma2_bot_mapid.c:28-43); the others generate from the obstacle grid (Killing Field 7947 nodes / 407 components; Over Falls 7381 / 513; Go Commando 2036 / 116). A custom map built on one of the four would load the RETAIL graph for edited terrain (roam points brain.c ~1080, flank via-points ~1021); the editor-written Pathfinding/Scn<ID>_Mech.map is never used. The bots find every other map feature by CLASS at run time, not by name or retail UID: vehicles = MAMech/MATank/MAFlyer/MATurret + entry zones from their MACrateGenerator children; helipads = any MABuilding with an MACollectionArea child; power-ups = MAPowerUp; CTF flags = MAFlagCTF + MATriggerFlagStatus; data cores = MASnatchItDataCore; checkpoints = MACheckpoint / MATriggerCheckpoint; water = MAWater; 'home' = the bot's first spawn spot (b->home_pos, brain.c:2485). No teleport/jump-pad logic exists. Missing features degrade gracefully (no vehicle: fight on foot; no pad: VTOL uses an armour power-up within 300 m; no objectives: deathmatch behaviour). *How:* Editor: MP map authoring; bots audit t3A-08, t3-custom-00.05.
- **Bots navigate custom terrain: the walking planner always runs on an obstacle grid built from the live terrain; the coarse 20 m node graph is generated unless the base level ships a 'Mech graph** [code-confirmed] Code + logs: (1) the walking planner (ma2_bot_path.c, 2 m grid A*) ALWAYS runs on an obstacle grid built at match start from the live terrain + colliders (core.c ensure_nav -> ma2_trav_build, then a fine prop pass), on retail and custom maps alike; this is what bots actually walk. (2) The coarse 20 m node graph (roam points, flank via-points, connectivity) is generated from that grid on any map whose base ships no 'Mech graph (3D's custom 6v6: '[BOT-NAV] obstacle grid ok 508x508 . source=generated:gen_B670C477 nodes=2601 components 1'). An unknown cache id -> terrain-match against the 4 shipped graphs, accepted only at score >= 0.5 and 0.2 ahead of the next; else generated and cached as %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\BotNav\gen_<terrain fingerprint>.map (edited terrain = new fingerprint; with the obstacle grid ready the cache is skipped and the graph regenerated each match). Only the 4 bases that ship a graph (In Your Face, New River City, Rush Hour, Witch Cauldron) give a custom map the RETAIL graph (bots3-nav-graph-chosen-by-loading-archive-.). The bot source has ONE real retail tie (the archive pick in ma2_bot_mapid.c: 14 MP archives + core.c k_nav_archives); everything else is map-agnostic (no retail UIDs, template ids, coordinates or names used as code). The optional stuck-memory file (off by default) is keyed by the archive name, so custom maps on one base would share penalties (t3-custom-A06). *How:* Editor: MP map authoring; bots audit t3A-08, t3-custom-A01.A06.
- **Bot lanes are planned from the live terrain at t >= 1 s in team modes only (up to 3 lanes, none in FFA or when the bases are < 300 m apart)** [verified-in-game] Code read: in TEAM modes at t >= 1 s the core plans team-centroid -> enemy-centroid on the obstacle grid, adds a danger corridor along it and re-plans twice, giving up to 3 distinct lanes ([BOT-LANES]); each bot takes one (g_lane, lane_pick / lane_point; flank via-points must be reachable on the node graph). Not built when the bases are < 300 m apart or in FFA modes (bots go straight and rely on roam/flank). Test map c3-proof\bots_custom_full.ma2map (id 0DAA6085) was rebuilt with two steep Plateau walls giving north hills / central valley with a building choke / south lake + bridge to measure per-lane traversal. GAME PROOF: [BOT-LANES] found exactly the 3 lanes built in the editor ('3 lane(s) from 156,509 to 869,507 (corridor 128 m) in 15 ms'; main = central valley, side +1 apex 498,332 = south lake/bridge, side -1 apex 668,662 = north hills); bots were handed lanes; traffic in x 400-650 by z band: central 252 samples (7 bots), south 57 (2), north 52 (2), 0 on the walls, so every lane is used (central-heavy: it holds the objective and is shortest). Only 5 no-progress stalls in the match; one pilot wedged 30 s at 181,291 by its own base. Lane use detail (t3-custom-path-D01): most bots stay in one lane all match (bots 5/6/8 central only, 9 south only, 7 north only, 10 used north+south); no wall jumps, 2 % of samples clumped (< 8 m), no bot stuck 20 s+ in one 3 m cell; retail-flat comparison td6v6 (no lanes): 25 % clumped, all in the centre. Retail comparison (t3-custom-path-A06, 3D's Killing Field copy TD 6v6, killingfield_td.log): '[BOT-LANES] 3 lane(s) from 387,1667 to 1112,921 (corridor 187 m)', side lanes 408 m and 301 m off the main route, graph generated from the obstacle grid (map=killingfield.mgf shipped=none, 7947 nodes), so custom terrain fans out like retail. Stuck counts there: 80 stalls (76 Battle Armor), 0 trapped, 3 learned obstacles, 2 escapes; the t3A-02 ledge-drop retry did not recur (BA start, 0 drops; needs a 'Mech-start run). *How:* Bots audit t3-custom-path-A02/A03; use bots_custom_full for lane counts.
- **A damaged VTOL repairs at an armour pack within 300 m or the nearest pad within 2.5 km, else fights on; a mode with missing flags/bases/cores scores no objective and plays as deathmatch** [code-confirmed] Code read: helipads = any MABuilding with an MACollectionArea child (core.c ~2363, ma2_bot_pad_add); the editor palette's 'Military VTOL pad' carries one (bots_custom_full: 6 collection areas). A damaged VTOL (hp < 20-45 % by skill) heads for an armour pack within 300 m (no enemy within 120 m of it), else the nearest pad within 2.5 km; with NEITHER, G_REPAIR is never scored and it fights on until it dies (no fly-home-and-hover path); ground units do not use pads at all. objective_eval scores objectives only when w->nobjectives > 0 and obj_find returns both sides' pieces (brain_obj.c ~47-57, 71-76, 269-283): CTF without flags or Snatch It without bases/cores gives objective score 0 and the bots fight as in Team Destruction (no freeze, no wandering). The editor flags these as Must fix ('[text omitted]', 'Snatch It needs the Snatch It bases / data core', verified on bots_custom_stripped, id 1C6565DE). The game does not require a helipad or heal pad at a base, so a missing pad is not a Must fix (suggested Check warning only). *How:* Editor Check wording t3-custom-A05; bots audit t3-custom-A03/A04.
- **A BattleArmor swapping into a 'Mech does not reserve it (claims exist only for GET_VEHICLE), so most BA bots chase the same free 'Mechs at every BA-start match** [verified-in-game] Log + code: claims are made only for MA2_ORD_GET_VEHICLE, and order_swap drives with travel/eject orders, so several BattleArmors chase the same free 'Mech; the first in takes it, the rest find it occupied, re-pick and set off again. ctf.log: 641 swap-go + 101 swap-eject notes; 7 of 11 BA bots start a swap at t = 1.2 and are still BattleArmor at t = 31 (again at 33 and 63); only 9 swaps complete in 180 s; snatch.log similar (16 stuck episodes, 6 swaps). Observed, root cause read from code (inferred). MORE EVIDENCE: goal=swap is 507 of ~2000 samples in CTF and 434 in Snatch It; on a retail-terrain map (Killing Field copy, Battle Armor start, TD 6v6, bots-t3d\killingfield_td.log) goal=swap is 1013-1110 of ~1900 bot samples (53-58 %), 8 of 11 BA bots start a swap at t = 1.1 and are still BattleArmor at t = 31, 2-4 bots chase the SAME 'Mech (02451C40) in every 5 s window for the first minute, only 8 boardings and 13 kills in 170 s. On foot, bots also dither between vehicles (t3-custom-D02: bot 2 set getveh on 4 different vehicles without boarding any; 170 getveh samples, 1 boarding). FIX PROOF: C3 smokes PASSED, no crash. Counters '[C7] c3': custom_full TD assigned = 16, reassigned = 1, switches = 14, foot_getveh = 4; Killing Field TD assigned = 30, swaps_claimed = 19, swap_cooldown_blocks = 11, commit_holds = 3, and goal=swap fell to 33 % of samples against the 51 % baseline. So claiming swap targets plus a per-bot swap cooldown and vehicle-target commitment cut the swap churn by about a third on the retail-terrain map (single runs, not a large sample). *How:* Bots audit t3B-08 (make the swap target a claim); explains t3D-05 churn.
- **On an editor-made map with vehicle pads only, Team Destruction had no vehicle entity at run time (CTF copy did), and pilots stalled 5-12 m short of an editor-placed 'Mech** [inferred] Run logs: on t3d_allmodes (pads: BattleArmor, Loki, Guided-Missile turret; no parked vehicles; players start on foot) Team Destruction had NO vehicle entity at run time (0 [BOT-HULL], 0 [BOT-VEHPICK], all 11 bots pilots for 180 s) while CTF on the BattleArmor-start copy had 'Mechs, VTOLs and turrets (46 [BOT-HULL]): the pads did not produce vehicles for Team Destruction, most likely because pads or their vehicles sit only in the CTF/BaseWar/Snatch game-type groups of the editor kit, or a pad only spawns when asked (inferred; matches the wiki rule that match logic and spawners live in MAMissionTypeGroup per game type). On the editor map bots_custom_full pilots reach the editor-placed 'Mech but stall 5-12 m from its hull without tapping Y, then silently drop it (custfull_td.log: 4 of 5 arrivals stalled, e.g. bot 0 frozen at 232.38,620.36 for 2 s, 5.7 m from hull 018A9020, dest = entry 241,624 behind it); retail runs never do this (574/574 boarded). Possible editor pad stand height / collision difference (inferred). UPDATE: on the stripped test map bots_custom_stripped (every MAPowerUp/MAPowerupDrop deleted, incl. ones nested in spawners / mission-type groups) in Team Destruction all 11 bots stayed pilots for 164 s: the 4 'Mechs EXIST (BOT-HULL kind=2 at 225,378 / 791,404 / 236,616 / 743,285) but none is usable (0 'Mech picks vs 11 in custfull2_td); the same 'Mechs were picked in custstrip_ctf. Cause is MAP DATA, not a bot fault: bot-side 'usable' needs an ARMED entry zone (see bots3-vehicle-usable-needs-armed-entry-zone.), and the strip evidently removed what arms the TD pads' entry zones. Proposed A/B (3D): RECOMP_TEST_DUMP_NEAR=791,404,15,5 on custstrip_td vs custfull2_td should list the 'Mech's children (expect MACrateGenerator + MATriggerPoint in full, missing/unarmed in stripped). Editor implication: deleting powerups/salvage must not touch pad internals; Check should warn 'This vehicle pad cannot be boarded: its entry zone has no crate generator/trigger point' (players hit the same dead pad). ROOT CAUSE FOUND: the editor copied a game type's retail objects only for some types; Team Destruction's vehicle bays and turrets sit in a retail group called 'TD Specific' that was never copied, so TD maps had no vehicles. 9982d3c makes EVERY ticked game type copy its retail objects on New / tick. Editor proof (MCP l3d): New map TD + Check It -> status 'Added the Team Destruction, Check It objects', TD bay groups present (f13_new_dialog.png); game proof pending on g3 (CheckIt + TD 5v6 on that map). This resolves the earlier 'pads sit in per-game-type groups' inference. *How:* Editor MP authoring: check which MAMissionTypeGroup the pad belongs to; bots audit t3-custom-06/07.
- **A bot treats a vehicle as usable only if it is free, alive, own or neutral nation and has an ACTIVE entry zone (armed MACrateGenerator / live MATriggerPoint); with no heal pad the bots just fight or flee** [code-confirmed] Code read: the bot-side usable test needs a vehicle that is free, alive, of own or neutral nation, and with an ACTIVE entry zone (MACrateGenerator armed -> live MATriggerPoint, ma2_bot_brain.c:1174-1183, ma2_bot_entry.c:84-104). Nothing logs WHY a vehicle is unusable (a one-shot [BOT-VEHSKIP] diag was proposed). The refusal is inside the weapon's own fire sub_12B234 -> sub_F13E9, which returns al=0 when the mount object w+0x9C does not resolve from the slot ids w+0x84.0x90, or when mount+0x13C == 0; otherwise it calls sub_CFE30. RESOLVED: BY DESIGN: a weapon fires only from a MOUNT = a MAModSubObjectState node (class [0x4EB01C], byte +0xBC == the weapon's slot id; slots are w+0x84.0x90, -1 = empty) in its MACorporeal owner's model tree (+0xA8). The lookup is sub_B2BE0(tree, id, callback 0xF13C2, 0) -> [0x4EAF48], then the node's vt+0x78 (0x107B2B on 'Mech mounts). Control (nrc_copy): every 'Mech, human and bot, has mount ids 0 and 1. Every on-foot pilot, HUMAN INCLUDED, has none (ids 0-7 all empty), and the human pilot shows no gun in the screenshot: the arsenal pistol (class C14020DA, slots 0,-1,-1,-1) is unmounted, so in the retail game an on-foot pilot cannot shoot. The bomb = DropPack 'Explosive Pack' (key 5A255EC2) on every pilot template (IsDropPackEnabled 1; ArmingTime 0.1 s, ManuallyTrigger 1; body 116392 Env_Detonator_Player, blast MAEffect 125315), with MATriggerLogic + MATriggerRadius + MATriggerTimer children. ## Bot VTOL pick-up ends when the BattleArmor stops wanting the ride (RideIntent, 2026-11-12)

### Facts

- **A bot BattleArmor's lift request outlived its intent: the VTOL chased / hovered over a BattleArmor that was fighting (RideIntent)** [verified-in-game] A bot BattleArmor re-posts its lift request (g_lift, live 3 s) on every evaluation its objective is over 250 m away and nobody is shooting at it, whatever goal it then picks; so while it fought someone else or ran for a power-up, a VTOL kept taking the request, flying to it and hovering over it (v29h1 NRC CTF: VTOL bot 10 t=101.6-110.7 from 258 to 48 m, then 4 s hovering 70-78 m off while BA bot 8 peeked and shot; v29h2: VTOL bot 2 t=113-119 behind BA bot 4 on a power-up run). RideIntent adds g_lift.want_t: the requester stamps it at the end of each evaluation whose goal is ride, or objective without a give-up (lift_off) on the VTOL coming; a VTOL skips (and drops its claim on) a bot's request whose stamp is over 2 s old, and takes it again once it is fresh. The player's requests (no brain) always count. *How:* Switch RideIntent / RECOMP_BOT_RIDE_INTENT (default on). [C7] rideintent: ended, claims_dropped; diag [BOT-RIDEINTENT] (RECOMP_BOT_DIAG). Commit fcab54e on v29-vtol; shipped in 1.0.7 (rc31). — ma2_bot_brain.c:262

## Cinematic levels: frame rate and fill view (v30-cine, 2026-11-12)

### Facts

- **Cinema shots letterbox through the camera viewport, only when the display aspect query says narrow** `001C494E`, `00044AE0`, `00044BE0` [verified-in-game] The cinema shot code asks the display aspect (renderer slot +0x174, hooked sub_382E0) at return address 0x1C494E , only when it is below the constant at 0x494048, animates the camera viewport (camera +0x90 x, +0x94 y, +0x98 w, +0x9C h, normalized, setter sub_44AE0) to a letterbox: y 0 -> 0.214, h 1 -> 0.571, about 2.33:1 inside 4:3, sliding in over the first second. On a widened display the query returns the wide aspect and no letterbox is drawn at all. The camera builder sub_44BE0 folds w/h into the projection aspect, so a letterboxed shot keeps the 4:3 horizontal field of view (projection m00 2.27 vs 2.31 full frame in Cinema_2_1). *How:* RECOMP_CINE_TRACE=<file> logs each camera build with P (m00 m11), VP (rect) and DEV (guest 640x480) columns and prints [CINE-ASPECT] callers. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Cinematic Fill view re-renders the authored band at full output resolution** `00044BE0`, `001C494E` [verified-in-game] [Display] CinematicView (env RECOMP_CINEMATIC_VIEW): 0 Pillarbox (old 4:3), 1 Fill cropped no further than 16:9, 2 Fill (default), 3 Wide (gameplay-like, no letterbox, wider view). In Fill the scene target is the full window size; the letterbox query at 0x1C494E keeps the authored 4:3 answer so the authored 2.33:1 band is still produced, and ma2_cine_camera_fill (called at the top of sub_44BE0) re-lays each perspective camera's viewport across the target at aspect max(authored, screen); ma2_cine_fov rescales the vertical FOV so the authored horizontal extent is kept. Result: 2.4:1 crops about 3 % of the band height and fills the screen; 16:9 shows the whole band full width with thin bars. Text overlays (planet captions) stay on screen. It is a real re-render: in Cinema_2_1 at 3840x1600 the same face covers 300 px in Fill vs 167 px in the 2017x900 pillarbox band. *How:* Proof: (compare3.png, c21_crew_zoom.png). Fill only applies while a cinema level is loaded and PreserveAspect=1. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **What changes in cinema levels above 30 FPS (measured with RECOMP_FIXED_DT)** `004E2440` [verified-in-game] Cinema_1_1a run with fixed dt 1/30, 1/60, 1/120 and 1/150 and compared at equal game time: camera paths and per-shot cameras are identical; each scripted shot lasts its duration plus one frame, so cuts and voice triggers come about one 30 Hz frame earlier per chained trigger at higher rates (0.13 s at the first cut, up to 0.45 s after 11 shots at 120 Hz; half that at 60 Hz). At 120-150 Hz two civilians (MAPerson 132048 and 132051, 'civs set 3', single waypoint 132046 at WaypointSpeed 5) block each other and stop 20 m short for good; at 30 and 60 Hz they reach the waypoint. Traffic MAVehicles diverge by up to 60 m at 150 Hz but only about 6 m at 60 Hz. ## Crash dumps 11-11 / 11-12 triage (v38-crash, 2026-11-12)

### Facts

- **sub_000B4F70 (world UID hash lookup) has no checks: an empty or garbage table faults with #DE or #AV** `000B4F70`, `002B0BB0`, `00107DA3`, `002B1270` [code-confirmed] sub_000B4F70(ecx=world, esi=uid) computes bucket = uid % (([world+0x38]-[world+0x34])>>2) with an unsigned div and walks the chain node->next ([node]), comparing [node+4] with the uid and returning [node+8]. A world pointer that is not a world gives #DE (bucket count 0, fast body +0x79) or #AV (+0x53, reading [world+0x34]). sub_002B0BB0 is the MAModSubObject owner lookup: ecx = sub+0x60 (world), esi = sub+0x80 (owner uid); it is reached from the entity tree Update walk sub_0015D4C7 -> sub_0015D2E9 -> sub_002B1270 (MoeEntitySubModifier slot 7) -> vt+0x64 sub_00107DA3 (slot 25 gate, only for sub-objects with a bound scene node +0xA4). In the fast bodies the guest registers live in the TLS block (rdi+0x42558 eax, +0x42554 ecx, +0x42544 esi, +0x42540 edi, +0x42534 esp) and guest RAM is at host r11 = 0x10000. *How:* Fault at sub_000B4F70__fast+0x53/+0x79: read r10 (= world). A float bit pattern there means the caller's object was overwritten, not a lookup bug. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Film-cap exe crashes (Iron Valley, Crimson Pass) = film_write_pose writing MACameraThird offsets into a different camera** `000B4F70`, `002B0BB0`, `00044BE0` [verified-in-game] Branch film-cap (0061cd2, exe v13-filmcap) only. film_write_pose takes c = g_last_human_cam when [[hc+0x78]+0x154] == v without checking its vtable. After the idle human dies the screen slot camera is another class whose builder is not at camera+0x390; the hook still writes floats at c+0x238.+0x28F, +0x7C, +0x90, +0x180.+0x197, over neighbouring heap objects. Three dumps (crash-43284/53264/27424) fault in sub_000B4F70 with world = sub+0x60 = rotation floats (0.514, -0.997, -0.9998). Reproduced on Crimson Pass CTF 5v6 (fixed dt 1/30, control file cycled): t=156.1 [FILM-POSE] c=02827020 with v=015A8DA0 (not c+0x390), next frame [ICALL] target 0 at ecx = c+0x27C = the 0.0f written at S+0x44, then AV. Not in the release code (film hooks are not merged; 35ae6f4 only reads g_last_human_cam). *How:* Fix if filming continues: accept hc only when MEM32(hc) is 0x0046D348/0x0046D208 and v == hc+0x390. Proof: — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **crash-115220 / crash-134120 = v13-v27p14 [BOT-GOTOWALK] fprintf with a missing %s argument (fixed before deb9b44)** [code-confirmed] Both dumps fault in ucrtbase's printf core reading a double as a char pointer; the [BOT-GOTOWALK] format string is on the stack. The test build v13-v27p14 (PE 6af40e55, deleted) had a %s with no argument; fixed before commit deb9b44 and the current line (ma2_bot_ctrl.c:3789) has 13 specifiers for 13 arguments. Only printed with RECOMP_BOT_DIAG. *How:* MSVC does not check fprintf formats at /W3; count specifiers when adding diagnostic lines. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Reading game crash dumps without cdb: minidump parser + .map + dumpbin** [verified-in-game] Game crash-<pid>.dmp files are MiniDumpNormal (about 300 KB): module list, thread contexts and stacks only, no guest RAM. Match the exe by the module's PE timestamp against build-*\mechassault2_recomp.map headers; symbolize offsets with the map (Rva+Base minus 0x140000000); disassemble fast bodies with dumpbin /disasm /range. *How:* Tools: (md.py dumps exception/regs/stack candidates, thr.py all thread stacks, mapl.py offset -> symbol). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

## CTF 2v2 stall at the flag stands: ExtractHome, the real capture rule (CapAnyway), LoneGround, StageComing (2026-11-14)

### Facts

- **2v2 CTF stall: the flag run's extract kept the ride at the stand; the carrier clawed on and was let go every 2 s, 22 m short** [verified-in-game] On 1.0.9 (rc33) a 2v2 CTF match where both VTOL+BattleArmor pairs took the other flag froze at the stands (Bogged Down c34bd0: all 4 bots still 49.7-131.4 s; VTOLs 'lift-pickup', BattleArmor 'ride-on obj=atk/hold'). order_ride lets a carrier go within 40 m of its own stand (rc33 ma2_bot_brain.c:5804), but the run's FR_EXTRACT stayed on (frun_step ends it only on 'not carrying', VTOL damage or 100 s,3478-3487) and frun_eval kept the BattleArmor's ride (G_RIDE 3.0 whenever its VTOL is within 120 m,3717) and the VTOL's fetch (G_LIFT 3.0,3703). The BattleArmor clawed onto the VTOL hovering 8.5 m over it (ctrl_do_hack, ReClaw 2 s), was let go at once 22 m from its stand, and repeated that ([BOT-CLAMP]/[BOT-LIFT] every 2 s) until the 100 s limit at 129.7/130.5. It never walked the last 12 m that score. *How:* ExtractHome (RECOMP_BOT_EXTRACT_HOME / [Bots] ExtractHome, default on): in FR_EXTRACT a carrier off its VTOL within 40 m of our stand takes no ride and its VTOL no fetch; the carrier walks onto the stand ([C7] extracthome: ride_dropped_s). Branch v34-ctf (NATIVE\the game source tree), exe Test 2026-10-31 \MechAssault 2 v13-v34ctf.exe. Proof on the recorded frames: fires at t=49.77 (nation 1, 22.3 m) and 50.61 (nation 2, 22.8 m) on — ma2_bot_brain.c:3717
- **MechAssault 2 scores a CTF capture with the carrier's own flag away (measured); the bots assumed the classic rule** [verified-in-game] Measured over 6 recordings (rc33 and v34, Bogged Down and Deliverance 2v2): all 11 flag changes 'carried -> home' came with the carrier alive 9.4-10.9 m from its OWN stand, and the game credited a capture (that player's stat 18 +1, every teammate's stat 25 +10) also when the carrier's own flag was carried by the enemy (c34bd_b1 t=57.5 port 4, c34bd_a1 t=54.6 port 4, c34de1 t=143.8 port 7). The bot code assumed a capture needs our flag on its stand: obj_ctf held a carrier 10-20 m off its stand (guard patrol) while ours was away, and RunNeedsHome blocked flag runs while our flag was carried; captures then happened only when the patrol strayed within 10 m. The 'flags time out home' seen in the stall report were these captures. CapAnyway (default on): a carrier walks onto its stand whatever the state of its own flag (a dropped own flag within 120 m is touched home first), and RunNeedsHome applies only with CapAnyway off. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_CTF_CAP_ANYWAY / [Bots] CapAnyway; [C7] capanyway: carrier_s. scripts\flagret.py (proof folder) lists every carried -> home with the carrier's distance to its stand; [OBJ-SCORE] lines (RECOMP_BOT_DIAG) carry the stats. The game code of sub_150880 is not in the tracked gen units, so the rule is measured, not read. — ma2_bot_brain_obj.c:291
- **LoneGround: a CTF bot with nobody to fly took the VTOL and flew lone cover; 1v1 had 0 flag grabs in 240 s** [verified-in-game] With one bot a side (1v1 + an idle player, rc33 c34bd1v Bogged Down) each bot took its team's VTOL (CtfVtolPick's pull 1.1-2.2 plus the 'no gunship up' +0.4) and flew solo cover over the enemy flag for a ground grab nobody could make: 0 grabs in 240 s. LoneGround (default on): with no other bot on the team and no teammate player in a BattleArmor, both VTOL bonuses are off (the bot takes a ground ride and grabs itself), and cover starts only with a ground teammate (a bot not in a VTOL, or a player in a ground vehicle). *How:* RECOMP_BOT_LONE_GROUND / [Bots] LoneGround; [C7] loneground: vtol_pick_skipped, cover_skipped. Branch v34-ctf. — ma2_bot_brain.c:2916
- **StageComing: the CTF stage hold waited 12 s for teammates who were not coming** [verified-in-game] the stage point waited for any live teammate (Veteran 12 s, Elite 15 s): the idle player at the spawn, a pilot respawning 700 m back and our own gunship fighting 250 m off all counted, so a 2v2 attacker stood the full wait twice in one match (c34bd_a1 bot 1, t=122-134 and 210-222). StageComing (default on): only a teammate already near (70 m of the point / 50 m of me) or a ground unit within 300 m that is not carrying their flag counts; nobody coming -> go now, latched 45 s like the staged go. *How:* RECOMP_BOT_STAGE_COMING / [Bots] StageComing; [C7] ctf: stage_nobody. Branch v34-ctf. — ma2_bot_brain_obj.c:150
- **Open: the bots' objective view lost both CTF flags mid-match (6v6 Bogged Down, after a 'carried -> carried carrier=0' event)** [verified-in-game, open-question] In c34bd_6v (v34 interim build, 6v6 CTF Bogged Down) both flags were dropped and picked up again at 96.9-99.1 s; at 105.2 [OBJ-EVT] printed 'carried -> carried carrier=00000000' and from then on Ma2World.nobjectives stayed 0 (the stale check in objective_update clears g_obj.n and objective_refresh, retried every 1 s, never found the flags again): no CTF play for the last 135 s, 0 captures. ## Mission messages (MAActionBroadcast / PopupMenu Execute 0x001A0991): one box, the later replaces the earlier; the custom-level queue (v35-edgame, 2026-11-14)

### Facts

- **MAActionBroadcast/MAActionPopupMenu Execute sub_001A0991: action layout, one message box, TimeDisplayedFor 0 = default -1.0 = nothing drawn** `001A0991`, `00019DE0`, `004E4E7C`, `00493AF4` [verified-in-game] sub_001A0991 (vtable slot 22, thiscall, ret 4, one stack argument it never reads) reads the action at ecx: +0x68 body text id, +0x6C TimeDisplayedFor (float; a value of exactly 0 is replaced by the float at 0x493AF4 = -1.0), +0x70 caption id, +0x74 destination, +0x78 PauseGame byte, +0x79 flag byte. It packs them with sub_00019DE0 into a 0x38-byte struct and calls vtable +0x10 of the composite 0x4E4E7C(1, struct, 0), i.e. the game's single message box. A second message shown while one is up replaces it in the same frame (two timers at 3 s showed only the second), PauseGame 1 does not stop the world (Q2), a message with TimeDisplayedFor 0 draws nothing (Q3), the caption is never drawn (Q5). Game clock for timing is the double at 0x4E2440 (stops while paused). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Custom levels queue their mission messages (FIFO 16, 0.25 s gap); retail levels call the original (commit on v35-edgame)** `001A0991` [verified-in-game] recomp_lookup_manual maps 0x001A0991 to ma2_scn_msg_execute (the icall resolver reaches it: the call is not devirtualised). On a retail level it calls sub_001A0991 unchanged. On a scenario level a message shows at once only when none is on screen; otherwise it waits in a FIFO of 16 (the oldest waiting one is dropped, logged) and msg_pump, run from every in-mission HUD frame (ma2_scn_menu_frame, vtable 00481EF8), shows the next one when the game clock passes the previous message's end + 0.25 s. TimeDisplayedFor <= 0 is never queued (it draws nothing; it is swallowed while another message shows so it cannot wipe it). The queue is emptied on level load and unload (checkpoint reloads included). Proved on F1 D0 Q1 (A1, A2, B1, B2 in order) and S-trig C1 (KILL 1, ANY FIRED, KILL 2, ALL FIRED, OBJ1 DONE all seen). *How:* RECOMP_SCENARIO_TRACE=1 logs '[SCENARIO] message shown / queued / shown from the queue / retail'. — ma2_scenario.c:2418

## How a mission ends: the level result (level descriptor +0x10C), its writers, the death path, and the custom-mission result screen (v35-edgame, 2026-11-15)

### Facts

- **Level descriptor [0x524A60] +0x10C is the level result: 1 lose (reload checkpoint), 2 win (next campaign entry), 3 restart, 4 quit to the hub; any nonzero value ends the level** `00524A60`, `00018F10`, `00015AF0`, `0014E259` [verified-in-game] sub_00018F10 returns the level descriptor (global [0x524A60], static object 0x52B798). Its +0x10C is the level result: 0 while the level runs; the frame step sub_00015AF0 ends the level once it is nonzero (no HUD menu frame runs after it is written; the level unloads about 0.5 s later). Traced in game (, hardware write watch on +0x10C): 1 = lose, the level reloads from the last checkpoint (or its start), silently; 2 = win, the campaign goes to its next entry (custom entries have returntolobby = true: hub, then Custom Scenarios; a retail cinematic level's win went hub -> credits); 3 = restart from the mission's own world (the pause menu's Restart Mission, p_restart.ggf handler sub_0022409B, also writes +0x118 = 2); 4 = quit to the hub (written by sub_00015AF0 when the menu stack update vt+0x18 returns 0 after pause -> Quit -> Yes; the quit leaves +0x118 = 1, which is what sends it to the front end: writing 4 alone with +0x118 = 2 reloads the level instead). After a win +0x110 = 2 and +0x118 = 3; the results menu (vt 0x482638, slot 14 sub_001FB241) copies +0x10C to +0x110 and builds failed.ggf only when +0x10C == 1. Writers: MAActionGameCondition Execute sub_0014E259 (value = action +0x64), the player death path (t49.player-death-path), the frame step (4), sub_0022409B / sub_00224075 (3), MP network handlers sub_001D1590 / sub_001D37E0 / sub_001D3A30, and sub_00016880 resets it to 0 at level start. *How:* To end a level from host code write the value the original path writes (and +0x118 = 1 for a quit to the hub); do it from a HUD frame with the world running. — ma2_scenario.c:2560
- **MAActionGameCondition Execute sub_0014E259 (slot 22) only writes the level result: descriptor +0x10C = action +0x64** `0014E259`, `00018F10`, `0014E215` [verified-in-game] MAActionGameCondition (class key 812C9027; loader sub_0014E215 reads 'GameCondition' into +0x64) Execute is vtable slot 22, sub_0014E259: thiscall, ret 4 (one stack argument, unused); it calls sub_00018F10 and stores [ecx+0x64] at descriptor +0x10C, nothing else. It is reached through the icall resolver (trigger fire, return address 0x0014561E), so recomp_lookup_manual can override it. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Player death -> lose: player entity update sub_000C80DB (vtable 0x4654CC) -> sub_000C9F32 -> sub_0015E6F5 writes descriptor +0x10C = 1; no menu, retail and custom alike** `000C80DB`, `000C9F32`, `0015E6F5`, `0015E213` [verified-in-game] When the player is destroyed (after the death explosion, about 3 s) the player entity update sub_000C80DB (only reference: vtable 0x4654CC, called through the world walker sub_0015D2E9) calls sub_000C9F32, which calls sub_0015E6F5; that one asks sub_0015E213 and stores its nonzero answer (1) at descriptor +0x10C (0x15E73E). Found with a hardware write watch; with FastCode on the running copy is sub_0015E6F5__fast. The level then reloads with no screen: on retail Mission_17b (, menu path) the player died at 00:25:32, LOADING at:38, the mission's intro cinema again; no menu object, no failed.ggf. So the retail campaign does NOT show the 'Mission failed' (failed.ggf) screen on death (closes F1 D0 Q8(c)); failed.ggf belongs to the results menu (vt 0x482638) built for result 1, which the death path never opens. *How:* To hold a death, override 0x000C80DB in recomp_lookup_manual: call the original and put +0x10C back to 0 when it turned 0 -> 1 (F1 G2 does this on custom missions). — ma2_scenario.c:2560
- **Writing 1 to 0x50C9E8 freezes the whole campaign world (clock, units, HUD) until 2 is written; the game's message box shows and takes input meanwhile** `0050C9E8`, `004D382A`, `00015AF0`, `001F6ABF` [verified-in-game] 0x50C9E8 is the pause request the frame step sub_00015AF0 reads each frame: 1 sets the world freeze byte 0x4D382A, 2 clears it and the request (game writers: sub_001F6ABF = 1, sub_001F7354 = 2, the pausing menus). Host code can write it from a HUD frame: in F1 G2 runs the frames outside the result box stayed pixel-identical for 10.7 minutes (1289 frames at 0.5 s) while the native message box (ma2_gui_dialog -> sub_001FB975) was drawn and answered Enter / Esc, and the mission went on normally after 2. — ma2_scenario.c:2560
- **A restart from a checkpoint loads the world from the checkpoint file (MASaveGame.wdf / MAScnsGame.wdf), so the level descriptor no longer names Scn<ID>.wdf** `00524A60`, `0050E844` [verified-in-game] After a lose (result 1) in a mission that saved a checkpoint, the level load hook sees the world path MASaveGame.wdf (the checkpoint file named by the string 0x50E844), not the scenario's Scn<ID>.wdf: anything that recognises a custom level by the world name (level_scenario in ma2_scenario.c) loses it after a checkpoint restart (G1's message queue, the [Assets] archive mount, the result screen). ma2_scenario.c keeps the last scenario level for a checkpoint world (level_scenario_or_checkpoint). — ma2_scenario.c:2560
- **Custom missions show a result screen (MISSION FAILED: Retry / Quit, MISSION COMPLETE: Continue / Replay) instead of the silent restart (v35-edgame, )** `0014E259`, `000C80DB`, `00524A60`, `0050C9E8` [verified-in-game] recomp_manual.c maps 0x0014E259 -> ma2_scn_gamecond_execute and 0x000C80DB -> ma2_scn_player_update. On a scenario level of Type Mission a GameCondition 1/2 is held (not executed) and a death's result 1 is put back to 0; the next HUD frame writes 0x50C9E8 = 1 and opens the game's message box: title MISSION FAILED / MISSION COMPLETE, the line = scenario.ini [Mission] LoseText / WinText or a default ('The mission was lost.', 'Your 'Mech was destroyed.', 'All objectives complete.'), Enter button (action 0x466) Retry / Continue, Esc button (0x465) Quit / Replay. The choice writes 0x50C9E8 = 2 and the result: Retry 1, Continue 2, Replay 3, Quit 4 (+0x118 = 1), then on the hub the Custom Scenarios item is chosen with the mission selected. --quick-test takes Quit / Continue after 3 s. Retail levels and multiplayer maps run the originals (logged 'original path' under RECOMP_SCENARIO_TRACE). *How:* Editor E3 writes WinText / LoseText in scenario.ini [Mission]. — ma2_scenario.c:2560

<a id="t50_cinema_skip_1115"></a>

## Cutscene skip: fixed 0.2 s world steps, the skip flag, MACinema offsets, [Cutscenes] NoSkip (v35-edgame, 2026-11-15)

### Facts

- **The cutscene skip does not stop the cinema: the frame step runs the world in fixed 0.2 s steps (game singleton +0x42 set) until the last shot's Stop, so every remaining shot trigger and timer runs once** `00015AF0`, `00017B20`, `0001DD80`, `0001DE70` [verified-in-game] Traced in game (, per-HUD-frame clock log + hardware write watch on 0x4EB19C). sub_00015AF0 (frame step) stores al = sub_00017B20 at [esp+0x18]; nonzero -> sub_0001DD80(0.2) (fixed 0.2 s step, double 0x493CF8) instead of sub_0001DE70 (real frame time). sub_00017B20 returns game singleton ([0x50C958], sub_00161B4B) byte +0x42 after updating it. After a Space press the step dt (0x4E2428) reads 0.2000 every frame while the QPC time 0x4E2408 moves ~7 ms per frame: 8-12 s of game time pass in ~0.4 s wall; shot advance and Stop (sub_00155B53, called from the advance sub_001559A0, return 0x155A93) run as usual. 3-shot test (4 s shots, a message on each shot's starts/ends trigger, a 14 s timer): skip in shot 1 ran S1-end, S2-start, S2-end, S3-start, the timer, S3-end once each, in order; the natural play-through ran the same set once each. Time scale 0x4A14F0 stays 1.0 (only Stop writes it). *How:* Do not add trigger firing on skip; to block a skip, clear [0x50C958]+0x42 while that cinema is active (custom levels: [Cutscenes] NoSkip). — ma2_scenario.c:2700
- **sub_00017B20 sets the skip flag (+0x42) when the button's press stamp is newer than the previous frame's counter and player +0x90 == 0; works at any frame rate** `00017B20`, `00017CD0`, `004E32AC`, `004E3BAC` [verified-in-game] sub_00017B20 (eax = frame arg): if pause byte 0x4D382A or the menu stack has more than one entry -> other path. S = [0x50C958]. If S+0x42 == 0: when the input object's vt+8 returns [0x4EC078] nothing; else if [0x4E32AC] (input time, ms) > [0x4E3BAC] (previous frame time, copied from 0x4E3BA8 by sub_0001F3F0) then S+0x42 = (sub_00017CD0 == 0), sub_00017CD0 = player 0 (sub_000C8DAE) +0x90. If S+0x42 != 0: input type == [0x4EC044] -> S+0x42 = (sub_00017CD0 == 0), else 0. Cinema Start sets S+0x42 = 1. CORRECTION 2026-11-15 (, t52.cinema-skip-frame-counter): the skip is NOT frame-rate dependent. 0x4E3BA8 is a frame counter (+1 per frame) and the press stamp is that counter at the poll, so the check passes in the press frame at any rate (retail 2/2 at 55-140 fps, custom 3/3 at ~140 fps). G3's 'no skip' reading came from the game clock: a skipped cinema ends at the same game clock as an unskipped one; judge a skip by wall time. *How:* Judge a skip by wall time (the cinema's game-clock end is the same either way). — ma2_scenario.c:2700
- **MACinema +0x2C uid, +0x78 playing, +0x7C time, +0x80/+0x84 controllers vector, +0x8C shot index; MAFreeCameraController +0x9C triggerInit uid, +0xA0 triggerExit uid** `004EB198`, `004EB19C` [verified-in-game] Read in game from the live objects (editor uids 130004 cinema, 130015/130018 shot 1 triggers): MACinema uid at +0x2C (also +0x5C), +0x78 byte playing, +0x7C float time, +0x80/+0x84 std:vector of controller pointers, +0x8C current shot index. MAFreeCameraController triggerInit uid at +0x9C, triggerExit uid at +0xA0. Editor uids are not renumbered by the game (remap_world only remaps text ids and cues), so [0x4EB198]+0x2C equals the editor's MACinema uid. *How:* Match a cutscene from scenario.ini by MEM32([0x4EB198] + 0x2C). — ma2_scenario.c:2700

### Facts

- **MATriggerDestroyed Damage % fires when the unit's health is down to N% (health left, not damage dealt)** [verified-in-game] An editor 'Units are destroyed' trigger with Damage % N fires when the watched unit has N% health or less. The editor label 'Damage % (0 = destroyed)' reads as damage dealt, which is the wrong way round. *How:* Use a high number for 'early damage' (80) and a low one for 'nearly dead' (20). ## Keep these alive: diagnosis (2026-11-15)

### Facts

- **The editor saves 'Win: every objective done' switched ON with zero inputs when no objective has a completing trigger (keep-alive only), and the mission wins at load** [verified-in-game] Editor app_tabs.cpp:2600-2613 sets the win trigger's TriggerEnabled from want.empty only inside 'if (have != want)'; a new MATriggerLogic (triggers.cpp:1022 gives TriggerEnabled 1) with no completers has have == want == empty, so it stays enabled with 0 inputs. Keep-alive objectives never have a completer. Proven: mapB3 + the box ticked, saved by the released editor = MATriggerLogic 'Win: every objective done' TriggerEnabled 1, 0 MoeEntityReference; quick-test: '[text omitted]', hub menu 00481B70 (win). The same map with TriggerEnabled 0 plays 45 s. Check scenario (scenario.cpp:2200) already blocks Test for it, but a saved mission started from Custom Scenarios wins at once. *How:* Fix (editor): keep TriggerEnabled in step with want.empty on every sync pass, not only when the inputs change. Repro: the audit notes — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **A unit removed by 'Remove units' (or any watched UID that no longer resolves) counts as destroyed for MATriggerDestroyed** `001491EF`, `001494AC`, `000B4F70` [verified-in-game] sub_001491EF with TypeOfCheck 1 looks up each MoeEntityReference ReferenceUID with sub_000B4F70 (recomp_0033.c:4897); a failed lookup goes to the walker sub_001494AC with a null entity (4902 -> 4916-4922), which increments the checked count +0xC8 and returns 1 = destroyed (5231-5242). Game-proven: a keep-alive (Any, Damage 0, Lose) on a live friendly Hackman plays 55 s; with a timer that removes the unit at 12 s the mission is lost at 12 s on every start (AllowJacking 0 or 1 alike). A deleted or stale watched UID therefore fires the trigger at load. *How:* Do not use Remove units on a unit a Lose trigger watches unless the loss is wanted. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

## Checkpoint restart keeps the scenario [Assets] archive; frame counter and button press stamps (cutscene skip) (v35-edgame, 2026-11-15)

### Facts

- **A checkpoint restart unloads the level (our hook drops the [Assets] archive); ma2_scn_level_load now mounts it again for the checkpoint world** `000138A0`, `000171E0`, `00524A60`, `0050BAC8` [verified-in-game] Traced in game (, S-trig D3 mission with a checkpoint and the MadDog from mission_06a.mgf in [Assets]): Retry after a lose runs the level unload (ma2_scn_level_unload unmounts T:\scenarios\Scn<ID>_assets_<hash>.mgf) and then the level load with world MASaveGame.wdf, which level_scenario does not match, so before c108940 the archive stayed unmounted for the rest of the mission. Models loaded before the restart still drew (the MadDog player and units looked normal), so the loss only hits files first read after the restart. c108940 takes the scenario from level_scenario_or_checkpoint for the mount: trace 'mounted . -> 1' after each checkpoint load, balanced unmount/mount over two Retries, unmounted on Quit to the hub. *How:* Commit c108940 (v35-edgame). Any per-level host state keyed on the world name must also accept the checkpoint world (MASaveGame.wdf / MAScnsGame.wdf). — ma2_scenario.c:1373
- **0x4E3BA8 counts frames (0x4E2D40 stays 0.0, sub_0001F3F0 forces +1); button press stamps use it, so the cutscene skip check works at any frame rate** `0001F3F0`, `004E3BA8`, `004E3BAC`, `004E2D40` [verified-in-game] sub_0001F3F0 copies 0x4E3BA8 to 0x4E3BAC, then sets 0x4E3BA8 = ftol(double [0x4E2D40] * 1000) (sub_0030A5C0 is _ftol, not a clock) , if that is not above the old value, old + 1. In the recomp [0x4E2D40] reads 0.0 in the front end and in missions, so 0x4E3BA8 is a plain frame counter. Pad 0 button slot at 0x4E32A8 (pad stride 0xF0): +0 float value (1.0 while held), +4 press stamp, +8 release stamp, both = the frame counter of the poll. Per HUD frame (probe, ): in the press frame stamp == 0x4E3BA8 and prev 0x4E3BAC = stamp - 1, the frame step's sub_00017B20 sees stamp > prev and sets the fast flag, next frame dt = 0.2. Retail Cinema_1_1a and Mission_01b intro skipped at ~55 and ~140 fps, custom g3a skipped 3/3 at ~140 fps (menu path, --quick-test, no-probe exe). The G3 'no skip on the final exe' and NoSkip 'cleared on 0 frames' were test artefacts: game-clock end times look the same skipped or not, and the g3n test map had '[Cutscenes]
NoSkip' with a literal backslash-n, so NoSkip was never parsed. *How:* No host fix needed for the cutscene skip. A probe that wants 'input this frame' compares a slot's press stamp with 0x4E3BAC. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

## Defend, side change, counter, match clock, effect, player vehicle (2026-11-16)

### Facts

- **MADefend guards (caps chase radius); it does not walk the unit to its marker** `001B3B9B`, `001B8D08`, `001B42E5`, `001841F3` [verified-in-game] The mech Defend handler start (sub_001B3B9B; tank twin sub_001B8D08) only stores the marker uid (AI+0xD8), sets AI+0x94 = 1 and stores the radius (behaviour +0x7C) in AI+0xDC, and switches the AI to mode 2 (go for the current target; sub_001841F3 does nothing with no target at AI+0x16C). The combat think (sub_001B42E5) uses AI+0x94/+0xDC to cap the engage radius (AI+0x208). No code walks the unit to the marker. In a run two friendly Hackmen with Defend (marker 52-58 m away, one AI on from the start, MAEvent selected) moved 0.0 m in 47 s. Retail uses Defend on enemy 'Mechs placed at their spot (12 MAMech uses, radius 100-190). The older wiki claim that a tank drove to its marker is not reproducible by code. *How:* Use Walk a path once (MAPatrol, TraverseType 1) to send a unit somewhere; Defend to make it hold and fight inside a radius. Editor wording updated (8397f86). Repro: shots1t1/maps/mapC7.ma2map with RECOMP_ENT_DUMP=file,3 and a 'file.now' dump at 50 s. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **A neutral editor unit is an empty vehicle; changing its side makes an enemy with no pilot (stands idle)** [verified-in-game] The editor places a Neutral 'Mech with StartAbandoned 1, AttackPilot 0, m_bAIEnabled 0 and an owner controller (boardable, no pilot). MAActionNation (+ MAActionAI EnableAI 1) later turns it red on the radar but nobody is inside, so it never acts (F1-T1 row 6, 60 s idle). The same map with StartAbandoned 0 (crewed): the Hackman moved 164 m after the 8 s change; built with the editor's crew checkbox: 157.8 m. *How:* Editor commit 8397f86: the Change-side action crews an empty unit from the start (StartAbandoned 0, AttackPilot 1, owner controller removed). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **MATriggerCounter sums the fire counts of the triggers it references and compares with CounterValue** `0014FC90`, `001452D4` [verified-in-game] sub_0014FC90 walks the counter's MoeEntityReference children (ReferenceUID) and adds up each referenced entity's fire count (+0x98, incremented every time sub_001452D4 fires a trigger), then compares the sum with CounterValue (+0xB4) by CheckType (+0xB0): 0 equal, 1 greater, 2 less, otherwise not equal. In a run a counter referencing a 8 s timer with 'exactly 1' fired (D-COUNT at clock 14.26, queued). With no references the sum is 0 and it never fires (unless asked for exactly 0). *How:* Editor: Triggers tab 'Triggers it counts' list (8397f86). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **MATriggerGameTime needs a match with a time limit: never fires in a mission** `0019F40A` [verified-in-game] sub_0019F40A compares m_nPercentLeft with (time left x 100 / time limit) from the game's rules object (game+0x4C vt+0x7C / +0x80); with no rules object or a zero limit it does nothing. A mission trigger with percent 100 never fired in a run. It is for multiplayer maps (the retail GameOver trigger). *How:* Editor shows the field and warns on missions (8397f86). Direction of the compare is inferred (fires when the remaining percent is at or below the field). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **MAActionMoeEFX plays the effect at the entity that set the trigger off; a timer passes none and shows nothing** `0014EA23` [verified-in-game] The action's execute (sub_0014EA23) takes the triggering entity as its argument and spawns the effect at that entity's position; a NULL argument does nothing. Retail uses it under circle triggers (43 of 44 uses) and one box. Effect id 125706 under a Player-enters-circle trigger at the player start gave a large explosion on the player at mission start; the same id under a timer showed nothing. *How:* Editor: note and warning in the action panel (8397f86). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **MAActionChangePlayerVehicle wants a MAPlayerConfiguration uid (GlobalEntities), not a unit template** [verified-in-game] ConfigTemplateUID must be a MAPlayerConfiguration in GlobalEntities (Mad Dog 33088, Blood Asp 123588 and others; retail PlayerNum 0, UseHeading 1, SetAsDefaultConfig 0). A plain unit template (Atlas) changed nothing in F1-T1. With a real configuration (Stiletto, Mad Dog player) the view changed at once (fade, then a HUD-less ground camera): CORRECTED in part 2: the failure was missing configuration files, not mech-to-mech; see maactionchangeplayervehicle-needs-config-files. *How:* Editor picker lists the game's configurations; saving ships the chosen configuration's files (53f7c38). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Defend a point guards; a walk-once path plus an arrival circle makes the unit go there first** [verified-in-game] MADefend holds a marker and a radius: a unit placed at its spot and engaged by enemies advances to the radius (60 m measured: 0 positions beyond 60.1 m) and fires, never further. It does not walk to the marker. A friendly 'Mech given MAPatrol TraverseType 1 walks the route once and stands at the last point (Hackman, 2 waypoints, game run). An MATriggerRadius with RadiusSet = a MoeEntitySet holding the unit, TypeOfCheck 2, PlayerEntitesOnly 0, NationInverse 1, NationCompare 11 fires when that unit is inside (message queued at clock 6.9 s as the Hackman arrived). Enemies in sight (about 450 m) pull a walking or patrolling unit off its route. *How:* Editor 27d5148: Defend a point in the orders chooser builds walk-once path to the spot + that circle + MADefend started by the circle. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **A player-configuration swap needs the configuration files in the mission archive** [verified-in-game] The swap works from an on-foot start (Mad Dog: HUD, new body, W moves it) and from a 'Mech start. What broke Mech to Mech and on foot to Blood Asp in F1-S2 part 1 was missing files: the configuration's body, camera and models were not in the Base, common.mgf or the mission [Assets] archive, so the game left a HUD-less ground camera and no body. Shipping the files fixes it (on foot to Blood Asp and Mech start to Blood Asp: HUD, model, control). *How:* Editor 53f7c38: saving a map with a Put the player in a vehicle action ships the configuration's templates (closure) like the start body's. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

### Facts

- **The "bridge-foot lamps without cones" are the near bank of the same Canal_Wall_ST: its cone mesh is single-sided and the game culls it seen from behind** [code-confirmed] Canal_Wall_ST (139 x 140 m) holds both banks of a canal and a lamp column on each. Its cone mesh vcone (material light_016 mat, Light_016_spot.tif, additive, shading material_only) is a plain visible mesh in node optimize0: no node_light, no .mtb rule, two_sided=false. From the G0 spot-A eye (494, 13.6, 343; section at 599.7, 6.07, 296.3) all 64 near-bank cone triangles face away and all 64 far-bank ones face the eye (fmt_test E2). The game draws the far-bank cones and never the near-bank ones in every look (G0 L8): it back-face culls single-sided transparent meshes. Env_PedBridgeB has no lamp heads; its lights node (point_light01, additive) is hidden by its .mtb and holds no node_light, so neither program draws it. *How:* Cull single-sided meshes whatever their blend mode (editor core/lamp_rule.h cull_back_faces; decals excepted). — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

With the offset in world axes, a camera facing east had the box 10 m to its side: G0 L9 measured editor flake coverage about 0.5x the game (changed-pixel share 0.044 vs 0.091, thr 20). With the offset and emitter frame turned by the camera heading the same pose gives 0.13-0.18 (1.4-2.0x), flakes over the whole view as in the game frame. The game also draws smaller flakes (limit_screen_size=true; the editor does not clamp sprite screen size). *How:* Editor add_precip_effect: rotate the precip offset and emitter frame by the camera yaw. Open: the game limit for limit_screen_size. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

The game fogs everything there (fog colour at the horizon). - **Starry space drew nothing on custom maps because the world named Env_SkySpace.MGMODEL while [Assets] shipped Env_SkySpace.NODE** [verified-in-game] Env_SkySpace exists as .MGMODEL only in cinema_2_4 and as .NODE in cinema_2_1 (and other cinemas); the editor's dependency collector resolves per archive in order and found the .NODE first, so [Assets] carried the NODE and its .mesh files but not the MGMODEL the world named.
