## Generated water / wall models on custom levels, and the Starry space (second) sky brightness (2026-11-16)

### Facts

- **A placed MACorporeal's [obj+0x198] already points at a block holding the TEMPLATE's Corporal3DObj path, so an instance's own model (resized water, cut wall, base, parking lot) is ignored by the slot-113 build** `000D75C7`, `000D6EC6`, `000D6E33` [verified-in-game] Traced in a custom level (RECOMP_SCENARIO_TRACE): on the build call sub_000D75C7 (ecx = object, UID at +0x2C) every placed MAWater / MAWall / base / parking lot already has [obj+0x198] non-null. It points at a 0x18-byte block of two begin/end/cap std:strings, +0 Corporal3DObj and +0xC CorporalMTB (getters sub_000D6EC6 returns the block, sub_000D6E33 returns block+0xC), holding the template's path (Env_Water1000x1000.MGMODEL, Env_MedWall_Span.MGMODEL, Env_ParkingLot_30x30.NODE .); the world entry's Corporal3DObj is never read. So the editor's generated MA2SE_<model>_<W>x<L>.MGMODEL / cut models were never built. A lookup override on 0x000D75C7 that swaps [obj+0x198] for a block holding the world entry's path for the call and puts the old pointer back after makes the game build them: the three resized waters of the p10 map then draw 10 vertices each (before: 878-vertex strips, extents -500.500) and the 1000 m sheet over the ground is gone. *How:* kit/source/game/src/scenario/ma2_scenario.c ma2_scn_corporeal_build (custom levels only, entries whose path holds MA2SE_, matched by UID). Guest strings: xbox_HeapAlloc, never freed; restore [obj+0x198] because the destructor frees what it finds there. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

The editor's frame (static, no .mtb rotation; two screenshots minutes apart are byte-identical) is 73.9, 72.3, 54.8 = 1.02 x the level start. There is no brightness bug in the static sky. *How:* Compare skies with the game at level start (first shots), not a late frame. ## In-game live editor: live session, scenario reload in place, loading screen timing, hidden-game audio CPU (2026-11-16)

### Facts

- **The in-game editor no longer restarts the game: a shared block (--from-game-live) lets the two processes take turns on screen** [verified-in-game] J4 (v35-edgame + editor track-c-s2): the game creates Local\MA2SE-live-<pid>-<n> (Ma2seLive, 1696 bytes, same layout in the editor's from_game_live.h) and starts the editor with --from-game-live <name>. Back to the game and Test are requests in the block; the game reloads changed files in place, walks its menus while hidden and comes on screen when Custom Scenarios (Back) or the tested level's loading screen (Test) is up. The editor stays alive and hidden during a test and comes back when the player leaves it (pause > Quit, Continue / Quit on the result screen, the match results, or any front-end menu). Switch: the incoming window shows just below the outgoing one without activation, draws two frames, then the outgoing one hides itself. Both processes set AppUserModelID "MechAssault2.Recomp" (one taskbar button); the editor takes the game's class icon and rectangle. RECOMP_EDITOR_LIVE=0 or an older editor (no attach within 15 s) = the old exit-code / restart protocol. Test to control: 13.8 s with the restart (Day 1 logo, boot loading, title, hub, picker, loading) vs about 2.4 s live (no list change). *How:* Log lines "[SCN-LIVE] <tick> ." trace every step. Contract: NOTES section 6b. — ma2_scenario.c:1
- **A changed, new or deleted .ma2map is taken in without a restart: every index archive unmounted, one new full index mounted** [verified-in-game] live_resync compares each loaded scenario with its file (write time + size): same Id = loaded again into its slot (new text_base, pointers g_level_last / g_end / g_mission_scn moved, old buffers freed), gone / unfinished / new Id = marked deleted (out of the campaign; a deleted multiplayer map keeps its last version in the index because the game's map list still has it), new files added. live_rebuild then unmounts every index archive mounted so far (boot index_<stamp>.mgf, rescan deltas, earlier live ones) and mounts index_<stamp>_L<nnn>.mgf with every scenario (MissionSet63.ini and the campaign file included; remap_world runs once per world). The campaign file keeps its name: Custom Scenarios mode holds the name in the campaign path format, and a renamed campaign whose old file was unmounted made the picker start a level with a garbage world name (seen in game). The Custom Scenarios rows are built when it opens: it is entered again (Esc to the hub, item 8) only when the rows (Ids, names, descriptions) changed. Proven: an edited mission started from the picker showed the new message at once; a Save as file was listed and selected. *How:* Never keep the old index mounted next to a rebuilt one with the same paths; keep the campaign stem stable across live rebuilds. — ma2_scenario.c:1
- **Pause > Quit in a custom mission: Quit to Main Hub, "Abort mission in progress?" In a custom mission the level unloads, 3DLobby.wdf loads, the hub (00481B70) comes and Custom Scenarios mode moves on to the mission picker (0048F3E0) without any press. During the load the game presents rarely: J4 shows the game once no frame came for 150 ms after the level-load hook, or at the first INGAME frame. *How:* Use xbox_FramebufferFlipCount gaps to tell the loading screen from the menu fade. — ma2_scenario.c:1
- **A RECOMP_FB_HIDDEN game window cannot be shown: the framebuffer thread hides it again every loop** [code-confirmed] fb_present.c thread loop: "if(diagnostic_hidden && !IsIconic(hwnd) && IsWindowVisible(hwnd)) ShowWindow(hwnd,SW_HIDE)". ShowWindow / SetWindowPos(SWP_SHOWWINDOW) from other code is undone at once, so harness runs cannot measure the game window's own show/hide; J4 logs those steps ("quiet: game window would .") and shows only the editor (off screen, tool window). *How:* For window-switch checks in harness runs measure the editor window and the game's log; a visible game needs a real desktop run. — fb_present.c:1

The APU frame loop has a pause (pause_requested / is_idle, mcpx_apu_wait_for_idle / mcpx_apu_resume) but the helpers are static in apu_core.c; pausing it while the game thread may still talk to DirectSound risks a wait on the doorbell ack. SUPERSEDED 2026-11-16 (e04f328): the APU is now held while the editor is on screen and the game idles, hidden game ~6% of a core; see t59.apu-hold-behind-editor. *How:* Getting under 1% needs an exported APU pause in apu_core.c used only while the game thread is parked (outside the files J4 may change). — apu_core.c:1

<a id="t59_j4_apu_hold_1116"></a>

## J4 follow-up: audio emulation held while the in-game editor is on screen

### Facts

- **mcpx_apu_hold parks the whole APU while the hidden game idles behind its live editor (55% -> ~6% of a core)** [verified-in-game] apu_core.c mcpx_apu_hold(1) makes mcpx_apu_frame_thread wait on its condition at the top of its loop, between frames (never inside the guest ISR or an output wait), so the voice processor, the GP/EP DSP frames (dsp_thread_main only runs when the frame thread hands it one), the doorbell ack, the output and interrupt delivery all stop with nothing reset; mcpx_apu_hold(0) wakes it under the APU lock. It is separate from the title's pause_requested. Measured: hidden game 47-63% of a core before, 5.2-6.7% after; the remainder is nv2a_ack_thread (~1.7%), kernel_timer_thread (~1.6%, 1 ms timer), ohci_thread (~1.3%), fb_thread, XAudio2, clock_worker and the game's one menu frame a second, none of it audio. *How:* Commit e04f328 on v35-edgame (exe f84e9098). Log: [APU] audio emulation held / running again and [SCN-LIVE] audio emulation held / running. Getting under 5% would also need the nv2a ack (250 us poll), the kernel timer (1 ms) and the USB thread to idle (other files). — apu_core.c:1

## Reach overlay: per-unit movement facts ("Can it get here?")

## "Can it get here?" reach overlay: per-unit movement facts (2026-11-16)

### Overview
Source for the numbers in the editor's reach overlay (`kit/source/game/src/core/reach_rules.h`, branch `reach`): what each unit type can climb, jump, drop off, fly or land on, each with its source. Rows are `measured` (in-game run M1-M6, notes `reach\MEASURED.md`), `code` (bot planner source v35-edgame, `reach\`), `catalog` (GlobalEntities templates) or `estimated`. Estimated values are marked "estimated" and the overlay shows "(est.)" when one decided a verdict. Status of this pack: final (2026-11-17; M5 claw and a few runs not done, marked).

The overlay's two views: **Player** = real ability; **Bots** = min(planner rule, real ability). The differences are on the bot-gaps page (`t61_reach_bot_gaps_1116`).

### Unit table
| Unit group | Climb / step | Jets | Drop (edge) | Notes | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 'Mech with jets (14 chassis) | Atlas 148% measured (all chassis est.) | apex 24.7-27.3 m (M1); overlay = apex - 1; Uziel/Summoner est. (same jet stats as Belial / Hellbringer) | >= 30 m (Atlas, M3) | Jump key is Shift | M1, M3 measured |
| 'Mech without jets (16 chassis) | Atlas 148%, blocked at 171% | none | >= 30 m (Atlas, M3) | planner walls at 55% | V4 + M3 measured |
| Battle Armor | slope no walker limit found in the final M2 run: the Atlas, Hackman, Mad Dog, pilot and BA climbed a 66 m single-cell face (825%) and the Atlas every lane up to 375%; the Rommel tank climbed up to a +50 m cell (625%) and was blocked at 825% (measured, MEASURED.md M2) | apex 19.71 m (M1); median 16.9, overlay keeps 16 | >= 30 m (M3) | claw (Space) latches objects only; not measured (M5 was tried twice on the Bogged Down power plant, the claw did not latch; no MACorporeal wall in the base archive) | M1, M3; UpStretch |
| Pilot on foot | bracket: 39-50 deg blocks, 66 grid passes (est. 1.32 m/2 m) | none | >= 30 m (M3) | speed p90 12.1 m/s | wiki FootSlope; M3 |
| Tank (Rommel) | planner 55 (real: no walker limit found in the final M2 run: the Atlas, Hackman, Mad Dog, pilot and BA climbed a 66 m single-cell face (825%) and the Atlas every lane up to 375%; the Rommel tank climbed up to a +50 m cell (625%) and was blocked at 825% (measured, MEASURED.md M2)) | none | >= 30 m (M3) | AI-only tracked variants not player-usable | code + M3 |
| VTOL | flies | n/a | n/a | ceiling terrain + 48.4 m; landing a VTOL settles on a 30% slope and slides off a 50% slope (bracket 30-50%, measured M4); the overlay uses 0.30, still estimated | measured ceiling |
| Turrets | immobile | n/a | n/a |  | catalog |

Also: no hover vehicles exist in MA2; mission AI (20 m nav graph) is not covered by overlay v1; `--start-in` is an editor flag. Water flags: the Atlas, Rommel and pilot cross a 4.7 m deep and a 1.2 m shallow editor pond at full speed (Bogged Down flags all 1); BA, type-16 cells and flags 0 not tested (M6).

### Corrections
The older BankDive fact ("a jetless 'Mech did not come down a long bank") concerned a slope band, not a vertical edge: see `t60.bankdive-correction-slope-band-not-edge`.

Space is the Battle Armor claw (latch climb), not a jump. VTOL climb demand is also Shift (+30 up, Ctrl -30). Measured in the M1 run with Shift held. *How:* Any player-side reach measurement or test script that jumps must hold Shift, not Space. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

- **Tanks: only the Rommel Mk2 is player-usable; Manticore, Partisan, Gator and APCs are AI-only tracked** [code-confirmed] Player-usable tank = Rommel Mk2 (pad vehicle on every MP map; Kurita-player and WOB variants have identical movement): speed 20, mass 33 t. AI-only plain tracked MATank (not offered to players): Manticore, Partisan, VMil_THE_Gator (speed 25, mass 60), the VMil_APC_* set, VMil_Aircraft_Carrier turret. The bot planner plans tanks on the LIGHT grid plus slp > 55 impassable (CTRL:2337; 28.8 deg) with a drop limit of 6 m; floor_model.py wrongly uses the heavy grid (FM:110, gap G15). The real tank slope limit: no walker limit found in the final M2 run: the Atlas, Hackman, Mad Dog, pilot and BA climbed a 66 m single-cell face (825%) and the Atlas every lane up to 375%; the Rommel tank climbed up to a +50 m cell (625%) and was blocked at 825% (measured, MEASURED.md M2). Step-off: the Rommel drives off 6, 10, 20 and 30 m edges and lands (M3, measured). Tank faces that the grid leaves open at slp 43-53 stall tanks (learned TankFace). *How:* Overlay tank_step 1.1 (est.), drop_tank raise to >= 30 for the player view. Gaps G7, G15 and G16. — ma2_bot_ctrl.c:2337
- **VTOL: ceiling is terrain + 48.4 m (MaxVTOLHeight 55 - 6.6); landing slope unknown** [verified-in-game] MaxVTOLHeight (flyer actor +0x4E0, default 55) is a property of the flyer, not of the map. A stick-flown VTOL levels off at the height-map terrain under it + (MaxVTOLHeight - about 6.6) = terrain + 48.4 m: measured 48.0-48.7 over New River City and 28.2-28.4 over the Bogged Down bog (terrain -19/-20). Climb demand 30 m/s with Shift, -30 with Ctrl; holding Y lowers the craft to ~2 m and the pilot gets out. Bot lane cells shut when building top + 7 m (13 with a rider) exceeds ceiling + 1 (CTRL:1956). Landing slope and pad radius: a VTOL settles on a 30% slope and slides off a 50% slope (bracket 30-50%, measured M4); the overlay uses 0.30, still estimated; the overlay uses 0.30 slope (was 0.25) and a 5 m radius, ESTIMATED (radius not measured). Ceiling note: M4 read ground + 49.55 m on a tracked node vs 48.4 earlier; use 48.4 for the cautious side. *How:* Overlay vtol_land_slope 0.30 (bracket 30-50%) and vtol_land_radius 5 are estimates. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Player turrets are immobile (speed 0): no reach, only a position** [documented] The five PlayerTurret templates (Laser, Autocannon, LRM, Gauss, Guided Missile; MATank class) have CorporalMaxSpeed 0 and a 360 deg arc; only the Guided Missile one is placed on MP maps (1-4 per map). The overlay treats them as immobile: the only reachable point is the unit's own spot. *How:* Overlay group Turret: no step, no drop, no climb. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Step-off (M3): Atlas, Rommel, pilot and BA all walk or drive off 6-30 m edges and land** [verified-in-game] Measured 2026-11-16 on built maps: the Atlas, the Rommel tank, the pilot on foot and the Battle Armor each leave a vertical terrain edge of 6, 10, 20 and 30 m under their own power and land on the ground below. So the overlay drop_mech_nojet, drop_tank and drop_foot (estimates 6, 6, 10) are too low for the player view and are set to >= 30 (measured). Fall damage was not measured; limits beyond 30 m were not tested. The bot planner keeps its own limits (tank 6, pilot 10, 'Mech/BA 60), so the Bots column keeps them (gap G16). *How:* Source string for those rules: MEASURED.md M3. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **CORRECTION: the BankDive 'did not come down' failure was a slope band, not a vertical edge** [verified-in-game] The fact t30.bankdive-first-pass-dive-legs says a jetless 'Mech 'did not come down a long bank' at 6 rim spots. M3 shows the Atlas (and tank, pilot, BA) walk off vertical edges of 6-30 m and land, so that failure concerned a long steep SLOPE band (the planner's wall/stall on a bank face), not a vertical edge. Do not read it as 'jetless Mechs cannot drop 6 m+'. That fact itself is left unedited (this note corrects the reading, not the data). *How:* Use the M3 fact for drop limits; use the slope facts for banks. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Water in reach: per-map MAEnvironment flags (meaning unconfirmed); the planner ignores water for walking** [documented] Water is the type-map bit (8 shallow, 16 deep, 32 waterway) plus per-level MAEnvironment keys Mech/Tank/BA/Pilot x Shallow/Deep/Waterway with Speed/Damage/Cooling. The 0/1 'may enter' reading is a guess; no code consumer of the deep fields was found. A pilot wades a 1.2 m basin and walks submerged in a 4 m lake. The planner keeps the bed as the walkable surface and only refuses landings in water unless carrying a flag (NAV:396, PATH:744+). Flag meaning: the Atlas, Rommel and pilot cross a 4.7 m deep and a 1.2 m shallow editor pond at full speed (Bogged Down flags all 1); BA, type-16 cells and flags 0 not tested (M6). *How:* Overlay v1 does not block water unless M6 proves the flags. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **MechAssault 2 has no hover vehicles: only tracked MATank, one AI barge, and the VTOL** [code-confirmed] No class, template, flag or model name in GlobalEntities mentions hover (3,449 templates scanned). Manticore, Partisan, Gator and the APCs are plain tracked MATank; the only boat is the AI Vciv_Barge01. 'Hover over water' applies to the VTOL only (it flies). *How:* No hover-tank entry in the reach picker. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **Mission AI (20 m nav graph) is not covered by the reach overlay v1** [documented] The overlay answers 'can the player (or the MP bot planner) get here'. Campaign/mission AI units path on a separate 20 m node graph with their own rules; the overlay does not model it. Treat the Bots view as the MP bot planner of v35-edgame (2 m grid) only. *How:* Not in v1; revisit if mission-AI reach is needed. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0
- **start-in <unit> is a developer flag of the editor exe, not of the game** [code-confirmed] The game has no start-in or start-vehicle option (grep of the whole the game source tree tree). The editor's --start-in <uid or label> sets the document's player start container on every StartVehicles* key of MARoot. Labels: On foot (pilot), Battle Armor, the 30 'Mech names as in the catalog, VTOL, Rommel Mk2 tank; Avatar/Cinema/Lobby/NoBomb/NearClip/Kurita/WOB/Turret/Elemental names are skipped. *How:* Use it to place the reach tests' player in a given body. — maintainer analysis notes (not in the repository):0

## Reach overlay: bot behaviour gaps (planner vs real limits)

## Bot behaviour gaps: planner limits vs what each unit can really do (2026-11-16)

### Overview
Status: final (2026-11-17; M5 claw and a few runs not done, marked). Proposal for the bots owner; the bot code (read-only for the reach track) is unchanged. Planner rules with file:line are in `reach\` (NAV = ma2_bot_nav.c, PATH = ma2_bot_path.c, CTRL = ma2_bot_ctrl.c, BRAIN = ma2_bot_brain.c, FM = tools/floor_model.py). Real ability: the per-unit facts of `t60_reach_units_1116` and the in-game measurements M1-M6.

The "Can it get here?" overlay shows **Player** (real ability) and **Bots** (the stricter of planner and real ability); where they differ on a map, a gap below is the reason.

### Gap table

Other chassis: no walker limit found in the final M2 run: the Atlas, Hackman, Mad Dog, pilot and BA climbed a 66 m single-cell face (825%) and the Atlas every lane up to 375%; the Rommel tank climbed up to a +50 m cell (625%) and was blocked at 825% (measured, MEASURED.md M2) | Bots route round hills and ramps the player walks straight up; they lose high ground and arrive late at hill objectives | Raise `TG_STEP_HEAVY` toward the measured limit with a margin (1.1 -> 2.0 m, 100%) behind a flag; or keep 1.1 as the cost knee and make 55-100% a costly, not blocked, step | Controller must really drive up (stall learning TG_NLEARN catches failures). A/B on the objective-reach matrix + parity table |

### Order to take them in
1. G1 ('Mech slope) and G2 (walk down): largest effect on high ground and objective parity.
2. G3 + G4 (jet priors) and G16 (tank/pilot drops): small code, removes timidity the player does not have.
4. The rest as cleanups.

## Environment variables

- `MA2_KIND_TURRET` — Fixed guns are turrets and are never ridden
- `MA2_SUPPORT_URL` — One support-address placeholder: MA2_SUPPORT_URL (game: ma2_release.h; installer: precheck.py; docs token {{MA2_SUPPORT_URL}}); empty until the project sets it
- `RECOMP_ABI_CHECK` — RECOMP_ABI_CHECK reports callee register and stack violations
- `RECOMP_AC97_READY` — AC97 codec-ready bit is forced for DirectSound; Titles that probe the AC97 codec can skip their whole engine init
- `RECOMP_AC97_READY, RECOMP_AUDIO_VOLUME, RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS` — Audio and watchdog env vars
- `RECOMP_AFFINITY` — RECOMP_AFFINITY=<hex> restricts the whole game to a CPU mask (test only)
- `RECOMP_ALLOC_TRACE` — RECOMP_ALLOC_TRACE logs contiguous allocations
- `RECOMP_APU_DSP` — RECOMP_APU_DSP and RECOMP_APU_DSP_THREAD; RECOMP_APU_DSP=0 selects the older audio fallback
- `RECOMP_APU_DSP_HEADROOM` — DSP headroom is on by default (RECOMP_APU_DSP_HEADROOM=0 turns it off); RECOMP_APU_DSP_HEADROOM
- `RECOMP_APU_GAIN_TRACE` — RECOMP_APU_GAIN_TRACE
- `RECOMP_APU_HRTF` — HRTF is off by default; RECOMP_APU_HRTF switches it; RECOMP_APU_HRTF
- `RECOMP_APU_LIMITER` — Pre-GP bus limiter: opt-in only (RECOMP_APU_LIMITER=1); RECOMP_APU_LIMITER
- `RECOMP_APU_MIX_TRACE` — RECOMP_APU_MIX_TRACE
- `RECOMP_APU_MP_TRACE` — RECOMP_APU_MP_TRACE
- `RECOMP_APU_PIPELINE_CAPTURE` — RECOMP_APU_PIPELINE_CAPTURE, _START and _SECONDS
- `RECOMP_APU_STACK_BA` — RECOMP_APU_STACK_BA
- `RECOMP_APU_STREAM_STATS` — RECOMP_APU_STREAM_STATS and RECOMP_APU_STREAM_TRACE
- `RECOMP_APU_VOICE_LOCK` — RECOMP_APU_VOICE_LOCK
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_ACTIVE_GUARD` — RECOMP_AUDIO_ACTIVE_GUARD (default on, 0 = off): DirectSound ActiveGuard, no second active-list insert for a still-linked voice
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_CAPTURE` — RECOMP_AUDIO_CAPTURE=<absolute wav path>; RECOMP_AUDIO_CAPTURE writes mixed PCM to a WAV; RECOMP_AUDIO_CAPTURE records audio under RECOMP_AUDIO_SILENT
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_DEFER_GUARD` — RECOMP_AUDIO_DEFER_GUARD (default on, 0 = off): DirectSound DeferGuard, no second deferred-list insert for a queued voice
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_ISR_STATS` — RECOMP_AUDIO_ISR_STATS
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_SILENT` — RECOMP_AUDIO_SILENT; RECOMP_AUDIO_SILENT silences only device submission
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_STATS` — RECOMP_AUDIO_STATS; RECOMP_AUDIO_STATS logs mix levels and queue health
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_STOP_ASSIST` — RECOMP_AUDIO_STOP_ASSIST
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_TAIL_STATS` — RECOMP_AUDIO_TAIL_STATS prints [APU-TAIL] every 5 s
- `RECOMP_AUDIO_VOLUME` — RECOMP_AUDIO_VOLUME
- `RECOMP_BAVT_SPAWN` — Test recipe to spawn a player straight into a vehicle
- `RECOMP_BAVT_TEST` — BattleArmor, VTOL and tank test phases
- `RECOMP_BOTS_MAX` — Bot cap: RECOMP_BOTS_MAX (6 a side)
- `RECOMP_BOT_* list` — Bot environment variables for tests
- `RECOMP_BOT_ATTACK_PILOT` — RECOMP_BOT_ATTACK_PILOT chooses AI flag bits
- `RECOMP_BOT_BANK_DIVE` — BankDive: jet bodies get HopDown's bank leaps in the planner's first pass
- `RECOMP_BOT_BOX_NEAR` — BoxNear: a boxed-in 'Mech with an enemy 'Mech or tank inside 120 m wedges after 3 s (6 s otherwise) so the brain finds a firing spot (default on, RECOMP_BOT_BOX_NEAR / [Bots] BoxNear)
- `RECOMP_BOT_CAMWATCH` — Camera diagnostics under RECOMP_BOT_DIAG
- `RECOMP_BOT_CHOKE_LEAP` — ChokeLeap: a bot leaping off a choke's mouth does not queue in the choke
- `RECOMP_BOT_CLIMB_AHEAD` — ClimbAhead: jet 'Mechs jet straight up steep climbs and replans no longer reset the climb clock
- `RECOMP_BOT_DIAG` — RECOMP_BOT_DIAG master diagnostic switch; Bot diagnostics ([C7], [CAM-WATCH], [BOT-NOBOARD], [BOT-TRACE], [BOT-ROOFS]) print only with RECOMP_BOT_DIAG=1 or [Bots] BotLog=1
- `RECOMP_BOT_DROPS` — Ledge drops are allowed in planning (RECOMP_BOT_DROPS)
- `RECOMP_BOT_FOOT_BODY_SKIP` — FootBodySkip: a terminal FootPrecheck found unwalkable is skipped while the bot stays in that hull
- `RECOMP_BOT_FOOT_PRECHECK` — FootPrecheck keeps a failed pilot-walk answer per bot for 10 s
- `RECOMP_BOT_FOOT_SLOPE` — FootSlope: the FootFallback pilot-walk precheck shuts cells steeper than slp 66 (33 deg)
- `RECOMP_BOT_HOT_UPJET` — HotUpJet: a 'Mech at 85% heat or more waits 2.5 s before an up-jet it wants (default on, RECOMP_BOT_HOT_UPJET / [Bots] HotUpJet)
- `RECOMP_BOT_JET_SHOW` — RECOMP_BOT_JET_SHOW makes a bot jet in front of the player
- `RECOMP_BOT_JET_TRY_FUEL` — JetTryFuel: a jet-up try is judged 6 s from its first burn, not from reaching the foot
- `RECOMP_BOT_LANGUAGE` — Bot text language override
- `RECOMP_BOT_LEAP_TOP` — LeapTop: the steering carrot stops at a leap's top and a body at any upcoming top takes that leap
- `RECOMP_BOT_LOW_JET_WALK` — LowJetWalk: a jet leg landing within ~4 m of its foot costs +40, so a similar ground route wins
- `RECOMP_BOT_MECH_JUMP` — 'Mechs jump long clear legs (RECOMP_BOT_MECH_JUMP)
- `RECOMP_BOT_NAV_CACHE` — NavCache: the bots' static obstacle grid is kept on disk, on by default since 1.0.1 (bots ready at t=0 on a cached map)
- `RECOMP_BOT_PATHTEST_SLICE` — Sliced plan equals synchronous plan on NRC
- `RECOMP_BOT_PATH_SLICE` — PathSlice switch and lane-build state machine
- `RECOMP_BOT_PERF / RECOMP_PROFILE` — Bot performance counters and sampling profiler
- `RECOMP_BOT_PU_OFF` — Power-up armour offset (RECOMP_BOT_PU_OFF)
- `RECOMP_BOT_REC_MAX_MB` — The bot recorder keeps the newest 4 recordings and caps one file at 150 MB (worst case 600 MB)
- `RECOMP_BOT_SKIP_HUMP` — SkipHump: the follower's clear-sight corner skip no longer cuts over a mound the planner routed round
- `RECOMP_BOT_STALL` — RECOMP_BOT_STALL stall monitor; RECOMP_BOT_STALL=1 also prints [CS-WAIT] lines: which thread waits on which guest critical section and who owns it
- `RECOMP_BOT_STUCK_MEMORY` — Persistent stuck memory is off by default; Stuck memory across matches is off by default; Stuck memory feedback loop disabled by default
- `RECOMP_BOT_TEST_JUMP` — Match-end test clock jump; RECOMP_BOT_TEST_JUMP advances the game clock
- `RECOMP_BOT_UPJET_DUR / RECOMP_BOT_UPJET_DUR10` — Up-jump burn duration (RECOMP_BOT_UPJET_DUR, UPJET_DUR10)
- `RECOMP_BOT_WATCH` — RECOMP_BOT_WATCH hardware write watch
- `RECOMP_CACHE_NAMESPACE, RECOMP_GAME_OVERLAY` — Cache namespace from cache.version
- `RECOMP_CAM_SET` — RECOMP_CAM_SET=ex,ey,ez,tx,ty,tz[,hfov] forces the human camera pose and the 3D world renders normally from it (M04 verified)
- `RECOMP_CINEMATIC_FPS` — What changes in cinema levels above 30 FPS (measured with RECOMP_FIXED_DT)
- `RECOMP_CINEMATIC_MODE` — Cinematic-only missions cap at 30 FPS and pillarbox
- `RECOMP_CINEMATIC_VIEW` — Cinematic Fill view re-renders the authored band at full output resolution
- `RECOMP_CONSOLE` — Console and log file env vars; RECOMP_CONSOLE=1 enables the development console
- `RECOMP_CS_MODE` — RECOMP_CS_MODE=single puts every guest lock behind one lock
- `RECOMP_CS_TRACE_CRT` — RECOMP_CS_TRACE_CRT logs CRT lock order
- `RECOMP_DEFENSE_CATALOG` — Catalogue dumps and projectile speeds
- `RECOMP_DEFENSE_PROBE` — Defence probe environment variables
- `RECOMP_DEFENSE_PROBE / RECOMP_DEFENSE_TEST / RECOMP_DEFENSE_CATALOG` — Defence diagnostics and test switches
- `RECOMP_EXIT_ON_CLOSE` — RECOMP_EXIT_ON_CLOSE=1 makes window close exit 0
- `RECOMP_EXT_VMA` — RECOMP_EXT_VMA: reserve addresses above the mirrors
- `RECOMP_FB_DUMP` — Framebuffer and texture dump switches
- `RECOMP_FB_HIDDEN` — RECOMP_FB_HIDDEN keeps the diagnostic window hidden
- `RECOMP_FB_VA` — GDI window environment switches
- `RECOMP_FIRSTUSE_TRACE` — Event-correlated first-use trace candidate
- `RECOMP_FORCE_RETURN` — RECOMP_FORCE_RETURN is read at init
- `RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE` — Frame trace: flag file plus per-batch and per-pixel dumps
- `RECOMP_GPU` — RECOMP_GPU must be d3d11 or the hardware renderer stays off; RECOMP_GPU=d3d11 selects the renderer
- `RECOMP_GPU_DEBUG` — D3D11 debug switches
- `RECOMP_GPU_TIMING_FLAG` — RECOMP_GPU_TIMING_FLAG: one-frame GPU timestamp capture
- `RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK` — Guest threads run truly in parallel (RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK is off)
- `RECOMP_HANG_MONITOR` — The hang monitor is on by default: after 30 s without a frame it writes a [HANG] report and hang-<pid>.dmp, and offers to close at 120 s
- `RECOMP_HEAP_CHECK` — RECOMP_HEAP_CHECK cross-checks heap frees
- `RECOMP_HEAP_RECLAIM` — RECOMP_HEAP_RECLAIM turns on real heap reuse; RECOMP_HEAP_RECLAIM is on by default
- `RECOMP_HEAP_RECLAIM, RECOMP_EXT_VMA, RECOMP_TITLE_KEVENTS, RECOMP_GUEST_LOCK` — Opt-in kernel switches for memory reclaim and guest synchronisation
- `RECOMP_HIGH_RES_PACING` — RECOMP_HIGH_RES_PACING: waitable-timer frame limiter
- `RECOMP_HITCH` — RECOMP_HITCH=25 tracer lives in nv2a_pb_exec.c
- `RECOMP_ICALL` — Every ICALL writes three shared non-TLS globals
- `RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE_AT` — RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE_AT names the call site for failure logs
- `RECOMP_KEYBOARD, RECOMP_MOUSE_AIM, RECOMP_MOUSE_SENSITIVITY, RECOMP_INVERT_Y, RECOMP_INVERT_FLIGHT, RECOMP_USB, RECOMP_INPUT_LATCH, RECOMP_MOUSE_GUEST_POLL, RECOMP_USB_PADS` — Input env vars and their INI twins
- `RECOMP_LENS_TRACE` — RECOMP_LENS_TRACE, RECOMP_TEST_LENS_FREEZE, RECOMP_LENS_FREEZE_FIX and RECOMP_COVER_TRACE
- `RECOMP_LIGHTNING_UNITS` — Fix: the lightning flash now lights only N.L-lit model draws (units), not terrain/sky/billboards
- `RECOMP_LOCO_TEST` — Locomotion test environment
- `RECOMP_LT_PAINT_FILE` — RECOMP_LT_PAINT_FILE: paint the draws of chosen vertex programs to see what they are
- `RECOMP_MENU_TRACE, RECOMP_MENU_DUMP, RECOMP_NO_BARREL_ARROWS, RECOMP_UI_LIVE, RECOMP_FOOTER_TRACE` — Menu, footer and pointer trace env vars
- `RECOMP_NV2A_SPIN` — NV2A ack idle backoff was part of the laptop fix in round 1
- `RECOMP_NV2A_TRACE` — RECOMP_NV2A_TRACE and RECOMP_PB_SCAN print pushbuffer activity
- `RECOMP_NV2A_TRACE / RECOMP_PB_EXEC` — NV2A trace and pushbuffer executor switches
- `RECOMP_NV2A_WAKE` — Executor poll+timer wake cuts spin to 0.1 ms/frame but raises 4-thread p99
- `RECOMP_PACK_VERIFY` — RECOMP_PACK_VERIFY=1 checks the fast fingerprint against the per-texel one
- `RECOMP_PB_BULK` — Bulk non-incrementing pushbuffer words decode in one call (2.48 M packets, 0 mismatches)
- `RECOMP_PB_EXEC` — main.c turns on the renderer chain by default
- `RECOMP_PEEK` — Pushbuffer inspection switches: peek, NaN and quad finders, texture state; RECOMP_PEEK and RECOMP_WATCH inspect globals and writers
- `RECOMP_PERF` — APU timing line [APU-TIME] and RECOMP_PERF; RECOMP_PERF turns on CPU phase timing and interval reports; RECOMP_PERF=1 enables PERF logging
- `RECOMP_QTE_TRACE` — RECOMP_QTE_TRACE (separate from capture flags)
- `RECOMP_RENDER_SCALE` — RECOMP_RENDER_SCALE: legacy render-scale variable
- `RECOMP_RENDER_TRACE` — Render and target trace switches
- `RECOMP_RUMBLE` — RECOMP_RUMBLE=0 keeps owned probes quiet
- `RECOMP_RUMBLE_TRACE / RECOMP_UPLOAD_TRACE / RECOMP_EFFECT_TRACE` — RECOMP_RUMBLE_TRACE, RECOMP_UPLOAD_TRACE and RECOMP_EFFECT_TRACE
- `RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY` — RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY diagnostic (opt-); RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY gate; RECOMP_SAVE_LATENCY: opt-in save-stall probes
- `RECOMP_SCENARIOS` — RECOMP_SCENARIOS=0 disables the whole layer
- `RECOMP_SCENARIO_AUTOSTART / RECOMP_SCENARIO_AUTOSTART_STALL` — RECOMP_SCENARIO_AUTOSTART and _STALL: scenario test autostart
- `RECOMP_SCENARIO_AUTOSTART_DROP` — RECOMP_SCENARIO_AUTOSTART_DROP drops each screen's first press
- `RECOMP_SCENARIO_DIR` — RECOMP_SCENARIO_DIR overrides the folder
- `RECOMP_SCENARIO_FILE` — RECOMP_SCENARIO_FILE names the Test file
- `RECOMP_SCENARIO_TRACE` — RECOMP_SCENARIO_TRACE logs cue ids
- `RECOMP_SHADER_PRELOAD` — RECOMP_SHADER_PRELOAD and per-level shader lists
- `RECOMP_STACK_RECLAIM` — Heap best-fit and stack reclaim; RECOMP_STACK_RECLAIM controls stack-to-heap reclaim
- `RECOMP_STALL_PROFILE` — RECOMP_STALL_PROFILE sampling profiler; RECOMP_STALL_PROFILE
- `RECOMP_STATE_HASH` — RECOMP_FIXED_DT + RECOMP_STATE_HASH (7a12416): A==A holds for the clock, not for all of .data
- `RECOMP_TANK_AIM_DIAG` — Aim transition diagnostic logs the controlled component, actor, root and camera
- `RECOMP_TANK_FIXEDSTEP` — Tank physics on by default; RECOMP_TANK_FIXEDSTEP=0 opts out
- `RECOMP_TANK_TRACE_SCENE` — Opt-in tank trace records actor, root and spring stages in a bounded binary
- `RECOMP_TEST_BOT_BA` — Test hooks RECOMP_TEST_BOT_BA / RECOMP_TEST_BOT_VTOL / RECOMP_TEST_HFERRY_REACH
- `RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_AUTOPILOT` — RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_AUTOPILOT feeds the test pad through ma2_bot_test_human_pad
- `RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_FERRY` — Deliverance player ferry 'stall at the pickup' = the test hook's 8 m claw gate, plus a 45 s second-rider chase
- `RECOMP_TEST_MISSION_INDEX` — Direct mission start on a cinema index plays the following cinemas too
- `RECOMP_TEST_VTOL_HURT` — RECOMP_TEST_VTOL_HURT and RECOMP_BOT_PADTRACE hooks
- `RECOMP_TEXTURE_PACK_ASYNC` — With async reads on (the default), the first time a matched texture is needed queue_read starts a and the orig
- `RECOMP_TEXTURE_QUALITY, RECOMP_FMV_QUALITY, RECOMP_TEXTURE_PACK_DIR` — Texture and FMV env vars
- `RECOMP_TITLE_KEVENTS` — KEVENTs written by the title need RECOMP_TITLE_KEVENTS
- `RECOMP_TRAP_NULL` — RECOMP_TRAP_NULL makes guest page zero fault
- `RECOMP_UPLOAD_TRACE` — Upload tracing is a separate switch from RECOMP_PERF
- `RECOMP_VBLANK` — Frame limiter and vblank: a limit of 0 does not wait; a 60 Hz vblank runs even when uncapped
- `RECOMP_VSH_VERIFY` — Vertex shader verification switches; RECOMP_VSH_VERIFY=1 checks vertex programs
- `RECOMP_WATCH=<va> / RECOMP_UNIMPL_TRAP=1` — RECOMP_WATCH and RECOMP_UNIMPL_TRAP locate writers and untranslated code
- `RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS` — Campaign coverage overrides run only in a bounded probe with a logs save folder and a watchdog; RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS dumps the guest stack and aborts; RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS dumps registers and the guest stack when progress stops
- `RECOMP_WINDOW_WIDTH, RECOMP_WINDOW_HEIGHT, RECOMP_FULLSCREEN, RECOMP_DISPLAY_TRACE` — Window and display env vars
- `REPLAY_*` — Replay environment variables
- `XBOX_LOG_FILE / RECOMP_KERNEL_SUMMARY` — Log hygiene: the kernel log goes to the game log (XBOX_LOG_FILE is opt-), no 'ordinal 0' lines for empty thunk slots, [KERNEL] summary only with RECOMP_PERF / RECOMP_KERNEL_SUMMARY
- `configure_pc defaults` — Launcher sets process defaults before the game starts
